title: feat: implement core services (metadata, event-bus, tmux, session-manager, lifecycle-manager)
body:
## Summary

Implements the 5 core service modules for the Agent Orchestrator (`packages/core/src/`), as specified in [INT-1327](https://linear.app/composio/issue/INT-1327):

- **`metadata.ts`** — Flat-file key=value session metadata read/write, matching the existing bash script format. Supports read, write, partial update, delete with archive, and list.
- **`event-bus.ts`** — In-process pub/sub with JSONL append-only persistence. Typed + wildcard listeners, priority inference, filtered history queries, and `createEvent()` helper.
- **`tmux.ts`** — Async wrappers around tmux commands via `execFile` (no shell injection). Handles long/multiline messages via `load-buffer`/`paste-buffer`. Covers list, create, send-keys, capture-pane, kill, and pane TTY discovery.
- **`session-manager.ts`** — Session CRUD orchestrating Runtime + Agent + Workspace plugins. Full spawn pipeline (workspace → runtime → agent), list with live runtime checks, kill with cleanup, batch cleanup (PR state + issue state + runtime liveness), and message delivery.
- **`lifecycle-manager.ts`** — State machine per session with configurable polling interval. Detects status transitions, emits events, triggers configured reactions (send-to-agent, notify, auto-merge) with retry counting and time-based escalation. Routes notifications by priority.

All services implement interfaces from `types.ts`. Updated `index.ts` to export all new modules. Typecheck and build pass cleanly.

## Test plan

- [ ] Run `pnpm typecheck` — verify zero type errors across all packages
- [ ] Run `pnpm build` — verify all packages compile
- [ ] Review metadata read/write matches existing bash key=value format
- [ ] Review event-bus JSONL serialization/deserialization round-trips correctly
- [ ] Review tmux wrappers handle edge cases (no server, long messages)

## Summary

Implements three core plugin interfaces from `packages/core/src/types.ts`, replacing the bash reference scripts with typed TypeScript plugins:

- **`scm-github`** (510 lines) — Full GitHub SCM integration via `gh` CLI
  - PR lifecycle: detect by branch, state tracking, merge, close
  - CI tracking: check status mapping, overall summary
  - Reviews: human reviews, review decision, pending comments (filters out bots)
  - Automated comments: bot detection (cursor[bot], codecov, dependabot, etc.) including review-level comments
  - Merge readiness: combines CI + reviews + conflicts + draft status into a single `MergeReadiness` result

- **`tracker-github`** (324 lines) — GitHub Issues tracker via `gh` CLI
  - All required Tracker methods: `getIssue`, `isCompleted`, `issueUrl`, `branchName` (`feat/issue-{N}`), `generatePrompt`
  - All optional methods: `listIssues` (state/label/assignee filters), `updateIssue` (state, labels, assignee, comment), `createIssue`
  - Maps GitHub's `NOT_PLANNED` close reason → `cancelled` state

- **`tracker-linear`** (447 lines) — Linear issue tracker via GraphQL API
  - Zero external dependencies — uses raw `node:https` with `LINEAR_API_KEY` env var
  - All required Tracker methods: `getIssue`, `isCompleted`, `issueUrl`, `branchName` (`feat/{IDENTIFIER}`), `generatePrompt`
  - All optional methods: `listIssues` (team/state/label/assignee filters), `updateIssue` (resolves workflow state IDs), `createIssue` (requires `teamId` in project config)
  - Linear state mapping: completed→closed, canceled→cancelled, started→in_progress

All three plugins follow the `PluginModule` pattern (export `manifest` + `create()`), pass full monorepo typecheck, and are registered in the plugin registry.

title: Fix cross-cutting code convention issues across all packages
body:
## Issues found during convention audit

1. **ao-3 (agent plugins)**: Uses `export default plugin` instead of `export default { manifest, create } satisfies PluginModule<T>` — loses compile-time type checking
2. **ao-5 (CLI)**: Uses `exec` (19 occurrences) instead of `execFile` — shell injection vulnerability
3. **ao-6 (web)**: 2 bare imports without `.js` extension; re-declares types locally instead of importing from `@agent-orchestrator/core`
4. **Duplicated code**: TTY process detection duplicated across 3 agent plugins; `getTmuxSessions()` duplicated across 5 CLI files; `gh()` helper duplicated in scm-github and tracker-github
5. **Missing shared utilities**: shell-escape function, session ID validator, AppleScript escaper

## Acceptance criteria
- All plugins use `satisfies PluginModule<T>` pattern
- Zero `exec` usage — all replaced with `execFile`
- All local imports use `.js` extension
- Web types import from `@agent-orchestrator/core` (only dashboard-specific extensions defined locally)
- Shared utilities extracted to core or a shared internal package
- `pnpm lint` passes with zero warnings

title: Design and implement end-to-end install & setup experience
body:
## Problem

A new user should be able to go from zero to managing parallel agents in under 5 minutes. Currently the install/setup path is fragmented — CLI exists but isn't published, config exists but isn't wired, and there's no guided onboarding.

## Vision

```bash
# 1. Install
npm install -g @agent-orchestrator/cli

# 2. Go to your repo
cd ~/my-project

# 3. Init — interactive wizard
ao init
# → Detects git repo, default branch, remote
# → Asks: which agent? (claude-code / codex / aider)
# → Asks: issue tracker? (github-issues / linear / jira)
# → Asks: notifications? (desktop / slack / webhook)
# → Creates agent-orchestrator.yaml
# → Optionally creates .cursor/BUGBOT.md

# 4. Start working
ao spawn my-project 42        # spawn agent for issue #42
ao status                      # see all sessions
ao dashboard                   # open web UI
```

## Design Questions to Flesh Out

1. **Global vs local install** — should `ao` be installed globally, or per-project via `npx @agent-orchestrator/cli`? Or both?
2. **Config location** — should `agent-orchestrator.yaml` live in the repo root (checked in, shared with team) or in `~/.config/agent-orchestrator/` (personal)?
3. **Multi-repo support** — how does one `ao` installation manage multiple repos? Is it one config per repo, or a central config listing all projects?
4. **Auto-detection** — `ao init` should auto-detect as much as possible:
   - Git remote → repo owner/name
   - Default branch (main vs master vs develop)
   - Existing `.claude` dir → suggest claude-code agent
   - Existing `.github/workflows/` → suggest github-actions CI provider
   - Package manager (npm/pnpm/yarn) → for postCreate hooks
5. **First-run experience** — after `ao init`, should it offer to spawn a test session to verify everything works?
6. **Prerequisites check** — `ao init` should verify: git, tmux, gh CLI, node >= 20, chosen agent CLI is installed
7. **Config validation** — `ao init` should validate the generated config before writing
8. **Upgrade path** — how do users update when we add new config options? `ao init --upgrade`?

## Scope

- [ ] Design the full install & setup flow (document decisions on above questions)
- [ ] Implement prerequisite checks in `ao init`
- [ ] Implement auto-detection in `ao init` 
- [ ] Add `ao doctor` command — checks health of setup (tmux running, git configured, agent CLI available, etc.)
- [ ] Publish to npm as `@agent-orchestrator/cli`
- [ ] Write a quickstart guide in README.md
- [ ] Dog-food: create `agent-orchestrator.yaml` for this repo and switch from bash scripts to `ao` CLI

## Related

- #8 — Integration (wiring core services to CLI)
- #9 — Code convention fixes

title: Claude Code: detect waiting_input and blocked states via hooks
body:
## Summary

The Claude Code agent plugin currently detects only 3 of the 5 `ActivityState` values: `active`, `idle`, and `exited`. The remaining states — `waiting_input` and `blocked` — were previously detected via tmux screen-scraping (terminal pattern matching), which was removed in the `getSessionInfo` refactor (#6) in favor of native JSONL-based detection.

Claude Code's JSONL session logs don't contain enough information to detect these states. However, Claude Code's **hooks system** provides native event callbacks that can.

## Research Findings

### Hooks that map to missing states

| Hook Event | Matcher | Maps to |
|---|---|---|
| `Notification` | `permission_prompt` | `waiting_input` — Claude needs tool permission |
| `Notification` | `elicitation_dialog` | `waiting_input` — Claude is asking the user a question |
| `Notification` | `idle_prompt` | `idle` (already detected via JSONL, but hooks give real-time signal) |
| `PostToolUseFailure` | (any) | `blocked` — tool execution failed, with error details |

### How hooks work

Hooks are configured in `~/.claude/settings.json` (or project-level `.claude/settings.json`). They receive structured JSON on stdin and execute a shell command. Example:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "Notification": [
      {
        "matcher": "permission_prompt",
        "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "..." }]
      }
    ],
    "PostToolUseFailure": [
      {
        "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "..." }]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### What doesn't exist

- No status files, sockets, PID files, or APIs from Claude Code
- No `claude status` CLI subcommand
- No real-time event stream for interactive (non `-p`) sessions
- The SDK's `stream-json` mode only works in non-interactive mode

## Proposed Implementation

### 1. State file convention

Each session writes activity state to a known path:
```
{dataDir}/{sessionId}/agent-state.json
```

Content:
```json
{
  "state": "waiting_input",
  "detail": "permission_prompt",
  "message": "Claude needs permission to use Bash",
  "timestamp": "2025-06-01T12:00:00Z"
}
```

### 2. Hook injection

The Claude Code agent plugin configures hooks during `postLaunchSetup()` (or via workspace setup). The hooks write to the state file on relevant events:

- `Notification[permission_prompt]` → write `waiting_input`
- `Notification[elicitation_dialog]` → write `waiting_input`
- `PostToolUseFailure` → write `blocked` (with error details)
- `PostToolUse` → clear state back to `active` (tool succeeded, session recovered)

### 3. Updated `detectActivity()` flow

```
1. No runtime handle → "exited"
2. Process not running → "exited"
3. Read agent-state.json (if exists and recent):
   - "waiting_input" or "blocked" → return that state
4. Fall back to JSONL detection:
   - File mtime > 30s → "idle"
   - Last type assistant/system → "idle"
   - Otherwise → "active"
```

### 4. Cleanup

State file is removed when the session is destroyed.

## Integration Tests

Integration tests already exist for the basic lifecycle (`isProcessRunning`, `detectActivity` → `active`/`exited`, `getSessionInfo`). When hooks-based state detection is implemented, the integration test at `packages/integration-tests/src/agent-claude-code.integration.test.ts` should be extended to:

- Trigger scenarios that produce `waiting_input` (e.g., permission prompt) and `blocked` (tool failure) states
- Verify `detectActivity()` returns the correct state in each scenario
- Ensure state file is cleaned up after session destruction
- Test fallback behavior when state file is missing or stale

## Considerations

- **Hook configuration scope**: Project-level `.claude/settings.json` is preferred to avoid polluting user's global config. Need to ensure the workspace plugin creates this.
- **Hook timeout**: Default 10-minute timeout per hook, which is fine for file writes.
- **Permissions mode**: `PermissionRequest` hooks don't fire in `--dangerously-skip-permissions` mode — so `waiting_input` detection only applies to interactive sessions (which is correct).
- **Race conditions**: State file writes are async. `detectActivity()` should treat missing/stale state files as "no signal" and fall back to JSONL.
- **Other agent backends**: This is Claude Code-specific. Codex and Aider can implement their own mechanisms for these states independently.

## References

- [Claude Code Hooks Guide](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/hooks)
- PR #6 — `getSessionInfo` refactor that removed terminal pattern matching

## Summary
Implements live terminal viewing in the web dashboard using xterm.js with proper tmux control mode streaming.

## Changes
- **WebSocket Server** (`packages/web/src/server/terminal-websocket.ts`):
  - Runs on port 3001 alongside Next.js dev server
  - Uses tmux control mode (`tmux -C attach-session`) for event-driven streaming
  - Incremental output updates via `%output` events (not polling or snapshots)
  - Bidirectional communication: terminal input + resize commands
  - Proper cleanup on disconnect/exit
  
- **Terminal Component** (`packages/web/src/components/Terminal.tsx`):

  - Added `ws` for WebSocket server
  - Added `concurrently` to run Next.js + WebSocket server together

## Architecture
Uses tmux control mode (industry standard used by iTerm2) instead of polling:
- **Event-driven**: Receives `%output` events as they happen (low latency)
- **Incremental updates**: Only sends new output, not entire screen snapshots
- **Single process**: One long-lived `tmux -C` process per connection (no unbounded spawning)
- **Proper cleanup**: Processes terminate cleanly on disconnect

## Summary

Implements INT-1355: Auto-update session metadata when agent creates PR or switches branch.

Adds a Claude Code PostToolUse hook that automatically updates session metadata files when agents run `gh pr create`, `git checkout -b`, or `gh pr merge` commands. This eliminates the need for manual metadata updates and keeps the orchestrator dashboard in sync with agent actions.

## Changes

### agent-claude-code plugin
- Implemented `postLaunchSetup` method that runs after agent launch
- Creates `.claude/settings.json` with PostToolUse hook configuration
- Writes metadata updater script to `.claude/metadata-updater.sh`

### session-manager
- Added `AO_DATA_DIR` environment variable to agent sessions
- Allows hooks to locate and update metadata files

### Hook Script Behavior
The hook monitors Bash commands and updates metadata on:
- **`gh pr create`** → Extracts PR URL from output, sets `pr=<url>` and `status=pr_open`
- **`git checkout -b <branch>`** / **`git switch -c <branch>`** → Sets `branch=<name>`
- **`git checkout <branch>`** / **`git switch <branch>`** → Updates branch for feature branches (contains `/` or `-`)
- **`gh pr merge`** → Sets `status=merged`

## Implementation Details

- Hook script embedded in TypeScript as a template string
- Written to workspace during `postLaunchSetup` for self-contained workspaces
- Uses atomic file operations (temp file + mv) to prevent corruption
- Falls back to basic regex parsing if `jq` is not available
- Exits silently for non-matching commands (zero overhead)

title: fix: resolve dashboard GitHub API rate limiting and PR enrichment
body:
## Summary

This PR resolves critical dashboard performance and reliability issues related to GitHub API rate limiting and PR enrichment failures.

**Problem**: The dashboard was making ~84 GitHub API calls per refresh (6 calls × 14 sessions with PRs), quickly exhausting the rate limit. When rate-limited, enrichment failed silently and showed misleading default data ("+0 -0", "CI failing", etc.).

**Solution**: Implemented caching, skipped enrichment for terminal sessions, added graceful error handling, and fixed missing type values.

## Key Changes

### Type System
- ✅ Add `"done"` and `"terminated"` to `SessionStatus` type (missing values used in metadata)
- ✅ Update `getAttentionLevel()` to correctly classify terminal sessions

### Performance Optimizations
- ✅ Skip PR enrichment for terminal sessions (merged, done, terminated, killed, cleanup)
- ✅ Skip PR enrichment when PR state is already merged/closed
- ✅ Implement 60-second TTL cache for PR enrichment data
- **Impact**: 10× reduction in API calls (84 → 7-10 per refresh)

### Error Handling
- ✅ Detect rate limit errors (all API calls fail)
- ✅ Show explicit "API rate limited or unavailable" blocker
- ✅ Don't cache failed enrichment attempts
- ✅ Improved default values ("Data not loaded" instead of misleading "CI failing")

### UI Improvements
- ✅ Add orchestrator terminal button to Dashboard header

### Test Coverage
- ✅ 54 new test cases across 3 test files
  - `cache.test.ts`: 9 tests (TTL cache behavior)
  - `types.test.ts`: 29 tests (attention level classification)
  - `serialize.test.ts`: 16 tests (serialization, caching, error handling)
- ✅ All tests passing

## Performance Impact

| Metric | Before | After | Improvement |
|--------|--------|-------|-------------|
| API calls per refresh | ~84 | ~7-10 | **10× reduction** |
| Rate limit exhaustion | Every ~60 refreshes | Every ~500+ refreshes | **10× improvement** |
| User experience | Garbage data when rate-limited | Explicit "unavailable" message | Clear communication |

## Files Changed

**Modified** (5):
- `packages/core/src/types.ts` - Add missing SessionStatus values
- `packages/web/src/lib/types.ts` - Fix getAttentionLevel
- `packages/web/src/app/page.tsx` - Skip enrichment for terminal sessions
- `packages/web/src/lib/serialize.ts` - Add caching and rate limit handling
- `packages/web/src/components/Dashboard.tsx` - Add orchestrator terminal button

**Created** (4):
- `packages/web/src/lib/cache.ts` - TTL cache implementation
- `packages/web/src/lib/__tests__/cache.test.ts` - Cache tests
- `packages/web/src/lib/__tests__/types.test.ts` - Attention level tests
- `packages/web/src/lib/__tests__/serialize.test.ts` - Serialization tests

## Test Plan

- [x] Build succeeds: `pnpm build`
- [x] ESLint passes: `pnpm eslint`
- [x] Tests pass: 54/54 new tests passing
- [x] Manual verification: Dashboard loads without rate limit errors
- [x] Manual verification: Terminal sessions show as "done"
- [x] Manual verification: Cache reduces API calls on refresh

## Design Decisions

1. **60-second cache TTL**: Balances freshness with API savings
2. **In-memory cache**: Simple, no external dependencies, server-side only
3. **Fail-closed on errors**: Explicit "unavailable" blockers, not misleading defaults
4. **Don't cache failures**: Prevents stale error states, allows retry on next refresh
5. **Skip terminal sessions**: No value in refreshing merged/closed PR data

## Summary

title: feat: wire up live activity detection for agent sessions
body:
## Summary

Implements deterministic activity detection for all agent plugins using agent-native mechanisms instead of terminal output parsing.

## Problem

Original PR wired up activity detection but used terminal output parsing via `detectActivity(terminalOutput)`, which was identified as hacky with potential edge cases. After review, the entire approach was refactored to use deterministic, agent-native state tracking.

## Solution

### New Agent Interface Method

Added `getActivityState(session: Session): Promise<ActivityState>` to the Agent interface:
- Replaces unreliable terminal parsing with native agent mechanisms
- Deprecated `detectActivity(terminalOutput)` method
- Each agent uses its own persistent state (JSONL files, SQLite, file mtimes)

### Implementation by Agent

**Claude Code** (`agent-claude-code`):
- Reads JSONL session files from `~/.claude/projects/`
- Maps event types to activity states:
  - `user`/`tool_use` → active
  - `assistant`/`system` → idle
  - `permission_request` → waiting_input
  - `error` → blocked
- Checks file modification time (30s threshold)

**Codex** (`agent-codex`):
- Searches JSONL rollout files in `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl`
- Maps event types (`user_message`, `tool_use`, `approval_request`, `error`)
- 30-second modification threshold

**Aider** (`agent-aider`):
- Checks recent git commits (Aider auto-commits changes within 60s)
- Monitors `.aider.chat.history.md` modification time (30s threshold)
- Dual signal detection for reliability

**OpenCode** (`agent-opencode`):
- Checks SQLite database at `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`
- 30-second modification threshold

### Core Changes

**Session Manager** (`session-manager.ts`):
- Refactored to use `agent.getActivityState()` instead of terminal parsing
- Extracted `enrichSessionWithRuntimeState()` helper to eliminate duplication
- Graceful fallback to "idle" on detection failures

**Tests**:
- Updated all test mocks to include `getActivityState()`
- Added unit tests for Claude Code path encoding
- All 138 tests passing ✅

## Activity States

- **active** - Agent processing (thinking, writing code, running tools)
- **idle** - Agent at prompt, waiting for input
- **waiting_input** - Agent asking permission or needs user decision
- **blocked** - Agent hit an error or is stuck
- **exited** - Agent process no longer running

## Benefits

✅ **Deterministic** - No terminal parsing heuristics
✅ **Reliable** - Uses agent's own persistent state
✅ **Testable** - Clear input/output without terminal emulation
✅ **Version-pinnable** - Can pin agent versions for stability
✅ **Future-proof** - Agents can enhance their state tracking independently

## Testing

```bash
pnpm build
pnpm typecheck  # All packages pass
pnpm test       # 138 tests pass
```

## Dashboard Impact

Activity badges and emoji now reflect real-time state from each agent's native tracking mechanism.

title: feat: add notifier-openclaw plugin for OpenClaw gateway
body:
## Summary

Adds a notifier plugin that sends session lifecycle events to an OpenClaw gateway via its webhook endpoint.

## Problem

OpenClaw is a WebSocket-based AI gateway (used for multi-channel agent orchestration). There was no way for AO's lifecycle manager to notify an OpenClaw-connected agent when sessions change state — spawn, exit, stuck, error, PR created, etc.

## Architecture

The plugin follows the existing notifier interface (`NotifierPlugin`). It registers itself with the lifecycle manager and receives events via `notify(event, priority)`.

Key design decisions:

1. Uses OpenClaw's `/hooks/wake` webhook endpoint (not REST API). The gateway is WebSocket-based and has no REST `/api/sessions/*/message` endpoint. The webhook injects a system event into the agent's active session.

2. Auth uses a hook token passed as `?token=<value>` query param, matching OpenClaw's webhook auth model.

3. Config accepts `host`, `port`, and `token`. The plugin reads `hookToken ?? token` from config to stay flexible.

4. Events are formatted as human-readable text (not JSON) since they appear as system messages in the agent's conversation.

## Files Changed

- `packages/core/src/plugin-registry.ts` — exports the notifier plugin type
- `packages/core/src/notifiers/openclaw.ts` — the plugin implementation
- `packages/core/src/notifiers/index.ts` — barrel export
- `packages/core/test/notifiers/openclaw.test.ts` — unit tests
- `packages/core/src/types.ts` — type additions
- `packages/core/src/notifier-types.ts` — notifier event types

## Testing

Unit tests cover: event formatting, HTTP POST behavior, auth token handling, error resilience. Full e2e tested: spawn session -> lifecycle detects -> kill session -> vanish detection fires -> notifier POSTs to /hooks/wake -> gateway injects system event -> agent receives notification.

title: feat: wire lifecycle manager into dashboard startup
body:
## Summary

Wires the lifecycle manager polling loop into the web dashboard startup so notifier plugins actually fire on session state changes.

## Problem

The lifecycle manager existed in `packages/core` but was never started anywhere. `lifecycle.start()` was never called, so session state polling never ran, and notifier plugins (desktop, OpenClaw, etc.) never received events. The entire notification pipeline was dead code.

## Architecture

1. Created `packages/web/src/services.ts` as a lazy-init singleton that starts the lifecycle manager on first API request
2. Lifecycle manager is initialized with the session manager and config
3. Notifier plugins are registered during init — config for each notifier is passed explicitly (not via `extractPluginConfig` which only handles workspace plugins)
4. Graceful shutdown added: SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers call `lifecycle.stop()` and clean up
5. Signal handlers use `once()` instead of `on()` to prevent double-fire
6. `agent-orchestrator.yaml` added to `.gitignore` since it contains deployment-specific config (host IPs, auth tokens)

## Key Design Decisions

- Lazy init via `getServices()` rather than top-level await — avoids blocking dashboard startup
- Notifier config passed explicitly during registration, not extracted from workspace plugin config. `extractPluginConfig` is scoped to workspace plugins and doesn't know about notifiers
- Removed `process.exit(0)` from signal handlers — let the process exit naturally after cleanup
- OpenClaw removed from default notification routing — it should only be active when explicitly configured

## Files Changed

- `packages/web/src/services.ts` — new file, lazy service initialization
- `packages/web/src/app/api/` — API routes updated to use `getServices()`
- `packages/core/src/lifecycle.ts` — minor fixes for plugin registration
- `.gitignore` — added agent-orchestrator.yaml
- Various test files

## Testing

All existing tests pass. E2E tested: start dashboard -> hit API endpoint (triggers lazy init) -> lifecycle manager starts polling -> spawn session -> lifecycle detects state change -> notifier plugin fires.

title: fix: scan project subdirs in session-manager list()
body:
## Summary

Fixes session discovery to scan project subdirectories, adds vanished session detection, and fixes the metadata write path.

## Problem

Three related bugs:

1. The dashboard showed 0 sessions because the CLI creates project-specific subdirectories (e.g. `~/.ao-sessions/ao-sessions/` for project "ao") but `session-manager.list()` only scanned the top-level `dataDir`. Sessions were invisible to the dashboard and lifecycle manager.

2. When a session was killed externally (e.g. `tmux kill-session`), the lifecycle manager silently dropped it from tracking. No notification was sent — the session just disappeared.

3. Session metadata was being written to the wrong directory — top-level `dataDir` instead of the project-specific subdirectory, causing `get()` to fail for sessions created by the CLI.

## Architecture

1. `list()` now recursively scans project subdirectories under `dataDir`, collecting sessions from all project folders
2. Added `resolveMetaDir()` helper so `get()`, `kill()`, and `send()` can find sessions regardless of which subdirectory they're in
3. Vanish detection: lifecycle manager tracks previously-seen session IDs between polls. If a session disappears (not in `list()` results but was there last poll), it fires a `session.killed` event with reason "killed externally" instead of silently dropping it
4. Added collision warning: if two projects have sessions with the same ID, a warning is logged (edge case but worth catching)
5. Fixed metadata write path to use the project-specific subdirectory, matching what the CLI expects

## Key Design Decisions

- Vanish detection over exit-time notification: we can't hook into external `tmux kill-session` commands, so polling-based detection is the only reliable approach
- `session.killed` event (not `session.exited`): distinguishes clean exits from unexpected disappearances
- Collision warning is non-fatal: multiple projects can theoretically have sessions with overlapping ID patterns

## Files Changed

- `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` — recursive list(), resolveMetaDir(), metadata write path fix
- `packages/core/src/lifecycle.ts` — vanish detection logic, previousSessions tracking
- `packages/core/src/types.ts` — killed event type additions
- Various test files — 127/127 core tests passing

## Testing

127/127 core tests pass. E2E tested: spawn session -> verify dashboard shows it -> kill session externally -> lifecycle detects vanish -> fires session.killed notification -> notification reaches OpenClaw gateway.

title: feat: implement DirectTerminal with XDA clipboard support
body:
## Problem

Browser clipboard (Cmd+C/Ctrl+C) only worked when an iTerm2 client was attached to the tmux session. Users had to keep iTerm2 tabs open in the background for clipboard to work in the web dashboard.

**Impact**: 12+ hours of investigation across Feb 15-16, 2026

## Root Cause

1. **tmux clipboard detection**: tmux uses XDA (Extended Device Attributes) queries (`CSI > q`) to detect terminal capabilities
2. **xterm.js limitation**: xterm.js doesn't implement XDA (marked as TODO in codebase)  
3. **Missing capability**: Without XDA response, tmux doesn't enable clipboard support (TTYC_MS)
4. **The iTerm2 "magic"**: iTerm2 responds to XDA queries, enabling clipboard for the entire tmux session (including browser clients)

## Solution

Implemented `DirectTerminal` component with custom XDA handler:

```typescript
terminal.parser.registerCsiHandler(
  { prefix: ">", final: "q" }, // CSI > q is XDA query
  () => {
    terminal.write("\x1bP>|XTerm(370)\x1b\\"); // Respond with XTerm ID
    return true;
  }
);
```

**How it works**:
1. Intercepts XDA queries from tmux
2. Responds with `XTerm(370)` identification
3. tmux detects `"XTerm("` and enables TTYC_MS capability
4. OSC 52 sequences flow: tmux → WebSocket → xterm.js → navigator.clipboard
5. **Clipboard works without iTerm2!**

## Changes

- ✅ Add `DirectTerminal` component with XDA handler
- ✅ Add `direct-terminal-ws` WebSocket server using node-pty  
- ✅ Replace `Terminal` with `DirectTerminal` in `SessionDetail`
- ✅ Add comprehensive test/docs page at `/dev/terminal-test`
- ✅ Fix ttyd port recycling (prevent EADDRINUSE errors)

## Test Page

Visit **http://localhost:3000/dev/terminal-test** for:
- Side-by-side comparison (OLD vs NEW)
- Complete root cause analysis
- Implementation details with code
- Node version requirements
- Debugging journey and lessons learned

## Node Version Requirement

⚠️ **CRITICAL**: Requires Node 20.x (currently 20.20.0)

**Why**: node-pty 1.1.0 is incompatible with Node 25+ (`posix_spawnp failed`)

**When can we upgrade?**
- Wait for node-pty 1.2.0 stable
- Test beta versions (1.2.0-beta.11)  
- Switch to alternative PTY library

**Testing upgrades**: See test page for step-by-step verification instructions

## Testing

1. Start dev servers: `pnpm dev`
2. Visit test page: http://localhost:3000/dev/terminal-test?old_session=ao-orchestrator&new_session=ao-20
3. Test clipboard in both terminals
4. Verify NEW terminal works without iTerm2 attached

## Key Learnings

**How we could have debugged faster**:
1. Start with tmux source code (not xterm.js/ttyd)
2. Monitor escape sequences with `tmux -vvv`
3. Compare working vs broken scenarios earlier
4. Check xterm.js known limitations first

## Files Changed

- `packages/web/src/components/DirectTerminal.tsx` - Main component
- `packages/web/src/server/direct-terminal-ws.ts` - WebSocket server
- `packages/web/src/components/SessionDetail.tsx` - Use DirectTerminal
- `packages/web/src/app/dev/terminal-test/page.tsx` - Test/docs page
- `packages/web/src/server/terminal-websocket.ts` - Fix port recycling

title: docs: Root Cause Analysis for CLAUDECODE Environment Variable Bug
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a comprehensive root cause analysis (RCA) document for the CLAUDECODE environment variable bug that was fixed in commit a686645. The bug caused all spawned sessions (ao-22 through ao-25) to fail silently when the spawn command didn't call `agent.getEnvironment()`, leading to spawned sessions inheriting CLAUDECODE from the parent orchestrator.

## Contents

The RCA document (`docs/RCA-CLAUDECODE-BUG.md`) provides:

### Investigation Findings
- Complete timeline of events (Feb 13-16, 2026)
- Detailed analysis of each commit in the sequence
- Code snippets showing the progression from working → broken → fixed
- Comparison between spawn (incorrect) and start (correct) implementations

### Root Cause
1. **Interface-Implementation Gap** - Agent interface defined `getEnvironment()` but spawn never called it
2. **Refactoring Oversight** - Original hardcoded `unset CLAUDECODE &&` worked; refactor to plugins forgot environment setup
3. **Inconsistent Implementation** - Start command (Feb 15) did it correctly, spawn (Feb 14) didn't
4. **Silent Failure Mode** - Sessions created, metadata written, but agent never started

### Why It Wasn't Caught
1. **Insufficient Test Coverage** - Tests mocked `getEnvironment()` but never verified it was called
2. **No Contract Validation** - No runtime/compile-time enforcement of the two-method pattern
3. **Manual Testing Gap** - Bug only manifests when spawning from inside Claude Code session
4. **Review Process Gap** - Start command PR showed correct pattern but wasn't cross-referenced

### Prevention Measures (Prioritized)

**High Priority:**
1. Integration tests verifying spawned agents actually start
2. Improved test assertions verifying `getEnvironment()` is called
3. Health checks that fail fast if agent doesn't start
4. Documentation of agent plugin contract
5. PR checklist for agent plugin changes

**Medium Priority:**
6. Runtime validation that spawn properly uses agent plugins
7. Documentation in CLAUDE.md

**Low Priority:**
8. ESLint rule for agent contract enforcement (future)

### Code Examples

The RCA includes concrete code examples for all prevention measures:

- ESLint rule skeleton

Fixes activity detection showing 'idle' for sessions with visible prompts waiting for input. Users expected this to show as active or ready state.

title: fix: increase delays in spawn prompt submission to ensure Enter is processed
body:
## Summary
Fixes issue where spawned sessions would send the prompt text but the Enter keystroke would not be submitted, requiring manual Enter press by the user.

## Changes
- **tmux.ts sendKeys()**: Increase delay after paste-buffer from 300ms to 1000ms to ensure tmux processes the paste before receiving the Enter keystroke
- **tmux.ts sendKeys()**: Add 100ms delay after Escape key to ensure it's processed before pasting begins
- **spawn.ts**: Increase wait time from 1s to 2s before sending initial prompt to allow Claude to fully initialize

## Root Cause
The issue occurred due to race conditions in tmux's paste buffer processing:
1. paste-buffer command queues the paste operation
2. If Enter is sent too quickly, it may be processed before the paste completes
3. This leaves the prompt unsent in the input buffer
4. Claude's permission prompts during initialization can also delay input readiness

## Testing Recommendations
Test by spawning sessions with different prompt lengths:
- Short single-line prompts (< 200 chars)
- Long multi-line prompts (> 200 chars, uses paste-buffer)
- Verify Enter is automatically submitted without manual intervention

Closes FIX-SPAWN-PROMPT-SUBMIT

title: fix: clean Next.js build artifacts in setup script
body:
## Problem

The setup script (`scripts/setup.sh`) can fail during the build phase when stale Next.js build artifacts exist in `packages/web/.next`. This happens when:

- Running setup after rebasing or switching branches
- Running setup after a failed previous build
- Running setup in a fresh clone that had artifacts committed (shouldn't happen, but can)

Error seen:
```
Error: Cannot find module './705.js'
packages/web build: Failed
```

## Solution

Add cleanup step before building:
```bash
echo "🧹 Cleaning stale build artifacts..."
rm -rf packages/web/.next
```

This ensures a clean build every time the setup script runs, preventing module resolution errors from webpack's internal chunk files.

## Testing

✅ Tested setup script end-to-end - completes successfully
✅ All packages build without errors  
✅ No impact on normal build workflow (Next.js will recreate .next)

- Discovered during verification of PR #66
- This fix ensures seamless onboarding works reliably for new users

title: fix: activity detection — fix path encoding bug, add ready state
body:
## Summary

- **Fix critical path encoding bug**: `toClaudeProjectPath()` stripped the leading `/` instead of replacing it with `-`, causing JSONL-based activity detection to **never find any session files**. The entire feature from PR #45 was silently broken.
- **Add "ready" ActivityState**: Distinguishes sessions that finished their turn and are waiting at the prompt (`ready`) from sessions actively processing (`active`) and sessions stale beyond a threshold (`idle`).
- **Configurable threshold**: `readyThresholdMs` in `agent-orchestrator.yaml` (default: 5 minutes) controls when ready/active transitions to idle.
- **Explicit JSONL type handling**: Maps real Claude Code entry types (`progress`, `assistant`, `user`, `system`) plus spec types (`tool_use`, `summary`, `result`, `permission_request`, `error`) to the correct activity states.

## Activity State Logic

| JSONL Last Entry | Age < threshold | Age > threshold |
|---|---|---|
| `user`, `tool_use`, `progress` | `active` | `idle` |
| `assistant`, `system`, `summary`, `result` | `ready` | `idle` |
| `permission_request` | `waiting_input` | `waiting_input` |
| `error` | `blocked` | `blocked` |
| No JSONL found / process alive | `active` | `active` |

title: fix: agents silently block at Claude trust dialog when permissions: skip is not set
body:
## What this fixes

Every new user who runs `ao init --auto` and then spawns agents ends up with all sessions stuck at **"spawning"** forever. The dashboard shows 0 working, 0 PRs, no errors. The system appears to be doing nothing.

The actual cause: Claude shows an interactive trust prompt when it enters a directory for the first time —

```
Do you trust the files in this folder?
/Users/you/.worktrees/my-project/session-1

❯ 1. Yes, proceed
  2. No, exit

Enter to confirm · Esc to cancel
```

This prompt is waiting for a keypress that never arrives. The agent process is blocked inside tmux. There's no error output, no log, nothing in the dashboard to indicate what happened. For a new user this looks like a broken installation.

## Why this was the default behavior

`ao init --auto` (in `packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts`, `handleAutoMode()`) built the config object without the `agentConfig.permissions` field. The claude-code plugin defaults to `"default"` when the field is absent, which means no `--dangerously-skip-permissions` flag is passed to Claude. Every spawned agent hits the trust dialog, blocks, and stays at "spawning" indefinitely.

The option existed in `agent-orchestrator.yaml.example` as a commented-out line, so it was known — it just wasn't wired into the auto-setup path.

## What changed

**`packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts`**
Added `agentConfig: { permissions: "skip" }` to the defaults block that `ao init --auto` emits. Includes an inline comment explaining *why* it's required so anyone reading the generated file understands it's not optional.

**`README.md`**
- Updated the Configuration code example to show `agentConfig.permissions: skip`
- Added a callout block explaining the trust-dialog failure mode, why the flag is safe in the AO context (user owns the worktrees), and what happens without it
- Added the symptom ("all agents stuck at spawning") to the Troubleshooting quick-reference so users who hit this after editing their config manually can find the fix

## Why `permissions: skip` is safe here

`--dangerously-skip-permissions` bypasses Claude's per-directory trust check. In normal interactive use this is a meaningful security boundary. In the AO context it is safe because:

1. AO itself creates every worktree from the user's own repository
2. The user already chose to run `ao spawn` against that repo
3. Without this flag, AO simply does not function — all sessions block silently

The flag should be the default for `ao init --auto`. Users who want the stricter behavior can remove the field from their config.

## Reproducing the bug (before this fix)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator.git
cd agent-orchestrator && bash scripts/setup.sh
cd ~/any-github-repo
ao init --auto   # generates config WITHOUT agentConfig.permissions
ao start
ao spawn my-project 1  # agent launches, hits trust dialog, blocks forever
# dashboard: 1 session, 0 working, stuck at "spawning"
```

## After this fix

`ao init --auto` generates:

```yaml
defaults:
  runtime: tmux
  agent: claude-code
  workspace: worktree
  notifiers: [desktop]
  agentConfig:
    permissions: skip  # required — see note in README
```

Agents launch with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, skip the trust dialog, and start working immediately.

title: bug: web dashboard loads wrong config when run from packages/web — findConfigFile does not walk up directory tree
body:
## Problem

When `ao start` launches the Next.js dashboard from `packages/web/`, calling `loadConfig()` inside the web server resolves to `~/.agent-orchestrator.yaml` (the home-directory fallback) rather than the project root `agent-orchestrator.yaml`.

This happens because `findConfigFile()` only checks:
1. `process.cwd()/agent-orchestrator.yaml` → `packages/web/agent-orchestrator.yaml` (doesn't exist)
2. `~/.agent-orchestrator.yaml` (matches — uses this stale/wrong file)

The monorepo root `agent-orchestrator.yaml` (two directories above CWD) is never checked.

## Impact

- Dashboard shows 0 sessions even when sessions exist on disk
- Projects configured in the root yaml are invisible to the dashboard
- Users with a stale `~/.agent-orchestrator.yaml` (e.g., from the legacy bash-script era) get wrong `dataDir`, wrong projects

## Reproduction

1. Have `~/.agent-orchestrator.yaml` present with a different `dataDir` than the project root yaml
2. Run `ao start <project>` (Next.js CWD becomes `packages/web`)
3. `/api/sessions` returns 0 even though `ao spawn` correctly wrote sessions to disk

## Root cause

`findConfigFile()` in `packages/core/src/config.ts` does not walk up the directory tree. Almost all modern tools (Cargo, Node, ESLint, etc.) walk from CWD up to the filesystem root to find config files.

## Fix options

**Option A** (minimal): Pass the resolved config path from `ao start` to the web server via an env var (`AO_CONFIG_PATH`), and have `loadConfig()` in the web server use it.

**Option B** (proper): Implement directory traversal in `findConfigFile()` — walk from `process.cwd()` up to `/`, checking each level for `agent-orchestrator.yaml`.

Option A is simpler and avoids changing the config loading semantics.

## Workaround

Keep `~/.agent-orchestrator.yaml` in sync with the project root yaml (matching `dataDir`, `worktreeDir`, and projects list).

title: fix: defaults.agentConfig not merged into project config — agents ignore permissions:skip in defaults
body:
## Problem

\`spawn.ts\` reads \`project.agentConfig?.permissions\` directly — it never merges \`defaults.agentConfig\` into the resolved project config. So if a user puts \`agentConfig.permissions: skip\` under \`defaults:\` (as the README example shows), agents still block at the Claude trust dialog.

## Reproduction

\`\`\`yaml
defaults:
  agentConfig:
    permissions: skip   # ← this is silently ignored

projects:
  myproject:
    repo: org/myproject
    # no agentConfig here — inherits nothing
\`\`\`

Run \`ao spawn myproject 1\`. Agent spawns but blocks at "Do you trust files in this folder?"

## Expected

\`defaults.agentConfig\` should be deeply merged into each project's resolved config, the same way \`defaults.runtime\`, \`defaults.agent\`, etc. are applied.

## Fix

In \`applyProjectDefaults()\` in \`config.ts\` (or wherever project defaults are merged), add:

\`\`\`typescript
project.agentConfig = {
  ...config.defaults?.agentConfig,
  ...project.agentConfig,
};
\`\`\`

This is analogous to how other plugin configs handle defaults.

title: fix: ao spawn leaves orphaned worktrees and branches on failure — re-spawn fails with "branch already exists"
body:
## Problem

When \`ao spawn\` fails partway through (network error, git error, Claude crash, etc.), it leaves behind:
- A git worktree at \`~/.worktrees/{project}/{session}\`
- A git branch \`feat/{issue}\` in the repo
- A metadata file at \`{dataDir}/{project}-sessions/{session}\`

On the next \`ao spawn\` attempt for the same issue, git refuses to create the branch because it already exists:

\`\`\`
fatal: a branch named 'feat/4' already exists
Error: Failed to create worktree
\`\`\`

The user must manually run:
\`\`\`bash
git worktree prune
git branch -D feat/4
\`\`\`

## Expected

\`ao spawn\` should either:
1. Detect existing orphaned state and clean it up before retrying, or
2. Provide a \`--force\` flag to overwrite, or
3. Give a clear error message with the exact cleanup commands to run

## Additional context

\`ao session cleanup\` only removes sessions where the PR is merged. It does not handle the orphaned-worktree case where a session never got off the ground.

feat: orchestrator session should be an AI agent, not a dumb shell
body:
## Problem

The current UX loop is:

1. User opens GitHub to create an issue (or uses `gh issue create` manually)
2. User notes the issue number
3. User runs `ao spawn <project> <number>`
4. Repeat for every issue

The \"orchestrator\" tmux session that `ao start` creates is just a plain shell. There's no AI in it. It offers nothing beyond what the user could do in any terminal.

## What it should be

The orchestrator session should be a Claude Code (or similar) session that:

- **Understands the project** — repo, open issues, recent PRs, running agents
- **Creates issues from descriptions** — \"fix the config loading bug\" → creates GitHub issue → spawns agent
- **Monitors agents naturally** — you ask \"how's ao-1 doing?\" → it peeks at the tmux session and summarizes
- **Coordinates dependencies** — \"spawn issue 8 only after 5, 6, 7 are merged\" → it watches and acts

Concretely, the loop should become:

```
# In the orchestrator session (Claude Code running there)
> we found a bug where defaults.agentConfig is ignored by spawn
→ Creates issue #74 with proper description
→ Spawns ao spawn ao 74
→ "Agent ao-1 is working on feat/74. I'll notify you when it opens a PR."
```

## Why this matters

Without this, AO is infrastructure that requires manual orchestration. The viral moment — \"I described work and 4 agents started in parallel\" — doesn't happen because the human is still doing all the coordination manually.

The CLAUDE.orchestrator.md file hints at this vision but the implementation is just a blank tmux shell.

## Suggested implementation

1. Instead of `tmux new-session` for the orchestrator, launch Claude Code in the project root with a system prompt that gives it:
   - `ao` CLI access
   - `gh` CLI access  
   - Awareness of all running sessions and their status
   - Instructions to act as orchestrator (create issues, spawn agents, monitor, coordinate)

2. The user interacts with it conversationally and the AI handles all the `ao spawn` / `gh issue create` plumbing.

title: bug: session status never updates after spawn — dashboard permanently shows 'spawning'
body:
## Problem

`ao spawn` writes `status=spawning` to the metadata file. Nothing ever updates it afterward.

The dashboard shows all sessions as "spawning" indefinitely — even sessions where the agent has been working for hours, created PRs, and gone idle. The working/PR/review counters are always 0.

## Root cause

There is no background process that:
- Detects when an agent transitions from spawning → working (tmux session active, Claude running)
- Detects when an agent creates a PR (could poll `gh pr list --head <branch>`)
- Updates `status` in the metadata file accordingly

The agent itself (Claude Code) has no mechanism to write back to AO metadata.

## Impact

The dashboard's primary value — at-a-glance session state — is completely broken for `ao spawn` sessions. Every session card shows "spawning" regardless of actual state.

## Fix

A background status-sync loop that runs periodically (e.g. every 30s) and for each session:
1. Checks if the tmux session is alive → if dead, set `status=exited`
2. Checks if a Claude process is running in that session → if yes, set `status=working`  
3. Runs `gh pr list --head <branch> --json number,url` → if PR exists, write `pr=<url>` and set `status=pr_open`
4. Checks PR review state → update to `review_pending`, `changes_requested`, `approved` accordingly

This loop could run inside `session-manager` or as a separate reconciler triggered by the SSE events endpoint.

title: bug: PR URL never written to session metadata — dashboard always shows 'No PR associated'
body:
## Problem

When an agent (Claude Code) runs `gh pr create` and opens a PR, nothing writes the PR URL back to the session metadata file. The dashboard shows "No PR associated with this session" for all sessions, even those with open PRs.

## Root cause

The metadata file format supports a `pr=` field:
```
status=pr_open
pr=https://github.com/org/repo/pull/42
```

But there is no mechanism that:
- Detects when a branch gets a PR on GitHub
- Writes `pr=<url>` into the session metadata
- Updates `status` to `pr_open`

Claude Code agents don't know about AO's metadata format and won't write to it themselves.

## Fix

As part of the status-sync loop (see related issue), periodically run:
```bash
gh pr list --head <branch> --repo <repo> --json number,url,state
```

If a PR exists, call `updateMetadata(dataDir, sessionId, { pr: url, status: "pr_open" })`.

This would also unlock the CI/review enrichment in the dashboard (which already has the code to show CI status and review state — it just never gets a PR URL to work with).

title: feat: Mission Control tab — live visualization of agent activity (Gource-inspired)
body:
## Goal

Add a \"Mission Control\" tab to the dashboard that makes parallel agent activity feel alive — the viral moment where someone screen-records 8 agents autonomously building a codebase in real time.

Reference: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=97irLVqYJCI (Overstory dashboard aesthetic)

## What to build

A new `/activity` tab in the Next.js dashboard with three panels:

### 1. Live event stream (right panel)
Real-time scrolling feed of agent actions via SSE:
```

● ao-1  pushed feat/74 → opened PR #82                       14s ago  
● ao-2  modified packages/core/src/session-manager.ts         31s ago
● ao-3  CI passing on feat/79                                  1m ago
```
Powered by watching git activity (new commits on worktree branches) and GitHub webhook/poll events.

### 2. Branch timeline (center panel)
Horizontal swimlane per agent. Commits appear as nodes on the lane as they happen. Visual diff of how far each branch has diverged from main.

```
main  ──────────────────────────────────────────
ao-1  ──────●─────────●──                  feat/74
ao-2  ──────────●─────────●───             feat/78  
ao-3  ──────●──────●──────────●──          feat/79
```

Use `gitgraph.js` or a lightweight D3 SVG renderer.

### 3. Gource-inspired agent map (left panel)
D3 force-directed canvas visualization:
- Central node = main branch (repo)
- Each active agent = labeled glowing node orbiting the center
- File paths = leaf nodes that light up when touched by a commit
- Edges pulse when an agent modifies a file
- PR opened = arc connecting agent node back to center

Inspired by Gource (https://gource.io) but rendered entirely in browser via D3/Canvas. No native dependency.

## Data sources

- **Git activity**: poll `git log --oneline --since=5min` on each worktree every 10s
- **File changes**: `git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD` per agent's latest commit
- **PR/CI state**: existing GitHub polling already in session-manager
- **SSE**: extend existing `/api/events` endpoint with commit/push/PR event types

## Why this matters for virality

The current dashboard is a static metadata table. This visualization makes the *feeling* of autonomous parallel work visceral — you can see files being touched in real time, branches growing, PRs opening. That's what gets screen-recorded and posted on Twitter.

## Implementation notes

- Add `GitActivityPoller` service that watches worktree branches for new commits
- Emit events via the existing SSE infrastructure

title: ao stop logs 'Dashboard stopped' even when no dashboard was running
body:
## Problem

`ao stop` always logs `Dashboard stopped` in green, even if no dashboard process was actually running. This is misleading.

## Current behavior

```
$ ao stop
Stopping orchestrator for my-project
Orchestrator session stopped
Dashboard stopped        ← always green, even if nothing was killed
✓ Orchestrator stopped
```

## Expected behavior

Should distinguish between "stopped a running dashboard" and "no dashboard was running":

```
Dashboard stopped              ← when processes were actually killed
Dashboard not running on port 4000  ← when no processes found
```

## Location

`packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts` line ~391 — unconditionally logs success after `dashboardManager.stop()`.

`ProcessManager.killByPorts()` silently succeeds when no PIDs are found on the given ports, so the caller has no way to know if anything was actually killed.

## Fix

Either:
- Have `ProcessManager.killByPorts()` return the count of killed PIDs
- Or have `DashboardManager.stop()` check `isRunning()` first and return whether it stopped anything

title: feat: implement session restore for crashed/exited agents
body:
## Summary

- **True in-place session restore**: same session ID, worktree, and metadata — previously, "restore" just spawned a new session, losing the existing workspace and identity
- **Claude Code `--resume` support**: automatically finds the latest JSONL session file and resumes the conversation, so the agent picks up where it left off
- **Plugin extensions**: workspace-worktree/clone get `exists()` + `restore()`, scm-github gets `branchExists()`, agent-claude-code gets `getRestoreCommand()`
- **CLI + Web**: `ao session restore <id>` command, web dashboard restore button now calls `sessionManager.restore()` instead of `spawn()`
- **Centralized terminal/restorable state**: `TERMINAL_STATUSES`, `TERMINAL_ACTIVITIES`, `NON_RESTORABLE_STATUSES` sets with helpers, shared between core and web

## Details

The restore flow (9 steps):
1. Find session metadata across all projects
2. Reconstruct Session object from metadata
3. Validate with `isRestorable()` — reject merged/working sessions
4. Resolve plugins for the session's project
5. Check workspace exists — recreate via plugin if missing
6. Get launch command — try `getRestoreCommand()` (claude --resume), fall back to `getLaunchCommand()`
7. Create runtime (reuses tmux session name)
8. Update metadata (status=spawning, new runtimeHandle, restoredAt timestamp)
9. Run postLaunchSetup (non-fatal)

title: feat: configurable terminal server ports for multi-dashboard support
body:
## Summary
- Moves default terminal server ports from 3001/3003 to **14800/14801** (zero IANA registrations, zero dev tool conflicts)
- Adds `terminalPort` and `directTerminalPort` to `agent-orchestrator.yaml` config schema
- **Auto-detects available ports** when no explicit config is set — second `ao start` automatically gets 14802/14803

## Problem
When two `ao` dashboard instances run simultaneously (e.g., `ao start` for project A then project B), both try to start terminal WebSocket servers on the same ports, causing EADDRINUSE. The old defaults (3001/3003) were also in the most contested port range in dev tooling (Next.js auto-increments from 3000).

## Solution

### 1. Better default ports (14800/14801)
Researched IANA registry, common dev tools, databases, CI services, macOS system services, and OS ephemeral ranges. The 14800-14899 range has:
- Zero IANA registrations
- Zero known dev tool, database, or CI conflicts  
- No macOS system service conflicts (unlike 5000/7000 for AirPlay)
- Safely below ephemeral ranges (32768 Linux, 49152 macOS)

### 2. Auto-port detection (zero config)
When no terminal ports are configured, `buildDashboardEnv` probes for a free port pair starting at 14800. Scans in steps of 2 to keep ports consecutive. The second dashboard instance automatically gets 14802/14803 without any user configuration.

### 3. Configurable via YAML
For explicit control:
```yaml
port: 3002
terminalPort: 14804
directTerminalPort: 14805
```
Priority: config value > `TERMINAL_PORT` env var > auto-detect from 14800.

## Problem

Tab titles and favicons currently update via polling (5s interval on session detail pages, full page reload on the main dashboard). This means:

2. **Main dashboard favicon**: `DynamicFavicon` currently recomputes health from the full sessions array prop. Instead, it should subscribe to SSE and maintain its own health state, updating the favicon color instantly when any session's attention level changes.

3. **Main dashboard title**: Could also reflect live state (e.g., show count of sessions needing attention: `ao | ao (2 need attention)`).

title: Eliminate TOCTOU race in terminal server port auto-detection
body:
## Context

PR #113 introduced auto-port detection for terminal WebSocket servers. When no explicit port is configured, `buildDashboardEnv` probes for a free port pair starting at 14800, then passes the ports as env vars to the dashboard process.

## Problem

There's a small TOCTOU (Time Of Check To Time Of Use) race: we probe the port (bind + release), then the terminal server binds to it ~2 seconds later. In that window, another process could theoretically grab the port.

**Practical risk: extremely low.** The 14800 range has zero known consumers (zero IANA registrations, no dev tools). This would only matter in heavily loaded CI environments with many parallel processes.

## Potential solutions

1. **Next.js WebSocket proxy** — Route all terminal WebSocket traffic through the dashboard port (e.g., `/ws/terminal`). Eliminates separate terminal ports entirely. Cleanest long-term but most work.
2. **Port discovery via file** — Terminal servers write their actual bound port to a known file. Add an `/api/terminal-ports` endpoint that reads it. Client fetches real ports before connecting.

## Priority

Low — the current probe approach works 99.99% of the time. Only revisit if someone actually hits this in practice.

title: refactor: agent summary should include source metadata to eliminate prompt-detection heuristic
body:
## Problem

When an agent hasn't produced a summary yet, `extractSummary()` falls back to the first user message truncated to 120 chars. That message is typically the spawn prompt, making a poor title. The dashboard currently uses a string-matching heuristic (`looksLikePromptExcerpt()` in `packages/web/src/lib/format.ts`) to detect these, but this is fragile — any new prompt template could slip through.

## Proposed Fix

Have the agent plugin's `getSessionInfo()` (or `extractSummary()`) return a `summarySource` field:

```typescript
interface AgentSessionInfo {
  summary: string | null;
  summarySource: "agent" | "first_message_fallback";
  agentSessionId: string | null;
}
```

This way the dashboard knows definitively whether a summary is real, and `looksLikePromptExcerpt()` can be removed entirely.

## Files Involved

- `packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts` — `extractSummary()` and `getSessionInfo()`
- `packages/core/src/types.ts` — `AgentSessionInfo` type (if it exists, or add it)
- `packages/web/src/lib/format.ts` — remove `looksLikePromptExcerpt()`, simplify `getSessionTitle()`
- `packages/web/src/lib/serialize.ts` — `enrichSessionAgentSummary()` could set a flag

title: feat: instant session tab titles from local metadata
body:
## Problem

Session detail page titles take ~5 seconds to show activity emoji and branch because the page waits for the full `/api/sessions/[id]` response, which includes PR enrichment from the GitHub API. But the title only needs local data:

- **Session ID** — from the URL param (instant)
- **Activity state** — from local metadata file (instant)
- **Branch** — from local metadata file (instant)
- **PR number** — from local metadata file (instant)

None of these require external API calls. The GitHub API is only needed for PR enrichment (CI status, review state, mergeability) which the title doesn't use.

## Proposed Fix

Split the session API into two tiers, or convert the session detail page to a server+client split:

### Option A: Two-phase fetch in client
1. Add a lightweight `/api/sessions/[id]/meta` endpoint that returns only local metadata (no SCM enrichment) — should respond in <50ms
2. Session page fetches meta first, sets title immediately
3. Then fetches the full enriched session data for the detail view

### Option B: Server component with generateMetadata
1. Make the page a server component that fetches local metadata
2. Use `generateMetadata()` to set the title server-side (in the initial HTML)
3. Pass initial data to a client child component for polling/interactivity
4. Title is correct from first paint, no JS needed

Option B is cleaner — the title is in the HTML before any JS executes.

## Related
- PR #111 — added dynamic tab titles
- Issue #115 — event-driven live updates (SSE instead of polling)

title: fix: don't treat UNSTABLE merge state as blocker when CI is pending
body:
## Summary

GitHub's `mergeStateStatus: UNSTABLE` means required status checks exist but aren't all passing. Previously we unconditionally added "Required checks are failing" as a blocker, which caused two problems:

1. **False alarm for pending CI** — dashboard showed "Required checks are failing" while CI was just running
2. **Redundant blockers for failing CI** — both "CI is failing" (from CI section) and "Required checks are failing" (from UNSTABLE section) appeared simultaneously

**Fix**: Gate the UNSTABLE blocker on `ciPassing` — it only fires when the CI section didn't already report the problem. This is also the fail-closed safety net for edge cases where our CI aggregation says "none" (all skipped) but GitHub still reports UNSTABLE.

### Blocker matrix after fix

| ciStatus | CI section blocker | UNSTABLE blocker | Notes |
|----------|-------------------|-----------------|-------|
| failing | "CI is failing" | *(none)* | CI section covers it |
| pending | "CI is pending" | *(none)* | Not failing, just running |
| none | *(none)* | "Required checks are failing" | Fail-closed safety net |
| passing | *(none)* | "Required checks are failing" | Fail-closed safety net |

## Test plan

- [x] `reports CI failures as blockers` — UNSTABLE + FAILURE: only "CI is failing", no duplicate
- [x] `falls back to CI failing when CI fetch fails` — UNSTABLE + error: only "CI is failing"
- [x] `does not treat UNSTABLE as a blocker when CI is pending` — UNSTABLE + PENDING: only "CI is pending"
- [x] `reports UNSTABLE as blocker when CI status is none (fail closed)` — UNSTABLE + SKIPPED: "Required checks are failing"
- [x] All 56 scm-github tests pass
- [x] Full suite: typecheck + lint + test all green

title: fix: handle PRs with no CI checks in dashboard
body:
## Summary

Fixes #117

When a PR has no CI checks configured, `gh pr checks` exits with code 1 and the message `"no checks reported on the '<branch>' branch"`. Previously this was treated as a CI failure, causing the dashboard to show "CI failing" / "CI status unknown" for PRs that simply have no CI.

### Changes

- **`gh()` helper** (`scm-github/src/index.ts`): Now extracts `stderr` from `execFileAsync` errors — Node places CLI output in `err.stderr`, not `err.message`, so callers can inspect the actual error text
- **`getCIChecks`**: Detects "no checks reported" in the error message and returns `[]` instead of throwing
- **`getCISummary`**: Empty checks array already mapped to `"none"` status (neutral, not failing) — no change needed here

### Edge cases handled

- **Detection scoped to `getCIChecks` only** — the "no checks reported" match is in `getCIChecks`'s catch block, not the shared `gh()` helper, so it can't accidentally suppress errors from unrelated commands (`pr view`, `pr merge`, etc.)
- **Real errors still fail-closed** — network failures, rate limiting, auth errors propagate normally and result in `"failing"` status for open PRs
- **Merged/closed PRs** — `getCISummary` already checks PR state before fail-closing, so merged PRs with no checks won't show as failing
- **Frontend `"none"` handling** — `SessionCard.getAlerts()` only triggers on `CI_STATUS.FAILING`, so `"none"` shows no alert (neutral display)

## Test plan

- [x] `getCIChecks` returns empty array when gh reports "no checks reported"
- [x] `getCIChecks` still throws on real errors (fail-closed)
- [x] `getCISummary` returns `"none"` for the no-checks case
- [x] `mockGhError` updated to simulate real `execFileAsync` error shape (`err.stderr`)
- [x] Frontend `SessionCard` shows neutral display (no alert) for `ciStatus: "none"`
- [x] Frontend still shows yellow "CI status unknown" when API genuinely fails (`ciStatus: "failing"` + empty checks)

title: fix: persist session model/permissions in metadata for restore
body:
## Summary

Fixes metadata serialization gaps in the session restore pipeline. Three issues addressed:

- **Metadata fields silently dropped**: `writeMetadata()` and `readMetadata()` didn't serialize `model`, `permissions`, or `restoredAt` fields, even though `SessionMetadata` defined them and `session-manager.ts` wrote them. Values were silently discarded.

- **Restore uses stale config**: `getRestoreCommand()` only read from `project.agentConfig` (current config), not from session metadata (config at spawn time). If the project config changed between spawn and restore, the session would be restored with wrong settings.

- **Typecheck CI failure**: `pnpm -r typecheck` ran all packages in parallel, but agent plugins depend on built type definitions from `@composio/ao-core`. Without building core first, TypeScript couldn't find new interface methods.

## Changes

1. **`packages/core/src/metadata.ts`** — Add `permissions`, `model`, `restoredAt` to both `readMetadata()` and `writeMetadata()`
2. **`packages/core/src/types.ts`** — Add `permissions` and `model` to `SessionMetadata` interface  
3. **`packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts`** — `getRestoreCommand()` now prefers persisted metadata over project config, with fallback for older sessions
4. **`package.json`** — Build core before running typecheck across workspace

title: feat: ao status — support showing exited/historical sessions and search
body:
## Problem

`ao status` only shows active sessions. When a session exits or gets cleaned up, it disappears entirely, even though its metadata still exists in the session metadata files (e.g. `~/.integrator-sessions/`).

As an orchestrator agent, I frequently need to find which session worked on a specific PR or issue. Currently I have to fall back to `grep -rl` on raw metadata files, which is fragile and doesn't give the formatted output that `ao status` provides.

### Real Example

User asked "which agent session was working on PR #1189?" — `ao status` showed nothing. I had to manually grep through `~/.integrator-sessions/` to find it was `integrator-54`. This should be a single command.

## Proposed Solution

### 1. Show historical sessions

`ao status --all` or `ao status --include-exited` — Show all sessions including exited/cleaned up ones, with a clear visual distinction (e.g. dimmed, or grouped separately at the bottom).

### 2. Filter by state

`ao status --state exited` to show only exited sessions, `ao status --state active` for current behavior (default).

### 3. Search capability (highest impact)

`ao status --search "1189"` or `ao status --search "from-scratch"` to find sessions by PR number, branch name, issue ID, or summary text.

This would let the orchestrator instantly answer "which session worked on X?"

## Why This Matters

- **Session continuity**: When respawning work on an existing PR, need to know what the previous session did, what branch it used, and what state it left things in
- **Debugging**: Tracing back to which session created a PR or branch is essential
- **User questions**: Users regularly ask "which session was working on X?" — should be answerable instantly
- **Audit trail**: Historical session data exists in metadata files — `ao status` should surface it

## Implementation Notes

The session metadata files in `~/.{project}-sessions/` already persist after cleanup. `ao status` just needs to:
1. Read all metadata files (not just ones with active tmux sessions)
2. Mark sessions as "exited" / "cleaned" based on whether their tmux session still exists
3. Support flags to control which are shown
4. Optionally support text search across metadata fields (branch, pr, issue, summary)

title: Event-triggered peer code review using local agents
body:
The orchestrator reacts to external review comments but cannot spawn its own agents to perform initial code review. This requires external infrastructure (Bugbot, Copilot) for the first round.

**Proposed:**

When a session reaches `pr_open`, optionally spawn a **reviewer agent**—a separate session with distinct configuration:

```
reactions:
  pr-created:
    action: spawn-reviewer
    reviewerAgent: code-reviewer
    maxRounds: 3
```

Flow:
1. Reviewer checks out PR branch, posts comments via SCM
2. Original agent receives changes-requested reaction
3. Loop continues or escalates to human

Questions:
- Is this achievable with existing reaction system?
- Should reviewer be ephemeral (spawn-review-die) or persistent?
- Static config vs. dynamic reviewer selection based on file patterns?

Related: #78 (both explore multi-agent coordination workflows—#78 focuses on human-directed orchestration, while this proposes event-triggered agent spawning for autonomous peer review.)

## What happened

3. At some point, the session was cleaned up:
   - tmux session `c13a0108f64e-integrator-54` — **gone**
   - Worktree `/Users/equinox/.worktrees/integrator/integrator-54` — **gone**
   - Metadata file `~/.integrator-sessions/integrator-54` — **still exists** (orphaned)
4. The PR is still **open**, not merged, not closed:
   ```json
   {"closedAt": null, "mergedAt": null, "state": "OPEN"}
   ```
5. The dashboard returns 404 for `/api/sessions/integrator-54`

## Expected behavior

Cleanup should **never** remove a session that has an open PR. The cleanup criteria should be:
- PR is **merged** → safe to clean up
- PR is **closed** → safe to clean up
- Issue is **closed** → safe to clean up
- **No PR, no issue, session exited** → maybe safe to clean up (with warning)
- **Open PR, any status** → **do NOT clean up**

## Likely cause

The session failed to start Claude (status stayed "starting") and a subsequent cleanup treated it as a dead/stale session without checking the PR state. The cleanup logic likely only checks tmux session liveness or session status, not the associated PR state.

## Impact

- PR #1189 is orphaned — no session owns it, no agent is working on it
- The worktree was deleted, so respawning requires creating a new session on the existing branch
- User had to manually grep metadata files to even discover which session previously owned this PR

## Suggested fix

1. Before removing any session, check if it has an associated PR and whether that PR is still open
2. If the PR is open, skip cleanup and optionally flag it as "needs attention" instead
3. Consider adding a `--force` flag for cleanup that explicitly acknowledges removing sessions with open PRs

title: fix: Codex detectActivity() is a stub — returns active for any output
body:
## Summary

The Codex agent plugin's `detectActivity()` returns `"active"` for any non-empty terminal output. This means the orchestrator can never distinguish between an idle Codex (waiting for input), a Codex awaiting approval, or a Codex actively working. Stuck detection and needs-input detection don't work.

## Current State

```typescript
detectActivity(terminalOutput: string): ActivityState {
  if (!terminalOutput.trim()) return "idle";
  // Codex doesn't have rich terminal output patterns yet
  return "active"; // ❌ Always returns active
}
```

## Fix

Implement terminal pattern matching following the same structure as the Claude Code plugin's `classifyTerminalOutput()`, adapted with Codex-specific patterns from [dmux](https://github.com/standardagents/dmux):

| Pattern | State | Source |
|---------|-------|--------|
| Last line is bare prompt (`>`, `$`, `#`) | `idle` | dmux agentLaunch.ts |
| Last 5 lines contain `approval required` or `(y)es (n)o` | `waiting_input` | dmux PaneAnalyzer.ts |
| `(esc to interrupt)` visible | `active` | dmux PaneWorker.ts |
| Progress spinners `✶⏺✽⏳` + `"ing"` words | `active` | dmux PaneWorker.ts |
| Fallback | `active` | — |

## Files Changed

- `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts` — `detectActivity()`

## Related

- #17 — Codex: implement getSessionInfo and richer activity detection
- #16 — Claude Code: detect waiting_input and blocked states via hooks

title: feat: Codex setupWorkspaceHooks and postLaunchSetup with PATH-based shell wrappers
body:
## Summary

The Codex agent plugin does not implement `setupWorkspaceHooks()` or `postLaunchSetup()`. This means:

- No metadata auto-updates when Codex runs `gh pr create`, `git checkout -b`, or `gh pr merge`
- Dashboard is blind to PRs created by Codex agents
- CI monitoring, review detection, and notifications don't work for Codex sessions

Claude Code solves this with its built-in PostToolUse hook system. Codex has no equivalent, so we need an alternative.

## Proposed Implementation

### PATH-based shell wrappers

Install thin wrapper scripts for `gh` and `git` at `~/.ao/bin/` and prepend that directory to `PATH` in `getEnvironment()`. When Codex runs `gh` or `git`, the shell finds our wrapper first.

Each wrapper:
1. Strips `~/.ao/bin` from PATH to find the real binary (no infinite recursion)
2. Runs the real command, passing through all args and exit code
3. On success, parses output for metadata-relevant events
4. Updates the session metadata file using `$AO_SESSION` and `$AO_DATA_DIR` env vars

| Wrapper | Intercepts | Updates |
|---------|-----------|---------|
| `~/.ao/bin/gh` | `gh pr create`, `gh pr merge` | `pr=<url>`, `status=pr_open`, `status=merged` |
| `~/.ao/bin/git` | `git checkout -b`, `git switch -c` | `branch=<name>` |
| `~/.ao/bin/ao-metadata-helper.sh` | — | Shared `update_ao_metadata()` function |

### AGENTS.md (secondary signal)

Append an ao section to workspace `AGENTS.md` as defense-in-depth. The wrappers are the primary mechanism; AGENTS.md reinforces the intent if wrappers are somehow bypassed.

### getEnvironment() PATH prepend

```typescript
getEnvironment(config: AgentLaunchConfig): Record<string, string> {
  const env: Record<string, string> = {};
  // ... existing env vars ...
  env["PATH"] = `${AO_BIN_DIR}:${process.env["PATH"] ?? "/usr/bin:/bin"}`;
  return env;
}
```

## Why PATH wrappers?

This is the same pattern used by nvm, rbenv, and pyenv. It works because Codex executes commands through the shell (tmux pane), so PATH resolution applies. The wrappers are transparent — Codex never knows they're there.

## Files Changed

- `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts` — `setupWorkspaceHooks()`, `postLaunchSetup()`, `getEnvironment()`

## Related

- #17 — Codex: implement getSessionInfo and richer activity detection
- #147 — Codex permission flag fix
- #148 — Codex detectActivity fix

feat: Add jira tracker plugin
body:
## Problem

AO had no Jira tracker plugin. Users with Jira-based workflows couldn't use AO to orchestrate agents against Jira issues. Issue #137 requested adding Jira support alongside the existing GitHub and Linear tracker plugins.

## Solution

Adds `@composio/ao-plugin-tracker-jira` — a full `Tracker` interface implementation with **two transports**:

1. **Direct transport** — HTTPS calls to the Jira REST API v3 using Basic Auth (`JIRA_EMAIL` + `JIRA_API_TOKEN`)
2. **Composio transport** — Uses the Composio SDK to call Jira actions (`JIRA_GET_ISSUE`, `JIRA_SEARCH_ISSUES`, etc.)

### Transport design

The original PR used a REST-based transport (`method, path, body`), but this didn't map cleanly to Composio's action-based API (as discussed in the PR comments). Instead of maintaining a fragile path-to-action mapping, the transport was refactored to an **action-based interface**:

```typescript
interface JiraTransportActions {
  getIssue(key: string, fields?: string): Promise<JiraIssue>;
  searchIssues(jql: string, maxResults: number, fields: string): Promise<JiraSearchResult>;
  getTransitions(key: string): Promise<JiraTransitionsResponse>;
  transitionIssue(key: string, transitionId: string): Promise<void>;
  updateIssueFields(key: string, fields: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<void>;
  addComment(key: string, body: unknown): Promise<void>;
  createIssue(fields: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<JiraIssue>;
}
```

Both transports implement this interface. The direct transport maps actions to HTTPS calls; the Composio transport maps them to Composio SDK `execute()` calls. No path-to-action resolution needed.

### Auto-detection

`create()` picks the transport automatically:
- If `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` is set → Composio transport (with optional `COMPOSIO_ENTITY_ID`)
- Otherwise falls back to direct transport (`JIRA_EMAIL` + `JIRA_API_TOKEN`)
- `JIRA_HOST` is always required

### State mapping

Jira status categories are mapped to standardized states:
- `new` → `open`
- `indeterminate` → `in_progress`
- `done` → `closed`
- Status names containing "cancel" → `cancelled`

## How it works

### Configuration

```yaml
# agent-orchestrator.yaml
projects:
  my-project:
    tracker:
      plugin: jira
      projectKey: PROJ
```

### Environment variables

**Option A — Composio (recommended):**
```bash
export JIRA_HOST=mycompany.atlassian.net
export COMPOSIO_API_KEY=your_composio_key
export COMPOSIO_ENTITY_ID=default  # optional
```

**Option B — Direct API:**
```bash
export JIRA_HOST=mycompany.atlassian.net
export JIRA_EMAIL=you@company.com
export JIRA_API_TOKEN=your_api_token
```

### Supported operations

All `Tracker` interface methods are implemented:
- `getIssue` — fetch issue by key (e.g. `PROJ-123`)
- `isCompleted` — check if issue is in a "done" status category
- `listIssues` — JQL search with state/assignee/label filters
- `createIssue` — create with summary, description, type, priority, labels
- `updateIssue` — transition state, add comments, update fields
- `issueUrl` / `issueLabel` / `branchName` / `generatePrompt` — URL generation, branch naming, prompt generation

## Files changed

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `packages/plugins/tracker-jira/src/index.ts` | Main plugin implementation (both transports) |
| `packages/plugins/tracker-jira/src/composio-core.d.ts` | Ambient types for optional `@composio/core` peer dep |
| `packages/plugins/tracker-jira/test/index.test.ts` | 39 unit tests — direct transport |
| `packages/plugins/tracker-jira/test/composio-transport.test.ts` | 20 unit tests — Composio transport |
| `packages/plugins/tracker-jira/test/smoke.ts` | Manual smoke test script |
| `packages/integration-tests/src/tracker-jira.integration.test.ts` | Integration tests against real Jira API |
| `packages/core/src/plugin-registry.ts` | Register `jira` in builtin plugins |

## Testing done

- **59 unit tests passing** — 39 direct transport + 20 Composio transport
- **Build, typecheck, lint all pass** (`pnpm build && pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint`)
- **Integration tests** — exercise all plugin methods against real Jira API; auto-skipped when credentials are missing. Requires `JIRA_HOST` + credentials + `JIRA_PROJECT_KEY`.

Closes #137
