title: feat(agent-codex): mature Codex plugin to match Claude Code support
body:
## Summary

Brings the Codex agent plugin to feature parity with Claude Code by fixing four key gaps identified via cross-referencing with the [dmux](https://github.com/anthropics/dmux) codebase (production-tested Codex orchestration patterns).

### Code changes

**`packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts`** — Codex agent plugin (main changes)

- **Permission flag fix**: Changed `--approval-mode full-auto` → `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` to match the actual Codex CLI flag for unattended mode
- **Terminal-based activity detection**: Implemented `detectActivity()` with Codex-specific terminal patterns:
  - `idle` — bare prompt (`>`, `$`, `#`), empty output
  - `waiting_input` — approval prompts (`approval required`, `(y)es / (n)o`)
  - `active` — `(esc to interrupt)`, spinner symbols (`✶⏺✽⏳`) with `-ing` words
- **PATH-based shell wrappers**: Installs `gh` and `git` wrapper scripts to `~/.ao/bin/` that intercept commands and auto-update session metadata (same pattern as nvm/rbenv/pyenv). Wrappers:
  - `gh` wrapper — captures `gh pr create` / `gh pr merge` output, extracts PR URL, updates `pr` and `status` metadata. All other commands use `exec` for transparent passthrough (no stderr merging)
  - `git` wrapper — captures `git checkout -b` / `git switch -c`, updates `branch` metadata
  - `ao-metadata-helper.sh` — shared helper providing `update_ao_metadata <key> <value>`
- **`getEnvironment()`** — Prepends `~/.ao/bin` to `PATH` so wrappers intercept commands without agent awareness
- **`setupWorkspaceHooks()`** / **`postLaunchSetup()`** — Writes wrappers + appends AGENTS.md section as secondary signal
- **`getActivityState()`** — Returns `{ state: "exited" }` when process is dead, `null` (unknown) when running (Codex lacks per-session tracking)

**`packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts`** — Branch-based PR fallback

- Added step 3 in `determineStatus()`: when `metadata.pr` is missing, calls `scm.detectPR(session, project)` which runs `gh pr list --head <branch>` to auto-discover PRs created by any agent (not just Claude Code which has PostToolUse hooks)
- Gracefully handles SCM failures — retries on next poll cycle

**`packages/cli/src/commands/spawn.ts`** + **`packages/core/src/types.ts`** + **`packages/core/src/session-manager.ts`** — `--agent` CLI override

- Added `--agent <name>` option to `ao spawn` to override the default agent plugin at spawn time
- Allows starting Codex (or any agent) sessions without changing config:
  ```bash
  ao spawn ao --agent codex           # interactive mode
  ao spawn ao --agent codex INT-1234  # with an issue
  ```
- Added `agent?: string` to `SessionSpawnConfig` interface
- Session manager resolves the override agent from the plugin registry before launch

### Security hardening (addressing BugBot review)

- **Sed metacharacter escaping**: Values passed to `sed` are escaped for `&`, `|`, `\` to prevent metadata corruption from branch names like `feat&fix`
- **Fixed-string grep**: PATH cleaning uses `grep -Fxv` instead of regex `grep -v` so `.ao` is matched literally
- **Empty PATH element filtering**: `grep .` removes empty PATH entries to prevent CWD search
- **Newline stripping**: Values sanitized with `tr -d '\n'` to prevent metadata line injection
- **Path validation**: `update_ao_metadata()` validates `AO_SESSION` has no path separators or `..` traversal, `AO_DATA_DIR` is under `~/.ao/`, `~/.agent-orchestrator/`, or `/tmp/`, and resolves symlinks to verify the target stays within the data directory
- **Atomic wrapper writes**: Wrapper files written via temp file + rename to prevent concurrent sessions from reading partially written scripts. Version marker written last for crash-safe idempotency
- **Pipe instead of process substitution**: gh wrapper uses `2>&1 | tee` instead of `> >(tee)` to avoid race condition where tee may not finish writing before output is read

### Why PATH-based wrappers?

Claude Code has built-in `PostToolUse` hooks that fire after every tool invocation, making metadata updates automatic. Codex has no equivalent hook system. Instead of relying on AGENTS.md instructions (which LLMs may ignore), we intercept the actual shell commands via PATH precedence — the same battle-tested pattern used by nvm, rbenv, and pyenv. The wrappers:
1. Remove `~/.ao/bin` from PATH to find the real binary (no infinite recursion)
2. Run the real command, capturing output only for PR/branch operations
3. Parse output for metadata (PR URLs, branch names)
4. Update the session metadata file via env vars (`AO_SESSION`, `AO_DATA_DIR`)

### Test coverage

- **85 tests pass** in `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.test.ts` (up from 27)
  - Updated 3 existing tests for new permission flag
  - Added 58 new tests replicating Claude Code test patterns:
    - `detectActivity` edge cases (idle/active/waiting_input, regression tests for history vs current state)
    - `isProcessRunning` boundaries (empty panes, name boundary matching, string PIDs)
    - `setupWorkspaceHooks` file I/O behavior (atomic writes, version skipping, AGENTS.md idempotency)
    - Shell wrapper content verification (sed escaping, grep -Fxv, exec passthrough, PR parsing)
- **245 tests pass** in `packages/core/`
- **All 22 packages typecheck clean**

## Closes

- Closes #147 — Codex plugin uses wrong permission flag
- Closes #148 — Codex detectActivity() is a stub
- Closes #149 — Codex setupWorkspaceHooks and postLaunchSetup with PATH-based shell wrappers
- Closes #150 — Branch-based PR auto-detection fallback in lifecycle manager

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run` in `packages/plugins/agent-codex/` — 85 tests pass

title: fix: prevent cleanup from killing sessions with open PRs
body:
## Problem

`ao session cleanup` removed sessions with dead runtimes even when those sessions had open, unmerged PRs. This orphaned the PRs — no active session owned them, the worktree was deleted, and users had to manually grep metadata files to discover which session previously owned a PR.

**Root cause:** The cleanup logic checked three conditions sequentially — (1) PR merged/closed, (2) issue completed, (3) runtime dead — and condition 3 would kill sessions without verifying whether an open PR existed. A session that failed to start (status `starting`, dead tmux) but had already pushed a PR would be killed by the dead-runtime check.

Closes #146

## Solution

Restructure the cleanup decision logic to **short-circuit on PR state**:

1. **PR gate first**: If a session has a PR, check its state immediately. Open PR → skip (never clean up). Merged/closed PR → mark for kill. PR check fails or no SCM plugin → skip to be safe.
2. **Issue check**: If no PR, check if the linked issue is completed.
3. **Runtime fallback**: Only if no prior check resolved, check if the runtime is dead. Emit a warning when killing via this fallback path (since there's no conclusive PR/issue status).
4. **Warning ordering**: Warnings are only emitted after `kill()` succeeds, avoiding contradictory state in `CleanupResult` if kill fails.

### Key behaviors

| Scenario | Result |
|----------|--------|
| PR merged/closed | Kill |
| PR open | Skip (protected) |
| PR exists, no SCM plugin | Skip (safe default) |
| PR check throws | Skip (safe default) |
| Issue completed | Kill |
| No PR, no issue, runtime dead | Kill + warning |
| Issue check fails, runtime dead | Kill + warning |

## Changes

- **`packages/core/src/session-manager.ts`** — Restructured `cleanup()` to gate on PR state first, added `warnings` field tracking, emit warnings only after successful kill
- **`packages/core/src/types.ts`** — Added `warnings: Array<{ sessionId: string; message: string }>` to `CleanupResult`
- **`packages/cli/src/commands/session.ts`** — Render warnings in CLI output for both dry-run and real cleanup; include warnings in the "no sessions" empty-state check
- **`packages/core/src/__tests__/session-manager.test.ts`** — Added 8 new cleanup tests covering: open PR skip, PR state short-circuit, SCM error handling, tracker error fallback, no-tracker fallback, open issue with dead runtime
- **`packages/cli/__tests__/commands/session.test.ts`** — Updated `CleanupResult` mocks to include `warnings` field

## Breaking changes

- `CleanupResult` now has a required `warnings` field. Any code that constructs `CleanupResult` literals (e.g., tests, custom callers) must include `warnings: []`.

## Test plan

- [x] Core tests pass (251 tests)
- [x] CLI tests pass (131 tests)

title: feat(agent-codex): PATH wrappers for git/gh to auto-update session metadata
body:
## Problem

Claude Code uses `PostToolUse` hooks (`.claude/settings.json`) to auto-detect PR creation, branch creation, and PR merge — updating session metadata in real-time. Codex has **no equivalent hook mechanism**, so `setupWorkspaceHooks()` and `postLaunchSetup()` are not implemented.

This means the core "spawn, walk away, get notified" flow is degraded for Codex: ao can't detect when Codex creates a branch, opens a PR, or merges — it has to fall back to polling via `gh pr list --head <branch>`.

## Proposed Solution

Create PATH wrapper scripts (`~/.ao/bin/git` and `~/.ao/bin/gh`) that:

1. Delegate to the real `git`/`gh` binary
2. Inspect command args after execution
3. Update the session metadata file (same `sed` logic as Claude's `metadata-updater.sh`)
4. Prepend `~/.ao/bin` to `PATH` in Codex's `getEnvironment()`

### Wrapper behavior

| Command detected | Metadata update |
|---|---|
| `gh pr create` | Extract PR URL from stdout → `pr=<url>`, `status=pr_open` |
| `git checkout -b <branch>` / `git switch -c <branch>` | `branch=<branch>` |
| `git checkout <branch>` / `git switch <branch>` (with `/` or `-` in name) | `branch=<branch>` |
| `gh pr merge` | `status=merged` |

### Why PATH wrappers over other approaches

- Agent-agnostic — works for Codex, Aider, OpenCode, or any agent that shells out to git/gh
- No dependency on agent-specific hook mechanisms
- Same metadata format as Claude Code hooks — no core changes needed

## Implementation

1. Implement `setupWorkspaceHooks()` in `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts`
   - Write wrapper scripts to `~/.ao/bin/git` and `~/.ao/bin/gh` (executable, mode 0755)
   - Each wrapper: find real binary via `command -v` (skipping self), exec it, inspect args, update metadata
2. Implement `getEnvironment()` to prepend `~/.ao/bin` to `PATH`
3. Implement `postLaunchSetup()` as fallback (same logic)

## Files to modify

- `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts`
- Possibly extract wrapper script templates to a shared location in `packages/core/` for reuse by other agents

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ao spawn --agent codex` auto-detects branch creation via git wrapper
- [ ] `ao spawn --agent codex` auto-detects PR creation via gh wrapper
- [ ] `ao spawn --agent codex` auto-detects PR merge via gh wrapper
- [ ] Wrappers don't break normal git/gh usage (transparent passthrough)
- [ ] Wrappers handle edge cases (no `AO_DATA_DIR`/`AO_SESSION` set → no-op)

title: feat(agent-codex): rich terminal activity detection patterns
body:
## Problem

Claude Code's `detectActivity()` has rich terminal pattern matching (~17 patterns) that distinguish between active, idle, waiting-for-input, and blocked states. Codex's implementation is minimal:

```typescript
// Current: empty → idle, else → active
if (!trimmed) return "idle";
return "active";
```

This means the dashboard and notification system can't distinguish between a Codex agent that's actively working vs. waiting for user input vs. stuck — degrading the "get notified when your judgment is needed" experience.

## Proposed Solution

Add ~15 Codex-specific terminal output patterns to `detectActivity()`:

### Patterns to detect

| State | Patterns |
|---|---|
| **waiting_input** | `"Apply patch?"`, `"Approve?"`, `"(y/n)"`, `"Do you want to proceed?"`, approval prompts |
| **ready** | Completion messages, `"Done"`, exit indicators, final summary output |
| **idle** | Shell prompt patterns (`❯`, `$`, `>`), empty output after completion |
| **active** | `"Thinking..."`, `"Reading..."`, `"Writing..."`, sandbox execution output, file operation indicators |
| **blocked** | Error messages, rate limit indicators, authentication failures |

## Implementation

1. Study Codex CLI terminal output across different scenarios (coding, reviewing, erroring)
2. Add pattern arrays to `detectActivity()` in `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts`

title: feat(agent-codex): session resume workaround via context re-injection
body:
## Problem

Claude Code supports `claude --resume <session-id>` to resume crashed or interrupted sessions. Codex CLI has **no `--resume` flag**, so `getRestoreCommand()` is not implemented. Crashed Codex sessions must start completely fresh, losing all context.

## Proposed Solution

Implement `getRestoreCommand()` with a context re-injection workaround:

1. Re-launch Codex with the **original prompt** augmented with session context
2. Append continuation context to the prompt:

```
Continue from where the previous session left off.

Context from previous session:
- Branch: feat/fix-login-bug
- PR: https://github.com/org/repo/pull/42
- Last known status: pr_open
- Summary: [if available from metadata]

Original task: <original prompt>
```

3. Read branch, PR, status, and summary from the session metadata file

### Limitations

- Not a true resume — Codex won't have the previous conversation history
- Works best for tasks with clear artifacts (branches, PRs, code changes)
- The agent will need to re-orient by reading the existing code/PR

### Future

Track upstream Codex CLI for a native `--resume` flag. When available, switch to the real resume mechanism.

## Files to modify

- `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts` — implement `getRestoreCommand()`
- May need to read metadata from `packages/core/src/metadata.ts`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `getRestoreCommand()` returns a valid Codex launch command with context
- [ ] Resumed session picks up from the existing branch/PR
- [ ] Graceful degradation if no metadata available (just re-run original prompt)

title: feat(agent-codex): session info extraction for dashboard cost/summary
body:
## Problem

Claude Code's `getSessionInfo()` parses JSONL session files to extract:
- **Summary**: Last summary entry or first user message
- **Cost**: Aggregated token usage with USD estimates
- **Session ID**: From JSONL filename

Codex's `getSessionInfo()` returns `null`. The dashboard shows no cost or summary for Codex sessions.

## Proposed Solution

Multi-pronged approach, from easiest to most complete:

### Approach 1: System prompt instruction (quick win)

Add to the system prompt / AGENTS.md:
> "At the end of your session, write a brief summary of what you accomplished to `.ao/summary.txt`"

`getSessionInfo()` reads this file for the summary field.

### Approach 2: Parse Codex rollout files

Codex stores session data in `~/.codex/sessions/`. If we can map a rollout file to our session (see related issue for session-scoped activity state), we can:

1. Parse the rollout JSON for conversation content → extract summary
2. Parse token usage fields → compute cost estimate
3. Use the rollout filename as session ID

**Challenge**: Codex sessions are globally scoped, not workspace-scoped. Need a reliable mapping strategy (PID correlation, timing-based, or env var marker).

### Approach 3: Wrapper-based logging

Extend the PATH wrappers (from the metadata hooks issue) to log git/gh command outputs to a session-scoped log file. `getSessionInfo()` reads this log to build an activity summary.

## Files to modify

- `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts` — implement `getSessionInfo()`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Dashboard shows a summary for Codex sessions
- [ ] Cost data displayed if available (ok to show "N/A" if not parseable)
- [ ] `getSessionInfo()` doesn't throw on missing/corrupted data

title: feat(agent-codex): native activity state detection via session file mapping
body:
## Problem

Claude Code's `getActivityState()` reads JSONL session files scoped to the workspace directory, providing accurate per-session activity state (active, ready, idle, waiting_input, blocked) with timestamps.

Codex's `getActivityState()` returns `null` because:
> Codex stores rollout files in a global \`~/.codex/sessions/\` directory without workspace-specific scoping. When multiple Codex sessions run in parallel, we cannot reliably determine which rollout file belongs to which session.

This means the lifecycle manager falls back to terminal pattern matching for Codex, which is less reliable and has no timestamp information for staleness detection.

## Proposed Solution

### Short-term: PID/timing correlation

1. In `postLaunchSetup()`, record the Codex process PID and launch timestamp
2. In `getActivityState()`:
   - List files in `~/.codex/sessions/`
   - Find the rollout file whose creation time is closest to (and after) the session launch time
   - Verify by checking if the file is still being written to (mtime advancing)
3. Parse the matched rollout file for activity state

**Limitations**: Breaks with multiple simultaneous Codex sessions launched within seconds of each other.

### Medium-term: Environment variable marker

1. Set a unique env var (e.g., `CODEX_SESSION_MARKER=<ao-session-id>`) in `getEnvironment()`
2. If Codex passes env vars to subprocesses, the rollout file may contain traces
3. Use this to map rollout files to ao sessions

### Long-term: Upstream support

File a feature request with OpenAI Codex CLI for:
- `--session-dir <path>` flag to scope session files to a directory
- Or `--session-id <id>` to tag sessions with an external identifier

When available, use the workspace path as session dir for clean per-session mapping.

## Files to modify

- `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts` — implement `getActivityState()`

## Dependencies

- Understanding of Codex rollout file format and structure
- Testing with parallel Codex sessions to validate correlation approach

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `getActivityState()` returns non-null for single Codex sessions
- [ ] Activity state reflects actual agent state (active vs idle vs blocked)
- [ ] Staleness detection works (active → idle after threshold)
- [ ] Graceful degradation when mapping fails (return null, not throw)

title: feat: add opencode agent plugin with full feature parity
body:
## Summary

- Wire OpenCode as a first-class agent in CLI, core, and web plugin registries
- Implement full feature parity between the OpenCode agent plugin and the Claude Code agent plugin

## What changed

### Plugin wiring (commit 1)
- Register `opencode` in CLI plugin resolution (`packages/cli/src/lib/plugins.ts`)
- Register in core built-in plugin registry (`packages/core/src/plugin-registry.ts`)
- Register in web services bootstrap (`packages/web/src/lib/services.ts`)
- Add workspace dependency in CLI and web `package.json`
- Update `ao init` prompt, `agent-orchestrator.yaml.example`, and `SETUP.md` to list `opencode`
- Add CLI plugin test coverage for opencode agent lookup

### OpenCode plugin rewrite (commit 2) — 150 → 768 lines

Ported all Claude Code agent features to OpenCode ([anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode)):

| Feature | Implementation |
|---|---|
| `getLaunchCommand` | Full CLI flag support: `--format json`, `--model`, `--session`, `--agent`, `--title`, `--dir` |
| `getEnvironment` | System prompt injection via `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` env var with `instructions` array |
| `detectActivity` | TUI-aware terminal pattern matching (idle/shell prompt, active, waiting_input/permission dialogs) |
| `getActivityState` | SQLite-backed session state detection — queries OpenCode's `~/.opencode/opencode.db` via `sqlite3` CLI |
| `getSessionInfo` | Extracts session title/summary, aggregates token costs from message JSON data, returns agentSessionId |
| `getRestoreCommand` | Session resume via `opencode run --session <id> --continue --format json` |
| `setupWorkspaceHooks` | Writes `.opencode/plugins/ao-metadata-updater.mjs` — JS plugin using `tool.execute.after` hook for PR/branch/merge metadata tracking |
| `postLaunchSetup` | Ensures metadata hooks are in place post-launch |

**Zero new runtime dependencies** — uses `sqlite3` CLI via `execFile` (no native Node.js SQLite module). Graceful `null` fallback when `sqlite3` is unavailable.

### Design decisions

- **SQLite via CLI, not library**: OpenCode stores sessions in SQLite. Rather than adding `better-sqlite3` as a native dep (build complexity, platform issues), we shell out to `sqlite3` CLI which is available on macOS/Linux. Falls back to `null` gracefully.
- **System prompts via env var**: OpenCode has no `--append-system-prompt` flag. We inject system prompts through `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` env var (JSON with `instructions` array), which OpenCode merges with its config at startup.
- **Metadata hooks via plugin system**: Claude Code uses PostToolUse bash hooks. OpenCode has a JS plugin system with `tool.execute.after` hooks. We write an `.mjs` plugin that detects `gh pr create`, `git checkout -b`, and `gh pr merge` commands to auto-update AO session metadata.
- **Config merging**: `setupWorkspaceHooks` safely merges with existing `opencode.jsonc` (handles JSONC comments and trailing commas).

## Testing

- 40/40 tests passing (`pnpm --filter @composio/ao-plugin-agent-opencode test`)
- `pnpm typecheck` ✅
- `pnpm build` ✅
- gitleaks pre-commit scan clean

title: feat: pre-flight CLI binary check before agent session spawn
fix: preflight agent binary on spawn
body:
## Summary

When spawning a session with `ao spawn <project> --agent codex`, the system validates that the agent **plugin** is registered — but never checks whether the actual **CLI binary** (`codex`, `claude`, `aider`, `opencode`) is installed. If the binary is missing, tmux creates a pane, the command fails silently with "command not found", and the user sees a misleading "Session created" success message.

This PR adds a pre-flight binary check that fails fast with a clear error **before** any resources (worktree, tmux session, metadata) are created.

### Changes

- **`Agent` interface** (`types.ts`): Add optional `binaryName?: string` property so each agent plugin can declare its CLI binary
- **`session-manager.ts`**: Add PATH-based binary lookup before spawn — scans `PATH`/`Path` env, skips directories, handles empty segments as cwd (cross-platform)
- **All 4 agent plugins**: Wire in `binaryName` — `claude` for claude-code, `codex` for codex, `aider` for aider, `opencode` for opencode
- **New test suite** (`agent-binary-check.test.ts`): 140-line test covering found/not-found/skip-when-undefined cases
- **Integration test fix**: Update assertion in `agent-claude-code.integration.test.ts` for correct aliasing

### Design decisions

- Uses direct PATH lookup instead of `which` — avoids external dependency, works on Windows
- `binaryName` is optional — custom/third-party agent plugins without it gracefully skip the check
- Check runs before any resource creation so there are no orphaned worktrees or tmux sessions on failure

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm test` — new unit tests pass (binary found, not found, skip when undefined)
- [x] `pnpm test:integration` — integration test updated and passing
- [ ] Manual: `ao spawn <project> --agent codex` without `codex` installed → clear error message
- [ ] Manual: `ao spawn <project> --agent claude-code` with `claude` installed → spawns normally

Closes #165

title: feat(agent-codex): token usage tracking via getSessionInfo() JSONL parsing
body:
## Summary

`getSessionInfo()` currently returns `null` for Codex sessions. The dashboard shows no cost or summary for Codex agents. Implement JSONL parsing of Codex session files to extract token usage and model info.

**Related:** #162 explored multiple approaches — this issue implements the specific JSONL parsing approach.

## How Codex stores sessions

- Codex writes session logs to `~/.codex/sessions/` as JSONL files
- Each line is a JSON object with a `type` field
- `type: "session_meta"` contains `cwd` and `model`
- `type: "event_msg"` with subtype `token_count` contains usage data: `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cached_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens`

## What to implement

- In `getSessionInfo()`, scan `~/.codex/sessions/` for JSONL files
- Match session to our session by checking `cwd` field matches `session.workspacePath`
- Parse token usage from `token_count` events and aggregate totals
- Return `AgentSessionInfo` with cost estimate (`inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `estimatedCostUsd`), model name, and session ID
- Handle missing/corrupt files gracefully (try/catch, don't crash)
- Use `readFile` + `readdir` from `node:fs/promises`, not `exec`

**Reference pattern:** `packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts` — `getSessionInfo()`, `parseJsonlFileTail()`, `extractCost()`

## Files to modify

- `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts` — implement `getSessionInfo()`
- `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.test.ts` — add tests for JSONL parsing, missing files, corrupt data

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `getSessionInfo()` returns non-null `AgentSessionInfo` when a matching session file exists
- [ ] Token usage (input, output) is correctly aggregated from `token_count` events
- [ ] Model name extracted from `session_meta` entry
- [ ] Returns `null` gracefully when no matching session file found
- [ ] Doesn't throw on missing `~/.codex/sessions/` directory
- [ ] Doesn't throw on corrupt/malformed JSONL lines
- [ ] Tests cover: happy path, no session dir, empty dir, corrupt lines, multiple sessions (picks correct one by cwd)

title: feat(agent-codex): configurable approval mode and sandbox policies
body:
## Summary

Currently we only support `permissions: "skip"` which maps to `--full-auto` (a deprecated alias). Codex CLI actually supports granular control over approval modes and sandbox policies. Implement proper flag mapping.

## Codex CLI flags

**Approval modes:**
- `--approval-mode suggest` — suggest changes, ask before applying
- `--approval-mode auto-edit` — auto-apply edits, ask before commands
- `--approval-mode full-auto` — auto-apply everything (DEPRECATED, use `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`)
- `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` — bypass all approvals AND sandbox

**Sandbox modes:**
- `--sandbox-mode full` — full sandbox (default)
- `--sandbox-mode network-only` — only sandbox network
- `--sandbox-mode off` — no sandbox

## What to implement

In `getLaunchCommand()`, map `config.permissions` values:
- `"skip"` → `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` (replaces current `--full-auto`)
- `"auto-edit"` → `--approval-mode auto-edit`
- `"suggest"` → `--approval-mode suggest`
- `"default"` or unset → no flag (Codex defaults to suggest mode)

If `AgentLaunchConfig` gains a `sandbox` field in the future, also map:
- `"full"` → `--sandbox-mode full`
- `"network-only"` → `--sandbox-mode network-only`
- `"off"` → `--sandbox-mode off`

**Note:** The current `--full-auto` flag is deprecated by Codex CLI. Replace with `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` for `permissions: "skip"`.

## Files to modify

- `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts` — update `getLaunchCommand()` permissions mapping
- `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.test.ts` — update existing tests, add tests for new approval modes

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `permissions: "skip"` produces `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` (not `--full-auto`)
- [ ] New permission values (`"auto-edit"`, `"suggest"`) map to correct `--approval-mode` flags
- [ ] Default/unset permissions produce no approval flag
- [ ] Existing tests updated to reflect new flag output
- [ ] Tests cover all permission modes

## Summary

Currently `getLaunchCommand()` hardcodes `"codex"` as the binary name. Some users install the Codex CLI in non-standard locations, or have it under a different name. Add a helper to resolve the binary path dynamically.

## What to implement

Add a `resolveCodexBinary()` helper that checks (in order):
1. `config.binaryPath` if provided in the agent config (passed via `AgentLaunchConfig` or plugin-specific config)
2. `which codex` via `execFile` to find it on PATH
3. Common fallback locations: `/usr/local/bin/codex`, `~/.npm/bin/codex`

Use the resolved path in `getLaunchCommand()` instead of hardcoded `"codex"`. If resolution fails, fall back to `"codex"` (let the shell resolve it at runtime).

**Security:** Use `execFile("which", ["codex"])` — not `exec("which codex")`.

## Files to modify

- `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts` — add `resolveCodexBinary()`, update `getLaunchCommand()` to use it

## Problem
Next.js fails to build the web dashboard with:
`Module not found: Can't resolve '@composio/core' in '.../packages/plugins/tracker-linear/dist'`

tracker-linear optionally uses the Composio SDK (`@composio/core`) when `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` is set. The web package does not depend on it, so bundling the plugin causes resolution to fail even when only the direct Linear (or GitHub) tracker is used.

## Solution

- Alias `@composio/core` to the stub in next.config.js.

If the Composio transport is ever used at runtime without the real package installed, the stub throws a clear error. No behavior change for users who install `@composio/core` or who only use LINEAR_API_KEY / GitHub tracker.

title: feat(agent-codex): conversation resume via getRestoreCommand()
body:
## Problem

Claude Code's plugin implements `getRestoreCommand()` which builds a `claude --resume <sessionId>` command, allowing sessions to resume with full conversation history. The agent-codex plugin does NOT implement `getRestoreCommand()`, so `session-manager.ts` always falls back to a fresh `getLaunchCommand()` — all conversation context is lost on restore.

**Related:** #161 explored resume workarounds via context re-injection.

## Codex CLI Resume Limitations

Unlike Claude Code (`claude --resume <id>`), the Codex CLI does not have a `--resume` or `--thread-id` flag for CLI mode. True conversation resume requires the app-server's `thread/resume` JSON-RPC method.

## What to implement

Implement `getRestoreCommand()` as a **context re-injection workaround**:

1. Reuse `findCodexSessionFile()` to find the matching JSONL session file for the workspace
2. Extract the thread/session ID from the JSONL filename
3. Extract conversation context from the JSONL (last user prompt or session summary)
4. Build a CLI command with context as the initial prompt: `codex [flags] -- "Continue previous session. Context: <summary>"`
5. Return `null` if no session found (falls back to fresh `getLaunchCommand()`)

**Reference:** `packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts` lines 732-759 — `getRestoreCommand()` pattern.

## Files to modify

- `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts` — add `getRestoreCommand()` method
- `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.test.ts` — add tests

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `getRestoreCommand()` returns a valid CLI command when a matching session exists
- [ ] Command includes the same flags as `getLaunchCommand()` (permissions, model, reasoning)
- [ ] Extracted context is shell-escaped and passed as prompt
- [ ] Returns `null` when no matching session found
- [ ] Returns `null` when workspacePath is missing
- [ ] Does not throw on corrupt/missing session files

title: feat(agent-codex): app-server JSON-RPC client for programmatic Codex control
body:
## Problem

The agent-codex plugin currently launches Codex as a CLI subprocess in a terminal (tmux/process), communicating via shell commands and terminal scraping. Codex provides a much richer **app-server mode** — a stdio-based JSON-RPC API that enables:

- Programmatic session management (create, resume, archive threads)
- Structured turn management (start, interrupt, stream events)
- Proper conversation resume via `thread/resume`
- Typed approval handling (accept/decline file changes, command execution)
- Token usage streaming via `thread/tokenUsage/updated` notifications
- Model discovery via `model/list`

**Reference:** [codex-autorunner](https://github.com/Git-on-my-level/codex-autorunner) — `integrations/app_server/client.py` implements a full JSON-RPC client.

## Codex App-Server Protocol

Codex's `app-server` subcommand starts a stdio-based JSON-RPC server:

```bash
codex app-server   # communicates over stdin/stdout, newline-delimited JSON
```

**Protocol**: Newline-delimited JSON (no `"jsonrpc": "2.0"` header). Four message types:
- Client request: `{"id": "<uuid>", "method": "<name>", "params": {...}}`
- Server response: `{"id": "<same>", "result": {...}}`
- Server error: `{"id": "<same>", "error": {"code": N, "message": "..."}}`
- Server notification: `{"method": "<event>", "params": {...}}`

**Handshake**: `initialize` request → response → `initialized` notification.

**Key methods**: `thread/start`, `thread/resume`, `thread/list`, `turn/start`, `turn/interrupt`, `model/list`.

## What to implement

Add a `CodexAppServerClient` class in a new file `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/app-server-client.ts`:

1. **Subprocess lifecycle**: Spawn `codex app-server`, manage stdin/stdout pipes, handle process exit/crash
2. **JSON-RPC protocol**: Send requests (with UUID IDs), receive responses, route notifications
3. **Initialization handshake**: `initialize` + `initialized` sequence
4. **Thread management**: `threadStart()`, `threadResume()`, `threadList()`
5. **Turn management**: `turnStart()`, `turnInterrupt()`
6. **Event handling**: Callback-based notification routing for streaming events
7. **Graceful shutdown**: SIGTERM → SIGKILL with timeout

Export the client class for use by the agent plugin and future integrations.

## Architecture note

This is **foundation infrastructure** — the client module is self-contained and does not change the existing CLI launch workflow. Full integration with the `Agent` interface (using app-server as primary launch mode instead of CLI) requires architectural changes to the Runtime interface and is a separate effort.

## Files to create/modify

- `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/app-server-client.ts` — new file, JSON-RPC client
- `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/app-server-client.test.ts` — new file, tests
- `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts` — export the client

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `CodexAppServerClient` spawns and manages a `codex app-server` subprocess
- [ ] JSON-RPC request/response correlation works correctly (by ID)
- [ ] Initialization handshake completes successfully
- [ ] `threadStart()` creates a new thread and returns thread ID
- [ ] `threadResume()` resumes an existing thread by ID
- [ ] `turnStart()` sends a turn and streams notification events
- [ ] Notifications are routed to registered callbacks
- [ ] `close()` gracefully terminates the subprocess
- [ ] All errors handled gracefully (process crash, malformed JSON, timeouts)
- [ ] Uses `spawn` (not `exec`) for subprocess — security-safe
- [ ] Tests cover: handshake, request/response, notifications, error handling, process lifecycle

title: docs: JARVIS spec simplification research
body:
## Summary

- Research analysis evaluating the JARVIS build spec against AO's existing architecture
- Identifies MVP features vs unnecessary complexity across 6 areas: real-time (Convex vs SSE), supervisor (LangGraph vs TypeScript), data layer (PostgreSQL+pgvector+Redis vs flat files), subprocess orchestration, auth, and self-improvement
- Proposes a simplified architecture delivering 80% of the value at 20% of the complexity — ~7 days of incremental AO improvements instead of a ground-up rewrite with 10+ new dependencies

## Key Findings

- **Skip Convex**: SSE already works, Convex creates architectural mismatch with flat-file storage
- **Skip LangGraph**: ~120 lines of TypeScript replaces the entire Python supervisor graph
- **Skip PostgreSQL + pgvector + Redis**: Flat files handle tens of sessions; SQLite is the natural upgrade path
- **Skip FastAPI**: No reason to add Python to a TypeScript codebase
- **Defer auth**: Localhost-only tool doesn't need Auth.js v5 + RBAC
- **Defer self-modification**: Use prompt refinement (lessons-learned.md) instead

## Test plan

- [ ] Review research analysis for accuracy and completeness
- [ ] Validate that proposed simplified architecture covers JARVIS spec requirements
- [ ] Check that recommended phase ordering is sound

title: feat(agent-codex): mature Codex plugin with full Agent interface parity
body:
## Summary

- Adds 6 major features to the Codex plugin: token/cost tracking, approval policy mapping, reasoning support for o-series models, binary resolution with fallback chain, conversation resume via native `codex resume`, and a full JSON-RPC app-server client
- Implements PATH-based shell wrappers (`~/.ao/bin/git`, `~/.ao/bin/gh`) for automatic session metadata updates (branch, PR, status)
- Adds rich terminal activity detection patterns (idle, active, waiting_input) and mtime-based `getActivityState()` using session file modification times
- Fixes all CLI flags to match actual Codex documentation (`--ask-for-approval`, `-c model_reasoning_effort=high`, date-sharded session files)
- Streams JSONL session files line-by-line to handle 100MB+ rollout files without loading them into memory
- Adds comprehensive test coverage: 183 tests (131 plugin + 52 app-server client)

Closes #176, #177, #178, #179, #183, #184, #159, #160, #161, #162, #167, #17

## Claude Code vs Codex — Feature Parity Comparison

### Agent Interface Implementation (8 required + 3 optional)

| Member | Claude Code | Codex | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `"claude-code"` | `"codex"` | — |
| `processName` | `"claude"` | `"codex"` | — |
| `getLaunchCommand()` | `claude` CLI flags | `codex` CLI flags | Different flag names; shared helpers for approval/model flags |
| `getEnvironment()` | Sets `CLAUDECODE=""`, `AO_SESSION_ID` | Sets `AO_SESSION_ID`, prepends `~/.ao/bin` to `PATH` | Different metadata hook approach |
| `detectActivity()` | Terminal pattern matching | Terminal pattern matching | Both detect idle/active/waiting_input |
| `getActivityState()` | JSONL introspection (rich) | Session file mtime-based (active/idle/exited) | Codex lacks per-entry type granularity but detects activity via file writes |
| `isProcessRunning()` | tmux TTY + PID detection | tmux TTY + PID detection | Nearly identical logic |
| `getSessionInfo()` | JSONL tail parsing (128KB) | Streaming JSONL parsing (`createReadStream` + readline) | Both extract summary, cost, session ID |
| `getRestoreCommand()` | `claude --resume <uuid>` | `codex resume <threadId>` | Native resume in both |
| `postLaunchSetup()` | Writes `.claude/settings.json` hooks | Writes `~/.ao/bin` wrappers + AGENTS.md | Different hook mechanisms |
| `setupWorkspaceHooks()` | PostToolUse hook in settings.json | Shell wrappers for gh/git | Different hook mechanisms |

### CLI Flag Differences

| Feature | Claude Code | Codex |
|---|---|---|
| Skip permissions | `--dangerously-skip-permissions` | `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` |
| Auto-approve | (not needed) | `--ask-for-approval never` |
| Approval prompt | (default behavior) | `--ask-for-approval untrusted` |
| Model selection | `--model <model>` | `--model <model>` |
| Reasoning | (auto, model-dependent) | `-c model_reasoning_effort=high` |
| System prompt | `--append-system-prompt <text>` | `-c developer_instructions=<text>` |
| System prompt file | `--append-system-prompt "$(cat file)"` | `-c model_instructions_file=<path>` |
| Prompt | `-p <prompt>` | `-- <prompt>` |
| Resume | `--resume <sessionUuid>` | `resume <threadId>` (subcommand) |

### Metadata Update Mechanism

| Aspect | Claude Code | Codex |
|---|---|---|
| Hook type | PostToolUse hook (JSON stdin/stdout) | PATH-based shell wrappers (intercept gh/git) |
| Config location | `.claude/settings.json` per workspace | `~/.ao/bin/` global wrappers |
| Events captured | `gh pr create`, `gh pr merge`, `git checkout -b`, `git switch -c` | Same events |
| Security | Hook reads JSON from stdin | Wrappers validate `AO_DATA_DIR`, path traversal protection, atomic writes |
| Concurrency | Per-workspace (no conflicts) | Shared wrappers with version marker, atomic writes via temp+rename |

### Session Introspection

| Aspect | Claude Code | Codex |
|---|---|---|
| Session files | `~/.claude/projects/{encoded-path}/*.jsonl` | `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl` |
| File discovery | Flat readdir, filter by `.jsonl` | Recursive traversal with `lstat` (symlink-safe, depth-capped at 4) |
| Path encoding | `toClaudeProjectPath()` replaces `/` and `.` with `-` | `session_meta.cwd` field match via 4KB partial read (first 10 lines) |
| Parsing | Reads only last 128KB via file handle | Streams line-by-line via `createReadStream` + `createInterface` |
| Summary source | Dedicated `"summary"` type entries, falls back to first user message | Model name from `session_meta` (always fallback) |
| Cost tracking | `costUSD`, `usage{}`, `inputTokens/outputTokens` fields | `event_msg` with `token_count` subtype (cached/reasoning tokens are subsets, not additive) |
| Pricing baseline | Sonnet 4.5: $3/$15 per 1M tokens | GPT-4o: $2.50/$10 per 1M tokens |

### Activity Detection Depth

| Aspect | Claude Code | Codex |
|---|---|---|
| `getActivityState()` | Full JSONL-based: maps entry types to `active`/`ready`/`waiting_input`/`blocked` | Mtime-based: recently modified session file → `active`, stale → `idle`, process dead → `exited` |
| `detectActivity()` | Rich terminal patterns: idle (`❯`/`$`/`>`), waiting_input (permission prompts), active (default) | Rich terminal patterns: idle (`>`/`$`/`#`), waiting_input (approval prompts, y/n), active (default) |
| Idle threshold | Configurable via `readyThresholdMs` (default 5 min) | Same: configurable via `readyThresholdMs` (default `DEFAULT_READY_THRESHOLD_MS` = 5 min) |
| Limitation | Full granularity (6 states) | Cannot distinguish `ready` vs `waiting_input` (no per-entry type info in mtime) |

### Binary Resolution

| Aspect | Claude Code | Codex |
|---|---|---|
| Default binary | `claude` (hardcoded) | `resolveCodexBinary()` with fallback chain |
| Fallback paths | None (relies on PATH) | `which` → `/usr/local/bin` → `/opt/homebrew/bin` → `~/.cargo/bin` → `~/.npm/bin` → `"codex"` |
| Caching | None | Cached after first resolution, concurrent-safe via promise guard |
| Shell escaping | N/A | Binary path shell-escaped in launch/restore commands |

### App-Server Client (Codex-only)

Codex ships an additional `CodexAppServerClient` class for programmatic JSON-RPC interaction:
- Thread management: `threadStart`, `threadResume`, `threadList`, `threadArchive`
- Turn management: `turnStart`, `turnInterrupt`
- Model discovery: `modelList`
- Approval handling with auto-accept/custom handler
- Full connect/close lifecycle with graceful shutdown (SIGTERM → SIGKILL)
- JSON-RPC 2.0 compliant (`jsonrpc: "2.0"` on all messages)
- Proper error ordering: pending rejection before `emit("error")` to prevent cleanup skip
- 52 dedicated tests

No Claude Code equivalent — Claude Code is CLI-only.

### Test Coverage

| Metric | Claude Code | Codex |
|---|---|---|
| Main plugin tests | 51 | 131 |
| App-server client tests | N/A | 52 |
| **Total** | **51** | **183** |

## Issues Resolved

| Issue | Title | How |
|---|---|---|
| #176 | Token usage tracking via getSessionInfo() | Streaming JSONL parsing of `event_msg`/`token_count` entries |
| #177 | Configurable approval mode and sandbox policies | `--ask-for-approval` flag mapping via shared `appendApprovalFlags` helper |
| #178 | Reasoning flag for o-series models | `-c model_reasoning_effort=high` via shared `appendModelFlags` helper |
| #179 | Resolve Codex binary location dynamically | `resolveCodexBinary()` with fallback chain + shell escaping |
| #183 | Conversation resume via getRestoreCommand() | Native `codex resume <threadId>` subcommand |
| #184 | App-server JSON-RPC client | Full `CodexAppServerClient` class with 52 tests |
| #159 | PATH wrappers for git/gh metadata updates | `~/.ao/bin/git` + `~/.ao/bin/gh` wrappers with atomic writes |
| #160 | Rich terminal activity detection patterns | `detectActivity()` detects idle/active/waiting_input |
| #161 | Session resume workaround | Superseded by native `codex resume` (better than context re-injection) |
| #162 | Session info extraction for dashboard | `getSessionInfo()` returns model summary + cost estimate |
| #167 | Auto-update session metadata for Codex | PATH wrappers + `setupWorkspaceHooks()` + `postLaunchSetup()` |
| #17 | Codex: getSessionInfo + richer detection | Both fully implemented; `getActivityState` uses mtime-based detection |

## Known Limitations

- **`getActivityState()` limited granularity**: Mtime-based detection provides `active`/`idle`/`exited` but cannot distinguish `ready` (finished turn) from `waiting_input` (approval prompt). Full granularity would require Codex app-server mode integration.
- **Pre-flight binary check** (#165 remains open): Requires a core/session-manager change, not plugin-level

## Test plan

- [x] All 183 Codex tests pass (`pnpm test` in agent-codex)
- [x] Typecheck clean (`pnpm typecheck`)
- [ ] Verify `codex` CLI flags match installed Codex version
- [ ] Test app-server client with live `codex app-server` process
- [ ] Test session resume with `codex resume <threadId>`

title: TF readiness workflow needs machine-checkable end-to-end pass/fail and per-repo action outputs
body:
## Objective 1 (Orchestrator viability)

Current goal: when running the TestFlight readiness flow, the system should produce a reliable machine/ human conclusion without manual prompting.

### Requirements
1. Provide deterministic end-to-end flow for project `tf`:
   - Sessions can be spawned and are discoverable.
   - Issue status is tracked per repo.
   - Final coordinator conclusion appears automatically with explicit `READY`, `BLOCKED`, or `WAITING` verdict.
2. Add machine-readable outputs (e.g., stable JSON or standardized format) from a coordinator watcher script.
3. Define required status schema for worker reports:
   - `Status: Ready | Blocked | Waiting for input` (case-insensitive)
   - `Blockers:` section when blocked
   - include a deterministic source of truth file or label indicating finalization.
4. Make coordinator robust when a repo issue has no status yet:
   - report `PENDING` with explicit timeout behavior
   - no silent or ambiguous completion
5. Add a one-command test in README for:
   - launching sessions
   - watching all open readiness issues
   - capturing summary

### Acceptance criteria
- Running the documented command returns within `MAX_ATTEMPTS` with:
  - explicit state for each issue (`READY`, `BLOCKED`, `WAITING`)
  - a final recommendation line (`HOLD` / `WAIT` / `PROCEED`)
- The orchestrator no longer requires manual follow-up to know if tests succeeded.

### Immediate expected run
Use script:
- `AO_CONFIG_PATH=~/.config/agent-orchestrator/config.yaml scripts/tf-coordinator-watch tf 1 2 3 4 5`

### DoD
- Issue status is consistently machine parseable in the `GJ-testflight-release` issues.
- Objective 1 success is a single reliable pass/fail signal and can be retested by any operator without live agent babysitting.

title: feat: Add issue-comment reaction support (polling-based)
body:
## Summary

Add support for reacting to new GitHub issue comments, so the orchestrator can automatically spawn agents to work on issues when comments are added (e.g., a user attaches a reference image and the agent picks it up).

## Motivation

Currently the reactions system supports `ci-failed`, `changes-requested`, `approved-and-green`, and `agent-stuck`. There is no way for the orchestrator to react when a new comment is posted on a GitHub issue. This is needed to enable workflows like:

- User creates an issue, adds a comment with a screenshot → agent picks it up and starts working
- User gives follow-up instructions via comment → agent continues the task
- Works across all configured projects without per-repo workflow files

## Proposed Approach: Polling (matches existing architecture)

The orchestrator already polls for CI status and review changes via the `gh` CLI. Extend this pattern for issue comments.

### 1. New Event Type

Add to `packages/core/src/types.ts`:

```typescript
// Issue events
| "issue.comment_added"
```

Add to `SessionStatus`:

```typescript
ISSUE_COMMENTED: "issue_commented" as const,
```

### 2. New Reaction Config

Enable in `agent-orchestrator.yaml` per project:

```yaml
reactions:
  issue-commented:
    auto: true
    action: spawn-agent
    filter:
      labels: ["agent"]        # Only react to issues with this label
      authors: ["marcmantei"]  # Only react to comments from these users
    escalateAfter: 30m
```

### 3. Polling Logic in Lifecycle Manager

In `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts`:

- During each poll cycle, for each project, check for new issue comments
- Use `gh api` to fetch recent comments
- Track last-seen comment timestamp per issue to detect new ones
- When a new comment is detected → trigger the `issue-commented` reaction

### 4. Tracker Plugin Extension

In `packages/plugins/tracker-github/src/index.ts`, add a method to fetch comments newer than a given timestamp using `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/comments?since={ISO}&sort=created&direction=desc`.

### 5. Agent Spawn Behavior

When `issue-commented` triggers with `action: spawn-agent`:

1. Read the full issue (title, body, all comments including images)
2. Generate a prompt with the issue context
3. Spawn a new session in a worktree for that issue
4. Agent works on it, creates a PR

## Security Considerations

- **Author filtering** is critical — only react to comments from trusted users to prevent prompt injection via public issue comments
- **Label gating** — only issues with a specific label (e.g., `agent`) trigger the reaction, preventing accidental spawns
- **Rate limiting** — max one active session per issue to prevent infinite loops
- **Bot comment detection** — ignore comments from the orchestrator's own bot account to prevent feedback loops

## Out of Scope (for now)

- Webhook-based approach (would require a tunnel since the server is on local network)
- Image/screenshot parsing within the orchestrator itself (the spawned Claude agent handles this natively)
- Automatic label assignment (user must add the `agent` label manually for now)

## Affected Files

- `packages/core/src/types.ts` — new event type + status
- `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts` — polling logic + reaction mapping
- `packages/plugins/tracker-github/src/index.ts` — getRecentComments method
- `packages/core/src/config.ts` — validation for new reaction config
- `packages/core/src/prompt-builder.ts` — prompt generation for issue context

title: feat: adopt externally-created PRs for lifecycle management
body:
## Summary

- **Automatic PR discovery**: Scans configured projects for open PRs from `allowedUsers` every ~5 minutes and creates lightweight "adopted" sessions for them
- **Full lifecycle tracking**: Adopted sessions get the same CI failure detection, review comment handling, merge conflict alerts, and notifications as agent-created sessions
- **Graceful degradation**: `send-to-agent` reactions fall back to `notify` for adopted sessions (no agent runtime), prefixing messages with `[adopted PR]`

## Changes

| File | What |
|------|------|
| `packages/core/src/types.ts` | Add optional `SCM.listOpenPRs()`, make `SessionMetadata.worktree` optional, add `adopted` field |
| `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/index.ts` | Implement `listOpenPRs` via `gh pr list --json` |
| `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts` | Add `scanForExternalPRs()`, integrate into poll loop, add adopted session fallback |
| `packages/core/src/metadata.ts` | Handle optional worktree, serialize `adopted` field |

## How it works

1. Every 10th poll cycle (~5 min), `scanForExternalPRs()` calls `SCM.listOpenPRs()` for each project
2. Filters PRs by `allowedUsers` config, skips any already tracked by existing sessions
3. Creates a metadata-only session (no worktree, no runtime, no agent) with `adopted=true` and `status=pr_open`
4. The existing `pollAll()` → `checkSession()` → `determineStatus()` pipeline handles the rest
5. When a reaction would `send-to-agent`, the adopted check falls back to notification

title: feat: Codex activity detection via tmux + system monitoring endpoints
body:
## Summary

Two improvements to the AO dashboard and Codex plugin:

### 1. Codex Plugin: Activity Detection via tmux

`getActivityState()` currently returns `null` for all Codex sessions because Codex doesn't provide per-workspace session tracking (ref: #13). 

This PR wires the existing `detectActivity()` helper to `tmux capture-pane`, giving real activity states (`active`/`idle`/`waiting_input`) instead of unknown.

Also fixes `permissions: skip` to use `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` instead of `--full-auto` (which Codex doesn't recognize as a flag).

### 2. Web Dashboard: System Monitoring Endpoints

Three new API routes for system monitoring:

| Endpoint | Returns |
|----------|---------|
| `GET /api/sessions/[id]/terminal` | tmux pane output with secret scrubbing, ID validation, line cap |
| `GET /api/system/resources` | CPU, memory, disk usage |
| `GET /api/system/crons` | Parsed crontab with human-readable schedules |
| `GET /api/system/processes` | Running agent processes (Claude Code, Codex) with PID/runtime/CPU |

The terminal endpoint includes security hardening:
- Session ID regex validation (`^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$`)
- Secret scrubbing (`ghp_`, `sk-`, `xoxb-`, Bearer tokens)
- Line cap (default 50)

### Testing
- Tested with 6+ concurrent agent sessions on VPS
- Activity detection correctly identifies active/idle/waiting_input states
- System endpoints return correct data shapes for dashboard consumption
- Secret scrubbing verified against real tmux output containing tokens

[codex] harden lifecycle manager validation and edge cases
body:
Closes #232

This change hardens the core lifecycle polling manager around the edges that were still weak after the earlier iterations. The lifecycle loop is the component responsible for normalizing session state, running reactions, and driving operator-visible status transitions, so ambiguous runtime failures here are costly: they make debugging configuration problems harder and can cause otherwise-fixable operator input mistakes to look like missing sessions or silent no-ops.

The root cause was that the public lifecycle-manager entry points trusted a few runtime assumptions that TypeScript alone cannot enforce. `createLifecycleManager()` only checked for truthy values and produced generic errors, `check(sessionId)` did not normalize externally supplied IDs before lookup, and reaction config validation treated any string as an action even though the supported action set is fixed. That left a gap between compile-time types and runtime behavior.

The fix adds explicit runtime guards for supported reaction actions, introduces more descriptive dependency and session-ID validation errors, trims session IDs before lookup, and validates `start()` arguments before ignoring duplicate starts. The exported `createLifecycleManager()` JSDoc was also expanded so the module’s external contract is clearer. The test suite now covers the new constructor validation, duplicate-start validation, trimmed session IDs, non-string IDs, and the fallback path for malformed reaction actions.

Validation run for this change:
- `pnpm --filter @composio/ao-core typecheck` ✅
- `pnpm --filter @composio/ao-core exec vitest run src/__tests__/lifecycle-manager.test.ts` ✅
- `pnpm --filter @composio/ao-core exec eslint src/lifecycle-manager.ts src/__tests__/lifecycle-manager.test.ts` ✅
- `pnpm typecheck` ⚠️ fails outside this change in `packages/plugins/agent-aider/src/index.ts` because `@composio/ao-core` cannot be resolved
- `pnpm lint` ⚠️ existing repo warnings only; no errors introduced by this change
- `pnpm test` ⚠️ existing unrelated failures in `packages/core/__tests__/config.test.ts`, `packages/core/src/__tests__/session-manager.test.ts`, and `packages/core/src/__tests__/plugin-integration.test.ts`

title: refactor(core): harden lifecycle manager validation and loop edge cases
body:
## Summary

The lifecycle polling manager needs stronger runtime validation and better coverage around edge cases. The current implementation mostly works for happy paths, but malformed inputs and unsupported reaction config values can fail ambiguously.

## Problems

- `createLifecycleManager()` throws generic dependency errors that do not identify the missing field clearly.
- `check(sessionId)` accepts whitespace-wrapped IDs without normalizing them, which causes avoidable lookup failures.
- A malformed reaction `action` value is treated like any other string at runtime even though the type only allows a small fixed set.
- Existing tests do not pin these edge cases, so regressions are easy to miss.

## Desired outcome

- Clear, specific runtime errors for missing lifecycle-manager dependencies and invalid `check()` inputs.
- Normalized session ID handling for externally supplied IDs.
- Runtime guarding of supported reaction actions so invalid config falls back safely.
- Added lifecycle-manager tests covering the validation and loop edge cases.

### BUG-02 — Missing `name` field → "Starting orchestrator for undefined"

`ao init --auto --smart` prints a warning then generates the same template as without `--smart`. Users expecting AI output are confused.

**File:** `packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts` lines 430–437

`findFreePort` falls back to 3000 if all ports 3000–3099 are busy, without warning. `ao start` then fails to bind.

**Fix:** After `findFreePort`, check if the result is the fallback. If so, warn the user to set the port manually.

**File:** `packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts` lines 19–25, 446

title: fix(terminal): OSC 52 clipboard, resize frame cap, and hardcoded height
body:
## Summary

Three independent bugs in the browser terminal components:

### BUG-06 — Copy/paste broken (OSC 52 not wired)
xterm.js strips unrecognised OSC sequences. `DirectTerminal.tsx` never registers an OSC 52 handler so tmux clipboard writes are silently dropped. Text copied inside the terminal never reaches the system clipboard.

**Fix:**
\`\`\`typescript
terminal.parser.registerOscHandler(52, (data) => {
  const parts = data.split(";");
  if (parts.length < 2) return false;
  const b64 = parts[parts.length - 1];
  try { navigator.clipboard?.writeText(atob(b64)).catch(() => {}); } catch {}
  return true;
});
\`\`\`

**File:** `packages/web/src/components/DirectTerminal.tsx` lines 142–155

---

### BUG-07 — Resize gives up after 10 animation frames (~166ms)
The fullscreen resize logic polls with `requestAnimationFrame` up to `maxAttempts = 10`. On slow machines or with CSS transitions >166ms the resize is skipped, leaving the terminal at the wrong size.

**Fix:** Remove the `maxAttempts` cap or increase to 60.

**File:** `packages/web/src/components/DirectTerminal.tsx` lines 267–304

---

### BUG-09 — Hardcoded `h-[600px]` overflows on laptop screens
`Terminal.tsx` uses a fixed 600px height. On 13" laptops the terminal bottom is cut off and unreachable.

**Fix:** `height: "max(440px, calc(100vh - 440px))"` (matches `DirectTerminal.tsx`).

**File:** `packages/web/src/components/Terminal.tsx` line 76

---

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Copying text in the browser terminal writes to system clipboard
- [ ] Toggling fullscreen on a slow machine sizes the terminal correctly
- [ ] Terminal height is responsive on small screens

title: fix(core): atomic metadata writes, restoredAt persistence, and session count/sorting bugs
body:
## Summary

Four independent bugs in core data handling:

### BUG-28 — Non-atomic metadata writes → race condition data loss
`updateMetadata()` does read + merge + `writeFileSync` (not atomic). The bash shell wrappers use atomic `mv`. A concurrent TypeScript + bash write causes one to silently overwrite the other with stale data.

**Fix:**
\`\`\`typescript
const tmpPath = \`\${filePath}.tmp.\${process.pid}.\${Date.now()}\`;
writeFileSync(tmpPath, content, "utf-8");
renameSync(tmpPath, filePath); // atomic on POSIX
\`\`\`

**File:** `packages/core/src/metadata.ts` lines 162–187

---

### BUG-29 — `restoredAt` written to metadata but never read back
`session-manager.ts` writes `restoredAt` on restore. `readMetadata()` doesn't map it. `SessionMetadata` type doesn't include it. After a process restart `session.restoredAt` is always `undefined`.

**Fix:** Add `restoredAt?: string` to `SessionMetadata`. Read and parse it in `readMetadata()`.

**Files:** `packages/core/src/metadata.ts` lines 84–108, `packages/core/src/types.ts` line 981

---

### BUG-12 — Working session count excludes `idle`/`ready` sessions
Stats bar counts only `activity === "active"`. Sessions alive but momentarily idle are excluded, making the "Working" counter always understated.

**Fix:**
\`\`\`typescript
workingSessions: sessions.filter(
  (s) => s.activity !== null && s.activity !== "exited"
).length
\`\`\`

**File:** `packages/web/src/lib/serialize.ts` line 383

---

### BUG-13 — Errored sessions appear in the wrong Kanban zone
`getAttentionLevel()` checks `activity` before `status`. A session with `status = "errored"` but `activity = "active"` falls into "working" instead of "respond" for up to 30 seconds.

**Fix:** Move `status === "errored"` and `status === "needs_input"` checks before the activity checks in `getAttentionLevel()`.

**File:** `packages/web/src/lib/types.ts` lines 196–202

---

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Two concurrent metadata writers (TS + bash) never lose data
- [ ] `session.restoredAt` is populated after a server restart
- [ ] Working session count includes idle/ready sessions
- [ ] Errored sessions immediately appear in the "Respond" Kanban zone

title: fix(cli): lifecycle never started, silent 5s spawn freeze, and wrong agent plugin in status

title: fix(cli): ao init missing sessionPrefix, name, and port validation
body:
## Summary

Fixes four bugs in `ao init` that broke the first-run experience, plus a pre-existing false positive in port detection.

---

## BUG-01 — `sessionPrefix` missing → session IDs were `undefined-1`

`ao init` never wrote `sessionPrefix` to the config. Every session ID produced by `ao spawn` became `undefined-1`, `undefined-2`, etc. because the code does:
\`\`\`ts
`${project.sessionPrefix}-${num}`  →  "undefined-1"
\`\`\`

**Fix:** `init.ts` now calls `generateSessionPrefix(projectId)` to derive a short prefix (e.g. `test-init` → `ti`). Sessions are now named `ti-1`, `ti-2`, etc.

---

## BUG-02 — `name` missing → "Starting orchestrator for undefined"

`ao init` never wrote the `name` field. `ao start` prints `Starting orchestrator for ${project.name}` which output "undefined".

**Fix:** `init.ts` now writes `name: projectId` to the project config.

---

## BUG-05 — `--smart` flag was a silent no-op

`ao init --auto --smart` printed a warning then generated the same templates as without `--smart`, confusing users who expected AI output.

**Fix:** Updated the flag description to say `(coming soon)` so users know upfront it isn't implemented yet.

---

## BUG-32 — Port fallback written without warning

`findFreePort` returned 3000 as a fallback even when all ports were busy. `ao start` would then fail to bind with a cryptic Node.js error.

**Fix:** `findFreePort` now returns `null` when no free port is found. Both interactive and auto mode show a clear warning and suggest the next available port.

---

## Bonus fix — `isPortAvailable` false positive on macOS

The original `isPortAvailable` probed by binding to `127.0.0.1`. On macOS, Next.js / `pnpm dev` listens on `::` (IPv6 wildcard) with `IPV6_V6ONLY=1`, so binding `127.0.0.1` succeeded even when the port was taken — causing the port warning to never fire.

**Fix:** Switched from a bind-based to a **connect-based** probe. A successful TCP connect means something is listening (port in use); `ECONNREFUSED` means the port is free. This works regardless of whether the occupying process is bound to `127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `0.0.0.0`, or `::`.

---

## Verified manually

\`\`\`bash

ao init --auto && cat agent-orchestrator.yaml
# → name: test-init, sessionPrefix: ti

# port warning when 3000 is busy
ao init --auto
# → ⚠ Port 3000 is busy — using 3001 instead.
# → port: 3001 in config

# --smart flag description
ao init --help | grep smart
# → (coming soon)
\`\`\`

  - gh not authenticated — offers `gh auth login`
  - claude CLI not found — prints install command
- **pnpm install** — skips if already available, tries corepack first with fallback to `npm install -g pnpm` for permission-restricted environments
- **PATH verification** — after `npm link`, checks if `ao` is on `$PATH` and prints the exact `export PATH=...` line if not

### `packages/cli/src/lib/preflight.ts` — shared pre-flight utilities

New module with four checks, all using a consistent `throw` contract so callers can catch and clean up:

| Check | What it validates | Used by |
|-------|-------------------|---------|
| `checkPort(port)` | Dashboard port is free | `ao start` |
| `checkBuilt(webDir)` | Core packages are compiled (checks `ao-core/dist/index.js` from web's `node_modules`) | `ao start` |
| `checkTmux()` | tmux is installed (only when runtime is `"tmux"`) | `ao spawn`, `ao batch-spawn` |
| `checkGhAuth()` | gh CLI installed + authenticated (distinguishes ENOENT from auth failure) | `ao spawn`, `ao batch-spawn` |

### `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts` — dashboard pre-flight

- Port and build checks run only when actually starting the dashboard (respects `--no-dashboard`)
- Build check runs after the `package.json` existence check so "Run: pnpm install" takes precedence over "Run: pnpm build" when the web package itself is missing

### `packages/cli/src/commands/spawn.ts` — spawn pre-flight

- Pre-flight checks extracted into `runSpawnPreflight()`, called once before any session is created
- `batch-spawn` runs checks upfront before the loop — a missing prerequisite fails fast with one error instead of N identical failures
- tmux check respects per-project runtime overrides (`project.runtime ?? config.defaults.runtime`)

title: feat(scripts): add try-pr.sh for testing PR worktrees locally
body:
## Summary

Adds `scripts/try-pr.sh` — a helper script for manually testing changes in any agent session's worktree without permanently changing the global `ao` command.

Also fixes a false positive bug in `isPortAvailable()` that caused port-busy warnings to never fire on macOS.

---

## `scripts/try-pr.sh`

### Why it's useful

This project runs AO on AO — agents open PRs against this very repo. When an agent finishes its work, you want to manually verify the changes before merging. But the global `ao` command still points to `main`, not the PR's code.

**Example:** `ao-22` fixed `ao init` to write `sessionPrefix` and `name` into the config. To verify it works you need to run `ao init` from the PR's code — not main:

```bash
# Switch ao to point at ao-22's worktree (~15s build)
bash scripts/try-pr.sh ao-22

ao init --auto && cat agent-orchestrator.yaml
# ✔ name: my-project
# ✔ sessionPrefix: mp

# For PRs with dashboard changes — builds Next.js + starts dev server
# on a free port with your real config so actual sessions show up
bash scripts/try-pr.sh ao-22 --with-web

# Switch back to main when done
bash scripts/try-pr.sh --restore
```

Without this script you'd have to manually build, relink, test, and remember to restore — easy to forget the last step and end up running PR code thinking it's main.

### How it works

- Builds the worktree (CLI/core/plugins only by default, full build with `--with-web`)
- Rewrites the pnpm shim at `$(which ao)` to point at the worktree's `dist/index.js`
- Saves the original shim so `--restore` can put it back exactly
- With `--with-web`: finds a free port starting at 3001 (avoids conflicting with `ao start` on 3000), passes `AO_CONFIG_PATH` pointing at your real config
- Detects if the PR has web changes and hints to use `--with-web` if you forgot

---

## `isPortAvailable()` fix

**Problem:** The original implementation probed by binding to `127.0.0.1`. On macOS, Next.js / `pnpm dev` listens on `::` (IPv6 wildcard) with `IPV6_V6ONLY=1`, so binding `127.0.0.1` (IPv4) succeeded even when the port was taken — causing port-busy warnings to never fire.

**Fix:** Switched from bind-based to **connect-based** detection. A successful TCP connect means something is listening (port in use). `ECONNREFUSED` means the port is free. Works regardless of whether the listener is on `127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `0.0.0.0`, or `::`.

```ts
// Before: bind probe — false positive when listener is on ::
server.listen(port, "127.0.0.1");

// After: connect probe — reliable across all bind addresses
s.connect(port, "127.0.0.1");
s.once("connect", () => resolve(false)); // in use
s.once("error",   () => resolve(true));  // free
```

title: Entity-level semantic merge for worktree merges
body:
### Problem

When multiple agents work in parallel on the same repo, each in its own worktree, they often touch the same files. Two agents editing different functions in the same file creates a merge conflict that shouldn't exist. Git's line-level merge doesn't understand code structure.

Right now, the merge path is:
- `workspace-worktree` plugin creates isolated worktrees
- Agents open PRs
- `scm.mergePR()` squash-merges via GitHub API
- If there are conflicts → the PR is "not mergeable" and the user has to resolve manually

This becomes a real bottleneck as the number of parallel agents grows. The `auto-merge.yaml` example workflow breaks down when two agents touch overlapping files.

### Proposed solution

[Weave](https://github.com/Ataraxy-Labs/weave) is an entity-level semantic merge driver for Git. Instead of merging lines, it merges at the level of functions, classes, and methods using tree-sitter. On a 31-scenario benchmark, it resolves 100% cleanly vs git's 48%.

It could plug into Agent Orchestrator at two levels:

**1. Git merge driver (zero code changes)**

Weave installs as a git merge driver via `.gitattributes`. If the `workspace-worktree` plugin auto-configures this when creating worktrees, all local merges become entity-aware. Two agents editing different functions in the same file merge cleanly every time.

```
# .gitattributes (auto-configured per worktree)
*.ts merge=weave
*.py merge=weave
*.js merge=weave
*.go merge=weave
*.rs merge=weave
```

**2. Pre-merge conflict detection (new plugin or reaction)**

Weave ships as an MCP server with 14 tools. Relevant ones for AO:

- `weave_diff` → entity-level diff (which functions changed, not which lines)
- `weave_potential_conflicts` → detect when two branches modify the same entity
- `weave_impact_analysis` → transitive blast radius of changes

This could power a new reaction or a pre-merge check:
- Before an agent's PR is merged, check if it overlaps with other active sessions at the entity level
- Suggest merge ordering: sessions touching high-dependent entities (foundations) merge first, leaf changes merge last
- When conflicts do occur, classify them (signature change, body divergence, import conflict) so the agent gets structured context instead of raw diff hunks

**3. Smarter `ci-failed` reaction**

When CI fails after a merge, `weave_impact_analysis` can identify which entities were affected by the merge and narrow down the failure cause, giving the fixing agent a smaller search space.

### Details

Weave supports TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, Rust, Java, C, C++, Ruby, C# and more. Installs via Homebrew (`brew install ataraxy-labs/tap/weave`) or as a single binary.

Happy to help with integration or answer questions. The plugin architecture makes this a natural fit as either a workspace plugin enhancement or a new plugin slot.

title: fix: poll for agent ready indicator instead of fixed 5s sleep
fix: replace fixed 5s sleep with polling for agent ready state before sending initial prompt
body:
## Problem

In `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts`, when an agent uses `post-launch` prompt delivery, the orchestrator waits with a hardcoded 5-second sleep before sending the initial prompt:

```typescript
// Wait for agent to start and be ready for input
await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 5_000));
await plugins.runtime.sendMessage(handle, agentLaunchConfig.prompt);
```

This has two failure modes:

- **Too slow** — on fast machines, the agent is ready well before 5s, wasting time on every spawn
- **Too fast** — on slow machines or under load, 5s may not be enough and the prompt arrives before the agent can accept input, causing it to be dropped or mishandled

## Expected Behaviour

The orchestrator should detect when the agent is actually ready to receive input and send the prompt at that point, rather than relying on a fixed delay.

## Suggested Fix

Poll the terminal output for Claude Code's `❯` ready indicator with a reasonable timeout (e.g. 30s), sending the prompt as soon as readiness is confirmed or falling back to best-effort if the timeout is reached.

title: feat: add --continue flag to ao start
body:
## Summary

- Adds `--continue` flag to `ao start` for orchestrator conversation continuity
- When the orchestrator needs a fresh system prompt (e.g. CLAUDE.local.md was updated), `ao start --continue` kills the existing session and respawns with `claude --continue`, preserving conversation history while reloading all system prompts
- Implemented at the interface level (`AgentLaunchConfig.continue`) so all agent plugins can support it

## Changes

- **`packages/core/src/types.ts`**: Add `continue?: boolean` to `AgentLaunchConfig` and `OrchestratorSpawnConfig`
- **`packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.ts`**: Pass `--continue` to Claude CLI when `continue` is set
- **`packages/core/src/session-manager.ts`**: Forward `continue` from orchestrator config to agent launch config
- **`packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts`**: Add `--continue` CLI option — kills existing session first, then respawns with continue flag
- **`packages/plugins/agent-claude-code/src/index.test.ts`**: 3 new tests for --continue flag behavior

## How it works

```bash
# Normal start (existing behavior unchanged)
ao start

# Continue with fresh system prompt + conversation history
ao start --continue
```

When `--continue` is used:
1. If an orchestrator session exists, it's killed first
2. A new session is spawned with `claude --continue`, which continues the most recent conversation in the project directory
3. Fresh system prompts are loaded (via `--append-system-prompt`)

title: fix: reduce PR cache staleness + live CI status updates
body:
## Summary

Fixes stale PR state on dashboard (e.g. 'Ready to merge' badge showing for already-merged PRs) and adds live CI check status updates without manual refresh.

### Cache staleness fixes
- Reduced default PR enrichment cache TTL from **5 minutes → 60 seconds**
- Reduced rate-limit fallback cache TTL from **60 minutes → 10 minutes**
- Added `TTLCache.invalidate(key)` method for targeted cache busting
- Added `?refresh=true` query param to `/api/sessions` and `/api/sessions/[id]` that bypasses cache entirely
- Terminal PR states (merged/closed) use a longer 5-minute TTL since they won't change

### Live CI status updates
- **Adaptive cache TTL**: 15s when CI is pending/running (checks change rapidly), 60s default for stable open PRs
- **SSE PR patches**: Snapshots now include `prState`, `ciStatus`, `reviewDecision` from cache (cheap reads, no extra API calls)
- **Client-side merging**: `useSessionEvents` reducer applies PR status patches from SSE, so dashboard cards reflect CI changes in real-time

### How it works
1. Session detail page polls every 5s → hits cache (60s/15s TTL) → fresh data on expiry
2. When CI is running, cache expires in 15s → CI status updates within ~20s
3. SSE snapshots read cached PR data → dashboard cards update when any page fetches fresh data
4. Force-refresh (`?refresh=true`) bypasses cache entirely for manual refresh scenarios

defaults.agentConfig (e.g. permissions: skip, model: opus) was never merged into per-project agentConfig. Users who set agent config under defaults: expected it to apply to all projects, but agents would still block at trust dialogs because project.agentConfig was empty.

Fix: add agentConfig to DefaultPluginsSchema and DefaultPlugins type, then merge it into each project in applyProjectDefaults() with spread-based shallow merge (project values override defaults).

- project agentConfig fields override defaults per-field

title: fix: prevent cleanup from removing sessions with open PRs
body:
Before this fix, cleanup would kill sessions with dead runtimes regardless of whether they had an open PR. This caused orphaned PRs where no session owned them anymore.

Now when cleanup detects a dead runtime, it checks if the session has an associated PR that is still open. If so, the session is skipped (preserved for human attention) rather than silently removed.

Conservative fallback: if the PR state check fails (API error), the session is also preserved to avoid data loss.

Added two regression tests:
- Dead runtime + open PR → session skipped
- Dead runtime + PR check fails → session conservatively skipped

Closes #146

Fix: catch the lsof error gracefully and check the PID list. When empty, show 'Dashboard not running on port N' (yellow). When PIDs are found and killed, show 'Dashboard stopped' (green).

Added two regression tests:
- No dashboard running → shows 'Dashboard not running on port'
- Dashboard running → shows 'Dashboard stopped' only
