title: feat (core): inject worker prompt as instructions file
body:
## Summary

This PR updates worker prompt handling so sessions can pass persistent system instructions separately from task-specific input, and adds OpenCode-specific support for materializing worker and orchestrator system prompts into each session worktree's `AGENTS.md`.

## What Changed

- Split `buildPrompt()` in `packages/core/src/prompt-builder.ts` to return:
  - `systemPrompt`: persistent AO guidance, project context, issue context, and project rules
  - `taskPrompt`: only the explicit user-provided prompt
- Updated worker spawn flow in `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` to:
  - write `systemPrompt` to `worker-prompt-<sessionId>.md`
  - pass `taskPrompt` separately to the agent launch config
  - skip post-launch prompt delivery when no task prompt exists
  - clean up prompt files alongside workspace/metadata on failure
- Added OpenCode worker support by writing the worker system prompt into the worker worktree's `AGENTS.md`
- Updated OpenCode `AGENTS.md` generation in `packages/core/src/opencode-agents-md.ts` to:
  - accept a role parameter (`worker` or `orchestrator`)
  - render a role-specific heading (`## Agent Worker` / `## Agent Orchestrator`)
  - use the current AO system prompt markers
- Fixed restore behavior in `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` so OpenCode restore re-materializes `AGENTS.md` for both:
  - orchestrator sessions via `orchestrator-prompt-<sessionId>.md`
  - worker sessions via `worker-prompt-<sessionId>.md`

## Why

- Codex-style worker sessions need a clean split between persistent instructions and the immediate task prompt.
- OpenCode does not consume `systemPromptFile` directly, so its session-scoped system prompt needs to be materialized into `AGENTS.md` inside the session worktree.
- Worker and orchestrator OpenCode sessions need different `AGENTS.md` headings and restore behavior, even though both use the same helper.

## Test Coverage

- Updated prompt-builder tests to validate the new `{ systemPrompt, taskPrompt }` shape
- Added/updated spawn tests for:
  - worker system prompt file generation
  - OpenCode worker `AGENTS.md` writing
  - no post-launch prompt send when there is no task prompt
- Added restore coverage for OpenCode worker `AGENTS.md` re-materialization
- Updated OpenCode `AGENTS.md` helper tests for the role-aware output

## Verification

```bash
pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test -- opencode-agents-md

pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test -- restore
```

title: fix(core): write long worker prompts to file to prevent truncation
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1304

When `ao spawn --prompt "xyz"` is used, `buildPrompt()` composes a layered prompt (BASE_AGENT_PROMPT + project context + rules + user prompt) that easily exceeds 500 chars. The full string was being inlined into a compound shell command and sent via tmux paste-buffer, where it could silently fail if session ID discovery failed.

**Fix:** Mirrors `spawnOrchestrator()`'s `systemPromptFile` pattern — long prompts (>500 chars) are written to a file, and the agent launch config uses `systemPromptFile` instead of the inline prompt. The opencode plugin already handles `systemPromptFile` correctly via `$(cat ...)` substitution.

## Changes

- **`packages/core/src/session-manager.ts`**: In the worker `spawn()` path, after composing the prompt via `buildPrompt()`, if the result exceeds 500 characters, write it to a file (`worker-prompt-<sessionId>.md`) and set `systemPromptFile` on the launch config. Falls back to inline prompt on write failure (non-fatal).

## Test Plan

1. `ao spawn --prompt "Fix the authentication bug"` — verify agent receives prompt
2. `ao spawn --prompt "short"` (under 500 chars) — verify inline prompt still works
3. Spawn from orchestrator — verify worker picks up the prompt
4. `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` — verify existing tests pass

title: ao start intermittently kills existing orchestrator and spawns a new one
body:
## Bug
`ao start` intermittently kills the existing orchestrator agent session and starts a new orchestrator instead of reusing the current one / ensuring there is only one stable orchestrator.

## What I observed
On April 18, 2026, running `ao status` in my local setup showed multiple orchestrator sessions for the same project at the same time:

- `aa-orchestrator-1`
- `aa-orchestrator-2`
- `aa-orchestrator-3`

This matches the behavior I’ve been seeing where `ao start` will sometimes replace the active orchestrator by spawning a fresh one, leaving multiple orchestrators around or killing the previously active one unexpectedly.

## Expected behavior
`ao start` should be idempotent with respect to the orchestrator:

- if an orchestrator is already running for the project, it should reuse it (or at least leave it alone), and
- it should not randomly terminate the active orchestrator and create a new one.

## Actual behavior
Intermittently, `ao start` appears to:

- kill the current orchestrator agent, and/or
- spawn a new orchestrator session unexpectedly.

## Reproduction
I don’t have a deterministic repro yet. So far this appears intermittent / timing-dependent.

High-level pattern:
1. Start the project with `ao start`
2. Later run `ao start` again (or restart parts of the setup)
3. Occasionally the original orchestrator gets replaced and a new orchestrator session is created
4. `ao status` then shows multiple orchestrators or an unexpected new orchestrator instance

## Environment

title: fix: restore dead orchestrators on ao start
body:
## Summary
- restore the most recently active dead-but-restorable orchestrator on `ao start` instead of silently spawning a new one when tmux is gone
- harden startup-lock handling so stale locks are cleaned up promptly, `EPERM` owners are treated as alive, failed lockfile writes do not leak fds, and startup-lock acquisition failures go through the normal CLI error path
- fix worker session orchestrator navigation to prefer the most recently active live orchestrator for the project instead of defaulting to the first sorted orchestrator id
- fix Codex worker restore commands to resume with `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` instead of `never`
- replace manual package changelog edits with a single repo-standard changeset

## Why
The main issue in #1306 is the long-gap restart path: when the original tmux-backed orchestrator is gone hours later, `ao start` was treating that orchestrator as terminal and creating a fresh one instead of resuming it.

While fixing that path, two related follow-ups also surfaced on this branch:
- the worker session page could link to the wrong orchestrator when multiple orchestrators existed for a project because it effectively fell back to the first sorted id
- Codex restore commands for worker sessions could resume in `---dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`, which is too permissive for restored worker sessions

## Implementation
### `ao start` restore behavior
- `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts` now prefers `sm.restore(...)` for the newest restorable dead orchestrator after checking for live orchestrators
- it only falls back to `spawnOrchestrator()` when there is nothing live or restorable

### startup lock hardening
- `packages/cli/src/lib/running-state.ts` now:
  - checks lock owners during the retry loop instead of waiting for the full timeout
  - treats `EPERM` as alive when probing a PID
  - closes the lockfile fd in a `finally`
  - unlinks a partially-created lockfile if the metadata write fails
- `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts` now acquires the startup lock inside the main `try` path so lock-acquisition failures get standard CLI error handling

### worker session orchestrator button
- `packages/web/src/app/api/sessions/route.ts` now returns a preferred project-scoped `orchestratorId` for worker session pages by selecting the most recently active live orchestrator, instead of leaving the client to fall back to the first sorted orchestrator id

### Codex restore approval mode
- `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts` now uses restore-specific approval flag handling
- worker restores no longer resume with `--ask-for-approval never`
- worker restores use `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox ` for permission less mode. 
- permissionless orchestrator restores still use `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`

### release metadata
- replaced package-level unreleased changelog edits with `.changeset/fix-start-restore-and-codex-resume.md`

## Evidence
- CLI regression coverage verifies `ao start --no-dashboard` restores the most recently active dead orchestrator instead of spawning a new one
- CLI startup-lock tests cover lock release ordering and lock-acquisition failure handling
- web API coverage verifies project-scoped worker navigation selects the most recently active live orchestrator when multiple orchestrators exist
- Codex plugin tests verify restore commands now use `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` for worker restores and keep explicit bypass for permissionless orchestrator restores

## Validation
- `pnpm build`
- `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm test`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli exec vitest run __tests__/commands/start.test.ts`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web exec vitest run src/__tests__/api-routes.test.ts`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web exec vitest run 'src/app/sessions/[id]/page.test.tsx'`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-codex exec vitest run src/index.test.ts`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-agent-codex exec tsc --noEmit`

Closes #1306.

title: feat(core): auto-terminate sessions on PR merge (#1309)
body:
## Summary

Closes [#1309](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1309) (part of [#536](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/536)). When a session's PR was detected as merged, AO marked the status `merged` but left the tmux runtime alive, the worktree on disk, and the metadata in the active `sessions/` directory. Users were running an external watchdog to archive zombies. This closes the loop inside AO.

- On the `merged` transition (last step of `checkSession`, after reactions fire), invoke `sessionManager.kill()` with `reason: "pr_merged"` to destroy the runtime, remove the worktree, and archive the metadata.
- Guarded by an idleness gate (`session.activity in {idle, ready, exited}` OR grace window elapsed) so we never kill an agent mid-task. Deferred cleanups set `mergedPendingCleanupSince` in metadata and retry each poll.
- Config opt-in under `lifecycle.autoCleanupOnMerge` (default `true`) with `mergeCleanupIdleGraceMs` (default 5 min) — operators can preserve merged worktrees for inspection if they want.

## Why

The cleanup logic in `kill()` already existed and worked correctly — the gap was that nothing called it on the `merged` transition. Adding the call is the minimal fix; the rest of the changes are there to make it safe:

- `kill()` is now idempotent (short-circuits on already-archived/terminated sessions) and takes a `reason` option so auto-terminations don't record misleading `"manually_killed"` lifecycle reasons.
- Scope is deliberately narrow to `"merged"`. `done`/`errored` often need the worktree preserved for debugging, and `killed` is produced by `kill()` itself so auto-triggering it would self-recurse. See commit message for the full rationale.
- Reactions-before-cleanup ordering is preserved so `merge.completed` events and `merge.ready` auto-merge reactions observe a live session before it is destroyed.

## Codex review

Plan was reviewed by Codex before implementation. Verdict: conditional pass. Their concerns (scope narrowing, reactions ordering, idleness gate, real idempotency, config opt-in, more test coverage) are all reflected in the implementation and commit message.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core typecheck` — clean
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` (full workspace) — clean
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` — 788 passed (+6 new)
- [x] 6 new unit tests in `lifecycle-manager.test.ts` under `auto-cleanup on merge (#1309)`:
  - [x] kills session with `reason=pr_merged` when PR merges and agent is idle
  - [x] defers cleanup when agent is still active and records `mergedPendingCleanupSince`
  - [x] forces cleanup after grace window elapses even if agent is still active
  - [x] does not trigger cleanup when `autoCleanupOnMerge` is disabled
  - [x] does not trigger cleanup for terminated/killed sessions (no self-recursion)
  - [x] retains `merged` status when `kill()` fails so the next poll retries
- [ ] Manual end-to-end: spawn a session, merge its PR, verify `ao status` no longer shows it within one poll cycle after agent idles

## Notes for reviewers

- The `SessionManager.kill` return type changed from `Promise<void>` to `Promise<KillResult>`. All existing callers (CLI, tests) ignored the old return value so this is effectively additive. One test (`lifecycle.test.ts:163`) was updated to match.
- Two new enum variants added to `CanonicalSessionReason` (`pr_merged`, `auto_cleanup`) and `CanonicalRuntimeReason` (`pr_merged_cleanup`, `auto_cleanup`) — additive union widening only.
- No changes to notifier plugins, webhook handlers, or the dashboard. The existing `merge.completed` event is sufficient; cleanup is silent.

title: fix(workspace-worktree): resolve symlink source to absolute path
body:
## Summary

`postCreate` in `packages/plugins/workspace-worktree/src/index.ts` builds `sourcePath` with `join(repoPath, symlinkPath)`. When `project.path` is a relative path like `"."`, `repoPath` stays `"."` and `join(".", "node_modules")` returns `"node_modules"` — a relative string. `symlinkSync("node_modules", "/path/to/worktree/node_modules")` then creates a self-referential link:

```
<worktree>/node_modules -> node_modules
```

Symlinks are resolved relative to the **symlink's own directory**, so the link loops back to itself. The next `pnpm install` fails with:

```
ELOOP: too many symbolic links encountered, open '<worktree>/node_modules/.pnpm-workspace-state-v1.json'
```

`ao spawn` only surfaces the top-level `✖ Failed to create or initialize session` / `✗ Command failed: sh -c …` message, so the real ELOOP is swallowed — took a while to find it.

## Fix

Use `resolve(repoPath, symlinkPath)` instead of `join(…)`. `resolve()` anchors a relative `repoPath` against `process.cwd()` and leaves absolute / `~`-prefixed paths unchanged, so existing configs are unaffected.

```diff
- const sourcePath = join(repoPath, symlinkPath);
+ const sourcePath = resolve(repoPath, symlinkPath);
  const targetPath = resolve(info.path, symlinkPath);
```

The adjacent `targetPath` line already uses `resolve()` for the same reason — this just makes the two consistent.

## Repro

```yaml
# agent-orchestrator.yaml
projects:
  myproject:
    path: .
    symlinks: [node_modules]
```

Run `ao spawn` — every spawn fails until `symlinks:` is removed or the `path:` is made absolute.

## Tests

Added `produces an absolute symlink source when project.path is relative` in `workspace.postCreate()`. Fails on `main`, passes with the fix.

- 47/47 tests pass (`pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-workspace-worktree test`)
- `pnpm typecheck` clean
- `pnpm lint` on changed files: 0 errors, 0 warnings
- `prettier --check` clean

Patch-level changeset included.

## Verified in production

Applied the equivalent patch to an installed 0.2.5 instance that had been blocked by this bug for ~2 days. `ao spawn` immediately started producing real sessions that progress through the full lifecycle and open PRs. Reverted once upstream publishes with the fix.

This change captures the thrown error during SSR, passes it to the dashboard as `dashboardLoadError`, and shows an alert banner with the message plus a short pointer to `agent-orchestrator.yaml` and `ao doctor`. title: bug: cross-project spawn tags session with wrong projectId
body:
## Description

When multiple projects are defined in `agent-orchestrator.yaml` (e.g. `agent-orchestrator` and `x402-identity`), spawning a session for a non-default project's issue still assigns `projectId` of the project the AO instance was started for.

## Reproduction

1. Add a second project to `agent-orchestrator.yaml`:
```yaml
projects:
  agent-orchestrator:
    name: Agent Orchestrator
    repo: ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator
    ...
  x402-identity:
    name: x402 Identity
    repo: harsh-batheja/x402-identity
    sessionPrefix: xid
    ...
```

2. Start AO for the default project: `ao start agent-orchestrator`
3. Spawn a session for the second project: `ao spawn x402-identity/1`
4. Check the session via API or dashboard

## Expected

- `projectId` = `x402-identity`
- Session prefix = `xid-*`
- Session appears under x402-identity on the dashboard

## Actual

- `projectId` = `agent-orchestrator`
- Session prefix = `ao-*` (default project prefix)
- Session appears under Agent Orchestrator on the dashboard
- Branch and issueId resolve correctly (`feat/x402-identity-1`, `x402-identity/1`), so the issue reference IS being resolved — just the project assignment is wrong

## Environment

- AO version: latest from `main`
- Config: single `agent-orchestrator.yaml` with multiple projects under `projects:`
- Runtime: tmux + claude-code

## Notes

The issue reference resolution works — `ao spawn x402-identity/1` correctly looks up the repo, creates the branch `feat/x402-identity-1`, and sets `issueId` to `x402-identity/1`. It's only the `projectId` and session prefix that fall back to the default running project. Suggest the spawn logic should derive `projectId` from the resolved issue prefix rather than from the running instance's primary project.

title: fix(cli): derive projectId from prefixed issue id on spawn
body:
## Summary

Fixes cross-project spawn tagging the session with the wrong `projectId` when `ao start` is running for a different project than the issue belongs to.

- **New core utility `resolveSpawnTarget(projects, issueRef, fallback?)`** — parses `<prefix>/<rest>` and routes to the matched project. Accepts either a project id (yaml key) or `sessionPrefix` as the prefix; project id wins on collision. Returns `null` when nothing matches and no fallback is supplied.
- **`ao spawn <projectId>/<issue>`** — now routes to the prefixed project and strips the prefix from the issue id. Previously `projectId` fell back to whichever project `ao start` was running for, giving the session the wrong prefix and dashboard column.
- **`ao spawn <sessionPrefix>/<issue>`** — also works (e.g. `xid/1` routes to the project whose `sessionPrefix` is `xid`).
- **`ao batch-spawn`** — groups issues by resolved project and runs preflight once per group, instead of erroring on mixed prefixes.
- **Web `/api/spawn`** — unchanged; it already requires an explicit `projectId`, so it's immune. Any future caller that wants free-form issue refs can opt in by calling `resolveSpawnTarget` before `sessionManager.spawn()`.
- **`SessionManager.spawn()`** — unchanged on purpose. Explicit `{ projectId, issueId }` stays authoritative; the utility is opt-in for callers that want routing.

Fixes #1329

## Design notes

The first commit was a CLI-only fix. The second commit lifts the routing into a core utility so any spawn entry point (CLI, web API, programmatic) can share the same behavior. The CLI now imports `resolveSpawnTarget` instead of duplicating logic.

Prefix disambiguation: project-id match wins over `sessionPrefix` match because yaml keys are unique by construction while `sessionPrefix` values are not guaranteed to be.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` — 800 tests pass, including 8 new unit tests for `resolveSpawnTarget` covering:
  - project-id prefix match
  - sessionPrefix prefix match
  - project-id wins on collision
  - fallback used when prefix doesn't match
  - returns `null` when nothing matches and no fallback
  - bare issue id passed through
  - leading/trailing slash inputs handled
  - `undefined` issueRef handled
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli test` — 485 tests pass, including 3 new `spawn.test.ts` cases:
  - routes `x402-identity/1` → `projectId: x402-identity`, `issueId: 1`
  - routes `xid/7` via `sessionPrefix` → `projectId: x402-identity`, `issueId: 7`
  - leaves `some-org/42` untouched when no project or prefix matches
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli typecheck` pass
- [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 errors (33 pre-existing warnings unchanged)
- [ ] Manual repro: multi-project config, `ao start agent-orchestrator`, `ao spawn x402-identity/1` → session prefix `xid-*`, `projectId` = `x402-identity`, appears under x402-identity on the dashboard
- [ ] Manual repro: `ao batch-spawn agent-orchestrator/1 x402-identity/2` → one session per project, each routed correctly

## Issue

`pnpm audit` reports vulnerable dependency chains in the current monorepo dependency graph. We should bump the affected direct and/or peer-resolved dependencies so the audit passes cleanly instead of relying on workflow tolerance or retry behavior.

## Affected Package

- Package path: `packages/web`, `packages/plugins/notifier-composio`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`
- npm package: `@aoagents/ao-web`, `@aoagents/ao-plugin-notifier-composio`
- Surface area: `security.yml` dependency audit, local `pnpm audit`, local `agent-ci` workflow execution
- Shared code touched: `none expected beyond lockfile and any package manifests needed for the bumps`

## Reproduction

1. Sync a working branch with `origin/main`.
2. Run local workflow validation: `npx @redwoodjs/agent-ci run --quiet --all --pause-on-failure`.
3. Observe the run pause in `security.yml > npm-audit > Run npm audit`.
4. Reproduce locally with `pnpm audit --audit-level=moderate --json`.

## Current Result

`agent-ci` pauses on the audit step, and local `pnpm audit --audit-level=moderate --json` reports `5` vulnerabilities (`1 low`, `4 moderate`).

## Expected Result

`pnpm audit` should pass cleanly on the repo dependency graph so `security.yml` and local `agent-ci` runs can complete in the cleanest possible way, without depending on tolerated failures, retries, or workflow-level suppression.

## Evidence

- Workflow step: `.github/workflows/security.yml`
  - `Run npm audit` executes `pnpm audit --audit-level=moderate`
- Local reproduction:
  - `pnpm audit --audit-level=moderate --json`
  - Result: `5` vulnerabilities, `1 low`, `4 moderate`
- Vulnerabilities observed:
  - `vite@5.4.21` via `GHSA-4w7w-66w2-5vf9`
  - `esbuild@0.21.5` via `GHSA-67mh-4wv8-2f99`
  - `follow-redirects@1.15.11` via `GHSA-r4q5-vmmm-2653`
  - `langsmith@0.5.18` via `GHSA-rr7j-v2q5-chgv`
  - `tmp@0.0.33` via `GHSA-52f5-9888-hmc6`
- Example dependency paths from local audit output:
  - `packages/web > @vitejs/plugin-react@4.7.0 > vite@5.4.21 > esbuild@0.21.5`
  - `packages/plugins/notifier-composio > composio-core@0.5.39 > axios@1.15.0 > follow-redirects@1.15.11`
  - `packages/plugins/notifier-composio > composio-core@0.5.39 > @langchain/core@1.1.39 > langsmith@0.5.18`

> [!NOTE]
> The following is the fix spec for AI agents.

## Steps

1. Open `packages/web/package.json`, `packages/plugins/notifier-composio/package.json`, and `pnpm-lock.yaml` and trace which direct or peer-resolved dependencies are responsible for the vulnerable chains.
2. Bump the relevant dependencies so the resolved graph no longer includes the flagged vulnerable versions.
3. Prefer real dependency upgrades over workflow suppression; do not solve this by weakening `security.yml`.
4. Update the lockfile with the narrowest dependency changes that eliminate the current audit findings.
5. Re-run `pnpm audit --audit-level=moderate` and local `agent-ci` to confirm the workflow now clears the audit step cleanly.
6. Commit only the manifest and lockfile changes needed for the audit cleanup.

## Validation

- Audit check: `pnpm audit --audit-level=moderate`
- Strict audit check: `pnpm audit --prod --audit-level=high`
- Relevant package checks: `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test`, `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web typecheck`
- Broader validation: `npx @redwoodjs/agent-ci run --quiet --all --pause-on-failure`

## Constraints

- Keep scope focused on dependency bumps and lockfile updates required to clear the current audit findings.
- Do not paper over the issue by changing the workflow to ignore or suppress the audit failure.
- Prefer the smallest version changes that remove the vulnerable resolved versions.
- Note any dependency that cannot be bumped cleanly as follow-up work instead of broadening scope unnecessarily.

## Acceptance

- `pnpm audit --audit-level=moderate` exits successfully on the repo checkout
- Local `agent-ci` no longer pauses on `security.yml > npm-audit > Run npm audit`

title: fix(core): dispatch detailed bugbot review comments to agents
body:
## Summary

Fixes #895 — the bugbot-comments reaction was sending a generic message, leaving the agent to rediscover comments on its own. The naive `GET /pulls/{pr}/comments` first-page scan misses new comments on later pages and trusts a stale `gh pr checks` status, causing the agent to falsely report "all reviews addressed."

## Changes

- `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts`
  - Add `formatAutomatedCommentsMessage(AutomatedComment[])`, mirroring `formatCIFailureMessage`. Lists each comment (severity, bot name, `path:line`, first-line excerpt, URL) and embeds correct-API guidance.
  - In `maybeDispatchReviewBacklog`, override the reaction config's `message` with the formatted one for `send-to-agent` dispatches of `bugbot-comments`. Fingerprint/dedup path unchanged.
- `packages/core/src/config.ts` — update the default `bugbot-comments` reaction text to embed the `/reviews` → `/reviews/{id}/comments` → paginated `/pulls/{pr}/comments` (checking `in_reply_to_id`) sequence as a fallback for custom configs that don't rely on the dispatcher.
- `packages/core/src/__tests__/lifecycle-manager.test.ts` — update the "dispatches automated review comments only once" test to assert the new message contains comment details AND the correct-API guidance.

## Why this design

The core already paginates `getAutomatedComments` correctly and knows every bot comment. The old code threw that data away when dispatching and let the agent re-query with a broken pattern. Passing the already-fetched data to the agent removes the failure mode entirely; embedding the correct verification steps guards against agents that still want to re-check.

## Test plan

title: feat: code-review plugin slot — AI-powered peer review for worker PRs (#1275)
body:
## Summary

Adds the **9th plugin slot** — `code-review` — to Agent Orchestrator. When a coding agent opens a PR, AO can auto-spawn a lightweight reviewer workspace (just a detached git worktree, no tmux/agent/runtime), run the configured CodeReview plugin in it, persist structured findings, and loop until the code is clean or a human intervenes.

Closes #1275 (the tracking issue for this feature).

## What's included

### Core (`packages/core/`)

- **Plugin slot types** (`types.ts`): `CodeReview` interface, `CodeReviewRun`, `CodeReviewFinding`, `CodeReviewThread`, `CodeReviewConfig`. `PluginSlot` and `ExternalPluginLocation` extended for the new slot.
- **Config** (`config.ts`): Zod `CodeReviewConfigSchema` on `ProjectConfig.codeReview` with `mode`, `prompt`, `autoSendNewFindingsToAgent`, `routing.publishToScm`, `limits` (`maxReviewRounds`, `maxBudgetPerRun`, `confidenceThreshold`, `stallWindow`), `severityThreshold`, `trigger.onPullRequestOpen/Update/manual`. External plugin collection honors the new slot.
- **Paths** (`paths.ts`): `getReviewsDir` and `getReviewWorkspacesDir` under the per-project base dir.
- **Plugin registry** (`plugin-registry.ts`): builtin `code-review-codex` registration; `updateConfigWithManifestName` handles the new `codeReview` project location.
- **Fingerprint + convergence** (`code-review-fingerprint.ts`): stable 16-hex `sha256(filePath\\0category\\0severity\\0anchor)` fingerprint, sliding-window union, stalled-detection per the spec, dismissal carry-forward.
- **Flat-file review store** (`review-store.ts`): CRUD for runs/findings/threads. Reviewer IDs (`{sessionPrefix}-rev-N`) allocated project-wide to prevent collisions across workers.
- **Review manager** (`review-manager.ts`): serializes at most one in-flight reviewer per worker+SHA, marks prior runs ``outdated``, creates detached reviewer worktrees, carries forward dismissed findings via fingerprint matching, runs convergence check, terminates with structured reasons (`cycle_cap`, `reviewer_failure`, `manual_cancel`, etc.), cleans up workspaces for done/stalled/failed runs (keeps `awaiting_context` alive for chat).
- **Lifecycle integration** (`lifecycle-manager.ts` + `code-review-trigger.ts`): generic `onSessionPolled` hook on `LifecycleManagerDeps` so the review manager can piggyback on the existing poll loop without entangling the lifecycle state machine in review internals. `createReviewTrigger` skips disabled/manual-only projects and dedupes per worker HEAD SHA via `git rev-parse`.

### Reference plugin (`packages/plugins/code-review-codex/`)

- Wraps `codex exec review --base <branch> --json`. Parses structured findings into `CodeReviewFindingInput` (flexible field mapping for codex/review shape drift). Maps P0/P1/P2/P3 priority to error/warning/info. Persists the codex session inside the reviewer workspace so `sendFollowUp` can reattach for chat.

### CLI (`packages/cli/src/commands/review.ts`)

- `ao review run <session>` — trigger a review
- `ao review list [session]` — list review runs
- `ao review show <runId>` — display findings
- `ao review dismiss <runId> <findingId>` — dismiss (persists across re-reviews)
- `ao review send <runId> [findingId]` — route findings to the coding agent
- `ao review cancel <runId>` — terminate a running review

### Web (`packages/web/`)

- `services.ts` registers the Codex code-review plugin, builds a `ReviewManager`, and wires `createReviewTrigger` into the lifecycle's new `onSessionPolled` hook.
- `/reviews` page: 5-column Kanban (Running, Awaiting context, Done, Stalled, Terminated) grouped by `loopState` with finding previews.
- `GET /api/reviews` — list review runs with findings (filterable by project/session)
- `POST /api/reviews/runs` — manually trigger a review
- `PATCH /api/reviews/findings/[runId]/[findingId]` — dismiss/reopen/send actions

### Tests

- Core: fingerprint stability, reviewer ID allocation (project-scoped), store CRUD, triage carry-forward, convergence (including flip-flop detection)
- Codex plugin: manifest, JSON payload extraction, finding normalization, priority-to-severity mapping
- Full test run: **812 core tests** and **483 CLI tests** green.

## Test plan

- [ ] `pnpm typecheck` — all packages
- [ ] `pnpm test` — unit + integration
- [ ] `pnpm lint` — no new errors
- [ ] `ao review run <session>` works against a real codex install
- [ ] Review Workbench (`/reviews`) renders grouped runs with findings
- [ ] Dismissing a finding on one run keeps it dismissed on the next re-review for the same worker (fingerprint match)
- [ ] A stalled loop (`maxReviewRounds: 3` with no convergence) transitions to STALLED and records `terminationReason: cycle_cap`
- [ ] `awaiting_context` keeps the reviewer workspace; `done` / `stalled` / `failed` / `outdated` cleans it up

title: feat(cli): filter terminated sessions from ao session ls / ao status by default
body:
Closes #1310.

## Summary

- `ao session ls` and `ao status` now hide terminated sessions (`killed`, `terminated`, `done`, `merged`, `errored`, `cleanup`, plus lifecycle-driven terminal states like `runtime.state=exited` and `pr.state=merged`) by default.
- A dim footer reports how many were hidden: `N terminated sessions hidden. Use --include-terminated to show.`
- New flag `--include-terminated` on both commands restores the pre-change behavior.
- Keeps `-a, --all` orthogonal — it still only governs orchestrator visibility on `ao session ls`. Combine the two flags when you want both.

## Breaking change: JSON shape

`ao session ls --json` and `ao status --json` now emit `{ data: [...], meta: { hiddenTerminatedCount: number } }` instead of a bare array. Scripts consuming the JSON must read `.data`. `--include-terminated` restores the full data set and reports `hiddenTerminatedCount: 0`.

A Changeset entry (`.changeset/filter-terminated-sessions-from-ls.md`) calls this out as a minor bump with migration guidance. `SETUP.md` and `docs/CLI.md` updated to match the new shape and flag.

## Scope & rationale

- **CLI-only.** Does not touch lifecycle auto-archival (that's #536 — different risk surface, different rollback story).
- **`ao session restore <id>` unchanged.** That path goes through `sm.get`, not `sm.list`, so terminated sessions remain restorable by id.
- **`--watch` respects the filter each tick** (recomputes `hiddenTerminatedCount` each render so transitions to terminal state are reflected live).
- **Web dashboard unaffected** — already handled via `packages/web/src/lib/orchestrator-utils.ts`.

## Review input

Planned with `/codex` consult before implementation, then reviewed with `/codex` against the diff. Codex flagged three nits, all addressed:

1. ✅ Stale JSON examples in `SETUP.md` and `docs/CLI.md` — updated.
2. ✅ Missing tests for the lifecycle branch of `isTerminalSession` (vs. the flat-status branch) — added on both commands.
3. Deferred (nit, not blocker): per-project "(no active sessions)" message still prints when a project has only hidden terminals. Global footer already discloses the count. Happy to follow up if preferred.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — clean across all packages.
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli test` — 486 passed (6 new tests: 3 per command covering filter, flag, JSON meta; 1 new lifecycle-branch test per command).

  - `ao session ls` / `ao status` → active-only with footer.
  - `ao session ls --include-terminated` / `ao status --include-terminated` → full list, no footer.
  - `ao session ls --json` / `ao status --json` → `{data, meta.hiddenTerminatedCount > 0}`, `data` filtered.
  - `ao session restore <terminated-id>` still works.
  - `ao status --watch` → footer updates when a session transitions terminal mid-watch.

title: fix(webhooks): restore killed sessions and auto-spawn on CI failure
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1290

When a CI webhook fires for a PR, `findAffectedSessions` only matches sessions in non-terminal states. If the session was previously killed or errored, the event was silently dropped with a bare `continue`. This means the CI failure signal never reached the agent.

- Add `findRestorableSessions()` in `scm-webhooks.ts` using the existing `isRestorable()` predicate from `ao-core` (covers killed/terminated/done/errored, excludes merged)
- In the webhook route handler, when `findAffectedSessions` returns empty for a CI event, restore any matching terminal sessions and re-run `lifecycle.check()` so the existing reaction engine handles the `ci-failed` signal
- If no restorable session exists and `autoSpawnOnCIFailure` is enabled in project config, spawn a new session with a targeted prompt to investigate and fix the CI failure
- Add `autoSpawnOnCIFailure?: boolean` to `SCMWebhookConfig` in `types.ts`
- Add 4 unit tests for `findRestorableSessions` covering: non-CI events, CI events without prNumber, matched killed session, and skipping merged sessions

- All 432 non-web tests pass
- Typecheck and build clean across all packages

title: fix(web): restore terminal cell metrics after xterm v6 upgrade
body:
## Summary

The xterm.js v5 → v6 upgrade (#1276) regressed the in-browser terminal: each character cell renders wider and shorter than the glyph drawn inside it, making horizontal spacing too loose and vertical spacing too tight. This PR restores correct cell metrics.

## What was broken

Four issues compounded in `packages/web/src/components/DirectTerminal.tsx`:

1. **`fontFamily` used `var(--font-jetbrains-mono)`.** xterm's internal character measurement ends up in canvas `ctx.font`, which cannot resolve CSS custom properties. The `var(...)` token poisoned the font string, so measurement fell back to a default font while DOM rows kept rendering in JetBrains Mono — cell width and glyph width drifted apart.
2. **xterm v6 defaults `lineHeight` to `1.0`.** Combined with JetBrains Mono's tall x-height, rows visually collide.
3. **`document.fonts.ready` resolved early.** `next/font` uses `font-display: swap`, so the initial `fit()` can run against the fallback font and xterm never re-measures when the real webfont swaps in.
4. **`p-1.5` padding on the fit-target div** skewed FitAddon's `cols`/`rows` computation.

## What changed

- Dropped `var(...)` from `fontFamily`; use a plain stack `"JetBrains Mono", "SF Mono", Menlo, Monaco, "Courier New", monospace`.
- Set `lineHeight: 1.2` on the Terminal options to restore vertical breathing room.
- Added a `document.fonts` `loadingdone` listener that clears the texture atlas and re-fits when the webfont swap actually completes. Unregistered in the effect's cleanup.
- Removed `p-1.5` from the terminal ref div so FitAddon sizes against the real viewport.

## Test plan

- [ ] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web typecheck` passes (verified locally)
- [ ] `pnpm dev` and open a session terminal — glyphs fill cells cleanly, no wide horizontal air between characters, no cramped rows
- [ ] Resize the window / toggle fullscreen — cell metrics remain correct
- [ ] Adjust terminal font size via the stepper — grid stays aligned
- [ ] Hard-reload with cache disabled — first paint uses fallback font, swap in to JetBrains Mono triggers a re-fit (verify via logs / visual)
- [ ] Light and dark themes both render correctly

title: fix(web): resolve dashboard issue URLs from tracker
body:
## Summary
- resolve issue links from tracker metadata when sessions only store issue identifiers (for example `42`)
- keep existing absolute URLs unchanged and continue to enrich `issueLabel`/`issueTitle` from the resolved URL
- add regression coverage for identifier-only issue IDs in dashboard metadata enrichment

## Root cause
`sessionToDashboard()` treated `session.issueId` as a URL. For GitHub sessions spawned with an identifier, this produced invalid links like `/42` and broke downstream issue enrichment assumptions.

## What changed
- `sessionToDashboard()` now only initializes `issueUrl` when `issueId` is already an absolute URL.
- `enrichSessionIssue()` now resolves `dashboard.issueUrl` via `tracker.issueUrl()` using the available issue reference (`issueId` or existing `issueUrl`).
- metadata enrichment now runs issue enrichment when either `issueUrl` or `issueId` exists.
- tests updated to verify numeric issue identifiers are converted into valid tracker URLs.

## Why this approach
This keeps backward compatibility for sessions already storing full URLs while fixing identifier-only sessions at the existing enrichment boundary, avoiding schema changes or broader refactors.

## Testing
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test -- src/lib/__tests__/serialize.test.ts`

Closes #1213.

title: fix(web): treat exited sessions as restorable in detail view
body:
## Summary
- treat `activity: exited` as a terminal condition in `SessionDetail`, even when lifecycle status is still non-terminal
- keep restore eligibility gated by existing `NON_RESTORABLE_STATUSES`
- add desktop regression coverage for crashed workers that still report `status: working`

## Root cause
`SessionDetail` only used `TERMINAL_STATUSES` to decide if a session had ended. Sessions that crashed and emitted `activity: exited` before status convergence were rendered as live and had no restore affordance.

## What changed
- include `TERMINAL_ACTIVITIES` in the detail-page terminal-ended predicate
- add a test that verifies ended placeholder + restore button for `status=working` + `activity=exited`

## Why this approach
The rest of the dashboard already uses status-or-activity terminal semantics. Aligning the detail page avoids behavioral drift without changing backend lifecycle logic.

## Testing

Closes #1225.

title: fix(core): make opencode worker prompt delivery reliable
body:
## Summary
- deliver OpenCode worker prompts via post-launch runtime messaging with retries
- stop inlining worker prompt payload into the OpenCode launch command path
- add regression coverage proving prompt delivery + metadata state for OpenCode workers

## Root cause
OpenCode worker spawns relied on inline launch-command prompt delivery. If the OpenCode startup flow did not complete cleanly, the prompt could be dropped while AO still marked it as delivered.

## What changed
- in worker `spawn()`, treat OpenCode as a post-launch prompt-delivery flow
- pass `prompt: undefined` to OpenCode launch config so launch only establishes session/runtime
- send the composed prompt through `runtime.sendMessage()` using existing retry logic
- preserve existing behavior for other agent plugins
- add test coverage for OpenCode worker prompt delivery and `promptDelivered` metadata

## Why this approach
This reuses an existing, battle-tested delivery path and keeps the fix tightly scoped to OpenCode worker spawning without changing plugin contracts or broader session lifecycle behavior.

## Testing
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test -- src/__tests__/session-manager/spawn.test.ts`

Closes #1304.

title: fix(core): stop foreign legacy session kind misclassification
body:
## Summary
- derive session kind during metadata reconstruction using project-scoped orchestrator ID rules
- pass explicit `sessionKind` into canonical lifecycle parsing from `sessionFromMetadata`
- add regression assertion that foreign-prefix legacy bare orchestrator records remain `worker` in-memory

## Root cause
When reading metadata, `parseCanonicalLifecycle()` could infer orchestrator kind from `sessionId.endsWith("-orchestrator")` when no role was present. That fallback misclassified foreign-prefix legacy records in-memory even though on-disk repair no longer stamped `role: orchestrator`.

## What changed
- introduced `deriveSessionKindFromMetadata()` in session manager reconstruction flow
- threaded `sessionKind` through `sessionFromMetadata` options into lifecycle parsing
- updated read/get call sites to provide project session prefix context
- extended existing issue #1048 regression test to assert in-memory `lifecycle.session.kind === "worker"`

## Why this approach
This keeps canonical lifecycle parsing deterministic at read time with project context, without changing persisted metadata format or broad lifecycle behavior.

## Testing
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test -- src/__tests__/session-manager/query.test.ts`

Closes #1323.

title: fix(scm-github): avoid conflict misclassification for draft/blocking states

## Summary
- compute `noConflicts` from explicit `mergeable === CONFLICTING` only
- prevent blocked/draft/unknown GitHub merge states from being interpreted as merge conflicts
- add regression assertions for `BLOCKED` and `UNKNOWN` mergeability outcomes

## Root cause
`getMergeability()` set `noConflicts` to true only for `MERGEABLE`. For draft or branch-protection-blocked PRs, GitHub can return non-`MERGEABLE` values without actual conflicts, which caused conflict-based reactions to trigger via `!noConflicts`.

- updated tests to assert non-conflicting behavior for `BLOCKED`/`UNKNOWN` states

## Why this approach
It matches GitHub semantics more closely and keeps conflict reactions tied to explicit conflict data, while preserving existing blockers for review/branch-protection/draft conditions.

title: fix: ETag Guard mishandles HTTP 304, SSE stream controller-closed spam
body:
## Summary

Three runtime issues observed in the web dashboard (`pnpm dev`) — two are bugs, one is transient/informational.

---

## Issue 1: ETag Guard treats HTTP 304 as failure (P1 — wastes API quota)

**File:** `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/graphql-batch.ts` (lines 336–381, 394–440)

**Symptom:**
```
[ETag Guard 1] PR list check failed for owner/repo: Command failed: gh api ... gh: HTTP 304
```

**Root cause:** The `gh` CLI exits with a non-zero exit code on HTTP 304 (Not Modified). This causes `execFileAsync` to throw, so the code that correctly handles 304 in stdout (line 357) is **never reached**. Execution jumps to the catch block (line 373), which:
1. Logs a misleading "PR list check failed" warning
2. Returns `true` (assume changed), triggering a redundant GraphQL batch query

**Impact:** The entire 2-Guard ETag caching optimization is defeated — every poll cycle falls through to the expensive GraphQL batch call, wasting GitHub API quota. The caching logic is correct in theory but broken in practice because of how `gh` handles 304.

**Fix:** In both catch blocks (Guard 1 line 373, Guard 2 line 431), detect "HTTP 304" in the error message and return `false` (unchanged) instead of `true`.

---

## Issue 2: SSE stream — unhandled "Controller is already closed" rejections (P2)

**File:** `packages/web/src/app/api/events/route.ts`

**Symptom:**
```
TypeError: Invalid state: Controller is already closed
⨯ unhandledRejection: TypeError: Invalid state: Controller is already closed
```
Repeated many times per client disconnect.

**Root cause:** When an SSE client disconnects, `cancel()` fires and clears the `setInterval` timers. But async polling callbacks (`void (async () => { ... })()` at line 130) that were already in-flight continue to execute and call `controller.enqueue()` on the closed controller. The inner try/catch (line 182) handles some cases, but the race window between `cancel()` and in-flight async callbacks produces unhandled rejections.

**Impact:** Floods the server console with unhandled rejection errors. Not a data-loss bug, but it pollutes logs and could mask real errors.

**Fix:** Track a `closed` boolean flag, set it in `cancel()`, and guard every `controller.enqueue()` call with a check on that flag.

---

## Issue 3: GraphQL batch — TLS handshake timeout (P3 — transient)

**File:** `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/graphql-batch.ts` (lines 547–594)

**Symptom:**
```
[GraphQL Batch Warning] Batch enrichment partially failed: ... Post "https://api.github.com/graphql": net/http: TLS handshake timeout
```

**Root cause:** Transient network issue — GitHub API latency or local network hiccup during TLS negotiation. The code already handles this gracefully (logs warning, continues to next batch, retries next poll cycle).

**Impact:** Low — affected PRs miss enrichment for one cycle. Fixing Issue 1 would reduce exposure since ETag caching would skip unnecessary batch calls.

**No code change needed** unless this becomes recurring, in which case adding retry-with-backoff for TLS errors specifically would help.

---

## Priority

| Priority | Issue | Reason |
|----------|-------|--------|
| P1 | ETag Guard 304 | Defeats caching, wastes API quota every poll cycle |
| P2 | SSE controller closed | Log noise, unhandled rejections |
| P3 | TLS timeout | Transient, already handled |

title: Add  to fully wipe a project's local AO state and reinitialize from scratch
body:
## Problem
There is currently no single command to completely reset an AO project on a machine. Over time, a project can accumulate local AO state such as archives, worker sessions, orchestrator sessions, project config/state, and other persisted metadata.

If I want to make AO treat the project as if it is being seen for the first time on this machine, I should not have to manually hunt through all the AO-managed files and directories.

## Requested behavior
Add an `ao reset`-style command that fully deletes a project's local AO state and returns it to a clean, first-run state on that machine.

## What it should remove
For the targeted project, the reset should remove things like:
- archived AO history/state for the project
- worker sessions
- orchestrator sessions
- project-specific AO config/state
- cached metadata and local persisted session/project records
- any other AO-managed local data that would cause the project to be remembered

In other words, after `ao reset`, AO should behave as though the project has never been configured locally before.

## Expected outcome
After running the reset command for a project:
- there should be no surviving local AO history for that project
- no worker/orchestrator sessions should remain
- no archived session state should remain
- the next AO interaction should require project setup/configuration as if it were the first time

## Why this matters
- makes it easy to recover from local AO state drift or corruption
- gives users a clean way to start over during testing and development
- avoids error-prone manual deletion of hidden AO-managed files/directories
- improves confidence that a reset is complete and not partial

## Possible UX
Something like:

```bash
ao reset
ao reset <project>
ao reset -p <project>
```

Because this is destructive, it should probably:
- show exactly what will be deleted
- require confirmation (unless `--yes` is passed)
- clearly scope the reset to one project unless the user explicitly requests a broader/global reset

## Notes
The important part is that this is not just session cleanup. It should wipe the full local AO footprint for a project so the project is effectively brand new to AO on that machine.

title: bug: spawn prompt message delivered but enter key not pressed
body:
## Description

When spawning a session with `ao spawn --prompt "..."`, the prompt message is delivered to the tmux session but the enter key is not pressed. The text appears in the terminal but is never submitted to the agent, so the agent sits idle without receiving the instruction.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `ao spawn --prompt "Wait for further instructions."`
2. Session spawns successfully
3. Attach to the session — the prompt text is visible in the terminal but was never submitted (no newline/enter sent)

## Expected Behavior

The prompt message should be fully sent to the agent (including pressing enter) so the agent receives and acts on it.

## Actual Behavior

The message text appears in the terminal buffer but the enter key (`Enter`/`C-m`) is never sent, so the agent never processes the instruction.

## Environment

- OS: macOS
- AO version: latest main

## Summary

- Change the `appleboy/ssh-action` SSH user in `.github/workflows/deploy-vps.yml` from `root` to `aoagent`, and update the working directory in the same step from `/root/agent-orchestrator` to `/home/aoagent/agent-orchestrator`.

## Why

The VPS deploy currently SSHes in as `root` but operates on files owned by `aoagent` through the `/root/agent-orchestrator` → `/home/aoagent/agent-orchestrator` symlink. Every `pnpm install` / `pnpm build` run then creates new cache entries (`.pnpm`, `.bun`, `.cache`, `node_modules`) owned by `root` inside an otherwise aoagent-owned subtree, leaking root ownership on each deploy. Running the deploy as `aoagent` removes that drift at the source.

## Notes

- No secret rotation needed — the existing `VPS_SSH_KEY` pubkey (`dhruv-ao-openclaw`, `SHA256:0i7ttaeLL1ZMDwKcvdnpoyTosX38+xLjJ0fuJgGZLlI`) is already present in `/home/aoagent/.ssh/authorized_keys` on the VPS, so the same key authenticates for `aoagent`.
- Working-tree path change is cosmetic: `/root/agent-orchestrator` is a symlink to `/home/aoagent/agent-orchestrator`, so we point the deploy at the canonical path.

title: fix: clear stale dashboard PR ownership
body:
## Summary
- clear closed-unmerged PR references from canonical lifecycle metadata so sessions stop carrying a stale PR URL/number
- re-run branch-based PR detection when a tracked PR closes and immediately attach a replacement PR if one already exists
- add regression tests for closed PR cleanup and replacement PR detection, plus a changeset entry

## Root Cause Analysis
The stale dashboard PR number came from a mismatch between raw session metadata and canonical lifecycle state:

1. PR ownership was persisted in two places:
   - legacy/raw metadata via `pr=<url>`
   - canonical lifecycle payload via `statePayload.pr.url` / `statePayload.pr.number`
2. The dashboard read path reconstructed `session.pr` from canonical lifecycle first, then fell back to raw metadata.
3. When lifecycle polling saw a PR become `closed`, it changed only the PR state/reason. It did not clear the stored PR URL/number.
4. Because `session.pr` stayed non-null, the poller never re-entered the `scm.detectPR()` path, so a replacement PR on the same branch was never discovered.
5. Even if a new PR was opened and the `gh pr create` wrapper updated raw metadata, the dashboard still preferred the stale canonical lifecycle PR reference.

That combination left the UI pinned to the first PR number indefinitely.

## Fix
- On `closed` PRs, clear the canonical PR URL/number when no replacement PR exists.
- On `closed` PRs, attempt `scm.detectPR()` for the session branch and attach the new PR immediately when found.
- Preserve merged PR identity; only closed-unmerged PRs are cleared/replaced.

## Validation
- `pnpm build`
- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm test`

Fixes ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator#1361.

title: feat(plugin): implement kimicode agent plugin
body:
## Summary

Add a new agent plugin for [kimicode](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-cli) so users can select it as the coding agent in `agent-orchestrator.yaml`, matching the same standards as the existing agent plugins (`agent-claude-code`, `agent-codex`, `agent-aider`, `agent-opencode`).

## Motivation

AO's plugin model already supports pluggable AI tools via the `Agent` slot. kimicode is a new coding agent we want to make available alongside the existing four. Dashboard features (PR tracking, cost display, activity/state detection, session resume) should all work the same way for kimicode sessions as they do for the other agents.

## Scope

Create a new plugin package at `packages/plugins/agent-kimicode/` that fully implements the `Agent` interface from `@composio/ao-core`, following the conventions documented in `CLAUDE.md` (§ Plugin Standards / Agent Plugin Implementation Standards).

### Package layout

```
packages/plugins/agent-kimicode/
├── package.json          # @composio/ao-plugin-agent-kimicode
├── tsconfig.json         # extends ../../../tsconfig.base.json
├── src/
│   ├── index.ts          # manifest + create + detect (default export)
│   └── __tests__/        # vitest tests
```

- Package name: `@composio/ao-plugin-agent-kimicode`
- `manifest.name`: `"kimicode"`
- `manifest.slot`: `"agent" as const`

### Required interface methods

All methods from the `Agent` interface must be implemented:

| Method | Notes |
|--------|-------|
| `getLaunchCommand` | Shell command to launch kimicode in the worktree |
| `getEnvironment` | Must set `AO_SESSION_ID`, optional `AO_ISSUE_ID`, and prepend `~/.ao/bin` to `PATH` via `buildAgentPath()` |
| `detectActivity` | Terminal-output classifier; match actual kimicode prompts (test against real output, do not guess) |
| `getActivityState` | Follow the 5-step cascade in CLAUDE.md — process check → actionable states → native signal → **JSONL entry fallback (mandatory)** → null |
| `isProcessRunning` | Support both tmux (TTY + `ps` regex) and process runtime (PID signal-0). Regex must match both the node wrapper and the actual binary name |
| `getSessionInfo` | Extract summary, cost, and native session ID from whatever introspection kimicode exposes; return `null` if unavailable |

### Optional interface methods (implement where applicable)

| Method | Notes |
|--------|-------|
| `getRestoreCommand` | Implement if kimicode supports resuming a prior session; return `null` otherwise |
| `setupWorkspaceHooks` | **Required** for PR tracking. If kimicode has native post-tool hooks, wire them up; otherwise call `setupPathWrapperWorkspace(workspacePath)` |
| `postLaunchSetup` | Re-ensure hooks, resolve binary path, etc. |
| `recordActivity` | Delegate to `recordTerminalActivity(workspacePath, output, (o) => this.detectActivity(o))` unless kimicode emits its own fully-featured JSONL |

### Activity detection pattern

Pick one of the two documented patterns based on what kimicode provides:

1. **Native JSONL** (like Claude Code / Codex) — if kimicode writes a rich JSONL log including tool calls, permission requests, and errors, map entries to activity states.
2. **AO Activity JSONL** (like Aider / OpenCode) — otherwise, implement `recordActivity` via `recordTerminalActivity` and read via `readLastActivityEntry` → `checkActivityLogState` → `getActivityFallbackState`.

All 6 lifecycle states must be reachable: `spawning`, `active`, `ready`, `idle`, `waiting_input`, `blocked`, `exited`.

### Tests

`src/__tests__/index.test.ts` using Vitest. At minimum, cover:

- Manifest values (`name`, `slot`, `version`)
- `create()` return shape
- All public methods happy path
- Error paths (missing binary, invalid config)
- **`getActivityState` required cases (from CLAUDE.md):**
  1. Returns `exited` when process is not running
  2. Returns `waiting_input` from JSONL at a permission prompt
  3. Returns `blocked` from JSONL on error
  4. Returns `active` from native signal when recently active
  5. Returns `active` from JSONL entry fallback when native signal fails (fresh entry)
  6. Returns `idle` from JSONL entry fallback with age decay (old entry)
  7. Returns `null` when both native signal and JSONL are unavailable

Mock external CLIs, file I/O, and HTTP calls. Use `beforeEach` to reset mocks.

### Wiring

- Add the package to the pnpm workspace (inherits from root `pnpm-workspace.yaml`).
- Add `@composio/ao-plugin-agent-kimicode` as a dependency of `packages/cli` so it is bundled into the CLI like the other agent plugins.
- Register it in the plugin registry loading code if registration is explicit (check how `agent-codex` is wired).
- Update default YAML / example config (`agent-orchestrator.yaml` template, onboarding wizard if applicable) so users discover the option.

### Documentation

- Add a section to any agent-comparison docs (e.g. README plugin table) listing kimicode.
- Ensure `detect()` returns `true` only when the kimicode binary is available on `PATH`.

## Constraints

- TypeScript strict mode, no `any` (CLAUDE.md § Code Style).
- Use `shellEscape()` from core for all command arguments — no raw string interpolation into shell commands.
- No hardcoded secrets; use `process.env` and throw with a descriptive message if a required env var is missing.
- Validate plugin config once in `create()`, store via closure — don't re-validate per call.

title: fix(web): killing session from session page shows error instead of returning to dashboard
body:
## Summary

When a worker session is killed via the Terminate button on the session detail page (`/sessions/[id]`), the dashboard does not navigate away. Instead the now-invalid session URL renders the error boundary (`error.tsx`) because the session no longer exists / is no longer restorable.

Expected: after a successful kill from the session detail page, navigate the user back to the dashboard (or the project view they came from).

## Repro

1. Spawn a worker session: `ao spawn`.
2. Open the session detail page in the browser: `/sessions/<id>`.
3. Click the Terminate button.
4. Observe: the page transitions to an error screen (the App Router `error.tsx` boundary) rather than going back to `/`.

## Root cause (likely)

- Kill handler POSTs to `/api/sessions/[id]/kill` and updates local state.
- The session detail page re-renders. Either:
  - SSE / page data fetch returns 404 / error for the killed session and throws, triggering `error.tsx`, or
  - Server component re-renders with no session data and the page component errors on null access.
- No `router.push('/')` (or equivalent) is fired after a successful kill.

Relevant files:
- `packages/web/src/components/Dashboard.tsx` — `killSession` (~L337) already handles navigation from the dashboard context.
- `packages/web/src/components/BottomSheet.tsx` — \`confirm-kill\` flow and \`onRequestKill\` callback.
- `packages/web/src/app/sessions/[id]/page.tsx` — session detail page; needs a post-kill redirect.
- `packages/web/src/app/sessions/[id]/error.tsx` — currently what the user sees after kill.

## Proposed fix

1. In whatever component hosts the kill button on the session detail page, after the `POST /api/sessions/[id]/kill` call resolves successfully:
   - Use `useRouter()` from `next/navigation` and call `router.push('/')` (or the referring project URL if tracked).
   - Do **not** rely on state updates / SSE to re-render the detail page — navigate explicitly before the next render can fail.
2. If the kill request **fails**, stay on the page and surface an error toast; don't navigate.
3. Confirm the same flow works from both:
   - The session detail page Terminate button.
   - The dashboard BottomSheet confirm-kill path (already works; just verify no regression).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Clicking Terminate on `/sessions/[id]` and confirming routes the user to `/` (or the originating project dashboard) after success.
- [ ] The App Router error boundary is not triggered during the kill flow.
- [ ] Kill failures leave the user on the session page with a visible error indication.
- [ ] Test added to `packages/web/src/app/sessions/[id]/__tests__/` (or the component test file) covering post-kill navigation — mock `useRouter` and assert `push('/')` is called on success.
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @composio/ao-web test`, `typecheck`, and `lint` pass.

## Out of scope

- Changing where the session lands after merge / cleanup (separate flow).
- Redesigning the kill confirmation UX — keep existing BottomSheet / confirm dialog.

## References

- Kill API route: `packages/web/src/app/api/sessions/[id]/kill/route.ts`
- Dashboard kill handler: `packages/web/src/components/Dashboard.tsx` (~L337)

title: fix(web): orchestrator terminal session not visible on new dashboard UI
body:
## Summary

After the recent dashboard redesign, the orchestrator's own terminal session is no longer accessible/visible from the web UI. Users can see and attach to worker sessions, but the orchestrator session itself doesn't surface anywhere — so there is no way to watch what the orchestrator is doing or send it a message through the browser.

## Repro

1. Start an orchestrator: `ao start` (spawns `{prefix}-orchestrator` or `{prefix}-orchestrator-N`).
2. Open the dashboard.
3. Observe the session list / kanban / sidebar — worker sessions appear, orchestrator session does not.
4. Try to navigate to the orchestrator detail page. Either the direct URL works but nothing links to it, or the page itself renders without the terminal component.

## Expected

- Orchestrator sessions appear somewhere discoverable — at minimum, a dedicated entry in the `ProjectSidebar` (sidebar already has `isOrchestratorSession` filtering logic at `packages/web/src/components/ProjectSidebar.tsx:30,163`).
- Clicking the orchestrator entry opens its detail page and renders the terminal with `isOrchestrator` variant.
- The terminal is fully interactive (xterm.js + WebSocket) — same behavior as worker sessions.

## Likely cause

`ProjectSidebar.tsx` line 30 filters **out** orchestrator sessions from the main list (\`!isOrchestratorSession(...)\`). The old UI had a separate surface (header pill / orchestrator selector) that exposed them; the new UI may have dropped that surface without adding a replacement link.

Relevant files:
- `packages/web/src/components/ProjectSidebar.tsx` — filter excludes orchestrators from the worker list; need a separate section or entry for them.
- `packages/web/src/components/SessionDetail.tsx` — already supports the \`isOrchestrator\` variant (~L35, L342). Rendering path is fine; the problem is navigation to it.
- `packages/web/src/components/OrchestratorSelector.tsx` — may or may not still be wired up in the new layout; verify.
- `packages/web/src/app/sessions/[id]/page.tsx` — verify the detail page passes `isOrchestrator={true}` correctly when the session record indicates an orchestrator role.

## Proposed fix

1. In `ProjectSidebar.tsx`, add a dedicated section at the top (above the worker list) that lists the project's orchestrator session(s) with a link to `/sessions/<id>`. Keep the existing worker filter.
2. Ensure the session detail page correctly passes `isOrchestrator` when the target session's role is orchestrator — check `SessionDetail` wiring from `page.tsx`.
3. Sanity-check that the terminal (`DirectTerminal`) mounts and the WebSocket connects for orchestrator sessions same as worker sessions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Orchestrator session is visible in the sidebar (dedicated section or clearly distinguishable entry).
- [ ] Clicking the entry opens the orchestrator detail page with a live terminal.
- [ ] Terminal input/output works (can `send` commands, see output).
- [ ] Worker sessions still render correctly and are not double-listed as orchestrators.
- [ ] Dark theme preserved; no inline styles.
- [ ] Test coverage:
  - `ProjectSidebar.test.tsx` — orchestrator section renders when an orchestrator session is present and hides when absent.
  - Session detail page test — `isOrchestrator={true}` passed for orchestrator session records.
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @composio/ao-web test`, `typecheck`, `lint` pass.

## Out of scope

- Redesigning the orchestrator detail page layout.
- Changes to multi-orchestrator selection UX (see existing `OrchestratorSelector.tsx`).

## References

- `packages/web/src/components/ProjectSidebar.tsx`
- `packages/web/src/components/SessionDetail.tsx`
- `packages/web/src/components/OrchestratorSelector.tsx`
- `packages/web/src/app/sessions/[id]/page.tsx`

title: fix(web): kanban board layout breaks on non-13in displays (needs cross-size responsive pass)
body:
## Summary

The kanban board on the dashboard renders well on roughly one viewport size (looks like 13" MacBook — ~1440×900), and looks wonky on most other common displays: ultrawide, 4K, external 27" monitors, and smaller/medium laptops. It needs a proper responsive pass across the range of resolutions users actually have.

## Symptoms (not exhaustive — please enumerate while fixing)

- **Ultrawide / large monitors (≥1920px, ≥27"):** columns stretch to `max-width: 420px` and then leave large empty gutters on each side; or content sits cramped to the left with the rest of the viewport wasted. The board doesn't scale up.
- **4K / HiDPI:** same as above but worse — huge empty space around the board.
- **Medium laptops (~1280px):** columns get clipped or horizontally scroll earlier than expected; column headers wrap awkwardly; count pills overlap titles.
- **Small laptops (~1024–1180px):** horizontal scroll activates but the scroll affordance is not obvious; inner column content (SessionCard) overflows unpredictably.
- **Vertical sizing:** `.kanban-board` uses `height: calc(100vh - 280px)` — the `280px` header allowance is a magic number that breaks on short viewports (e.g. stacked browser toolbars on laptops) and wastes space on tall portrait monitors.

## Root-cause hints

From `packages/web/src/app/globals.css`:

- Line 1839–1846 — `.kanban-board { height: calc(100vh - 280px); ... }` — hardcoded header offset.
- Line 1900–1913 — `.kanban-column { flex: 1 0 260px; min-width: 260px; max-width: 420px; ... }` — fixed pixel min/max with no container-query or viewport-aware scaling.
- Line 1841 — `gap: 8px` — fixed; should likely scale with viewport.
- Breakpoints exist at ~L2112, L2139, L2507, L2515, L2522, L3095, L3099, but only seem to target mobile/tablet — nothing for wide / ultrawide / short-viewport cases.

Relevant code:
- `packages/web/src/components/Dashboard.tsx` L635–670 — board markup (`.kanban-board-wrap`, `.kanban-board`).
- `packages/web/src/app/globals.css` — all `.kanban-*` rules.
- `packages/web/src/components/SessionCard.tsx` — card sizing should also be checked at narrow column widths.

## Proposed approach

1. **Audit matrix** — test and screenshot each of these at 100% zoom, light + dark theme:
   - 1024×768, 1280×800, 1366×768, 1440×900 (current baseline), 1680×1050, 1920×1080, 2560×1440, 3440×1440 (ultrawide), 3840×2160 (4K).
   - Also short viewports: 1440×720 (laptop with docked toolbars).
   - Attach screenshots to the PR.
2. **Replace magic numbers with flexible sizing:**
   - `height: calc(100vh - var(--header-offset))` driven by a CSS variable computed from the actual header height (or use `flex: 1` on a properly-structured parent column). Do not hardcode `280px`.
   - Column width: consider CSS container queries for the column itself (scoped to the board wrap) rather than viewport media queries, so column sizing is independent of sidebar width.
   - Raise `max-width` ceiling on ultrawide so columns breathe, or add an outer `max-width` on `.kanban-board-wrap` centered in the viewport — pick whichever matches the intended UX.
3. **Explicit breakpoints to add:**
   - `@media (min-width: 1600px)` — cap board content width OR let columns widen gracefully.
   - `@media (min-width: 2000px)` — ultrawide treatment.
   - `@media (max-height: 780px)` — reduce the `--header-offset` so the board isn't a sliver.
4. **Gap scaling:** use `clamp()` for `gap` (e.g. `gap: clamp(6px, 0.6vw, 14px)`).
5. **Ensure horizontal scroll is discoverable** when columns overflow (keep the existing `overflow-x: auto` but verify a visible scrollbar shows up on macOS Safari with ephemeral scrollbars).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Audit matrix screenshots attached to the PR for all listed resolutions, in light + dark theme.
- [ ] No horizontal overflow at ≥1440px width unless there are genuinely more columns than fit.
- [ ] Columns scale sensibly on ultrawide (either widen, center the board, or both — per design decision).
- [ ] Board vertical height adapts to actual header height; no sliver rendering on short viewports.
- [ ] Column headers / count pills / captions don't overlap or wrap awkwardly on any tested resolution.
- [ ] SessionCard content renders correctly at the narrowest column width (260px) and the widest.
- [ ] Dark theme preserved.
- [ ] No inline styles added to components (per `CLAUDE.md` § Web / Styling).
- [ ] `pnpm --filter @composio/ao-web test`, `typecheck`, `lint` pass.
- [ ] If possible, add a visual-regression or snapshot test covering the board at two representative widths (laptop + ultrawide); if tooling isn't set up, skip and note it.

## Out of scope

- Redesigning the session card itself.
- Kanban column count/structure changes.
- Mobile kanban layout (already has dedicated mobile handling — leave unless bugs surface during the audit).

## References

- `packages/web/src/app/globals.css` L1839–1946 (kanban rules)
- `packages/web/src/components/Dashboard.tsx` L635–670
- `CLAUDE.md` § Web / Styling and Constraints C-01/C-02/C-05

title: fix: setup workspace hooks before launching agent to prevent trust prompt
body:
## Summary

- Moved `setupWorkspaceHooks` call before `runtime.create()` in both `spawnSession` and `spawnOrchestrator` flows
- Without this, Claude Code shows an interactive trust prompt in fresh worktrees and the agent never receives its task prompt, causing workers to idle and die

## Root Cause

Claude Code displays "Is this a project you trust?" on first launch in an untrusted directory. The spawn flow was:
1. Launch agent in tmux (triggers trust prompt)
2. Create `.claude/settings.json` via `setupWorkspaceHooks` (too late)

The agent sat at the trust prompt indefinitely, never reaching the task prompt. ~80% of spawns failed (4 out of 5 consecutive attempts).

## Fix

Reorder so `setupWorkspaceHooks` runs **before** `runtime.create()`:
1. Create `.claude/settings.json` (marks workspace as trusted)
2. Launch agent in tmux (skips trust prompt)
3. Deliver task prompt

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm build` passes
