title: Finish deprecation of Agent.detectActivity() — remove from interface and callers
body:
## Problem

`Agent.detectActivity()` has been `@deprecated` in favor of `getActivityState()` for a long time, but the migration was never finished. It's still a **required** method on the `Agent` interface and is still called from three places in core/cli, so every plugin must implement it.

**Evidence (verified on current `main`):**

- `packages/core/src/types.ts:483` — declares `detectActivity()` as a REQUIRED method on the `Agent` interface, with a `@deprecated` JSDoc note pointing to `getActivityState()`.
- Still called from:
  - `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts:604`
  - `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts:2167`
  - `packages/cli/src/commands/send.ts:58`
- Every agent plugin (`agent-claude-code`, `agent-codex`, `agent-aider`, `agent-opencode`) implements it to satisfy the interface.

`getActivityState()` is already the canonical source of truth — `CLAUDE.md` documents it as the required cascade for all agent plugins, and the dashboard/lifecycle manager/stuck-detection all depend on it. `detectActivity()` duplicates a subset of that signal (just the raw terminal-output classification) and is no longer needed at the interface level — where it *is* still useful (inside `recordActivity`/`classifyTerminalActivity`), it can remain as an internal helper on the plugin.

## Proposed change

1. Migrate the three remaining callers to use `getActivityState()` (or `checkActivityLogState()` / `classifyTerminalActivity()` directly where a raw classification is truly needed):
   - `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts:604`
   - `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts:2167`
   - `packages/cli/src/commands/send.ts:58`
2. Remove `detectActivity()` from the `Agent` interface in `packages/core/src/types.ts:483`.
3. Update agent plugins to drop the public `detectActivity` method. Plugins using the AO Activity JSONL pattern (Aider, OpenCode, Codex-as-safety-net) can keep an internal classifier function and pass it to `recordTerminalActivity()` — that's the only legitimate remaining use, and it doesn't need to be on the interface.
4. Update tests and any plugin docs in `CLAUDE.md` that still reference `detectActivity` as a required method.

This is a mechanical cleanup — no behavior change. The dashboard already consumes `getActivityState()` exclusively.

## Context

Surfaced during a codebase slop audit (April 2026), cross-validated by Claude and Codex reviews. Represents an incomplete deprecation: the method was marked `@deprecated` long ago but never actually removed, so plugin authors still have to implement it to satisfy the interface, and callers still invoke the deprecated path.

## Related issues

- #160, #17, #18, #19 — enhancement requests for richer `detectActivity()` patterns on Codex/Aider/OpenCode. These become less relevant once `detectActivity()` is removed from the public interface; the same classification logic belongs inside each plugin's `recordActivity`/internal classifier and should be driven by `getActivityState()` requirements instead.

title: refactor(core): consolidate duplicate interface declarations for PREnrichmentData and BatchObserver in types.ts
body:
## Problem

`packages/core/src/types.ts` declares two interfaces in two separate locations each, relying on TypeScript's declaration merging:

- `PREnrichmentData` — declared at line 815 **and** line 992
- `BatchObserver` — declared at line 844 **and** line 1023

These are **not pure duplicates** — the second `PREnrichmentData` declaration (around line 1015) adds a `ciChecks` field via TypeScript interface merging, so the behavior is intentional from the compiler's perspective. However, having two declaration sites for a single logical interface is a maintenance trap:

- Developers editing one site can easily miss the other.
- Field additions/removals can silently diverge in intent from the original declaration.
- Interface merging across widely-separated lines in the same file offers no real benefit (unlike cross-file augmentation).

## Proposed change

Collapse each interface into a single declaration site containing all fields:

- Merge the two `PREnrichmentData` declarations (lines 815 and 992) into one, including the `ciChecks` field.
- Merge the two `BatchObserver` declarations (lines 844 and 1023) into one.

Add a brief comment noting why the consolidated shape exists if any field ordering is load-bearing.

## Context

Surfaced during a codebase slop audit (April 2026), cross-validated by Claude and Codex reviewers. The initial audit incorrectly flagged these as pure duplicate declarations; Codex clarified that they are TypeScript interface merges (the second declarations add fields) rather than redundant copies. The fix is still worthwhile to reduce maintenance risk — a single declaration site is easier to keep coherent than two.

## Related issues

- #1341 — Architecture Analysis: Backend Complexity Hot Spots (broader backend hygiene)
- #772 — Refactor: Extract shared types package (type organization)

title: refactor(core): unify CanonicalSessionState and SessionStatus — eliminate dual state representation
body:
## Problem

`packages/core/src/types.ts` defines two parallel state enums for the same concept:

- `CanonicalSessionState` (8 states) — `packages/core/src/types.ts:29-37`
  `not_started | working | idle | needs_input | stuck | detecting | done | terminated`
- `SessionStatus` (18 states) — `packages/core/src/types.ts:117-136`
  `spawning | working | detecting | pr_open | ci_failed | review_pending | changes_requested | approved | mergeable | merged | cleanup | needs_input | stuck | errored | killed | idle | done | terminated`

The `Session` interface at `packages/core/src/types.ts:286-303` carries BOTH fields in parallel:

```ts
export interface Session {
  status: SessionStatus;                    // legacy projection
  lifecycle: CanonicalSessionLifecycle;     // canonical truth
  ...
}
```

A live bridge function, `deriveLegacyStatus()` at `packages/core/src/lifecycle-state.ts:412`, translates the canonical 8-state enum back into the 18-state legacy enum on every read. It is called extensively throughout `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts` (~2077 LOC) and `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` (~2829 LOC), and downstream by CLI/web formatters.

This is a backwards-compat shim from an incomplete migration. Consequences:

- Every state mutation must preserve two representations that can drift.
- New contributors face two vocabularies for the same concept (e.g. `terminated` vs `killed`/`cleanup`/`errored`; `working` vs `pr_open`/`ci_failed`/`review_pending`/...).
- The `deriveLegacyStatus()` bridge encodes status-selection logic (e.g. preserving `cleanup`/`errored`/`killed` when canonical says `terminated`) that is effectively a second small state machine living outside the primary lifecycle.
- Contributes heavily to `lifecycle-manager.ts` complexity flagged in #1341.

## Proposed change

Collapse to a single state model. Concretely:

1. Decide the target shape. The canonical 8-state `CanonicalSessionState` is the smaller/cleaner surface. The 10 extra `SessionStatus` values are a mix of:
   - PR/CI projections (`pr_open`, `ci_failed`, `review_pending`, `changes_requested`, `approved`, `mergeable`, `merged`) — these belong on `PRStateRecord` (already present in `CanonicalSessionLifecycle.pr`), not on session state.
   - Termination sub-reasons (`killed`, `errored`, `cleanup`) — these belong on `CanonicalSessionReason` (already present).
   - Ephemeral (`spawning`) — maps to `not_started` + a reason.
2. Migrate callers (CLI formatters, web dashboard mappers, SCM-derived columns) to read from `lifecycle.session.state` + `lifecycle.pr.state` + `lifecycle.session.reason` directly. Dashboard column mapping and CLI status strings can be derived by a single view helper instead of two enums.
3. Delete `SessionStatus`, `Session.status`, and `deriveLegacyStatus()`. Update persistence in `metadata.ts` to stop writing the derived status field.
4. Update `NON_RESTORABLE_STATUSES` and other status-keyed sets to use canonical states / reasons.

Expected win: `lifecycle-manager.ts` and `session-manager.ts` each lose a meaningful slice of conditional logic; the state machine becomes 8 states with orthogonal PR/runtime axes instead of 18 conflated states.

This is a breaking change to the core `Session` shape. It should be paired with a changeset and a brief migration note for external plugin authors (though the `Session` consumers inside plugins almost all read `session.status` only for logging, which is easily migrated to `lifecycle.session.state`).

## Context

Surfaced during codebase slop audit, April 2026, cross-validated between Claude sub-agents and Codex review.

## Related issues

- #1341 Architecture Analysis: Backend Complexity Hot Spots — catalogs the 16-state machine and the 450-line `determineStatus()` as complexity hot spots; this issue is one concrete simplification from that catalog.
- #344 (closed) Bug: session statuses mix lifecycle, activity, and merge readiness — closed without merging a fix; documented the same overloading of `SessionStatus` with PR/merge concerns that this refactor removes at the root.
- #855 Proposal: Replace split-brain architecture with durable JSONL append-only event log — different concern (persistence), but complementary: collapsing to a single state model makes an event log schema much cleaner.

title: chore(cli): remove deprecated 'ao init' command
body:
## Problem

`packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts` registers a deprecated `ao init` command that:

- Prints a deprecation warning directing users to `ao start`
- Calls `createConfigOnly()` from `./start.js` (it does *not* delegate to the full `ao start` flow)

Meanwhile, `ao start` already handles auto-config creation on first run in an unconfigured repo, making `ao init` redundant. The command adds to the visible CLI command surface (shows up in `ao --help`), confuses new users with a deprecation warning, and keeps a dead code path alive.

## Proposed change

Remove the `init` command entirely:

1. Delete `packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts`.
2. Remove the `registerInit(program)` call from the CLI entrypoint.
3. If `createConfigOnly()` is still considered valuable as a standalone action (config generation without launching the full orchestrator), expose it via `ao start --init-only` instead of keeping a separate top-level command. Otherwise, inline it or drop it if only `ao init` used it.
4. Add a changeset noting the removal. Users on the deprecation warning path have already been told to use `ao start`.

## Context

Surfaced during codebase slop audit, April 2026. Cross-validated by Claude and Codex. Codex correction on the original finding: the `init` shim does not delegate to the full `ao start` flow — it only calls `createConfigOnly()` — but the behavior is still replaceable by `ao start` (or an `--init-only` flag).

Evidence:

- `packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts:4` — the entire command body is a deprecation notice + `createConfigOnly()` call.
- Description already reads `[deprecated] Use 'ao start' instead — it auto-creates config on first run`.

## Related issues

- #984 (closed) — `ao start: add interactive init prompt for humans, print ao init for agents`. Context around how `ao start` should behave on a missing config; this proposal is the follow-through that retires the separate `init` entry point.
- #985 (closed) — `ao init: too many prompts — auto-detect defaults and skip confirmation`. Argued for making `ao init` painless; removing it outright is the stronger version of that fix now that `ao start` handles first-run setup.
- #236 (closed) — `fix(cli): ao init missing sessionPrefix, name, and port validation`. Historical validation bug in the same command, further evidence the surface has been drifting.

title: Extract duplicated hasRecentCommits() helper into @aoagents/ao-core
body:
## Problem

Two agent plugins have byte-identical copies of a `hasRecentCommits(workspacePath)` helper that shells out to `git log --since=60 seconds ago` to check whether the agent has produced new commits in the last ~60s. This is straight copy-paste — the implementations differ only in their surrounding comments.

**Locations:**
- `packages/plugins/agent-aider/src/index.ts` lines 38–49
- `packages/plugins/agent-cursor/src/index.ts` lines 39–50

Both use the same `execFileAsync` call, same args (`["log", "--since=60 seconds ago", "--format=%H"]`), same 5s timeout, same swallow-error-return-false semantics.

As more agent plugins adopt git-commit-based activity detection (a natural signal for agents without native JSONL), this duplication will keep growing.

## Proposed change

Extract to `@aoagents/ao-core` as a shared utility so any agent plugin can import it:

```ts
// packages/core/src/git-activity.ts
export async function hasRecentCommits(
  workspacePath: string,
  windowSeconds = 60,
): Promise<boolean>;
```

- Add re-export from `packages/core/src/index.ts`
- Update `agent-aider` and `agent-cursor` to import from core and delete their local helpers
- Keep the signature generic (parameterize the window) so future agents aren't locked into 60s

This matches the pattern already established for other shared agent-plugin helpers (`recordTerminalActivity`, `classifyTerminalActivity`, `getActivityFallbackState`, `normalizeAgentPermissionMode`, etc.) exported from core.

## Context

Surfaced during codebase slop audit April 2026, cross-validated Claude + Codex. A small, low-risk cleanup — no behavior change, just deduplication and a clearer extension point for future agent plugins that need git-commit-based activity signals.

## Related issues

- #783 — Extract shared `isProcessRunning` + `normalizePermissionMode` into core (same pattern: agent-plugin helpers duplicated across plugins should live in core)
- #9 — Cross-cutting convention audit, explicitly calls out duplicated code across agent plugins as a problem to fix

title: Consolidate recordActivity() thin-wrapper duplication across agent plugins
body:
## Problem

Three agent plugins implement `recordActivity()` as an identical 5-line thin wrapper around the core helper `recordTerminalActivity()`. The method is a required interface member, so every new agent plugin that uses the AO Activity JSONL pattern has to copy-paste this same snippet.

**Evidence (verified on current `main`):**

- `packages/plugins/agent-aider/src/index.ts:220-225`
- `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts:624-630`
- `packages/plugins/agent-cursor/src/index.ts:317-322`

All three are the same delegation:

```ts
async recordActivity(session: Session, terminalOutput: string): Promise<void> {
  if (!session.workspacePath) return;
  await recordTerminalActivity(session.workspacePath, terminalOutput, (output) =>
    this.detectActivity(output),
  );
}
```

`recordTerminalActivity` is already exported from core (listed under "Core Utilities Available to Plugins" in `CLAUDE.md`) and already does the classify + dedup + append work. The per-plugin wrapper contributes nothing beyond forwarding `this.detectActivity` as the classifier and null-checking `workspacePath`.

This is systematic duplication: the plugin-authoring guide in `CLAUDE.md` even documents the 5-line body as the canonical way to implement `recordActivity`, which is a strong signal that it belongs in core, not in every plugin.

## Proposed change

Two reasonable options — either is fine, (b) is smaller and preferred:

**(a) Core helper plugins alias**

Export a ready-made `recordActivityViaTerminal(classifier)` factory from core that returns the standard `recordActivity` implementation. Plugins become:

```ts
recordActivity: recordActivityViaTerminal((output) => detectActivity(output)),
```

**(b) Make `recordActivity` optional with a sensible default**

Change the `Agent` interface in `packages/core/src/types.ts` to make `recordActivity` optional. Lifecycle manager's caller already needs a null check for plugins using native JSONL (Claude Code) — extend that path so that when `recordActivity` is absent but `detectActivity` is present, core calls `recordTerminalActivity(workspacePath, output, agent.detectActivity)` itself. Plugins that need custom behavior still override.

Either way, delete the three duplicate wrappers in `agent-aider`, `agent-codex`, and `agent-cursor`, and update `CLAUDE.md`'s "For agents using AO Activity JSONL" section to point at the new helper/default instead of prescribing the copy-paste snippet.

No behavior change — the wrappers are pure forwards today.

## Context

Surfaced during a codebase slop audit (April 2026), cross-validated by Claude and Codex reviews. This is a small, mechanical consolidation but it pays off every time a new agent plugin is added (see the open requests for Amp #1016, Droid #1017, Pi #1059, Cline #171, kimicode #1384) — each one currently has to copy this snippet.

## Related issues

- #1412 — Finish deprecation of `Agent.detectActivity()`. These two are adjacent cleanups: #1412 removes the deprecated classifier from the public interface; this issue removes the other redundant boilerplate around the same classification path. Worth coordinating so `recordActivity` and `detectActivity` get cleaned up together rather than churning plugins twice.
- #1016, #1017, #1059, #171, #1384 — open agent-plugin requests that will benefit from less boilerplate when implemented.

title: refactor(web): reconcile duplicate SessionDetailPRCard implementations
body:
## Problem

There are two parallel implementations of `SessionDetailPRCard` in the web package, both rendering the same PR-card UI with the same comment-action state machine (sendingComments / sentComments / errorComments, Ask-Agent-to-Fix flow, branch copy, CI chips, etc.):

1. **Standalone file** — `packages/web/src/components/SessionDetailPRCard.tsx` (349 lines)
   - Exported `SessionDetailPRCard` at line 88
   - Richer API: accepts `lifecyclePrReason`, injected `onAskAgentToFix` handler, `BlockerChip` helper, `cleanBugbotComment` util
   - Appears to be the canonical / newer extraction

2. **Inline component** — `packages/web/src/components/SessionDetail.tsx:732`
   - Local `function SessionDetailPRCard({ pr, sessionId, metadata })` (~230 lines)
   - Used by `SessionDetail.tsx:602`: `<SessionDetailPRCard pr={pr} sessionId={session.id} metadata={session.metadata} />`
   - Simpler signature, inlines its own fix-comment handler

The standalone file is **exported but never imported** — a grep for `SessionDetailPRCard` shows no importers of the standalone module. Meanwhile `SessionDetail.tsx` shadows the name with a local definition and uses that instead.

This looks like a dead extraction or orphaned refactor. Any future change to PR card behavior must be made twice, or one copy will silently drift from the other.

## Proposed change

1. Confirm which implementation is canonical (the standalone file looks newer / more featureful — `lifecyclePrReason`, injected handler).
2. Update `SessionDetail.tsx` to `import { SessionDetailPRCard } from \"./SessionDetailPRCard\"` and pass through the required props (including `onAskAgentToFix`).
3. Delete the inline `function SessionDetailPRCard` at `SessionDetail.tsx:732` and the surrounding section comment.
4. Verify no behavior regression (comment send flow, CI chip rendering, branch copy, blocker chips).

This also drops ~230 lines from `SessionDetail.tsx`, which helps #770.

## Context

Surfaced during codebase slop audit (April 2026). The initial audit missed this — it was caught during Codex cross-validation of the audit findings. The duplication is not obvious from a single-file read because the import site uses an unqualified name that resolves to the local function.

## Related issues

- #770 — Refactor: Break down SessionDetail.tsx (728 lines). Removing the duplicate inline card meaningfully advances that refactor.
- #1287 — Add \"Resolve Conflicts\" action button to SessionDetail PR card. Depends on having a single canonical PR-card implementation to extend.

chore(lint): enforce C-04 (400-line component limit) mechanically via ESLint max-lines
body:
## Problem

`CLAUDE.md` declares constraint **C-04: Component files max 400 lines**, but nothing in the repo mechanically enforces it. Today the rule lives only in the contributor doc, so it is routinely violated — and the violations keep growing instead of shrinking.

Current offenders (well over the 400-line cap):

| File | Lines | Has split issue |
|------|-------|-----------------|
| `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` | 2829 | #1415 |
| `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts` | 2077 | #1417 |
| `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts` | 1827 | #1416 |
| `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/index.ts` + `graphql-batch.ts` | ~1065 + ~1025 | #1418 |
| `packages/web/src/components/SessionDetail.tsx` | 1089 | #770 |
| `packages/web/src/components/DirectTerminal.tsx` | 951 | #769 |
| `packages/web/src/app/globals.css` | 3363 | #771 |

Without mechanical enforcement, every new PR can add a 500-line file and no reviewer notices until it becomes another god-file. C-04 is a toothless guideline.

## Proposed change

Add a `max-lines` rule to the root `eslint.config.js` flat config:

```js
{
  rules: {
    \"max-lines\": [\"error\", { max: 400, skipBlankLines: true, skipComments: true }],
  },
}
```

Apply it broadly (core, cli, web, plugins). Use file-level overrides for the existing known offenders so CI stays green while the split issues proceed:

```js
{
  files: [
    \"packages/core/src/session-manager.ts\",
    \"packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts\",
    \"packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts\",
    \"packages/plugins/scm-github/src/index.ts\",
    \"packages/plugins/scm-github/src/graphql-batch.ts\",
    \"packages/web/src/components/SessionDetail.tsx\",
    \"packages/web/src/components/DirectTerminal.tsx\",
  ],
  rules: { \"max-lines\": \"off\" },
}
```

Or, equivalently, an inline `// eslint-disable-next-line max-lines` / `/* eslint-disable max-lines */` at the top of each offender. The override list *is* the migration TODO list — removing an entry from the array should become part of the acceptance criteria for each split PR.

Relax the cap for test files (`**/__tests__/**`, `**/*.test.ts{,x}`) — test files legitimately grow large due to fixtures and aren't read the same way as production code. A value like `800` or `\"off\"` is appropriate there.

Benefits:
- (a) Stops new god files from landing — any PR that pushes a file past 400 lines now fails CI, forcing the author to either split or add an explicit override (which a reviewer must approve).
- (b) The override list is a visible, auditable migration ratchet. Every entry corresponds to an open split issue; removing entries is the definition of done.
- (c) Gives C-04 the same teeth as the other ESLint rules (`no-explicit-any`, `consistent-type-imports`) already have.

## Context

Surfaced during a codebase slop audit in April 2026, cross-validated by Claude and Codex reviews. Same audit produced #1415, #1416, #1417, #1418 (file splits) — this issue is the policy sibling that prevents the problem from recurring after those splits land.

## Related issues

- #1415 — refactor(core): split session-manager.ts (2829 lines) into focused modules
- #1417 — refactor(core): split lifecycle-manager.ts (2077 lines) into focused modules
- #1416 — refactor(cli): split 1827-line start.ts into focused subcommands/helpers
- #1418 — refactor(scm-github): split oversized index.ts and graphql-batch.ts into per-resolver modules
- #770 — Refactor: Break down SessionDetail.tsx
- #769 — Refactor: Break down DirectTerminal.tsx
- #771 — Refactor: Split globals.css (3,363 lines) into modular stylesheets
- #1341 — Architecture Analysis: Backend Complexity Hot Spots (background motivation)

title: chore(ci): add unused-exports / dead-code detection (knip) to catch stranded code pre-merge
body:
## Problem

We have no mechanical check for unused exports or stranded dead code. Fully built but unwired modules can (and do) ship to `main` without anyone noticing.

Concrete example: `registerProject_cmd` in `packages/cli/src/commands/project.ts:31` — a 183-line command surface (`ls`/`add`/`rm`/`relink`/`set-default`) shipped to `main` but was never wired into `createProgram()` in `packages/cli/src/program.ts`. No call sites outside its own tests. Nothing in our CI caught it. See #1419.

A mechanical unused-export detector would have flagged this at PR time. Without one, \"built, unwired, undocumented\" code accumulates quietly and raises the maintenance cost of the repo.

## Proposed change

Add [`knip`](https://knip.dev/) to the repo and run it in CI.

Why `knip` over `ts-prune`:

- Monorepo-aware out of the box (understands pnpm workspaces and `workspace:*`).
- Detects unused files, exports, dependencies, and binaries — broader surface than `ts-prune`'s export-only view.
- Actively maintained; first-class Next.js and Vitest plugins (we use both).
- Config-driven entry points — we can mark plugin entry files, Next.js routes, and `packages/core/src/index.ts` as entries and suppress their exports being flagged.

Rollout plan:

1. Add `knip` as a root devDependency, commit a `knip.json` with explicit entry points:
   - `packages/core/src/index.ts` (public API — all exports are entries)
   - `packages/*/plugins/*/src/index.ts` (plugin default exports)
   - `packages/web` — use the Next.js plugin (App Router routes, API routes, layouts, `globals.css`)
   - `packages/cli/src/index.ts` and the `ao` bin
   - Vitest test globs
2. Add a `pnpm knip` script and a CI job (advisory-only on first run).
3. Triage the initial report — expect false positives from public APIs, plugin entries, and Next.js conventions. Tune config, not code.
4. Flip CI job to required once the report is clean.

`ts-prune` is the lighter alternative if `knip` proves too noisy to tame, but given the workspace layout `knip` is the better starting bet.

## Context

Surfaced during a codebase slop audit in April 2026, cross-validated by Claude and Codex. The `registerProject_cmd` finding is the motivating data point — a tool like `knip` would have reported an unused export at `packages/cli/src/commands/project.ts:31` and the stranded command would never have reached `main`.

## Related issues

- #1419 — chore(cli): decide fate of `ao project` subcommand — built but unwired. Direct motivating example: knip would have flagged this before merge.
- #1420 — chore(cli): remove deprecated `ao init` command (adjacent dead-code cleanup).
- #1421 — chore: remove orphan root-level files and stale `.gitignore` entries (adjacent dead-code cleanup).

title: Enforce deprecation decay — require `@deprecated` to include a cutoff version or removal date
body:
## Problem

Code marked `@deprecated` lingers indefinitely in this codebase because nothing tracks *when* it should actually be removed. The JSDoc tag is treated as documentation rather than a commitment, so deprecated surface area accumulates: plugin authors keep implementing deprecated methods to satisfy interfaces, callers keep invoking deprecated paths, and the cleanup only happens when someone notices during an audit.

**Evidence (verified on current `main`):**

- `packages/core/src/types.ts:483` — `Agent.detectActivity()` is `@deprecated` in favor of `getActivityState()`, but is still a **required** method on the interface and still called from 3 places (`lifecycle-manager.ts:604`, `session-manager.ts:2167`, `cli/src/commands/send.ts:58`). Every agent plugin must implement it. No cutoff version or removal date was recorded when it was deprecated, so it has drifted.
- `packages/core/src/types.ts:1558-1581` — `LegacyAgentPermissionMode` retains a deprecated `"skip"` alias for `"permissionless"`. JSDoc says "deprecated" but gives no version, no removal date, and no issue link. There is no signal to anyone reading the code when (or whether) this alias will actually go away.

These are just two examples surfaced in a single audit pass. The pattern is systemic: `@deprecated` without a decay marker is effectively permanent.

## Proposed change

Adopt a deprecation policy and enforce it with a lightweight CI check.

**Policy:** every `@deprecated` JSDoc tag must include a removal commitment. Pick one of two forms:

- `@deprecated v2.0 — use getActivityState()` (version cutoff)
- `@deprecated removeBy=2026-Q3 — use getActivityState()` (date cutoff)

Optionally include a `(#1412)` tracking-issue reference pointing at the removal ticket.

**Enforcement:** a simple grep-based CI check is sufficient to start — no custom ESLint rule needed. Something like:

```bash
# Fails if any @deprecated line lacks a version (v*) or removeBy= marker.
rg -n '@deprecated\b' packages --type ts \
  | rg -v '@deprecated\s+(v\d|removeBy=)' \
  && { echo 'Found @deprecated without cutoff'; exit 1; } \
  || exit 0
```

Wire it into the existing lint GitHub Actions workflow. If the grep approach proves noisy, upgrade to a custom ESLint rule later — but the grep is a one-line policy that catches new offenders immediately.

**Migration:** one-time sweep to annotate or remove the existing `@deprecated` tags (there are only a handful). For `detectActivity()`, annotating with a version points directly at #1412 as the removal vehicle.

## Context

Surfaced during the codebase slop audit in April 2026, cross-validated by Claude and Codex reviews. The policy is cheap to introduce, aligns with the \"Surgical Changes\" and \"Simplicity First\" principles in `CLAUDE.md`, and makes deprecation a commitment rather than a suggestion.

## Related issues

- #1412 — *Finish deprecation of `Agent.detectActivity()`* — the canonical concrete example. A decay marker on the original `@deprecated` tag would have tracked this to completion automatically.
- #1420 — *remove deprecated `ao init` command* — same pattern at the CLI layer: a command kept behind a deprecation warning with no removal milestone.

title: ci: detect unused CSS custom properties in globals.css (warn-only)
body:
## Problem

`packages/web/src/app/globals.css` defines a large number of `--color-*` design tokens (and other custom properties). Over time, tokens drift from actual usage:

- Likely-dead status tokens surfaced during audit: `--color-status-respond`, `--color-status-review`, `--color-status-pending`
- Various `--color-accent-*` entries, some of which duplicate the same hex value under different names
- Backwards-compat aliases such as `--color-bg-primary`, `--color-border-muted` that may no longer have callers

There is no automated signal when a token becomes unreferenced, so dead tokens accumulate silently and `globals.css` grows (see #771 for the broader size problem). `DESIGN.md` is the stated source of truth for the design system, but the CSS tokens drift from the doc over time with no enforcement.

## Proposed change

Add a small CI check (grep/node script, no new deps) that:

1. Parses `--color-*` (and optionally all `--*`) definitions from `packages/web/src/app/globals.css`.
2. Greps `packages/web/**/*.{tsx,ts,css}` (and any other consumers) for usages: `var(--color-foo)` and direct `--color-foo` references.
3. Reports any defined tokens with zero references.
4. Optionally flags multiple token names that resolve to the same hex value as potential duplicates.

Ship as **warn-only** initially (non-failing CI step, or a `pnpm run lint:css-tokens` job that posts a comment / logs a summary) so legitimately-reserved tokens don't block merges. Once the baseline is clean, flip to failing.

Nice-to-haves (not required for v1):
- Cross-reference against `DESIGN.md` so tokens documented there are always considered \"used\".
- Output a grouped report (dead / duplicate-hex / undocumented) to make cleanup PRs easy to scope.

## Context

Surfaced during a codebase slop audit in April 2026, cross-validated between Claude and Codex. The audit flagged the tokens listed above as strong candidates for removal, but manual cleanup is brittle without a check that keeps the list honest going forward. This is a low-risk, high-signal CI addition.

## Related issues

- #771 — Refactor: Split globals.css (3,363 lines) into modular stylesheets. Complementary: de-duping before splitting reduces churn in the refactor.

title: test(plugins): enforce non-trivial interface implementations across all plugins
body:
## Problem

Current plugin tests verify *structural* conformance (`create()` returns an object whose methods match the interface shape) but not *behavioral* conformance. A plugin can pass CI while being an effectively empty stub.

Motivating example: `packages/plugins/terminal-web/src/index.ts` is a 52-line file shipped in a \"done\" state. Its `attach()` implementation only `console.log`s the web terminal URL — the plugin is never actually plumbed through the web runtime, yet all existing tests pass because the method exists and returns the correct shape. This was only discovered during a manual slop audit.

The same failure mode can (and likely does) exist in other plugin slots. There is no guard-rail that catches a method body consisting of `return null`, `return \"\"`, `return true`, or a single `console.log` when the interface expects real work.

## Proposed change

Pick one (or combine) of the following:

1. **Runtime behavioral test harness** — a single test file in `packages/integration-tests` that loads every plugin from the registry, calls `create()`, and runs each required method against canned fixtures. Assertions target observable behavior (e.g. runtime `spawn` must actually start a process / return a usable handle; tracker `getIssue` must hit a mocked API and parse the response; terminal `attach` must return a non-stub attachment descriptor).
2. **AST stub-detector** — lint rule or standalone script that scans `packages/plugins/*/src/**/*.ts` and flags methods required by the plugin's declared slot whose body is exclusively `console.log(...)`, `return null`, `return \"\"`, `return true`, `return undefined`, or empty. Gate CI on zero violations (with an explicit allowlist for methods documented as optional no-ops).
3. **Required-methods coverage table** — for each of the 8 plugin slots, enumerate in `CLAUDE.md` (or a dedicated `docs/plugin-contract.md`) the methods that MUST do real work vs. the methods that may legitimately be no-ops. Enforce via (1) or (2) above so the table doesn't rot.

Option 2 is cheapest, option 1 is strongest; a hybrid (AST gate in CI, behavioral test for the critical runtime/agent/scm/tracker slots) would give the best ratio.

## Context

Surfaced during the codebase slop audit in April 2026, cross-validated by both Claude and Codex reviewers. The `terminal-web` finding is a concrete instance of a class of bug — plugins passing shape checks without delivering behavior — that the current test suite cannot detect.

## Related issues

- #1422 — Decide fate of the Terminal plugin slot — semi-vestigial with no non-test consumers (same audit; `terminal-web` is the motivating example here)
- #10 — Add comprehensive test coverage across all packages (this issue is a specific sub-problem: shape vs. behavior)
- #1135 — Dashboard does not load third-party agent plugins — activity/summary always null (another \"plugin loads but does nothing\" failure mode)

title: ci(web): detect unused CSS custom properties in globals.css (warn-only)
body:
## Summary
- Adds `packages/web/scripts/check-css-tokens.mjs`, a dependency-free Node audit that parses `--color-*` token definitions out of `packages/web/src/app/globals.css` and reports dead tokens (zero references across `packages/web/src/**` and `DESIGN.md`) plus multi-token groups that resolve to the same literal value (likely duplicates).
- Exposes it as `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web lint:css-tokens`.
- Wires a new `css-tokens` CI job with `continue-on-error: true` so the audit is warn-only until the baseline is cleaned up.

## Flags
- `--all` — audit every `--*` token, not just `--color-*` (the issue explicitly calls this out as optional).
- `--strict` — exit non-zero on findings, for flipping to failing once the baseline is clean.

## Notable behaviour
- Groups duplicate-value detection by scope (`:root` vs `.dark`) so light/dark redefinitions of the same token don't appear as false positives.
- Skips `var(--…)` aliases and no-ops (`transparent`, `inherit`, `none`) when hunting for duplicate values.
- Self-definition lines in `globals.css` don't count as references, but cross-token references inside `globals.css` (e.g. `--color-bg-primary: var(--color-bg-base)`) do — so backward-compat aliases that reference another token stay "used" on the alias target side but the alias itself is flagged dead if nobody else reads it.

## Initial findings (reproducible via `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web lint:css-tokens`)
- 7 dead `--color-*` tokens: `--color-accent-purple`, `--color-accent-violet`, `--color-alert-ci-unknown`, `--color-border-emphasis`, `--color-border-muted`, `--color-column-header`, `--color-tint-violet`.
- 23 duplicate-value groups pointing at likely consolidation candidates (e.g. `--color-accent-green` / `--color-ci-pass` / `--color-status-merge` / `--color-status-working` all resolve to the same green).

These are intentionally surfaced but not enforced yet, per the issue.

## Test plan

- [x] `node packages/web/scripts/check-css-tokens.mjs --strict` — exits 1 while findings exist.

title: refactor(web): break down DirectTerminal.tsx (#769)
body:
## Summary

Closes #769.

`DirectTerminal.tsx` had grown to **951 lines** — 2.4× over C-04's 400-line limit — with theme data, font helpers, the xterm setup effect, the fullscreen resize effect, clipboard handlers, and the chrome UI all in one file. The April 2026 audit comment on the issue confirmed the UI revamp has landed and the structural split is still wanted.

## Extractions

Everything moved under `packages/web/src/components/terminal/`:

| File | Lines | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `DirectTerminal.tsx` (rewritten) | 130 | Composition only |
| `terminal-themes.ts` | 67 | Dark/light `ITheme` builder |
| `terminal-font.ts` | 51 | Font size constants, `getStoredFontSize`, `resolveMonoFontFamily` |
| `terminal-clipboard.ts` | 58 | XDA (CSI > q) handler, OSC 52 decoder, Cmd+C keybinding |
| `useXtermTerminal.ts` | 375 | xterm instance + mux wiring + selection preservation + touch scroll + reconnect/theme/font-size effects |
| `useFullscreenResize.ts` | 100 | RAF-polling fullscreen resize effect |
| `TerminalControls.tsx` | 257 | Chromed bar + chromeless floating controls + OpenCode reload |

`buildTerminalThemes` and `resolveMonoFontFamily` are re-exported from `DirectTerminal.tsx` so the existing `DirectTerminal.test.ts` imports continue to work unchanged.

## Scope note

The ~280-line xterm setup effect inside `useXtermTerminal` is kept as a single effect. Its selection-buffering state (`writeBuffer`, `selectionActive`, `programmaticScroll`) crosses the WebSocket, ResizeObserver, and viewport-scroll concerns, and cleanup order matters. title: fix(web): prevent kanban card blink on attention-level column changes
body:
Fixes #1446

## Summary

The `kanban-card-enter` entrance animation (`opacity: 0 → 1`, `translateY: 8px → 0`) was unconditionally applied to every `SessionCard`. When a card's attention level oscillated between kanban zones on consecutive SSE updates, React unmounted the card from one column and remounted it in another, re-triggering the animation and causing a visible blink.

Added a module-level `Set<string>` (`enteredSessionIds`) that tracks which session IDs have already played their entrance animation. - Added `enteredSessionIds` Set at module scope
- Added `hasEntered` state derived from the Set
- Conditionally apply `kanban-card-enter` only when `!hasEntered`

2. Verify the card does NOT blink when it moves between columns on SSE updates

title: refactor(core,plugins): consolidate recordActivity duplication via factory
body:
Closes #1424.

## Summary
- Add `recordActivityViaTerminal(classifier)` to `@aoagents/ao-core` — factory that returns the standard `recordActivity` implementation (null-check `workspacePath`, delegate to `recordTerminalActivity`).
- Replace the identical 5-line `recordActivity` wrapper in `agent-aider`, `agent-codex`, `agent-cursor`, and `agent-opencode` with a 1-line factory call.

## Why option (a), not option (b)
Issue #1424 proposed two options, with (b) (lifecycle-manager default) preferred. I went with (a) (factory) after discovering (b) changes behavior for agents that don't use AO activity JSONL:

- Claude Code uses its own native JSONL (`~/.claude/projects/`) and doesn't override `recordActivity`. Under (b), the lifecycle manager would start calling `recordTerminalActivity` for Claude Code every poll cycle, producing orphan `.ao/activity.jsonl` writes nothing reads.

Option (a) keeps opt-in semantics, leaves the lifecycle manager untouched, and is truly no behavior change for any existing agent. See https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1424#issuecomment-4291773453.

title: bug(spawn): batch-spawn and `ao spawn` succeed when no daemon is polling the project — silent observability blackout
body:
## Summary

`ao spawn` and `ao batch-spawn` currently succeed even when the running `ao` daemon is not polling the target project. They print a stderr warning and then proceed to create full worktrees, tmux panes, and session metadata — but none of the lifecycle-driven behavior that a session needs to be useful (CI-failure routing, review-comment routing, revive transitions, event log, state advance) is actually wired up for that project.

The result is a silent observability blackout: the dashboard looks normal, sessions appear to run, and there is no visible indication that lifecycle reactions are dead. This is a footgun.

## Evidence

Warning emitted during a real batch-spawn of 23 sessions (from `packages/cli/src/commands/spawn.ts:78`):

```
⚠ The running AO instance (pid 66487) is not polling project \"agent-orchestrator\".
  Run `ao start agent-orchestrator` so the new session is tracked.
```

The spawn proceeded anyway and 23 sessions were created with full worktrees and tmux panes.

### Downstream effects observed

- No `~/.agent-orchestrator/15c372b67170-events.jsonl` is being written for this project (the project-scoped event log never gets created because nothing is polling).
- Lifecycle polling doesn't run — session metadata isn't being advanced by the daemon.
- The only reason PR URLs appear in metadata at all is that `next-server` (pid 66865) is separately polling `gh` via the dashboard web routes. That's partial, not a substitute for the lifecycle manager.
- Stale `terminated` states in metadata never get recovered because there is no revive poll.
- CI-failure routing, review-comment routing, and other lifecycle reactions are silently dead for every session in this batch.

A stderr warning is not sufficient. The user-visible dashboard looks normal; sessions appear to run; nothing in the UI hints that these sessions are un-orchestrated.

## Source

The warning is printed unconditionally without any enforcement, here:

`packages/cli/src/commands/spawn.ts:73-81`

```ts
if (!running.projects.includes(projectId)) {
  console.log(
    chalk.yellow(
      `⚠ The running AO instance (pid ${running.pid}) is not polling project \"${projectId}\". Run \`ao start ${projectId}\` so the new session is tracked.`,
    ),
  );
}
```

The check exists, it just doesn't gate anything.

## Proposed options (for maintainers to decide)

From most to least aggressive:

1. **Refuse to spawn** when the daemon isn't polling this project, with a clear actionable error (`Run \`ao start <project>\` first`). Simplest and probably correct — if the session can't be operated, it shouldn't be created. Matches the anti-over-engineering philosophy of this codebase.
2. **Auto-start project polling** inside the existing `ao` daemon when a spawn happens. Slight complexity (the daemon needs to pick up a new project at runtime), but removes the footgun entirely.
3. **Keep the warning** but also flag every session spawned in this state as \"unpolled\" in the dashboard so the blackout is visible. Least invasive but adds UI surface and still lets bad state exist.

My recommendation: **option 1**. If you can't operate the session, don't create it.

## Related work

- **PR #1308** (merged, commit `e45f34e1`) — \"fix: restore dead orchestrators on ao start\". Fixes a sibling daemon-reuse problem: `ao start` would spawn a duplicate orchestrator instead of reusing a dead-but-restorable one. Related theme (daemon/orchestrator lifecycle footguns around `ao start`) but does not cover the spawn-vs-polling mismatch.
- **Issue #1306** — original `ao start` intermittent-replacement report that led to #1308. Related class of problem.
- **Issue #1102** — `ao start` opens stale orchestrator session instead of picker page. Same area.
- **Issue #1279** — `ao start` in folder A shows dashboard of AO running on project B. Also daemon/project-association adjacent.
- **Issue #1188** — upgraded CLI silently attaches to stale daemon, no version-mismatch detection. Same failure mode class: spawn/start proceeds silently when daemon state is wrong.
- **Issue #1073** — lifecycle worker kills sessions with no audit trail. Tangentially related lifecycle-observability gap.

None of the above cover this exact bug: spawn succeeding while the daemon is not polling the project.

## Acceptance criteria

- Running `ao spawn <project> <issue>` or `ao batch-spawn <project> ...` when the daemon exists but does not include `<project>` in its polling set either:
  - fails fast with a clear error telling the user to run `ao start <project>` (option 1), OR
  - causes the daemon to start polling the project before any session is created (option 2), OR
  - creates the sessions but surfaces an unmistakable \"unpolled\" indicator in the dashboard for each affected session (option 3).
- No session is ever created in a state where the lifecycle manager will silently not run for it.

title: fix(core): refuse ao send when runtimeHandle is missing
body:
## Summary

- Fixes #1456 — `ao send` could spawn a zombie tmux session running a second Claude on the same worktree when a session's metadata was missing its `runtimeHandle`.
- `prepareSession` in `session-manager.ts` used to synthesize a handle from the bare `sessionId`. But real tmux sessions are named `{projectHash}-{sessionId}`, so `restore()` would create a brand-new tmux session under the wrong unprefixed name — alongside the real one.
- Refuse to operate when the persisted runtime handle is missing and throw a descriptive error instead.

## Details

The fabrication check has to read the **raw persisted metadata** (`session.metadata["runtimeHandle"]`) rather than the enriched `session.runtimeHandle`, because `get()` → `ensureHandleAndEnrich` also fabricates a handle from the sessionId for liveness-check/display purposes. Using the enriched handle in `send`/`restore` is what corrupts state.

The error message points users at `ao session ls` to inspect or `ao session restore` to recover explicitly, rather than silently doing the wrong thing.

## Test plan

- [x] Updated existing regression test `refuses to send when runtimeHandle is missing…` in `packages/core/src/__tests__/session-manager/communication.test.ts` — asserts `send()` rejects with a `missing its runtime handle` error and never calls `runtime.sendMessage` or `runtime.create`.

title: fix(core): preserve runtimeHandle and tmuxName across lifecycle writes
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1458 — a data-loss bug where `buildLifecycleMetadataPatch` (`lifecycle-state.ts`) and `buildTransitionMetadataPatch` (`lifecycle-transition.ts`) emitted empty-string values for `runtimeHandle` / `tmuxName` when the in-memory lifecycle had them null. `applyMetadataUpdates` treats empty strings as **deletions**, so a transient `terminated + runtime_lost` transition (from a probe disagreement — see #1063, #989) permanently wiped the session's routing address from disk while the tmux session was still alive.

- `ao send <id>` could no longer route (no handle)
- Dashboard terminal attach could not open (no tmux name)
- Even if the runtime came back alive on the next probe, AO had nothing to re-attach to

## The fix

Stop emitting the keys when the in-memory handle is null. Omitting the key in the patch leaves the existing disk value alone (`applyMetadataUpdates` skips `undefined`). Only explicit cleanup (archive) should ever delete the flat keys — and it already uses a different path.

No new handle-preservation subsystem, recovery layer, or rehydration logic. Just: if the handle is valuable metadata, stop destroying it.

## Changes

- `packages/core/src/lifecycle-state.ts` — `buildLifecycleMetadataPatch` emits `runtimeHandle`/`tmuxName` only when non-null
- `packages/core/src/lifecycle-transition.ts` — `buildTransitionMetadataPatch` same
- Tests updated to reflect the new contract
- New regression test: seeds a session with a valid handle, forces a `terminated + runtime_lost` decision, asserts the flat keys still exist on disk afterward and `readCanonicalLifecycle` rehydrates the original handle

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` — all 811 tests pass
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core typecheck` — clean
- [x] `pnpm lint` — no new warnings

## Related

- #1063, #989 — upstream triggers (transient mis-labeling) this bug makes permanent
- #1187 — zombie sessions from the opposite direction
- #1245 — sessions stuck in `working` with no recovery path
- #1454 — flicker issue; fixing this bug removes much of the visible damage
- #1456 — sibling to this one

Closes #1458

title: fix(core): stop single-shot dead probe from latching session to terminated
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1454. A single transient probe miss used to walk a session straight to `session.state=terminated` with `reason=runtime_lost`. There was no inverse transition — once terminated, subsequent probes showing the runtime alive and active activity could not flip the session back. The dashboard then flickered `idle → killed → ready` as different surfaces read different fields.

Two single-shot terminal latches removed:

- **`lifecycle-status-decisions.ts:resolveProbeDecision`**: `runtime=dead && process=dead && !recentActivity` now routes through `detecting`/`runtime_lost` instead of `killed`/`terminated`. The standard `detecting → stuck` escalation already handles persistence; `stuck` is recoverable, `terminated` was not.
- **`session-manager.ts:enrichSessionWithRuntimeState`**: a single `isAlive=false` observation no longer overrides `session.status` to `"killed"` or `session.activity` to `"exited"`. Lifecycle is set to `detecting`/`runtime_lost` and the legacy status is mirrored to `"detecting"` so the dashboard stays aligned.

Manual kills (`ao session kill`) and the explicit `done` path remain the only ways to reach a terminal state.

## Why this approach (vs. adding a revive subsystem)

The issue suggested two options: harden the probe OR add a revive transition (preferably both). I went with hardening alone — the simpler fix that addresses the root cause. Adding a revive subsystem would have been new infrastructure to compensate for a bad terminal decision; this PR removes the bad terminal decision instead. Net diff is mostly deletions.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` — 809/809 pass
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core typecheck` — clean
- [x] New regression test asserts: probe N sees dead+dead → `detecting`, probe N+1 sees runtime alive → session walks back to `working` (the exact scenario from the issue's metadata artifact)

title: feat(core): always-on event log + ao logs CLI (phase 1 of #1457)
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of the observability overhaul (#1457). Prerequisite for #1459.

Adds a project-level structured event stream that is written on **every** lifecycle tick, transition, reaction, and session action — not just while a daemon is polling. Exposes it through `ao logs`. Also tees `ao start`'s dashboard subprocess stdout/stderr to a rotated log file so the daemon's output is persisted.

### Philosophy — remove and simplify first

This PR deliberately does **not** build a logging framework, trace-span system, or pluggable sinks. The proposal in #1457 is a sketch; the actual surface that unblocks self-debug turned out to be:

1. **One JSONL per project**, appended to from any AO process
2. **One CLI** to filter / tail it
3. **One tee** for the dashboard daemon's output

Correlation-ids across subsystems, `ao doctor`, and sink pluggability are left for a follow-up once we know they earn their complexity.

### What's in it

- `packages/core/src/event-log.ts` — `appendEvent` / `readEventLog` / `followEventLog`, size-rotated to one `.1` rollover (default 10 MB, env `AO_EVENT_LOG_MAX_BYTES`), sensitive-key redaction, depth-bounded sanitization. Never throws.
- `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts` — four emission sites:
  - status transitions (with probe details + fromStatus/toStatus)
  - `lifecycle.sync` probe ticks (no status change)
  - reactions (success / escalation / action)
  - `pollAll` cycle (success or failure)
- `packages/cli/src/commands/logs.ts` — `ao logs [target]` with `--follow`, `--kind`, `--since {5m,30s,2h,1d}`, `--limit`, `--project`, `--correlation-id`, `--json`, `--path`.
- `packages/cli/src/lib/tee-log.ts` + wiring in `commands/start.ts` — mirrors the dashboard child's stdout/stderr to `{observabilityBaseDir}/dashboard.log` (5 MB rollover) **and** to the parent terminal, so interactive use is unchanged.

### Location

Lives under the existing hash-based observability directory — `{observabilityBaseDir}/events.jsonl` and `{observabilityBaseDir}/dashboard.log` — so it's already isolated per config / per checkout.

### Overlap with #855

#855 proposes a durable event log for state rehydration. That concern is complementary (state source-of-truth), not duplicated — this PR is about debug trails. If #855 lands on the same file format we can merge the two streams later.

### Scope intentionally NOT in this PR

- Correlation IDs across subsystems (schema has the field; we're not threading yet)
- `ao doctor` command
- Plugging in session-manager `destroyAllForProject` paths (#1073) — deferred; lifecycle transition events will capture the downstream status changes
- Replacing `observability.ts` (the snapshot/trace module stays)

## Test plan

title: refactor(core): storage redesign — projectId-based paths, JSON metadata
body:
## Summary

### Core storage redesign

- **V2 path layout**: `projects/{projectId}/sessions/{sid}.json`, `projects/{projectId}/worktrees/` replacing hash-based `{hash}-{name}/` directories
- **JSON metadata**: Replaces key=value flat-file format with structured JSON and typed `SessionMetadata`
- **storageKey removal**: Identity is `projectId`; removed storageKey plumbing from global config and runtime paths
- **SessionMetadata type evolution**: `statePayload`/`stateVersion` moved into `lifecycle`; runtime/dashboard/report fields are structured

### Archive removal

- **No more archive directory**: Sessions stay in `sessions/` with `lifecycle.state: "terminated"` instead of being moved to `sessions/archive/`
- Removed `getProjectArchiveDir`, `getArchiveFilePath`, `compactTimestamp` from core paths
- Removed `readArchivedMetadataRaw`, `updateArchivedMetadata` from metadata
- Removed `listArchivedSessionIds`, `markArchivedOpenCodeCleanup` from session manager
- `deleteMetadata` simplified to permanent delete (no archive boolean)
- `kill()` checks terminated state via lifecycle instead of archive lookup
- `restore()` reads directly from sessions/ (no archive fallback)
- `cleanupSessions()` iterates terminated sessions instead of archive directory
- Migration flattens old archives into `sessions/` as terminated records

### Session lifecycle: dual-truth elimination

- Source of truth is **`lifecycle-state.ts`**: `state` + `reason` replace the old `SessionStatus` enum
- Canonical states: `not_started | working | idle | needs_input | stuck | detecting | done | terminated`
- Terminal reasons: `manually_killed | runtime_lost | agent_process_exited | probe_failure | error_in_process | auto_cleanup | pr_merged`
- Legacy `SessionStatus` is **derived** at read time via `deriveLegacyStatus(state, reason, prState)` — used only for display backward-compat, never persisted
- `previousStatus` arguments removed throughout the codebase
- **Stale runtime reconciliation**: `sm.list()` checks if the tmux/process backing each session is still alive during enrichment. Dead ones get persisted as `runtime_lost` → legacy status `killed`. Without this, sessions whose runtime died silently would show "active" forever.

### Cross-project CLI rework

#### `ao stop`
- `ao stop` (no args): kills **all** sessions across **all** registered projects, stops parent process + dashboard, writes `last-stop.json` with `otherProjects` for cross-project restore
- `ao stop <project>`: surgical — kills only that project's sessions. **Does not** kill parent process or dashboard. Calls `removeProjectFromRunning(projectId)` so that `ao start <project>` can restart without hitting the "already running" gate
- Always loads global config (`~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml`) to see all projects

#### `ao start`
- Reads `last-stop.json` on startup and prompts to restore sessions — including cross-project ones
- **`projectNeedsRestart` gate**: if `ao start <project>` is called after `ao stop <project>` removed it from `running.json`, the "already running" menu is bypassed. An `isProjectId` guard (`!isRepoUrl && !isLocalPath`) prevents false triggers on path/URL arguments
- Project picker offers "Add this project" when launched in an unregistered cwd
- Auto-registers a flat local config on first `ao start` if missing

#### `Ctrl+C` graceful shutdown
- Mirrors `ao stop` exactly: kills all sessions, writes `last-stop.json`, unregisters `running.json`
- Async IIFE inside sync signal handler (Node.js signal handlers remove default exit behavior — must call `process.exit()` explicitly)

title: Enable tmux status bar in web terminal (currently forced off)
body:
## Problem

The tmux status bar is explicitly disabled when a web terminal PTY attaches to a tmux session. In `packages/web/server/mux-websocket.ts:288`:

```ts
const statusProc = spawn(this.TMUX, ["set-option", "-t", tmuxSessionId, "status", "off"]);
```

This hides useful session information that users (and agents) could see in the terminal — current session name, window list, datetime, etc.

## Proposed Fix

Change `"status", "off"` → `"status", "on"` in `mux-websocket.ts` so the tmux status bar is visible by default in the web terminal.

Optionally, configure a sensible status bar format (session name, active pane) via `set-option` for `status-right` / `status-left` to make the bar useful rather than just present.

## Context

Requested by @yyovil during design iteration on SubSession concepts. The status bar provides useful at-a-glance context when working with multiple tmux sessions/panes.

title: fix: reduce opencode session list churn
fix(core): prevent stale reaction dispatch on status oscillation
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1409

When `prEnrichmentCache` returns stale data that oscillates between CI failing/passing or conflicts/no-conflicts, the lifecycle manager was re-dispatching CI failure and merge conflict messages to agent sessions infinitely. The agent would dismiss them as "stale orchestrator noise" but they kept coming every 5 seconds.

## Root cause

Three reinforcing problems:

1. **Transition handler clears reaction trackers on status exit** (line ~1729): When status oscillates `ci_failed → working → ci_failed`, the `ci-failed` tracker is cleared on exit, creating a fresh tracker with `attempts: 0` on re-entry — resetting the retry budget every cycle.

2. **`maybeDispatchCIFailureDetails` clears tracker when leaving `ci_failed`** (line ~1338): Double-clears the tracker from a different code path, same effect.

3. **`maybeDispatchMergeConflicts` clears `lastMergeConflictDispatched` based on stale batch data** (line ~1531): When enrichment cache flips to `hasConflicts: false`, it clears the dedup flag. Next cycle when cache flips back to `hasConflicts: true`, the flag is gone and it dispatches again.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `lifecycle-manager.ts` | Transition handler: skip clearing `ci-failed` and `merge-conflicts` trackers on status exit |
| `lifecycle-manager.ts` | `maybeDispatchCIFailureDetails`: clear fingerprint metadata but preserve tracker when leaving `ci_failed` |
| `lifecycle-manager.ts` | `maybeDispatchMergeConflicts`: only clear dispatch flag when mergeability is from live API call, not stale batch enrichment |
| `lifecycle-manager.test.ts` | 2 new tests: CI failure oscillation and merge conflict oscillation |

## Test plan

- [x] New tests cover both oscillation scenarios
- [ ] Existing lifecycle tests pass (`pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test`)
- [ ] Manual verification: run a session with stale CI data, confirm no repeated dispatch

## Relationship to #1347

This is the companion fix to PR #1347 (issue #1290). That PR fixes the "CI signal never reaches dead sessions" gap in the webhook path. This PR fixes the "CI signal won't stop reaching live sessions" gap in the lifecycle polling path. Together they ensure CI signals are delivered exactly once to the right session.

title: bug(web): terminal shows connected but renders blank — no output despite agent running in tmux
body:
## Description

The web dashboard terminal connects successfully (shows "CONNECTED" status) but renders a completely blank viewport — only a blinking cursor is visible, no text output at all. The underlying agent process is confirmed running in tmux and producing output.

## Reproduction

1. `ao spawn` an agent (confirmed with both **opencode** and **codex**)
2. Open the session detail page in the web dashboard
3. Terminal header shows session name + "CONNECTED" (blue dot)
4. Terminal viewport is completely empty — solid black, just a cursor

## Expected

Terminal should render the agent output visible in the tmux session.

## Actual

Blank terminal despite successful WebSocket connection.

## Environment

- Affects: OpenCode and Codex agents (possibly all)
- Dashboard shows: session name, "CONNECTED" status, correct font size controls
- tmux: agent is running and producing output normally

## Suspected Area

Likely in the xterm.js ↔ tmux WebSocket bridge — the connection establishes but the data stream is not being written into the xterm terminal instance. Could be:

1. WebSocket message handler not piping data to `term.write()`
2. Terminal fit/render not triggering after initial mount
3. Race condition where terminal initializes before the WS data stream starts

## Related Issues

- #1197 — garbled rendering (xterm.js v5 issue)
- #1023 — clipped terminal
- #1151 — garbled on device switch

These are different symptoms but may share root cause in the xterm.js integration layer.

title: fix(scm-github): handle gh CLI exit code 1 on HTTP 304 in ETag guards
body:
## Problem

Both ETag guard functions treat HTTP 304 Not Modified as a failure, spamming warnings on every poll cycle:

```
[ETag Guard 1] PR list check failed for ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator: Command failed: gh api ...
gh: HTTP 304
```

## Root Cause

`execFileAsync("gh", args)` throws when `gh` exits non-zero. The `gh` CLI exits with code 1 on HTTP 304 — so the promise rejects *before* reaching the `output.includes("HTTP/2 304")` checks at lines 357/419, making that code **dead code**.

The catch blocks then:
1. Log a warning (the terminal spam)
2. Return `true` (assume changed) — defeating ETag caching entirely

## Fix

In both guard catch blocks, check if the error message contains `"304"` and return `false` (not modified) instead of logging + returning `true`.

## Impact
- ✅ Eliminates terminal spam during idle periods
- ✅ Restores ETag caching optimization (saves GraphQL rate limit)
- ✅ No behavioral change for actual errors — still logs + returns `true`

Closes #1482

title: bug(web): DirectTerminal can't find session — ao-web resolver doesn't know about the project-name segment in tmux session names
body:
## Summary

`ao-web`'s `resolveTmuxSession` fails to locate any tmux session created by `ao-core` whenever the project's `storageKey` contains a project-name segment (the common case). The dashboard logs `can't find session: <sessionId>` and the terminal never attaches, even though the tmux session exists and the agent is running.

The two packages disagree on the tmux session naming format:

- **`ao-core` writes** names as `{storageKey}-{prefix}-{num}`, where `storageKey` is typically `{hash}-{projectName}` — e.g. `361287ebbad1-smx-foundation-sf-orchestrator-1`.
- **`ao-web` reads** names assuming the format `{hash}-{sessionId}` — it strips exactly 13 characters (`{12hex}-`) and does an equality check against the user-facing session id.

Because the project-name segment sits between the hash and the user-facing session id, the equality check always fails, and `resolveTmuxSession` returns `null`.

## Reproduction

1. `npm install -g @aoagents/ao@0.3.0`
2. Create a project config with a `sessionPrefix` that differs from the project key, e.g.:
   ```yaml
   projects:
     smx-foundation:
       name: smx-foundation
       sessionPrefix: sf
       path: /Users/me/smx-foundation
       defaultBranch: main
   ```
3. `ao start`
4. Observe in the logs:
   ```
   ✔ Orchestrator session created
   Orchestrator: http://localhost:3000/projects/smx-foundation/sessions/sf-orchestrator-1
   [direct-terminal] [MuxServer] New mux connection
   [direct-terminal] can't find session: sf-orchestrator-1
   ```
5. `tmux ls` confirms the session actually exists, with the project-name segment embedded:
   ```
   361287ebbad1-smx-foundation-sf-orchestrator-1: 1 windows (...)
   ```
6. Open `http://localhost:3000/projects/smx-foundation/sessions/sf-orchestrator-1` — the terminal pane never attaches.

## Root cause

### Generator (ao-core)

`packages/core/src/paths.ts` (compiled: `ao-core/dist/paths.js:132-134`):

```js
function generateTmuxName(storageKey, prefix, num) {
    return `${requireStorageKey(storageKey)}-${prefix}-${num}`;
}
```

`storageKey` is the directory key used under `~/.agent-orchestrator/`. In practice it's `{hash}-{projectName}` — e.g. `361287ebbad1-smx-foundation` — which is confirmed both by the on-disk directory layout:

```
~/.agent-orchestrator/361287ebbad1-smx-foundation/sessions/sf-orchestrator-1
```

and by `session-manager.js` using `generateTmuxName(project.storageKey, orchestratorPrefix, num)` at the reservation site (line 612 in 0.3.0's compiled output).

So the tmux name for orchestrator #1 of project `smx-foundation` (prefix `sf`) is:

```
361287ebbad1-smx-foundation-sf-orchestrator-1
```

### Resolver (ao-web)

`packages/web/src/server/tmux-utils.ts` (compiled: `ao-web/dist-server/tmux-utils.js:74-83`):

```js
const output = execFn(tmuxPath, ["list-sessions", "-F", "#{session_name}"], { ... });
const sessions = output.split("\n").filter(Boolean);
const match = sessions.find(
  (s) => HASH_PREFIX_PATTERN.test(s) && s.substring(13) === sessionId,
);
```

where `HASH_PREFIX_PATTERN = /^[a-f0-9]{12}-/`.

For `sessionId = "sf-orchestrator-1"` and `s = "361287ebbad1-smx-foundation-sf-orchestrator-1"`:

- `HASH_PREFIX_PATTERN.test(s)` → `true`
- `s.substring(13)` → `"smx-foundation-sf-orchestrator-1"`
- `"smx-foundation-sf-orchestrator-1" === "sf-orchestrator-1"` → `false`

No match → `resolveTmuxSession` returns `null` → `DirectTerminal` logs `can't find session: sf-orchestrator-1`.

`parseTmuxName` in `ao-core/dist/paths.js:139-148` has the same blind spot — its regex `^([a-f0-9]{12})-([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)-(\d+)$` will greedily lump the project name into the `prefix` capture, which means any consumer relying on `parseTmuxName().prefix === project.sessionPrefix` is also broken.

## Impact

- Web dashboard terminal attachment is fully broken for any project where `storageKey !== hash` (i.e. any project whose directory includes the project name — the default on 0.3.0).
- Likely affects every orchestrator/worker session in a multi-project or even single-project install, not just orchestrators. The format mismatch is universal; my repro happened to be the orchestrator because that's the first session the dashboard tries to attach.
- Related issue #1456 references the format as `{projectHash}-{sessionId}`, which is also incorrect — confirming the format contract is under-specified across the codebase.

## Suggested fix

Pick one canonical format and align both sides:

**Option A (minimal, compatible with existing on-disk names):** Teach the resolver that the segment between the hash and the user-facing session id can be a project-name slug. The one-line patch that unblocked my install:

```diff
- const match = sessions.find((s) => HASH_PREFIX_PATTERN.test(s) && s.substring(13) === sessionId);
+ const match = sessions.find(
+   (s) =>
+     HASH_PREFIX_PATTERN.test(s) &&
+     (s.substring(13) === sessionId || s.substring(13).endsWith(`-${sessionId}`)),
+ );
```

The `endsWith` check is safe because `HASH_PREFIX_PATTERN` already gates the hash, and `sessionId` is already validated against `SESSION_ID_PATTERN` upstream. `parseTmuxName` should get an analogous fix (parse the trailing `{prefix}-{num}` off the end, treat everything between the hash and that as the project slug).

**Option B (cleaner contract):** Have `generateTmuxName` take a bare `hash` argument instead of `storageKey` so the on-wire name is truly `{hash}-{sessionId}` and matches the resolver as written. This is a breaking change to existing tmux session names and would require migration.

Option A is the correct tactical fix for 0.3.1; Option B is the right long-term direction if the team wants the naming invariant to hold without implicit project-name plumbing.

## Workaround

Patch `ao-web/dist-server/tmux-utils.js` in the global install with the diff above, then `kill $(pid from ~/.agent-orchestrator/running.json); rm -f ~/.agent-orchestrator/running.json; ao start`. Confirmed working on 0.3.0.

## Environment

- `@aoagents/ao@0.3.0` (global npm install)
- `@aoagents/ao-core@0.3.0`, `@aoagents/ao-web@0.3.0` (all subpackages on 0.3.0)
- macOS 26.4.1 (ARM, M2 Max)
- Node v25.9.0
- tmux 3.6a (Homebrew, `/opt/homebrew/bin/tmux`)

title: fix(web): resolve tmux sessions when storageKey is wrapped ({hash}-{projectName})
body:
## Summary

Closes #1486.

`ao-core` names tmux sessions as `{storageKey}-{sessionId}`, where `storageKey` is either a bare 12-hex hash or the legacy wrapped form `{hash}-{projectName}` (e.g. `361287ebbad1-smx-foundation`). The web resolver only handled the bare-hash form, so DirectTerminal logged `can't find session: <sessionId>` and never attached for any project whose storageKey includes a project-name segment — the default on 0.3.0.

## Fix

The resolver now looks up the owning `storageKey` on disk from `~/.agent-orchestrator/{storageKey}/sessions/{sessionId}`, then asks tmux for the exact `{storageKey}-{sessionId}` name via `has-session -t =`. The on-disk record is the authoritative disambiguator.

Design points:

- **No endsWith matching.** An earlier attempt using `substring(13).endsWith(`-${sessionId}`)` was flagged (review) as ambiguous: a bare session `{hash}-my-app-1` would falsely match a lookup for `app-1`. The on-disk lookup is unambiguous.
- **All candidates probed, not just the first.** If multiple projects happen to own the same `sessionId` on disk, each is checked against tmux in turn so a stale metadata dir can't shadow the live session of another project.
- **Permissive wrapped-suffix pattern.** `STORAGE_KEY_PATTERN` accepts any non-empty suffix after the hash (`^[a-f0-9]{12}(-.+)?$`), because legacy storageKeys are built from `basename(projectPath)` and can contain spaces or unicode. Safe because `storageKey` is passed to `execFileSync` which bypasses the shell.
- **Bare-hash fallback retained.** If the on-disk record is missing (e.g. scrubbed filesystem), the tmux-listing path still recovers bare-hash sessions with the same exact-remainder check as before — no behavior regression there.

## Known pre-existing limitation (not in scope)

If two different projects both have the same `sessionId` *and* both tmux sessions are live, the resolver returns the first match. This is identical to the prior bare-hash behavior (documented by the `returns first match when multiple hash-prefixed sessions exist for same ID` test). A proper fix requires threading `projectId` from the URL through the mux protocol to the resolver — tracked separately.

## Test plan

- [x] 90 unit tests pass, including new cases for wrapped storageKey, ambiguity safety, multi-candidate probing, unicode/space project names, and extraneous AO-base entries.
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web typecheck` clean.
- [x] Manual: start orchestrator in a project whose config uses a wrapped storageKey; confirm terminal attaches in the dashboard.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: resolveTmuxSession: cross-project sessionId collision — thread projectId through mux protocol
body:
## Summary

When two different projects on the same machine have both (a) the same user-facing `sessionId` (e.g. both have `ao-1`) and (b) live tmux sessions, `resolveTmuxSession` in [packages/web/server/tmux-utils.ts](packages/web/server/tmux-utils.ts) returns the first match. The dashboard terminal may attach to the wrong project's session.

This is a pre-existing limitation. The prior bare-hash code had identical behavior via `Array.find(...)`, documented by the existing test `"returns first match when multiple hash-prefixed sessions exist for same ID"`. It was surfaced during review of #1486 / #1488 but intentionally deferred from that PR to keep scope surgical.

## Root cause

The mux WebSocket protocol's `terminal.open` message carries only `id: string` — no project context — so the resolver has nothing to disambiguate with:

```ts
// packages/web/src/lib/mux-protocol.ts
{ ch: "terminal"; id: string; type: "open" }
```

The browser URL at the call site is `/projects/{projectId}/sessions/{id}`, so the information exists; it's just not plumbed through.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `openTerminal` (client-side, [packages/web/src/providers/MuxProvider.tsx](packages/web/src/providers/MuxProvider.tsx)) takes `(id, projectId)`.
2. The `terminal.open` protocol message carries `projectId`. Update both `ClientMessage` in [packages/web/src/lib/mux-protocol.ts](packages/web/src/lib/mux-protocol.ts) and its duplicate in [packages/web/server/mux-websocket.ts](packages/web/server/mux-websocket.ts).
3. `TerminalManager.open(id, projectId)` forwards `projectId` to `resolveTmuxSession`.
4. `resolveTmuxSession(sessionId, tmuxPath, execFn, fs, projectId?)` uses `projectId` to look up the owning `storageKey` directly (via the config service or by matching directory names), bypassing the scan of `~/.agent-orchestrator/*`.
5. Update the existing `"returns first match when multiple hash-prefixed sessions exist for same ID"` test to assert project-scoped behavior instead.
6. Add a test for the collision case: two projects with the same sessionId, each with a live tmux session — the resolver must pick the one matching the caller's `projectId`.

## Context

- Original bug: #1486
- Fix (scope-limited): #1488
- Review discussion that surfaced this: three-round Codex review during #1488, round 3 P1.

## Impact

Low in practice — requires a multi-project install with a sessionId collision. But the failure mode (attaching to the wrong project's terminal) is confusing and hard to detect.

title: fix(cli): hide legacy second positional from ao spawn help
body: ## Issue `ao spawn --help` shows a `[second]` positional argument even though `ao spawn` only supports zero or one positional argument. The optional positional is the issue identifier; project selection is handled by auto-detection or by the supported prefixed issue form. If users pass more than one positional argument, AO should reject the command with a direct arity error. The important message is that only one argument is accepted and two were passed, for example: ```text ✗ `ao spawn` accepts at most 1 argument, but 2 were provided. Use: ao spawn [issue] ao spawn ``` > [!NOTE] > The following is the fix spec for AI agents. ## Steps 1. Open `packages/cli/src/commands/spawn.ts` and confirm how Commander renders the hidden second positional. 2. Update the command definition so `ao spawn --help` no longer exposes `[second]` as a public argument. 3. If more than one positional arg is provided, return a concise arity error that says `ao spawn` accepts at most 1 argument and reports how many were provided. 4. Use standard CLI syntax in user-facing help/errors: `[issue]` for the optional issue argument, not ``. 5. Add or update focused CLI command tests around the help output and the too-many-arguments error. 6. Run the narrowest relevant validation for `@aoagents/ao-cli`. 7. Commit only the CLI command/test files required for this fix. ## Validation - Package-level test: `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli test` - Package-level typecheck: `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli typecheck` - Manual smoke check: `node packages/ao/bin/ao.js spawn --help` - Manual smoke check: `node packages/ao/bin/ao.js spawn 1234 2234` ## Constraints - Keep the scope inside `packages/cli` unless Commander requires a tiny shared helper. - Preserve current supported inputs: `ao spawn`, `ao spawn 123`, `ao spawn INT-100`, `ao spawn project-id/123`, and `ao spawn sessionPrefix/123`. - Do not reintroduce `ao spawn ` as supported syntax. - Do not use angle brackets for optional positional args in user-facing examples or help text. - Do not frame the second positional as backwards-compatible behavior; it should only produce a clear too-many-arguments error. ## Acceptance - `ao spawn --help` no longer presents `[second]` as a public argument. - The documented argument name is clear, preferably `[issue]` instead of `[first]`. - `ao spawn 1234 2234` exits without spawning and prints a concise error that says only one argument is accepted and two were provided. - The suggested replacement syntax uses `ao spawn [issue]`, not `ao spawn `. - Focused tests cover both the help output and the too-many-arguments error.
