title: fix(web): pin dashboard Next.js workspace root
body:
## Issue

Starting the AO dashboard in foreground mode currently prints a Next.js workspace-root inference warning when another lockfile exists above the repository checkout. The dashboard still starts, but the foreground logs include noisy warning output before `Ready`.

Observed from the complaint screenshot:

```text
[next] ⚠ Warning: Next.js inferred your workspace root, but it may not be correct.
[next] We detected multiple lockfiles and selected the directory of /Users/tanishqpalandurkar/package-lock.json as the root directory.
[next] To silence this warning, set `outputFileTracingRoot` in your Next.js config, or consider removing one of the lockfiles if it's not needed.
[next] Detected additional lockfiles:
[next]   * /Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/agent-orchestrator/pnpm-lock.yaml
```

The PR that resolves this issue must make a code/config change in the repo so the warning does not appear again the next time foreground dashboard logs are watched. It should not rely on manually deleting a user-level lockfile.

## Affected Package

- Package path: `packages/web`
- npm package: `@aoagents/ao-web`
- Surface area: dashboard startup / Next.js config / foreground `ao dashboard` logs
- Shared code touched: none expected unless investigation shows the dashboard launch path needs it

## Environment

- AO version: `0.2.5`
- Affected package version: `0.2.5`
- OS: macOS
- Node.js: `v22.22.2`
- pnpm: `9.15.4`
- Browser: not applicable; warning is emitted in foreground server logs

## Reproduction

1. Use a checkout at `/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/agent-orchestrator` with the repo `pnpm-lock.yaml` present.
2. Have another lockfile above the checkout, such as `/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/package-lock.json`.
3. From the repo root, run `node packages/ao/bin/ao.js dashboard`.
4. Watch the foreground logs as the Next.js dev server starts.

## Current Result

Next.js prints a workspace-root inference warning and says it selected the parent directory containing `/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/package-lock.json` as the root directory, with the repo `pnpm-lock.yaml` listed as an additional lockfile.

## Expected Result

The AO dashboard startup path should pin the intended Next.js workspace/tracing root for this monorepo so foreground dashboard logs start cleanly without the workspace-root inference warning.

## Evidence

- `packages/web/next.config.js` currently has no `outputFileTracingRoot` setting.
- Local filesystem evidence from the complaint environment has `/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/package-lock.json` above the checkout and `pnpm-lock.yaml` in the repo root.
- The visible startup command was `packages/ao/bin/ao.js dashboard`.

> [!NOTE]
> The following is the fix spec for AI agents.

## Steps

1. Open `packages/web/next.config.js` and the dashboard launch path used by `node packages/ao/bin/ao.js dashboard`.
2. Trace why Next.js is inferring the parent directory instead of the AO repository root when multiple lockfiles exist.
3. Fix the root cause with the smallest possible code/config change, likely by setting the Next.js output file tracing root to the repository root from `packages/web/next.config.js`.
4. Add or update focused validation if there is a practical way to assert the config behavior.
5. Run the narrowest relevant validation for `@aoagents/ao-web` and any touched package.
6. Verify foreground startup logs no longer contain `Next.js inferred your workspace root` when running the dashboard with the parent lockfile still present.
7. Commit only the required config/code changes and closely related tests. No unrelated cleanup.

## Validation

- Package-level typecheck: `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web typecheck`
- Web package test: `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test`
- Foreground smoke check: `node packages/ao/bin/ao.js dashboard` from the repo root while `/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/package-lock.json` still exists above the checkout

## Constraints

- Keep the scope inside `packages/web` unless shared CLI startup code must change to fix the bug correctly.
- Do not fix this by asking users to remove parent-directory lockfiles.
- Preserve existing public APIs, config shapes, dashboard routes, and plugin contracts.
- Prefer a minimal surgical edit over a dashboard startup refactor.
- Note follow-up work separately instead of expanding scope inside this issue.

## Acceptance

- Running `node packages/ao/bin/ao.js dashboard` from the repo root starts the dashboard without printing `Next.js inferred your workspace root`.
- The validation must be done with the parent lockfile still present, so the fix proves the repo handles this environment directly.
- The PR contains an actual code/config change that prevents the warning in future foreground logs.

title: fix(cli): scope ao stop <project> to named project only
body:
## Summary

`ao stop <project>` was unconditionally killing the shared `ao start` parent process, dashboard, and `running.json` — taking down ALL projects and the web UI when only one project was targeted.

**Root cause:** `registerStop()` had no conditional to distinguish per-project stops from full teardowns. The parent PID kill and dashboard stop ran on every code path.

**Fix:** Guard the host teardown (parent PID kill + dashboard stop + unregister) behind `projectArg !== undefined`. When a specific project is named, only its orchestrator session is killed. Full teardown (`ao stop` / `ao stop --all`) continues to work as before.

The lifecycle worker for the stopped project becomes a harmless no-op — it polls sessions, finds no orchestrator, does nothing.

Fixes #1495

## Test Plan

- [ ] Single project config: `ao stop` → full teardown (dashboard + parent killed) ✓
- [ ] Multi-project config: `ao stop <project>` → only that project's orchestrator stops, dashboard and other projects stay up ✓
- [ ] `ao stop --all` → full teardown ✓
- [ ] `ao stop <nonexistent>` → error, no collateral damage ✓

title: fix(web): pin Next.js workspace root to silence startup warning
body:
## Problem

Starting the AO dashboard in foreground mode prints a Next.js workspace-root inference warning when another lockfile exists above the repository checkout:

```
⚠ Warning: Next.js inferred your workspace root, but it may not be correct.
We detected multiple lockfiles and selected the directory of ~/package-lock.json as the root directory.
```

## Fix

Add `outputFileTracingRoot` to `packages/web/next.config.js`, pointing it at the monorepo root via `path.join(__dirname, "../..")`. This is the canonical Next.js solution — it tells Next.js exactly which directory is the workspace root, bypassing the heuristic that triggers when it finds lockfiles in parent directories.

## Changes

- `packages/web/next.config.js`: Added `import path` + `import { fileURLToPath }` + `outputFileTracingRoot: path.join(__dirname, "../..")` to the config object.

## Testing

- Config resolves correctly: `outputFileTracingRoot` → `/path/to/agent-orchestrator` (repo root containing `pnpm-lock.yaml`)
- Could not run `agent-ci` locally — `aoagent` user lacks Docker group membership (`EACCES /var/run/docker.sock`). CI will validate.
- Change is a pure config addition with no code logic changes.

Closes #1492

title: ui(sidebar): rework project row — info density, action button overflow, degraded state polish
body:
## Context

`packages/web/src/components/ProjectSidebar.tsx` (currently 791 lines) renders both project rows and session rows inline. The project row in particular has a few rough edges that are worth a focused pass.

## Observations

1. **Hit-target crowding** — each project row packs: chevron + name + count badge + Dashboard icon + Orchestrator icon + kebab menu. That's 5 interactive targets in one row, plus the toggle area. On narrower sidebars they jostle before the active state even paints.
2. **Action icon discoverability** — the Dashboard (grid) and Orchestrator (org-chart) icons live without labels. Users won't know what they are without hovering. Consider hiding them behind hover/focus, or moving them into the kebab menu.
3. **Collapsed mode has no per-project expansion** — a project with 30 sessions shows the first 5 + `+25`, but you can't expand without un-collapsing the whole sidebar. A hover/click flyout would help.
4. **Degraded variant is jarring** — uses warning-triangle in place of the chevron, an inline pill, and a "Config needs repair" subnote, but offers no way to fix from the sidebar (the Repair flow lives elsewhere). Either link directly into the repair modal or keep the row collapsed and silent until the user opens it.
5. **Active project styling** is only an amber color shift on the toggle text — easy to miss when the eye is scanning. Consider a left border/accent or background.
6. **\"+\" button placement** — the only way to add a project is the `+` next to the "Projects" header. There's no equivalent affordance to spawn a session from inside a project row; users have to navigate to the dashboard. Worth deciding whether the project row should host a per-project "spawn session" action.
7. **Component size** — at 791 lines, `ProjectSidebar.tsx` brushes the 400-line cap in CLAUDE.md. Extracting a `ProjectRow` (and `SessionRow`, sibling issue) would make iteration easier.

## Out of scope

Session row redesign — tracked in a sibling issue.

## Suggested next steps

- Brainstorm a denser project row layout (single hit target + secondary actions on hover/in menu).
- Decide whether per-project session spawn belongs here.
- Extract `ProjectRow` into its own file as part of the change.

title: ui(sidebar): rework session row — info density, filter clarity, grouping, active state
body:
## Context

The session row inside `ProjectSidebar.tsx` (sibling to the project-row issue) shows very little per session and has a few interaction quirks worth a focused pass.

## Observations

1. **Sparse info per row** — currently: colored dot (attention level) + branch-humanized title + lowercase status word. There's no PR number, no CI/review state, no last-activity timestamp, no agent kind, no issue label. To know anything beyond "is it working", users must click into the detail page. Decide what the minimum useful row is.
2. **Level word duplicates the dot** — the dot color and the trailing word both encode attention level. One of them is redundant; the freed space could carry richer info (PR #, CI badge, age).
3. **`Show session ID` is the only display option** — gated behind a gear popover that holds exactly that one checkbox. Consider folding the toggle inline with the killed/done toggles or removing the popover entirely.
4. **Killed/done filter asymmetry** — `showDone` reveals killed sessions too (they go through the `done` attention branch), so the two toggles overlap in confusing ways. Footer toggles are also icon-only (skull / check) with no labels — non-obvious without hovering.
5. **No grouping inside a project** — sessions are interleaved in arrival order. Grouping by attention level (`respond > review > working > pending > merge > done`) would let users see what needs human action at a glance.
6. **Active session has no strong visual mark** — only an amber title color. No left bar, no background. Easy to lose place when scanning a long list.
7. **`action` attention level is dead code** in the sidebar — `getAttentionLevel` is called without a mode, so `detailed` wins and `action` never appears. Either drop the branch or opt the sidebar into simple mode.
8. **Loading state is global** — when `sessions === null`, every project shows skeletons even if only one is loading. Per-project loading isn't tracked.
9. **`SessionDot` glow** is the only visual heartbeat. No progress, no token/cost hint, no time-in-state — could surface more without much real estate.
10. **Hover tooltip is just `aria-label="Open <title>"`** — a richer tooltip (PR, CI, last activity) would be high-leverage.

## Out of scope

Project row redesign — tracked in a sibling issue.

## Suggested next steps

- Decide on the minimum-viable info per row, then design density variants (compact / standard / detailed).
- Resolve the killed/done filter overlap.
- Extract `SessionRow` into its own file.

title: ui(sidebar): rework footer row — filter toggles, settings popover, theme toggle
body:
## Context

The bottom row of `ProjectSidebar.tsx` (lines ~680–782) crams four unrelated controls into a single horizontal strip: a "show killed" toggle (skull icon), a "show done" toggle (check icon), a gear that opens a popover, and the global `ThemeToggle`. It feels like a junk drawer.

## Observations

1. **Heterogeneous controls in one row** — two filter toggles (per-sidebar state), one settings popover (display preference), and one global app-wide toggle (theme) all share the same visual weight. Nothing tells the user that the theme toggle is global vs. the others are sidebar-scoped.
2. **Icon-only toggles, no labels** — skull = killed, check = done. Non-obvious without hovering. The pressed state (`--active`) is the only signal that they're stateful at all.
3. **Filter overlap with `showDone`** — see sibling issue (#1500); `showDone` also reveals killed sessions, making the two toggles feel redundant.
4. **Settings popover holds a single checkbox** — the entire gear → popover → label flow exists for one option (`Show session ID`). Either inline it as a third toggle or fold it into a richer "View" menu when there's actually more than one option.
5. **Theme toggle placement is incidental** — it lives here because there's no other obvious place, but the sidebar footer is a strange home for an app-global control. Could move to a top-level account/settings menu, or at least visually separate it (divider, right-justify, smaller).
6. **No labels in collapsed mode** — when the sidebar collapses, the footer disappears entirely (collapsed render path returns early), so killed/done filters and theme become unreachable until the user expands. Worth deciding whether the collapsed rail should keep these controls.
7. **Density wastes the only sticky-bottom row in the sidebar** — this is prime real estate (always visible, anchored). Today it shows four icons. Could host a session count summary, a search affordance, or a "spawn session" button.

## Suggested directions

- Replace the icon row with a labeled "View" / "Filter" menu (single button → dropdown) so behavior is discoverable and the footer regains breathing room.
- Move theme toggle to a global place (header, account menu) and use the sidebar footer for sidebar-scoped concerns only.
- Decide what *should* live in this anchored row — search, spawn, status summary — once the legacy controls move.

## Related

- #1499 (project row rework)
- #1500 (session row rework — filter overlap)

title: ui(kanban): rework SessionCard footer + visual hierarchy
body:
## Context

`packages/web/src/components/SessionCard.tsx` (1056 lines) renders the kanban card. The footer in particular is awkward — the leftmost label (`footerStatus` from `getFooterStatusLabel`) is wedged next to the kill button with no visual relationship between the two — but the broader visual hierarchy of the card has accumulated rough edges worth a focused pass.

## Footer issues (the original ask)

1. **Leftmost label is semantically homeless** — `card__status` shows either a 60-char-truncated `userPrompt` or one of several `getFooterStatusLabel` outputs (`mergeable`, `detecting`, `ci failing`, or whatever `getSessionTruthLabel`/`getPRTruthLabel` returns). It mixes prompt content (a *task description*) with lifecycle status (a *state machine label*) in the same slot. They should not share a visual treatment.
2. **Kill button placement is incidental** — the destructive action lives next to a status label, with no visual grouping. The only signal that it's destructive is the icon and `btn--danger` class. Two-step "kill?" confirmation is good; placement is not.
3. **Footer = "everything that didn't fit elsewhere"** — currently houses status text *or* a Merge PR CTA *or* a kill button. The merge CTA is a primary action; the kill is a destructive utility; the label is metadata. Three different priorities, one row, no separation.
4. **Truncation logic lives in JSX** — `userPrompt.slice(0, 60) + "…"` inline. Should be a util, and `60` is arbitrary — at narrow widths it still overflows the kill button.

## Broader visual hierarchy problems

Going top-to-bottom:

5. **Header row competes with itself** — activity dot + session id + restore button + terminal link. Restore and terminal are both pill-shaped controls with similar weight, but they mean different things (restore = revive a dead session, terminal = jump to live tty). The id is mono and dim, but it's the only stable identifier and gets less prominence than the icons.
6. **Title** (`card__title`) is the most important field but has no clear hierarchy advantage over `secondaryText` immediately below — both end up as similar small text in practice.
7. **Meta row** (`card__meta`) mixes branch, PR link, and additions/deletions/size with `·` separators. This is fine in isolation but *also* runs as a meta-chip row in the done-card variant, with different styling — two different layouts for the same information.
8. **`secondaryText` is overloaded** — it's `issueLabel · issueTitle` *or* `issueTitle` alone *or* `summary`. Three different meanings in one slot, distinguished only by which is non-null. The merge variant adds a checkmark icon; nothing else does.
9. **`truthLine`** — three-part lifecycle truth string ("Session X · PR Y · Runtime Z") sits as a 10px tertiary line below secondaryText. Useful for debugging, noisy in normal use; should probably be a tooltip or dev-only.
10. **Rate-limit/CI-passing/alerts/quick-reply stack vertically with no separators** — when a card has alerts *and* passing checks *and* a quick-reply pane, the body becomes a wall of small rows. No grouping.
11. **CI strip duplicates information** — passing checks render as `ci-chip--pass` chips (up to 3), failing checks render as alert rows. Two different visual languages for the same underlying data; users have to learn both.
12. **Alerts max at 3** with no `+N more` overflow indicator. If a PR has 4+ issues, the user silently sees only 3.
13. **Quick-reply pane (`level === "respond"`)** is large (agent message + view-context link + 3 preset buttons + textarea). It dominates the card whenever an agent waits for input. Probably correct prioritization but it makes the card height jump dramatically as level shifts.
14. **Done-card variant is almost a different component** — different padding scale (`px-3.5` vs `px-[10px]`), different chip class names (`done-meta-chip` vs `card__diff`), different status pill, different expand-on-click behavior, different action placement. Consolidating the two variants would be a major win.
15. **Frame/accent system** — `cardFrameClass` × `accentClass` produces a 3 × 5 matrix of border treatments (`merge-frame`, `alert-frame`, `fixed` × `merge`, `working`, `respond`, `attention`, `default`). Cognitive load for users; non-trivial to remember which combination means what.
16. **No persistent "now" signal** — `lastActivityAt` exists in the data model but is never displayed on the card. The activity dot animates ("working") but there's no "5m ago" / "2h ago" anywhere.
17. **Cost / token data not surfaced** — agents track this; cards don't show it.
18. **Component size** — 1056 lines, nearly 3× the 400-line cap. Done-card branch alone is ~210 lines. Extract `DoneSessionCard` and `SessionCardFooter` at minimum.

## Suggested next steps

- Split the footer into two zones: **status indicator** (left, neutral) and **primary action** (right, contextual: merge / kill / nothing). User prompt should not live in the footer at all — promote it to its own slot in the body or drop it (it's already the title source for sessions without an issue).
- Decide what the kanban card's *minimum useful payload* is, then design tiers (compact / standard / expanded) instead of stacking everything.
- Consolidate done variant into the standard card with a `--done` modifier.
- Surface `lastActivityAt` as a relative timestamp in the header.
- Extract `SessionCardHeader`, `SessionCardBody`, `SessionCardFooter`, `DoneSessionCard` into separate files.

## Related

- #1499 (sidebar project row)
- #1500 (sidebar session row)
- #1501 (sidebar footer row)

title: Add polished skeleton loading states across the dashboard
body:
## Problem

The dashboard has some skeleton loading states today, but they're inconsistent and visually rough — they don't match the dark theme polish of the rest of the UI and in places the loading state is jarring (layout shift, mismatched dimensions, plain spinners instead of skeletons).

## Goal

Audit and rework loading states across the web dashboard so that every async surface shows a skeleton that:

- Matches the actual rendered content's layout (no shift on load)
- Uses consistent design tokens (colors, radii, shimmer/pulse) from `globals.css`
- Feels cohesive with the dark theme
- Replaces ad-hoc spinners where a skeleton would communicate structure better

## Scope (initial sweep)

- Sidebar: project rows, session rows
- Dashboard: kanban columns / session cards
- Session detail: header, metadata, terminal area, PR/CI panels
- Any modal/drawer that fetches on open

## Suggested approach

1. Inventory current loading states (grep for existing skeletons + spinners + `isLoading`)
2. Define a small set of reusable skeleton primitives (e.g. `SkeletonLine`, `SkeletonBlock`, `SkeletonRow`) in `packages/web/src/components/`
3. Replace existing loading UI surface-by-surface, mirroring real layout dimensions
4. Verify against `DESIGN.md` tokens — no inline styles, no new UI libs

## Out of scope

- Changing data-fetching logic (SSE intervals, etc.)
- Redesigning the components themselves — only their loading state

title: docs: deep analysis of core engine
body:
## Summary

- Comprehensive static analysis of `packages/core/src/` covering all source files
- Identifies **25 findings** across 4 severity levels: 2 critical, 6 high, 9 medium, 8 low
- Written as `ANALYSIS.md` in the repo root with file:line references

### Critical findings
- **C-01**: Read-modify-write race in `updateMetadata` can lose concurrent writes from agent PATH wrappers
- **C-02**: Concurrent `checkSession` calls share mutable state via PR enrichment cache

### High findings
- **H-01**: `list()` performs expensive runtime probes for every session on every lifecycle poll (60+ IO ops/cycle for 20 sessions)

- **H-05**: `isTerminalSession` considers runtime-missing as terminal, contradicting session restoration semantics
- **H-06**: `parseCanonicalLifecycle` Zod schema accepts nearly-empty payloads silently

### Files analyzed
`types.ts`, `session-manager.ts`, `lifecycle-manager.ts`, `config.ts`, `plugin-registry.ts`, `metadata.ts`, `activity-signal.ts`, `lifecycle-state.ts`, `lifecycle-transition.ts`, `lifecycle-status-decisions.ts`, `agent-report.ts`, `report-watcher.ts`, `activity-log.ts`, `paths.ts`, `observability.ts`, `atomic-write.ts`, `agent-workspace-hooks.ts`, `notifier-resolution.ts`, `scm-webhook-utils.ts`, `key-value.ts`, `agent-selection.ts`

title: docs: deep audit of packages/core/src
body:
## Summary

- Read every file in `packages/core/src/` (~35 source files, ~7,000 lines)
- Identified 4 critical, 7 high, and 14 medium severity issues
- Written to `CORE-ANALYSIS.md` in the repo root with file:line references, reproduction steps, and suggested fixes

### Critical findings
- **C-01**: Race condition in session ID reservation (TOCTOU between list scan and atomic reserve)
- **C-02**: Shared `fetchOpenCodeSessionList` promise can't recover from rejection across sessions in same `list()` call
- **C-03**: `determineStatus` mutates session objects in place — shared reference causes state bleeding across poll cycles
- **C-04**: `updateSessionMetadata` reads already-mutated lifecycle state, losing auditability

### High findings
- **H-01**: `atomicWriteFileSync` temp file name collisions across containers with same PID
- **H-02**: Non-atomic read-then-write in `deleteMetadata` archiving
- **H-03**: Double-kill race in concurrent `kill()` calls
- **H-04**: Empty `PRInfo` fields from unparseable URLs cause silent API failures
- **H-05**: `getActivityFallbackState` age-based decay doesn't handle `exited` state
- **H-06**: Activity detection overrides confirmed-dead runtime state (probe_failed → alive)
- **H-07**: `parseKeyValueContent` skips `key=#value` lines as comments

## Test plan

- [ ] Review each finding for accuracy (file paths, line numbers, code snippets)
- [ ] Prioritize C-03/C-04 (in-place mutation) as highest-impact fix
- [ ] Verify H-06 (activity overriding dead runtime) with a killed tmux session

title: docs: deep analysis of web dashboard
body:
## Summary
- Comprehensive audit of `packages/web/src/` covering bugs, stale state issues, missing error boundaries, performance problems, SSE/WebSocket handling issues, caching bugs, and UX gaps
- All findings include `file:line` references and severity ratings

## Key Findings

**6 Critical Bugs:**
- SSE snapshot ignores server-computed attention levels on refresh (useSessionEvents.ts)
- Module-level mutable cache in session detail page shared across navigations (page.tsx:63-67)
- `useSSESessionActivity` opens duplicate SSE connections alongside dashboard SSE
- Session detail page polls 3 endpoints every 5s + SSE (8 requests per 5s cycle)
- `enrichSessionPR` mutates DashboardSession in place, breaking React memo comparison
- Race condition in mux reconnect + terminal re-open

**4 Stale State Issues:**
- Rate limit dismiss never resets across rate limit cycles
- Session activity state disagrees with lifecycle state after SSE patches
- SSE snapshot patches don't update PR data or lifecycle facets
- Done-bar expanded state not reset on session changes

**3 Missing Error Boundaries:**
- No error boundary around SessionDetail or DirectTerminal
- Global error boundary may have no CSS variables loaded

**6 Performance Problems:**
- SSE route calls `sessionToDashboard` every 5s per connected client
- `/api/sessions` enrichment waterfall (metadata → PR, sequential)
- Dashboard computes attention levels twice per session
- Session detail uses `JSON.stringify` for deep equality

**5 SSE/WebSocket Issues:**
- SSE connection has no maximum retry limit
- Mux WebSocket backoff caps at 30s, never gives up
- No ping/pong heartbeat on mux WebSocket
- SSE snapshot races with full refresh
- Mux `sessions` state update on every snapshot

**4 Caching Bugs:**
- `processedIssues` Set never cleared (unbounded growth)
- TTLCache `size()` includes stale entries
- PR cache hit doesn't revalidate rate-limit flag
- Issue title cache has no eviction trigger

**7 UX Gaps:**
- No merge confirmation dialog on session card
- No feedback when kill/restore fails in SessionDetail
- No offline state for terminal when mux disconnects
- No loading skeleton matching final layout

Adds a **preset system** to `ao spawn` — predefined, trusted multi-line prompts that bootstrap an agent session for a specific task. First two presets ship in this PR: `backlog` (project-wide analysis) and `triage` (single-issue investigation).

**Usage:**
- `ao spawn --preset backlog` — analyze sessions, PRs, issues; produce reports; instruct orchestrator to spawn agents
- `ao spawn 42 --preset triage` — investigate issue #42; post a structured triage comment

## The preset system

New module `packages/cli/src/presets/` with:
- `Preset` interface — `name`, `description`, `prompt`, `issueArg`
- Preset registry with `resolvePreset()` lookup
- Per-preset issue-arg policy: `"required" | "optional" | "forbidden"` (default: `forbidden`)

Spawn integration:
- New `--preset <name>` flag, mutually exclusive with `--prompt`
- Issue-arg validation is per-preset — specific error messages for both directions
- Preset prompts bypass the 4096-char sanitization limit (trusted multi-line markdown)

## Bundled presets

**`backlog`** (issue arg: forbidden)
- Gathers AO session data via `ao status --reports full --json --include-terminated` (with fallback for older AO versions)
- Fetches GitHub state (open PRs, assigned issues, review requests, changes-requested)

- **Does not commit code, open PRs, close the issue, add labels, or assign anyone** — analysis only

title: fix(core): keep terminated sessions in active dir after kill() (#1503)
body:
## Summary

- `kill()` no longer archives sessions immediately. Terminated sessions stay in the active directory so `list()`, the dashboard kanban, and `ensureOrchestrator()` can see them.
- The idempotency path inside `kill()` (fired when kill is called on an already-terminated session) archives the file. This is how `cleanup()` eventually removes it — when it detects a dead runtime, it calls `kill()` again, which hits the idempotency path and archives.
- The `delete` orchestrator strategy still explicitly archives after killing, so `reserveSessionId()` can immediately claim the same session name for the replacement.
- OpenCode cleanup marker is written to active metadata (instead of archived metadata) so the flag survives into the eventual archive.

## Root cause

`session-manager.ts` `kill()` called `deleteMetadata(sessionsDir, sessionId, true)` immediately after setting `lifecycle.session.state = "terminated"`. This archived the session, making it invisible to `list()` which only reads the active directory. Result: session disappeared from dashboard instead of showing in Done/Terminated column, and `ensureOrchestrator()` spawned a new orchestrator number on the next `ao start`.

title: Design: AO Activity Events Logging Layer (RCA / self-debugging trail)
body:
## Design: AO Activity Events Logging Layer

Tracking issue for the design and discussion of AO's activity events layer — a lightweight SQLite-backed RCA trail that lets AO diagnose itself when something behaves incorrectly or unexpectedly.

**Design doc (source of truth):** https://gist.github.com/ashish921998/c42db0234370f618fb81a496359831e2

**Author:** @ashish921998

### Summary

The activity events layer is a durable, queryable, local trail of structured events that AO writes as it operates — session spawn/kill, lifecycle transitions, `/api/sessions` results, major UI breakages. When a user reports an issue, AO can query the trail to reconstruct the timeline, identify the likely failure boundary, and guide or make a fix.

This is not a full observability platform, event sourcing system, or analytics product. It is a focused local RCA trail.

### V1 highlights (per the gist)

- SQLite (WAL mode) as durable substrate from day one
- One event envelope, one table, one core write API, one core query API
- CLI reader (`ao events`) — primary V1 read path for diagnostic agents (subprocesses can't rely on the dashboard server)
- Best-effort writes, 7-day retention, sanitization for secrets, 16 KB payload cap
- Initial instrumentation: session spawn, session kill, lifecycle transition, `/api/sessions` count/duration, major UI breakage / sidebar visibility events
- Parallel operation with existing `observability.ts` — no migration required for V1

### Discussion

This issue is the canonical thread for the design conversation. Clarifications, proposals, and tradeoffs will be posted as comments below so we keep everything in one place before V1 implementation lands.

cc @ashish921998

title: Dynamic project supervisor: auto-poll active globally-registered projects
body:
## Follow-up to PR #1466

This is a **follow-up issue, to be picked up after PR #1466 is merged.** It's intentionally scoped out of #1466 to keep that PR's blast radius bounded.

## Problem

Lifecycle polling (the 30s loop in `packages/cli/src/lib/lifecycle-service.ts`) is scoped to the project IDs passed to `ao start` at startup. Projects added to the global config later — by `ao start <URL>`, `ao project add`, manual YAML edits, web `POST /api/projects` — are visible to the dashboard but **not polled** by the running daemon.

Concretely, for a project not in the daemon's startup scope:

- Activity state (`active` ↔ `idle` ↔ `waiting_input` ↔ `blocked` ↔ `stuck`) does not transition.
- PR state (`pr_open` → `ci_failed` / `mergeable` / `merged`) is not refreshed.
- Reactions (auto-merge, notifications, agent re-prompts on review comments, auto-cleanup) do not fire.
- Stale-runtime reconciliation (\`runtime_lost\`) does not run.

The current workaround is `ao stop && ao start <id>`, which is disruptive when other projects have live sessions.

PR #1466 calls this out explicitly when registering a new project against an already-running daemon — printing a yellow warning that the user must restart to pick up polling. That warning should go away.

## Proposed fix

Add a thin **project supervisor** alongside the lifecycle workers. The per-project polling loop stays exactly as-is; only its *scoping* becomes dynamic.

```
every 60s OR on fs.watch(globalConfigPath):
  configured = loadConfig(globalConfigPath).projects
  active     = listLifecycleWorkers()

  for id in configured \\ active:    # newly added projects
      ensureLifecycleWorker(config, id)

  for id in active \\ configured:    # removed projects
      stopLifecycleWorker(id)
```

### Where it lives

- New file: \`packages/cli/src/lib/project-supervisor.ts\`
- Started from \`runStartup()\` in \`packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts\` after the initial \`ensureLifecycleWorker()\` call.
- Stopped in the existing graceful-shutdown handler (Ctrl+C / \`ao stop\`).

### Wire-up

After registering a new project (e.g. in the URL flow added by PR #1466), the user-facing message changes from:

> ⚠ Lifecycle polling for \"X\" runs inside the long-lived ao start process, which is currently scoped to: Y. Run \`ao stop && ao start X\` to enable polling.

…to a simple:

> ✓ Lifecycle polling attached for \"X\" within ~60s.

## Risks and mitigations

### 1. GitHub API rate limit blow-up

Each tracker poll = \`listIssues\` + \`listPRs\` + per-PR enrichment. At 30s ticks across N registered projects:

| Projects | Calls/hr (authenticated) |
|---------:|-------------------------:|
| 5        | ~600                     |
| 10       | ~1200                    |
| 20       | ~2400                    |

Authenticated \`gh\` cap is 5000/hr — fine for typical use, but it climbs fast if users accumulate idle registry entries.

**Mitigation:** the supervisor should only attach a worker when the project has **at least one non-terminal session on disk**. Idle registry entries cost nothing. When a session is spawned via the dashboard, the supervisor's next tick attaches the worker. When the last session terminates, the worker is detached.

This keeps polling cost proportional to active work, not registry size.

### 2. Failure isolation

If one project's tracker token is revoked / its repo is deleted / its tmux backend is down, its lifecycle worker will throw on every tick. The existing per-project loop already swallows these — but the supervisor must not block on one bad project. Specifically:

- Supervisor reconciliation must run \`ensureLifecycleWorker\` calls in parallel, not serially.
- A worker that has thrown its initial setup should not block subsequent supervisor ticks.

### 3. Concurrency / config races

Two \`ao\` invocations could write the global config simultaneously. \`registerProjectInGlobalConfig\` already uses \`withFileLockSync\`, so writes are atomic. The supervisor only reads, so no new lock is needed — but a re-read mid-write will see one valid state or the other, never a half-written state.

### 4. fs.watch reliability on macOS

\`fs.watch\` on macOS is famously flaky for some filesystems. The supervisor should fall back to polling (60s) regardless of whether the watcher is active, treating \`fs.watch\` as a latency optimization, not the source of truth.

## What this does NOT change

- Plugin instances and runtime are unchanged.
- Per-project \`LifecycleManager\` is unchanged.
- The 30s default poll interval is unchanged (CLAUDE.md C-14 covers SSE; lifecycle is separate but should stay at the documented 30s).
- Nothing about session storage, identity, or the migration path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After \`ao start\`, registering a new project via any path (\`ao project add\`, \`ao start <URL>\` against a running daemon, manual YAML edit, dashboard \`POST /api/projects\`) results in lifecycle polling attaching within 60s, with no daemon restart.
- [ ] Removing a project from the global config detaches its lifecycle worker within 60s.
- [ ] Idle registry entries (no non-terminal sessions) do not cause GitHub API calls.
- [ ] One failing project's poll cycle does not stall others — verified by integration test that injects a failing tracker.
- [ ] Existing \`ao spawn\` warning (\"the running AO instance is not polling project X\") is removed once attached.
- [ ] The \"⚠ Lifecycle polling … requires ao stop && ao start\" warning printed by \`ao start <URL>\` (added in PR #1466) is removed.

## Out of scope

- Multi-instance / multi-host daemons.
- IPC between separate \`ao\` invocations (the supervisor reads disk, doesn't message).
- Reducing the 30s poll interval.

## References

- \`packages/cli/src/lib/lifecycle-service.ts\` — current per-project worker registry
- \`packages/cli/src/commands/spawn.ts:warnIfAONotRunning\` — the warning this issue removes
- PR #1466 — adds the URL/path register-while-running flow that surfaces this gap most visibly

## Summary

title: ao migrate-storage doesn't relink Codex session storage when worktrees move
body:
## Follow-up to PR #1466

Filing as the **Codex counterpart to PR #1466's commit `ef944356`** (Claude Code session-storage relink). Same root cause, different fix shape — Codex's storage model means the physical-rename trick used for Claude does not apply.

## Background

When `ao migrate-storage` moves a session's worktree from V1 to V2, the workspace cwd changes:

- V1: `~/.agent-orchestrator/{hash}-{project}/worktrees/{sid}`
- V2: `~/.agent-orchestrator/projects/{projectId}/worktrees/{sid}`

For Claude Code this orphaned `~/.claude/projects/<old-encoded>/` because the directory name encodes the cwd. Commit `ef944356` fixed this by renaming the dir.

For Codex the failure mode is the same (`getRestoreCommand` returns null, agent launches with no chat history) but the storage layout is different:

- Sessions live at `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl`.
- The cwd is recorded **inside** each JSONL's `session_meta` line as a string, not in any directory name.
- `findCodexSessionFile` (`packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/index.ts`) walks every JSONL and matches by exact string equality on `session_meta.cwd === workspacePath`.

After migration, `session_meta.cwd` in the existing JSONLs still points at the V1 path. `findCodexSessionFile(newWorkspacePath)` returns null. Codex launches fresh, no resume.

## Proposed fix

Two viable approaches; the issue is to pick one and ship it.

### Option A — content rewrite at migration time

For each `(oldWorkspacePath, newWorkspacePath)` pair captured during `migrate-storage`:

1. Walk `~/.codex/sessions/` (date-sharded; bounded depth, the plugin already enforces this).
2. For every JSONL, parse the first N lines (only `session_meta` lives near the top — the plugin already caps this with `SESSION_MATCH_SCAN_LINE_LIMIT`).
3. If `session_meta.cwd === oldWorkspacePath`, rewrite the file replacing only that field with `newWorkspacePath`. Preserve all other content byte-for-byte.

**Risk:** content surgery on potentially-large JSONL files (long conversations grow MBs). One bug here corrupts chat history. Mitigations:
- Atomic write via temp + rename.
- Only rewrite the single line that contains `session_meta`. Other lines are streamed through unchanged.
- Refuse to rewrite if the parsed `session_meta` JSON does not round-trip byte-equivalent under our parser (paranoia gate).
- Dry-run flag must report file count and paths without touching anything.

### Option B — plugin-side path-aliasing

Teach `findCodexSessionFile` to match against a list of candidate cwds, not just the current workspacePath. Source of the alias list:

- A small JSON file written by `migrate-storage` at `~/.agent-orchestrator/codex-cwd-aliases.json` keyed by current workspacePath, mapping to historical paths.
- The plugin reads this file once per call and considers `[currentPath, ...historicalAliases]` as matching keys.

**Pros:** zero risk to existing JSONLs. Reversible by deleting the alias file.
**Cons:** the plugin grows a side-channel dependency on a migration artifact. Performance: every `findCodexSessionFile` call now reads an extra file (cheap but non-zero).

**Recommendation:** Option A. Plugin behavior stays clean; the fix is one-shot at migration time and matches the model used for Claude.

## Where to add it

`packages/core/src/migration/storage-v2.ts`, alongside `relinkClaudeSessionStorage`. The `WorkspacePathMove[]` accumulator is already in place from commit `ef944356` — Codex relink reads the same list.

Add a new helper `relinkCodexSessionStorage(moves, dryRun, log): number` that:
- Returns 0 if `~/.codex/sessions/` does not exist.
- For each pair where `oldWorkspacePath !== newWorkspacePath`, scans JSONLs at bounded depth, rewrites matching `session_meta.cwd` lines, returns the count of files touched.

Add `codexSessionsRewritten: number` to `MigrationResult` and surface it in the migration summary.

Mirror the rollback step in `rollbackStorage` (rewriting cwd back from V2 to V1).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Happy path test: seed `~/.codex/sessions/<date>/rollout-uuid.jsonl` whose first line is `{"type":"session_meta","payload":{"cwd":"<v1-path>",...}}`. After `migrateStorage`, the same file's `session_meta.cwd` reads `<v2-path>`. All other lines in the file are byte-identical.
- [ ] Safety test: a JSONL whose `session_meta.cwd` doesn't match any migration pair is left untouched.
- [ ] Atomic write: a simulated mid-write crash leaves either the original file or the new file complete — never a half-written file. Verify with a fault-injection harness or by asserting tmpfile-rename semantics.
- [ ] `--dry-run` prints the file count and paths without modifying anything.
- [ ] `--rollback` reverses the rewrite (V2 cwd → V1 cwd) for the same set of files.
- [ ] No new performance regression for `findCodexSessionFile` in normal (post-migration) operation.

## Out of scope

- Content rewrites for any other JSONL field. Only `session_meta.cwd` is rewritten.
- Codex sessions that pre-date `session_meta` (older Codex versions). If detected, log and skip.
- Cross-version Codex format migration. This issue assumes the current `session_meta` schema.

## Reference

- Claude counterpart: PR #1466, commit ef944356 (`fix(migration): relink Claude Code session storage when worktrees move`).
- Surfaced by Skittle's QA on PR #1466 (Discord).

title: feat: add SQLite-backed activity event logging layer
body:
## Summary

This PR adds an operator-facing activity event log for AO so session and lifecycle behavior can be inspected after the fact.

**Activity event infrastructure**
- Adds a SQLite-backed activity event store with WAL mode, retention cleanup, FTS search, structured filters, and process-local dropped-event accounting.
- Sanitizes event data before storage and search indexing, including token/password-like keys and credential-bearing URLs.
- Exports the event write/query APIs from `@aoagents/ao-core`.

**CLI**
- Adds `ao events list`, `ao events search`, and `ao events stats`.
- Supports project/session/type/since/limit filters and a versioned JSON envelope.

title: bug(web): removed project reappears on dashboard — missing router.refresh() after DELETE
body:
## Bug Report

**Summary:** Clicking "Remove" on a project in the dashboard sidebar hides it temporarily (optimistic UI), but the project reappears after any state reset (component remount, navigation, SSE cycle).

## Root Cause

The removal flow has a broken data refresh path:

1. **`ProjectSidebar.tsx` (~line 236)** — `handleRemoveProject()` calls `DELETE /api/projects/{id}`, which succeeds on disk (YAML config is updated correctly)
2. **Optimistic hide** — adds project ID to `removedProjectIds` Set (client-side only)
3. **`projects` prop is static SSR data** — computed once in `page.tsx` via `getDashboardPageData()`, never re-fetched after mutation
4. **Cleanup useEffect (~line 163-172)** expects `projects` to eventually update to reflect the deletion, but it never does
5. **Any state reset** (React remount, navigation, SSE refresh) wipes `removedProjectIds` back to empty → project reappears

## The Fix

In `ProjectSidebar.tsx`, after the DELETE response succeeds, add `router.refresh()` to force Next.js to re-fetch server component data:

```typescript
// After successful DELETE
await response.json();
router.refresh();  // Force server component re-render with fresh data
```

## Files Involved

- `packages/web/src/components/ProjectSidebar.tsx` — missing `router.refresh()` call
- `packages/web/src/app/page.tsx` — static SSR prop (no client-side refetch mechanism)
- `packages/web/src/lib/dashboard-page-data.ts` — `getDashboardPageData()` only runs on server render

## Reproduction

1. Start AO dashboard with multiple projects
2. Click "Remove" on any project in the sidebar
3. Project disappears temporarily
4. Navigate away and back, or wait for SSE refresh cycle
5. Project reappears — was never actually removed from the UI state

## Expected Behavior

Project is permanently removed from the sidebar after clicking "Remove" and confirming.

title: fix(core): preserve reaction tracker across status oscillation
body:
Closes #1409

## Summary

The lifecycle manager's reaction system has a retry + escalate mechanism: when CI fails, it sends a message to the agent, and after N retries (`retries: 2` = 3 attempts), escalates to a human. But the retry budget was resetting on every status oscillation, causing infinite message spam and preventing escalation.

**Three root causes fixed:**

1. **Reaction tracker cleared unconditionally on status exit** (`lifecycle-manager.ts:1878-1885`). Every transition away from `ci_failed` deleted the tracker. When CI failed again, a fresh tracker was created with `attempts: 0`. The retry budget never exhausted.

2. **Merge conflict dispatch bypassed `executeReaction` entirely** (`lifecycle-manager.ts:1654-1676`). `maybeDispatchMergeConflicts()` called `sessionManager.send()` directly, so the `escalateAfter: "15m"` config for merge-conflicts was dead code — escalation could never trigger.

3. **Merge conflict tracker cleared on resolve** (`lifecycle-manager.ts:1680`). When conflicts resolved, both the reaction tracker and dedup flag were cleared. When conflicts recurred, the escalation budget started from zero.

## Implementation Plan

### Change 1: Persistent reaction keys

Added `PERSISTENT_REACTION_KEYS = new Set(["ci-failed", "merge-conflicts"])`. These keys represent conditions that can oscillate (CI failing→pending→failing, conflicts resolving→recurring). Their trackers survive status exit so the escalation budget accumulates across oscillations.

At the status-exit clear (line 1883), persistent keys are now excluded:
```typescript
if (oldReactionKey && !PERSISTENT_REACTION_KEYS.has(oldReactionKey)) {
  clearReactionTracker(session.id, oldReactionKey);
}
```

### Change 2: Route merge conflicts through `executeReaction`

Replaced direct `sessionManager.send()` / `notifyHuman()` calls in `maybeDispatchMergeConflicts()` with a call to `executeReaction()`. This enables the existing `escalateAfter: "15m"` config that was previously ignored. Dynamic base branch messages are built before the call via an enriched config.

### Change 3: Preserve merge-conflicts tracker on resolve

When conflicts resolve, only the dedup flag (`lastMergeConflictDispatched`) is cleared — allowing re-notification if conflicts recur. The reaction tracker is preserved so the escalation budget continues counting. Terminal-state clearing (PR closed/merged) remains unchanged.

### Behavior after fix

**CI failure oscillation:**
```
Poll 1: CI failing  → send to agent       (attempts: 1)
Poll 2: CI pending  → tracker PRESERVED
Poll 3: CI failing  → send to agent       (attempts: 2)
Poll 4: CI pending  → tracker PRESERVED
Poll 5: CI failing  → attempts 3 > retries 2 → ESCALATE TO HUMAN
```

**Merge conflict oscillation:**
```
Conflict 1: send to agent (attempts: 1, firstTriggered = T)
Resolved:   dedup flag cleared, tracker preserved
Conflict 2: send to agent (attempts: 2)
Resolved:   dedup flag cleared, tracker preserved
Conflict 3: if T + 15min elapsed → ESCALATE TO HUMAN
```

## Test plan

- [x] **CI failure oscillation test**: Simulates 3 oscillations (ci_failed → pr_open → ci_failed). Verifies agent receives messages on attempts 1-2, then human is notified via escalation on attempt 3.
- [x] **Merge conflict time-based escalation test**: Simulates conflict → resolve → recur with `vi.useFakeTimers()`. Verifies escalation triggers after the `escalateAfter` window.
- [x] **Non-persistent keys test**: Verifies `changes-requested` tracker still clears on status exit (only persistent keys are protected).
- [x] All 917 existing tests pass
- [x] Full typecheck passes across all packages

title: fix(opencode): close stdin to prevent process leak on poll
body:
The lifecycle manager polls `opencode session list --format json` every few seconds via execFileAsync. opencode reads from stdin when piped and hangs forever when it's left open, so each poll orphaned a ~150MB process. Within minutes the box would OOM.

Use a dedicated runOpencode wrapper that closes the child's stdin immediately after spawn. Other execFileAsync callers (tmux, ps) keep the existing promisified path.

Test mock updated to use standard execFile callback semantics (err, stdout, stderr as separate args) and provide a util.promisify.custom implementation for promisified callers.

title: fix(web): refresh session sidebar from local metadata writes
body:
## Summary
- add TanStack Query to the web app provider and use it only for the session-detail sidebar sessions query
- keep the last successful sidebar session list visible when a background refresh fails
- add a sidebar-only `/api/sessions?view=sidebar` path that reads local session metadata via `listLocal()` instead of the live/enriched path
- make `/api/events` and `/api/sessions/patches` local-only with no-store responses so sidebar membership snapshots avoid runtime and agent probes
- watch AO project session metadata directories from the mux WebSocket server and broadcast a fresh sessions snapshot when session JSON files change
- pass the actual sidebar fetch error through to ProjectSidebar for better diagnostics

Closes #1410

## Why
The stale sidebar was not because local JSON reads are inherently slow. The slow path was that the detail-page sidebar and membership signals still depended on APIs that could touch runtime liveness, agent probes, OpenCode discovery, and metadata enrichment. Polling faster helped a little, but it did not make burst-spawn changes arrive when AO writes the local session metadata.

This PR makes the sidebar data path local-only and adds a direct local signal: when AO writes a project session metadata JSON file, the mux server debounces briefly, fetches `/api/sessions/patches`, and pushes that snapshot to connected browsers. The React Query sidebar then overlays known lightweight patch changes and refetches the full local sidebar list when membership changes, which is the piece needed for newly spawned workers to appear quickly.

title: fix(core): deliver enriched review content on changes_requested transition
body:
## Summary

Fixes a bug where the agent never received actual review comment content when a PR transitioned to `changes_requested`. The agent only got a generic message — *"There are review comments on your PR. Details will follow shortly."* — but the detailed review bodies (file paths, line numbers, authors, comment text) never followed.

Closes #1558

## Root Cause

The review dispatch in `maybeDispatchReviewBacklog` has two paths:

| Path | When | What it sends |
|------|------|---------------|
| **Transition reaction** | Status transitions to `changes_requested` | Generic message from config |
| **Backlog dispatch** | Comment fingerprint changes | Enriched content via `formatReviewCommentsMessage()` |

On the first transition, the transition reaction fired (generic message), then the backlog dispatch recorded the fingerprint hash as "already dispatched" — **without ever sending the actual comment content**. The deduplication logic then blocked the enriched dispatch from ever firing for those comments:

1. **Branch B** (lines 1477-1486): recorded `lastPendingReviewDispatchHash` when the transition reaction succeeded, burning the hash without delivering content
2. **Transition guard** (line 1488): `!(oldStatus !== newStatus && newStatus === "changes_requested")` explicitly skipped the enriched dispatch during the transition poll

This is unlike `ci-failed`, which enriches its transition reaction with actual CI check details from the batch cache. `changes-requested` never got the same treatment — review threads are fetched separately in `maybeDispatchReviewBacklog`, not in the batch PR enrichment.

## Fix

- **Remove Branch B** — the block that recorded the dispatch hash when the transition reaction succeeded without sending enriched content
- **Remove the transition guard** — so the backlog dispatch fires in the same poll cycle as the transition
- **Update default message** — remove the "Details will follow shortly" promise since details now arrive immediately

After the fix, the enriched review content (file paths, line numbers, authors, comment bodies, thread IDs) is dispatched in the same poll cycle as the transition. The agent receives two messages back-to-back: the generic transition notification followed immediately by the detailed review content. Subsequent polls skip dispatch because the fingerprint hash matches — no duplicates.

## Files Changed

- `packages/core/src/lifecycle-manager.ts` — removed premature hash recording and transition guard from `maybeDispatchReviewBacklog`
- `packages/core/src/config.ts` — updated default `changes-requested` message
- `packages/core/src/__tests__/lifecycle-manager.test.ts` — updated test to verify enriched content is delivered on transition

## Test plan

- [x] All 1006 core tests pass (`pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test`)
- [ ] Verify agent receives detailed review comments on first `changes_requested` transition
- [ ] Verify no duplicate dispatch on subsequent polls with unchanged comments
- [ ] Verify new comments arriving while in `changes_requested` trigger a fresh enriched dispatch

title: bug(scm-github): ETag guards and GraphQL batch spam console with warnings on expected HTTP 304 responses
body: ## Bug The ETag guards and GraphQL batch error handling in `packages/plugins/scm-github/src/graphql-batch.ts` use raw `console.warn()`/`console.error()` that fire on every poll cycle. HTTP 304 ("Not Modified") is the **expected** response when the ETag matches — it means nothing changed — but the catch blocks don't distinguish between 304 cache hits and real errors. This floods the orchestrator terminal with noise every poll cycle. ### Screenshot ## All Affected Locations There are **4 raw console statements** in `graphql-batch.ts` that bypass the observer logging pattern: | # | Line | Level | Message | Trigger | |---|------|-------|---------|---------| | 1 | 460 | `console.warn` | `[ETag Guard 1] PR list check failed for ${repoKey}: ${errorMsg}` | HTTP 304 on `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls` | | 2 | 525-527 | `console.warn` | `[ETag Guard 2] Commit status check failed for ${commitKey}: ${errorMsg}` | HTTP 304 on `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}/check-runs` | | 3 | 587 | `console.warn` | `[ETag Guard 3] Review comments check failed for ${cacheKey}: ${errorMsg}` | HTTP 304 on `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/comments` | | 4 | 1156 | `console.error` | `[GraphQL Batch Warning] Batch enrichment partially failed: ${errorMsg}` | GraphQL batch query exceptions | Meanwhile, the **other logging in the same file** (lines 1071-1082, 1138) correctly uses `observer?.log("info", ...)` with proper log level management. ## Root Cause All three ETag guard functions (`checkPRListETag`, `checkCommitStatusETag`, `checkReviewCommentsETag`) call `gh api` with an `If-None-Match` header. When the content hasn't changed, GitHub returns 304 and `gh` exits with a non-zero status. The catch blocks fire and log a warning — but they don't check whether the error is a 304 (expected) or an actual failure (network error, auth issue, 5xx). Example from line 460: ```typescript // eslint-disable-next-line no-console -- Observability logging for ETag errors console.warn(`[ETag Guard 1] PR list check failed for ${repoKey}: ${errorMsg}`); ``` ## Expected Behavior - HTTP 304 should be handled silently (or at debug level via observer) - Only actual errors (network failures, 4xx other than 304, 5xx) should warn - All logging should use `observer?.log()` instead of raw `console.*` for consistency ## Fix 1. Check for `304` in the error message before warning — skip or downgrade to debug for 304 2. Migrate all 4 instances from raw `console.warn()`/`console.error()` to `observer?.log()` (consistent with the rest of the file) 3. Only log at `"warn"` level for genuine errors, not cache hits ## Impact - **Noise:** Orchestrator terminal becomes unreadable due to warning spam on every poll cycle (3 warnings per cycle × every 5s) - **Misleading:** Operators may think something is broken when the system is working correctly - **No functional impact:** The 304 path works correctly despite the warnings — it just shouldn't log as a failure

title: chore: align workspace package.json versions with npm registry
body:
## What

Aligns committed `package.json` versions with what's actually published on npm. The in-tree files had drifted to `0.2.5` while releases (via Changesets) had already pushed most packages to `0.3.0`.

The original motivation was the `ao update available` prompt, which compares the installed `@aoagents/ao` version to the npm registry. Source of truth: `packages/cli/src/lib/update-check.ts` — `getCurrentVersion()` reads `@aoagents/ao/package.json`, and `fetchLatestVersion()` queries `registry.npmjs.org/@aoagents/ao`. So `packages/ao` is the only file the prompt strictly needs. But while we're here, every other workspace `package.json` was also stale relative to what's published, so this PR catches them all up at once.

## Version changes

| Bump | Packages |
|---|---|
| `0.2.5 → 0.3.0` | `ao`, `cli`, `core`, `web`, `agent-aider`, `agent-claude-code`, `agent-codex`, `agent-opencode`, `notifier-composio`, `notifier-desktop`, `notifier-slack`, `notifier-webhook`, `runtime-process`, `runtime-tmux`, `scm-github`, `terminal-iterm2`, `terminal-web`, `tracker-github`, `tracker-linear`, `workspace-clone`, `workspace-worktree` |
| `0.2.5 → 0.2.6` | `notifier-discord`, `notifier-openclaw`, `scm-gitlab`, `tracker-gitlab` |
| `0.1.0 → 0.1.1` | `agent-cursor` |

Each target version matches what `npm view <pkg> version` returns today.

## Test fixes

- `packages/plugins/agent-codex/src/package-version.test.ts`: hardcoded `0.2.5` → `0.3.0` to match the new manifest.
- `packages/cli/__tests__/lib/update-check.test.ts` (`uses cache when fresh and does not call fetch`): the test cached `latestVersion: "0.3.0"` and asserted `isOutdated === true`. That only worked while the repo's installed version was `< 0.3.0`. Once `packages/ao` reaches `0.3.0` (and pnpm makes it resolvable from cli at test time via `node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules/@aoagents/ao`), `getCurrentVersion()` returns `0.3.0`, the comparison flips to false, and the assertion fails. Fix: cache `latestVersion: "99.0.0"` so the test stays meaningful regardless of the repo's real version. The three invariants it guards are unchanged: cache is read, version comparison works, and no network call is made.

## Why

- **The `ao update available` prompt was effectively comparing `0.2.5` (committed) against `0.3.0` (registry) and reporting "outdated" forever** — even on fresh installs.
- The committed files were a misleading source of truth: `git log` and `package.json` disagreed with npm.
- Future Changesets releases work cleanly when the in-tree starting point matches the last published version.

title: Dashboard can lose CSS/JS when production .next artifacts are rebuilt or deleted while ao start is running
body:
## Summary

When AO is started via `ao start`, the dashboard can end up rendering as mostly raw, unstyled HTML if the production Next.js build artifacts under `packages/web/.next` are removed or replaced while the dashboard server is still running.

Observed locally:
- Dashboard at `http://localhost:3000/` rendered with browser-default styles.
- HTML referenced `/_next/static/css/397ea3e60645d3f3.css`.
- Requesting that CSS URL returned `HTTP 400 Bad Request` with a Next.js HTML error page instead of CSS.
- `packages/web/.next` was missing, while `packages/web/.next-dev` existed.
- The dashboard process was still running via `ao start` / `next start`.

## Why this matters

`ao start` runs the dashboard in optimized production mode by default from a source checkout. That server depends on the mutable `packages/web/.next` directory. If a later build/clean operation deletes or replaces `.next` while the dashboard is live, the server can continue serving HTML but fail to serve static CSS/JS assets.

This creates a confusing partially-working state:
- dashboard loads
- sessions may still appear
- styling is gone
- terminal bridge reconnect noise may appear, but the underlying tmux sessions can still be alive

## Likely trigger

`packages/web/package.json` has:

```json
"prebuild": "rimraf .next dist-server"
```

So commands like `pnpm build`, `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web build`, `pnpm clean`, or rebuild paths can remove `.next` while a dashboard started by `ao start` is still serving from it.

## Expected behavior

AO should not allow a live production dashboard to keep serving from build artifacts that are being deleted or replaced.

## Possible fixes

- Stop the running dashboard before `ao start --rebuild` deletes/rebuilds `.next`.
- Add a guard to the web `prebuild` script that refuses to delete `.next` if an AO dashboard is running from the same checkout.
- Use an atomic build/swap strategy for production dashboard artifacts.
- Add a startup or health check that verifies CSS/static asset serving, not just `BUILD_ID` existence.

## Current workaround

Stop AO/dashboard, rebuild, then start again:

```bash
ao stop
pnpm build
ao start
```

or use the appropriate rebuild flow after ensuring the dashboard is stopped.

title: ao update fails refreshing launcher when old global ao shim exists
body:
## Summary

`ao update` can successfully fast-forward, install dependencies, and rebuild packages, then fail at the final launcher refresh step if a user already has a global `ao` binary from the older package name (`@composio/ao-cli`).

The current script labels the first `npm link` failure as a permission problem and retries with `sudo`, but npm still fails with `EEXIST` because `/opt/homebrew/bin/ao` already exists.

## User-facing output

```text
Refreshing ao launcher...
  Permission denied. Retrying with sudo...
Password:
npm error code EEXIST
npm error path /opt/homebrew/bin/ao
npm error EEXIST: file already exists
npm error File exists: /opt/homebrew/bin/ao
npm error Remove the existing file and try again, or run npm
npm error with --force to overwrite files recklessly.
```

On the affected machine, the existing shim was:

```text
/opt/homebrew/bin/ao -> ../lib/node_modules/@composio/ao-cli/dist/index.js
```

The repo has since moved to the `@aoagents/ao` launcher package, so users with the old global shim can hit this during update.

## Why this matters

The expensive parts of the update already completed by the time this fails:

- `git fetch` / `git pull --ff-only`
- `pnpm install`
- clean rebuild of core, CLI, and web

The user is left with a failed update command and unclear guidance, even though the remaining work is only replacing the global launcher shim.

## Expected behavior

`ao update` should refresh the launcher successfully even when a stale global `ao` binary already exists from the old package name.

## Proposed fix

Use forced npm linking for source-checkout launcher refreshes:

```bash
npm link --force
sudo npm link --force
```

Also update the message so the sudo retry is not described as “Permission denied” for every possible npm failure. Something like this is more accurate:

```text
Launcher refresh needs elevated permissions. Retrying with sudo...
```

The same launcher-refresh logic exists in multiple places and should stay consistent:

- `packages/cli/src/assets/scripts/ao-update.sh`
- `packages/cli/src/assets/scripts/ao-doctor.sh`
- `scripts/setup.sh`

## Acceptance criteria

- `ao update` overwrites a stale existing global `ao` shim instead of failing with `EEXIST`.
- `ao doctor --fix` and `scripts/setup.sh` use the same robust launcher refresh behavior.
- Error copy no longer claims “Permission denied” for non-permission npm failures.
- Regression coverage simulates an existing `ao` shim / `EEXIST` style failure and verifies `npm link --force` is used.

title: Make update checks install-method aware for npm and git/source installs
body:
## Summary

`ao start` can show misleading update prompts because the update checker currently treats npm latest as the source of truth even when the user is running AO from a git/source checkout.

Example observed from a source checkout on `main`:

```text
Update available: 0.2.5 → 0.3.0 — Run: ao update
```

But the checkout was already at `origin/main`, and the repo package versions still reported `0.2.5`. In this install mode, `ao update` pulls git `main`; it does not install npm latest. So comparing against npm latest creates a false prompt.

Related: #1540
Related launcher-shim issue: #1591

## Desired behavior

Update checks should use the same source of truth that the user's install method uses for updates.

### npm global installs

If AO is installed via:

```bash
npm install -g @aoagents/ao
```

Then the update checker should compare the installed version against npm registry latest for `@aoagents/ao`.

Prompt should recommend:

```bash
npm install -g @aoagents/ao@latest
```

### pnpm global installs

If AO is installed via pnpm global, compare against npm registry latest and recommend:

```bash
pnpm add -g @aoagents/ao@latest
```

### git/source checkout installs

If AO is running from a cloned repo / source checkout, npm latest should not be used for the startup prompt.

Instead, compare the local git state against the remote branch that `ao update` would pull, usually:

```bash
git fetch origin main
git rev-parse HEAD
git rev-parse origin/main
```

If local `HEAD` is behind the update branch, then prompt with:

```text
Update available from origin/main — Run: ao update
```

If local `HEAD` matches the remote update branch, do not show an update prompt, even if npm has a newer published version.

## Problem details

There are two different update channels:

- npm users update from the npm registry
- source users update from git

A single cache entry like:

```json
{
  "latestVersion": "0.3.0",
  "currentVersionAtCheck": "0.2.5"
}
```

is unsafe because it can be produced under one install method and consumed under another. For example, an npm latest cache can make a source checkout repeatedly show an update prompt that `ao update` cannot resolve.

## Proposed fix

1. Make the update-check cache install-method aware.
   - Include `installMethod` in the cache data.
   - Ignore cache entries whose install method differs from the current install method.
   - Treat older cache entries without `installMethod` as unsafe for git/source installs.

2. Split latest-version resolution by install method.
   - `npm-global` and `pnpm-global`: use npm registry latest.
   - `git`: use git remote branch state, not npm latest.
   - `unknown`: either use npm registry with conservative messaging, or suppress startup prompts if install method cannot be resolved confidently.

3. Keep recommended commands aligned with install method.
   - git: `ao update`
   - npm-global: `npm install -g @aoagents/ao@latest`
   - pnpm-global: `pnpm add -g @aoagents/ao@latest`

4. Ensure startup notifier and `ao doctor` use the same install-aware cache semantics.

## Acceptance criteria

- A git/source checkout at `origin/main` does not show `0.2.5 → 0.3.0` just because npm latest is `0.3.0`.
- A git/source checkout behind `origin/main` does show an update prompt recommending `ao update`.
- npm global installs still show npm registry updates and recommend `npm install -g @aoagents/ao@latest`.
- pnpm global installs still show npm registry updates and recommend `pnpm add -g @aoagents/ao@latest`.
- Cache entries are scoped by install method and cannot leak between npm/global and git/source installs.
- Tests cover npm-global, pnpm-global, git/source current, git/source behind, stale cache from another install method, and legacy cache entries without `installMethod`.

## Notes

A conservative short-term mitigation is to suppress npm-registry prompts for git/source installs. The complete fix should compare source installs against the git branch that `ao update` actually pulls.

title: bug(web): stale session detail page spam-errors after project switch — dead terminal reconnect loop
body:
## Repro

1. `ao start` on Project A → open session detail page in browser
2. `ao stop` → `ao start` on Project B (different project)
3. Old browser tab is still on the Project A session detail page
4. Terminal gets spammed with errors — `Session not found` / connection failures in the server console

## Root Cause — Three Interacting Bugs

### Bug 1: MuxProvider re-opens dead terminals on reconnect (`MuxProvider.tsx:124-134`)

When the WebSocket reconnects, it blindly re-sends `open` for every entry in `openedTerminalsRef.current`. After a project switch, the old session's tmux session is gone → server throws `"Session not found"` → sends error back. MuxProvider logs it (line 178) but **never removes the dead entry from `openedTerminalsRef`**.

### Bug 2: Context value change triggers terminal recreation (`useXtermTerminal.ts:335-348`)

When mux status changes to `"connected"`, the `contextValue` useMemo in `MuxProvider.tsx:349-360` produces a new object (because `status` is a dep). `useMux()` returns new references → the main `useEffect` in `useXtermTerminal` sees deps changed → **destroys and recreates the entire xterm instance + WebSocket subscription** → re-opens the dead session → error again. This can cycle every time mux sessions update (every 3s from `SessionBroadcaster` polling).

### Bug 3: 404 doesn't show "session not found" after first successful load (`sessions/[id]/page.tsx:505-513`)

```ts
if (normalizedMessage.includes("session not found") || ...) {
  if (!hasLoadedSessionRef.current) {   // ← only triggers on FIRST load
    setSessionMissing(true);
  }
}
```

The polling loop (line 689-696) fires every 2s calling `fetchSession()`. After AO switches projects, the API returns 404 — but since `hasLoadedSessionRef` is already `true` from when the page originally loaded the session, the 404 is **silently swallowed**. The page never shows the "Session not found" error state, so it keeps retrying forever.

## Fix (3 parts)

### Fix 1: MuxProvider — clean up dead terminals on error
When receiving a `terminal.error` message with a permanent failure (e.g. "Session not found"), remove the entry from `openedTerminalsRef` so it doesn't get re-opened on next reconnect. Also clean up from `subscribersRef`.

File: `packages/web/src/providers/MuxProvider.tsx` — in the `msg.type === "error"` branch (line 177-178).

### Fix 2: useXtermTerminal — don't recreate terminal on mux status change
Stabilize the effect deps so a mux reconnect doesn't tear down and recreate the entire terminal. The mux functions (`subscribeTerminal`, `openTerminal`, etc.) are already stable `useCallback(fn, [])` — the problem is the `contextValue` useMemo producing a new object when `status` changes. Either:
- Split `status` out of the contextValue useMemo so terminal functions stay referentially stable, OR
- Use `useRef` for the mux functions inside `useXtermTerminal` to decouple from the effect deps, OR
- Handle the "Session not found" error from the `open` response by surfacing it up to the page component

File: `packages/web/src/providers/MuxProvider.tsx` line 349-360 and/or `packages/web/src/components/terminal/useXtermTerminal.ts` line 335-348.

### Fix 3: Session detail page — handle 404 after successful load
Remove (or relax) the `hasLoadedSessionRef.current` guard so that if the session was previously loaded but is now gone, it still sets `sessionMissing = true` and shows the error state instead of silently retrying forever.

```diff
 if (normalizedMessage.includes("session not found") || ...) {
-  if (!hasLoadedSessionRef.current) {
     setSessionMissing(true);
-  }
   setLoading(false);
   return;
 }
```

File: `packages/web/src/app/sessions/[id]/page.tsx` line 505-513.

## Severity
High — causes terminal spam and server log noise, makes old tabs unusable, requires manual tab close or page refresh to stop. Common when switching between projects during development.
