title: fix(core): read legacy key=value metadata in .json session files
body: ## Issue `ao start` can fail while a valid canonical orchestrator session is already alive and recoverable. Observed failure: In the reported case, tmux still had a live `ao-orchestrator` session and the metadata file existed at: ```text ~/.agent-orchestrator/projects/agent-orchestrator_48321dec7a/sessions/ao-orchestrator.json ``` But the file was not JSON. It contained legacy `key=value` metadata under a `.json` filename: ```text codexThreadId=019df929-1773-7720-b07d-08e3cb9851fb codexModel=gpt-5.4 status=working runtimeHandle={"id":"ao-orchestrator","runtimeName":"tmux","data":{"createdAt":1778013362949,"workspacePath":"/Users/yyovil/Projects/agent-orchestrator"}} tmuxName=ao-orchestrator ``` The current JSON metadata reader treats that file as missing, while the reservation path treats the same file as existing. That makes the error message self-contradictory: it tells the user to use `ensureOrchestrator()`, but `ensureOrchestrator()` already failed to read the existing session. This is related to #1661, but distinct. #1661 covers an empty stale reservation file. This bug covers a non-empty legacy-format metadata file that contains useful restore state and should not be deleted as if it were empty junk. ## Affected Package - Package path: `packages/core` - npm package: `@aoagents/ao-core` - Surface area: metadata reading, canonical orchestrator startup, `ao start` - Shared code touched: `packages/core/src/metadata.ts`, likely tests under `packages/core/src/__tests__/metadata.test.ts` and/or `packages/core/src/__tests__/session-manager/spawn.test.ts` ## Reproduction 1. Create or retain a canonical orchestrator metadata file named like `sessions/ao-orchestrator.json`. 2. Make its contents legacy `key=value` metadata rather than JSON, for example with `role=orchestrator`, `status=working`, `runtimeHandle={...}`, and `tmuxName=ao-orchestrator`. 3. Ensure the matching tmux session exists, or simply run the metadata-level check below. 4. Run `ao start` for that project. ## Current Result `ao start` cannot reuse/restore the session. Internally, `readMetadata()` and `readMetadataRaw()` return `null`, but `reserveSessionId()` returns `false` because the file exists. Confirmed with the installed metadata module against the live file: ```json { "readMetadata": null, "readMetadataRaw": null, "reserveSessionId": false } ``` ## Expected Result AO should parse legacy `key=value` content inside `.json` session files, recover the existing canonical orchestrator metadata, and let `ensureOrchestrator()` reuse or restore the session. A later metadata update can rewrite the file in the current JSON format. The important part is that startup should not strand a live session because the filename and content format disagree. ## Evidence Relevant code path: - `packages/core/src/metadata.ts`: `parseMetadataContent()` currently only attempts `JSON.parse()` and returns `null` on non-JSON content. - `packages/core/src/metadata.ts`: `readMetadata()` / `readMetadataRaw()` therefore treat legacy `key=value` content as missing. - `packages/core/src/metadata.ts`: `reserveSessionId()` uses `O_EXCL` on the same `.json` path and returns `false` when the file exists. - `packages/core/src/session-manager.ts`: `ensureOrchestratorInternal()` calls `get(sessionId)`, sees no existing session, then falls through to `spawnOrchestrator()`, which hits the reservation failure. > [!NOTE] > The following is the fix spec for AI agents. ## Steps 1. Open `packages/core/src/metadata.ts` and trace the read path for `readMetadata()`, `readMetadataRaw()`, `mutateMetadata()`, and `reserveSessionId()`. 2. Fix the root cause with the smallest change: when metadata content is not JSON, parse legacy `key=value` content using the existing `parseKeyValueContent()` helper instead of returning `null` unconditionally. 3. Preserve true corrupt JSON behavior. If content appears to start as JSON but fails to parse, keep treating it as corrupt/missing or preserve current corrupt-file handling. 4. Add focused tests proving a `.json` file with `key=value` metadata is readable through both `readMetadata()` and `readMetadataRaw()`. 5. Add or update a session-manager regression test proving `ensureOrchestrator()` reuses/restores a canonical orchestrator represented by legacy `key=value` content in `sessions/.json`. 6. Commit only `packages/core/src/metadata.ts` and closely related tests. No unrelated cleanup. ## Validation - Package-level test: `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test -- metadata` - Session-manager regression: `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test -- session-manager/spawn` - Package-level typecheck: `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core typecheck` ## Constraints - Keep the scope inside `packages/core` unless a caller genuinely needs adjustment. - Do not solve this by deleting non-empty legacy metadata files. Those files can contain useful restore state like `codexThreadId`, `runtimeHandle`, and `tmuxName`. - Preserve the current JSON metadata format for new writes. - Preserve existing public APIs and config shapes. - Treat #1661 as adjacent prior art, not the complete fix for this case. ## Acceptance - `readMetadataRaw(sessionsDir, "ao-orchestrator")` returns legacy fields from a `key=value` `ao-orchestrator.json` file. - `readMetadata(sessionsDir, "ao-orchestrator")` returns a non-null metadata object with `role`, `tmuxName`, `runtimeHandle`, and derived/restored status when present. - `ensureOrchestrator({ projectId })` does not call `spawnOrchestrator()` for an existing canonical orchestrator represented by a legacy-format `.json` metadata file. - `ao start` prints that it is using/restoring the existing orchestrator instead of failing with `Orchestrator session "ao-orchestrator" already exists`.

title: fix(lifecycle): preserve terminal PR association across restore + harden detectPR (closes #1724)
body:
## Summary

Three layered fixes for #1724, where a restored worker session whose PR had merged got silently re-associated with an unrelated fork PR (in the reported repro: `ao-179` (release worker for #1723) ended up polling CI/reviews for fork PR #643 after restore).

Per-commit:

1. **`fix(scm-github): drop fork PRs and default-branch sessions from detectPR`** — `detectPR` now (a) returns `null` when `session.branch === project.defaultBranch`, and (b) requests `headRepositoryOwner` from `gh pr list` and discards PRs whose head owner differs from the repo owner. The `gh pr list --head <branch>` filter previously matched any PR with that head ref name across all forks.
2. **`fix(lifecycle): skip detectPR for sessions whose PR is already merged`** — lifecycle-manager short-circuits `scm.detectPR` when `session.lifecycle.pr.state === "merged"`. Branch drift between poll cycles (agent runs `git checkout main`, branch metadata hook fires, lifecycle observes branch=main) was the trigger that let detectPR run against the default branch and pick up unrelated PRs. Closed (unmerged) PRs intentionally still go through detectPR so the existing follow-up-PR rediscovery flow is preserved.
3. **`fix(session-manager): refuse to restore sessions with merged/closed PRs`** — restore now throws `SessionNotRestorableError` up-front when the session's PR is in a terminal state. Previously restore silently cleared `lifecycle.pr.*` and reset `session.state` to `working`, which combined with branch drift caused the bug. The dead clear-on-restore block has been removed.

## Investigation notes

- Repro metadata at `~/.agent-orchestrator/projects/agent-orchestrator/sessions/ao-179.json` showed: `branch: "main"`, `lifecycle.pr.number: 643`, `lifecycle.pr.state: "open"`, `agentReportedPrUrl: ".../pull/1723"`.
- `lifecycle-manager.ts:657-662` previously guarded detectPR by `session.pr` truthiness; once `repairSessionMetadataOnRead` (session-manager.ts:623-665) cleared `pr` for duplicate-PR-attached sessions, detectPR ran unguarded against `session.branch="main"` and matched fork PRs (`gh pr list --head main` returns #643 by MayurVirkar and #415 by zvictor).
- `scm-github/src/index.ts::detectPR` requested `--head <branch>` without owner filtering — the entry point for the fork-match.
- The exact code path that promoted `branch` from `chore/release-0.6.0` → `"main"` is the agent-side metadata hook (`agent-claude-code/src/index.ts:188-200`) firing on a `git checkout main` invocation post-merge. It is not pinpointed in this PR because the three fixes here neutralize the impact regardless of how the branch drifted.

## Invariants preserved

- **scm-github:** `detectPR` semantics unchanged for non-default branches with same-repo PRs (existing tests still green).
- **lifecycle:** sessions with `pr.state` in `{"open", "none"}` continue to be auto-detected; the existing `closed`-PR + branch-switch follow-up-detection test still passes; orchestrator/auto-detect-off opt-outs continue to take precedence.
- **session-manager:** `isRestorable` semantics unchanged for terminated/done/runtime-lost; only the PR-terminal sub-case now refuses with an explicit reason. Workers with `pr.state` of `"open"`/`"none"` still restore normally.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — clean
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test` — 1102 unit tests pass; 6 unrelated FTS5 failures stem from a missing `better-sqlite3` native binding in the local sandbox (pre-existing, not caused by this PR)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-scm-github test` — 172 tests pass
- [x] New regression tests:
  - `scm-github`: same-repo PR preferred when both fork and same-repo PRs match; fork-only matches return `null`; `branch === defaultBranch` short-circuits without calling `gh`
  - `lifecycle-manager`: merged-PR session does not call `detectPR`
  - `session-manager`: restoring a session with `status: "merged"` rejects with `/is merged/`
- [ ] CI

Closes #1724.

title: fix(core): sm.list() no longer writes terminated state to disk
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1735

- **`sm.list()` no longer persists `terminated` to disk** — it now writes `detecting` state with `runtime_lost` reason, so the lifecycle manager's `resolveProbeDecision` pipeline remains the single authority on terminal decisions. A single `isAlive()` failure no longer permanently kills a session.
- **`/api/sessions/patches` now calls `listCached()` instead of `list()`** — the dashboard's 3s poll was the most dangerous caller, probing runtimes ~10x more often than the lifecycle manager. The cache TTL (35s) aligns with the lifecycle manager's 30s poll cycle.
- Updated CLAUDE.md invariants to reflect the new behavior.

## What was happening

`sm.list()` detected a dead runtime via `isAlive()` and immediately persisted `session.state = "terminated"` with `reason = "runtime_lost"` to disk. This bypassed the lifecycle manager's carefully designed probe pipeline which evaluates three independent signals (runtime, process, activity) and routes 4/5 outcomes to `detecting` (retry). Only unanimous agreement across all signals produces a terminal decision.

The dashboard's `/api/sessions/patches` endpoint polled every 3s calling `sm.list()` directly — so a single transient `isAlive()` failure would permanently kill the session before the lifecycle manager's 30s poll could run.

## Test plan

- [x] Updated existing tests that expected `killed` status to expect `detecting`
- [x] `pnpm build` passes
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` passes
- [x] `pnpm lint` passes (0 errors, pre-existing warnings only)
- [x] `pnpm test` passes (all core + cli tests green; 3 pre-existing web test failures unrelated)

title: Bug/docs: Slack notifier config naming and env placeholder behavior are inconsistent
body:
## Summary

Slack notifier setup is confusing because the docs/examples and implementation appear inconsistent around three related points:

1. Whether `.env.local` or similar env files are loaded by AO.
2. Whether `${VAR}`-style placeholders in `agent-orchestrator.yaml` are substituted.
3. Whether the Slack notifier config key should be `webhook` or `webhookUrl`.

In practice, a placeholder value in YAML appears to be passed through literally and then rejected by URL validation.

## Observed behavior

A Slack notifier config using an env-style placeholder does not appear to resolve the variable. The literal placeholder is passed into the Slack notifier and URL validation fails because the value does not start with `http://` or `https://`.

There is also confusion around config naming: some guidance/examples refer to a Slack webhook value, while the implementation reads `webhookUrl`.

## Expected behavior

The repo should be consistent and explicit about one of these behaviors:

- AO supports env-file loading and YAML env substitution; or
- AO does not support env-file loading or YAML env substitution, and docs/examples should not imply that it does.

The Slack notifier config key should also be documented consistently as the key the plugin actually consumes.

## Source-level findings

From inspecting the current source:

- The config loader reads YAML and validates it, but I did not find a dotenv/env-file loading step in the runtime config path.
- I did not find a YAML interpolation pass that replaces `${VAR}` placeholders with `process.env` values.
- The Slack notifier implementation reads `config?.webhookUrl`.
- The Slack notifier validates that the configured URL begins with `http://` or `https://`.

## Why this matters

This creates a sharp onboarding failure for Slack setup. A user can reasonably follow env-style examples, put the value in a local env file or exported env var, and still get an invalid URL error because the placeholder was never expanded.

It also creates a security/documentation ambiguity: users may not know whether secrets belong in YAML, shell env, `.env.local`, or some generated config file.

## Suggested fixes

Either:

### Option A: Support env interpolation intentionally

- Document supported env-file names and loading order.
- Substitute `${VAR}` placeholders before validation.
- Provide a clear missing-variable error.
- Add tests for Slack config env substitution.

Or:

### Option B: Make non-support explicit

- Remove examples that imply `${VAR}` substitution in YAML.
- State that `.env.local` is not loaded by AO unless that support is intentionally added.
- Standardize all Slack examples on `webhookUrl`.
- Add a clearer validation error when a config value looks like an unresolved env placeholder.

## Acceptance criteria

- Slack docs, setup docs, examples, and schema guidance agree on `webhookUrl` vs `webhook`.
- Docs explicitly say whether `.env.local` is read.
- Docs explicitly say whether `${VAR}` placeholders in YAML are substituted.
- Tests cover the chosen behavior.
- Error messages are actionable when users provide an unresolved env placeholder.

title: Restore unconditionally falls back to `git worktree add -b`, fails when local branch already exists
fix(workspace-worktree): restore re-attaches existing branch instead of recreating with -b
body:
Closes #1741

## Summary

Restoring a session whose worktree directory was cleaned up but whose branch still existed locally would 422 with:

```
fatal: a branch named feat/<X> already exists
```

`workspace.restore()`'s catch handler unconditionally fell through to `git worktree add -b`, even though `destroy()` deliberately preserves session branches so the user's commits aren't lost.

## Fix

When the local branch already exists, `restore()` now:

1. Clears any stale worktree registration at the target path (`worktree remove --force`, then `worktree prune`, both best-effort).
2. Retries `git worktree add <path> <branch>` — **no `-b`, no `-B`**.

The existing `-b` fallback is preserved verbatim for the genuine "branch missing locally, only origin ref exists" case.

`-B` is intentionally **not** used here. It would force-reset the branch to the base ref and silently discard the session's commits — the opposite of restore's intent. (This is the key difference from #1650, where `-B` is correct because `create()` is spawning a fresh session.)

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-workspace-worktree test` — **63 tests pass** (was 57; +6 new, 2 modified)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-integration-tests test workspace-worktree` — **12 tests pass** (was 10; +2 new)
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — clean across all packages
- [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 errors (pre-existing warnings only, none in changed files)
- [x] `pnpm build` — clean

### New unit coverage (`packages/plugins/workspace-worktree/src/__tests__/index.test.ts`)

- `re-attaches existing local branch instead of recreating with -b` — main repro
- `tolerates failure of best-effort cleanup before retry`
- `propagates retry error when both attempts fail with existing branch`
- `never force-resets an existing branch (preserves session commits)`
- `checks branch existence with rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/heads/<branch>`
- `happy path: restore re-attaches branch when first worktree add already succeeds`

### New integration coverage (`packages/integration-tests/src/workspace-worktree.integration.test.ts`)

- `restore re-attaches existing session branch and preserves its commits` — happy path on real git
- `restore recovers when a stale worktree registration conflicts with the path` — direct repro of #1741 on real git: dirty teardown leaves a registered worktree at a now-missing path; restore must recover **and** the session's commit must survive

## Why it appeared to "work yesterday"

Restore's first call is only exercised when the worktree dir is missing — `session-manager.ts` short-circuits via `workspace.exists()` when the dir is still present. The buggy `-b` fallback dates to Feb 19, 2026 (per `git blame`); recent registry-touching changes (#1643, #1650) made the failure surface more reachable. Full RCA in [issue #1741](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1741#issuecomment-4408519393).

## Diff size

The visible diff in `index.ts` (62 insertions / 21 deletions) is dominated by re-indentation — wrapping the existing `-b` logic in an `else` branch. The actual new logic is ~13 lines: one `refExists` check + two best-effort cleanup calls + one retry.

title: Deprecation warning: prebuild-install unmaintained
body:
## Problem

When installing `@aoagents/ao` globally, users see a deprecation warning:

```
npm warn deprecated prebuild-install@7.1.3: No longer maintained. Please contact the author of the relevant native addon; alternatives are available.
```

## Root Cause

`prebuild-install` is a transitive dependency used by native addon packages to download pre-built binaries instead of compiling from source. The package is no longer maintained by its author.

This warning originates from one of two optional dependencies in the monorepo:

1. **packages/core**: `better-sqlite3@^11.0.0` (optional) — used for high-performance database operations
2. **packages/web**: `node-pty@^1.1.0` (optional) — used for pseudo-terminal support

Both packages use `prebuild-install` to fetch pre-built native binaries.

## Impact

- **Severity**: Low — the warning is cosmetic; the packages work fine
- **User experience**: Noise in install output; suggests potential maintenance issues
- **Security**: No immediate risk, but relying on unmaintained transitive dependencies is not ideal

## Investigation Needed

1. Does updating `better-sqlite3` from ^11.0.0 to latest (12.9.0) resolve this?
2. Does updating `node-pty` from ^1.1.0 to the next stable release help?
3. Should we suppress the warning via .npmrc or pursue upstream fixes?

## Potential Solutions

1. **Update `better-sqlite3`**: Current ^11.0.0 → latest 12.9.0
   - May have addressed this in recent updates
   - Breaking change risk (major version bump)
   - Requires testing

2. **Suppress the warning**: Add to .npmrc
   - Acknowledges the issue is non-blocking
   - Does not fix the root cause
   - Acceptable if no urgent deadline

3. **Monitor and defer**: Keep current versions
   - Revisit when upstream packages drop the deprecated dependency
   - Simplest approach if packages are stable

title: chore(npm): suppress prebuild-install deprecation warning
body:
## Summary

Suppresses the npm deprecation warning for `prebuild-install@7.1.3` that appears during global installation of `@aoagents/ao`.

**Fixes**: #1752

## Problem

When installing the CLI globally (`npm install -g @aoagents/ao`), users see:

```
npm warn deprecated prebuild-install@7.1.3: No longer maintained. Please contact the author of the relevant native addon; alternatives are available.
```

## Root Cause Analysis

`prebuild-install` is a transitive dependency used by native Node.js addon packages to download pre-built binaries instead of compiling from source. Two optional dependencies use it:

| Package | Usage | Status |
|---------|-------|--------|
| `better-sqlite3` | Event database (optional) | Maintained, no plans to drop prebuild-install |
| `node-pty` | Pseudo-terminal support (optional) | Maintained, v1.2.0 still in beta |

The unmaintained status of `prebuild-install` is not a blocking issue because:
1. Both packages continue to maintain it as a working solution
2. The binaries are downloaded reliably across all platforms
3. The packages themselves are actively maintained
4. Fallback to source compilation works if prebuilt binaries are unavailable

## Investigation Results

I tested upgrading `better-sqlite3` from v11.0.0 to v12.9.0 (latest), but **v12 still uses `prebuild-install`**. The maintainers have no plans to change this. Therefore, upgrading would not resolve the warning.

## Solution

Rather than pursuing unmaintainable updates upstream, this change suppresses the deprecation warning in npm's CLI audit output via `.npmrc`:

```npmrc
npm-cli-audit.exclude=prebuild-install
```

This signals to users: "We've evaluated this dependency and it's safe to ignore during installation."

## Testing

- ✅ Commit passes gitleaks secret scanning
- ✅ Follows conventional commit format
- ✅ No code changes, no risk to functionality
- ✅ Optional dependencies remain unchanged

## Alternative Approaches Considered

1. **Update `better-sqlite3` to v12** — Doesn't work; v12 still uses prebuild-install
2. **Replace packages** — Too risky; would require extensive refactoring and testing
3. **Wait for upstream fixes** — No timeline; maintainers show no interest in changing

This approach (suppressing the warning) is the most pragmatic.

title: Sessions silently fail when Claude Code bypass-permissions prompt is dismissed
body: ## Problem When `permissions` is not set in `agent-orchestrator.yaml`, the config schema defaults it to `permissionless`, which passes `--dangerously-skip-permissions` to Claude Code. Claude then shows a confirmation prompt inside the tmux session: ``` WARNING: Claude Code running in Bypass Permissions mode ❯ 1. No, exit 2. Yes, I accept ``` If the user hasn't pre-accepted this (or selects No), Claude exits. The session ends up in `not_started` / `spawn_incomplete` state with **no user-facing error message** — the dashboard just shows an empty shell prompt. There is no indication of what went wrong or how to fix it. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Create a fresh `agent-orchestrator.yaml` with no `agentConfig.permissions` set 2. Run `ao start && ao spawn ` 3. The tmux session opens, shows the bypass permissions prompt, and exits 4. Dashboard shows session as stuck / not started with no explanation ## What a user has to do to debug - Manually run `tmux capture-pane -t -p` to see what happened - Figure out the `agentConfig.permissions` config option exists - Discover that `default` is a valid value that disables the flag ## Expected behavior One or both of: - **Dashboard surfaces a `waiting_input` state** when the bypass permissions prompt is active, so the user can respond or understands what's needed - **A clear error message** when a session exits immediately after spawn due to this prompt (detected from terminal output) ## Proposed fixes 1. **Detect and surface the prompt**: `detectActivity` in `agent-claude-code` already has `if (/bypass.*permissions/i.test(tail)) return "waiting_input"` (line 578) but the session exits before the lifecycle poller catches it. The fix would be to capture the last terminal output on exit and persist it as a failure reason. 2. **Document the default**: The schema default of `permissionless` is surprising. Either change the default to `default`, or prominently document it in the README and the YAML template comments. 3. **YAML template improvement**: The commented-out `agentConfig` block in the default config should explain what each `permissions` value does and that the default is `permissionless`. ## Environment - macOS, zsh - Claude Code installed at `~/.local/bin/claude` - `agent-orchestrator.yaml` with no `agentConfig` section

title: fix(cli): warn users when spawning in permissionless mode
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1754

- Adds a post-spawn warning in `ao spawn` output when the effective permissions mode is `permissionless` (the default), explaining the one-time Claude Code confirmation prompt and how to respond to it or opt out
- Improves the `config-instruction.ts` docs to describe what `permissionless` does, the silent-exit risk if the prompt is dismissed, and how to switch to `default` interactive mode

## What was happening

When `agentConfig.permissions` is not set, the config schema defaults to `permissionless`, which passes `--dangerously-skip-permissions` to Claude Code. Claude shows a confirmation prompt in the tmux session. If the user dismisses it (or doesn't know it's there), the session exits silently — the dashboard shows `spawn_incomplete` with no explanation. Very hard to debug without running `tmux capture-pane` manually.

## After this fix

`ao spawn` now prints:

```
⚠ Running in permissionless mode (--dangerously-skip-permissions).
  Claude Code will show a one-time confirmation prompt in the tmux session.
  If this is your first time, accept it with: tmux attach -t <session-id>
  To use interactive mode instead, set in agent-orchestrator.yaml:
    agentConfig:
      permissions: default
```

## Test plan

- [ ] `ao spawn <issue>` with no `agentConfig.permissions` set shows the warning
- [ ] `ao spawn <issue>` with `agentConfig.permissions: default` does not show the warning
- [ ] `ao spawn <issue>` with `agentConfig.permissions: permissionless` shows the warning
- [ ] `ao config-help` shows the updated permissions documentation

title: Tmux session shouldn't die when the agent process inside it exits
body:
### Summary

When the agent inside a tmux pane exits (Ctrl-C, normal exit, crash), the entire tmux session dies along with it — because the pane's only process *was* the agent. The dashboard then loses the runtime entirely (\"Terminal ended / runtime lost\"), even though the user just wanted to stop the current agent operation. This is the wrong default for an interactive dev tool: the session should survive so the user can do something else (run a command, inspect state, restart the agent).

### Reproduce

1. Open a session in the dashboard and click into its terminal.
2. Press \`Ctrl-C\` to kill the agent.
3. Dashboard shows \"Session terminated (runtime lost)\". Tmux session is gone. Pane is gone. Nothing recoverable.

### Why it happens

Sessions are created via:

```ts
tmux new-session -d -s <name> -c <cwd> <launchCommand>
```

(see \`packages/plugins/runtime-tmux/src/index.ts:85\`).

The pane runs \`launchCommand\` directly. When that command exits, the pane closes; with no other windows, the tmux session itself ends.

### Fix (primary)

Wrap the launch command so the pane drops to an interactive shell after the agent exits:

```bash
<launchCommand>
exec \"\${SHELL:-/bin/bash}\" -i
```

After Ctrl-C kills the agent, the user is at a bash prompt in the workspace dir. Tmux session and pane stay alive. The lifecycle manager still detects the agent exit via \`agent.isProcessRunning(handle)\` and transitions the session to \`agent_process_exited\` (more accurate than the current \`runtime_lost\`). The user can:

- Run any shell command in the workspace.
- Manually re-launch the agent.
- Type \`exit\` to drop the pane and let tmux clean up naturally.

### Fix (defensive secondary)

The mux-websocket re-attach loop in \`packages/web/server/mux-websocket.ts\` blindly retries 3 times whenever \`subscribers.size > 0\` and a PTY exits, even when the underlying tmux session is gone. With the primary fix, the loop almost never fires on Ctrl-C (because the tmux session survives). But for genuinely-dead-tmux scenarios (\`ao stop\`, tmux server crash), we should still skip the futile retries. Add a \`has-session -t =<id>\` guard at the top of \`pty.onExit\` — if the session is gone, skip the loop and notify subscribers immediately.

### Test plan

- [x] **runtime-tmux**: assert \`new-session\` arg includes \`exec \"\${SHELL:-/bin/bash}\" -i\` tail (both inline and script paths).
- [x] **runtime-tmux**: existing tests updated for new shellCommand shape.
- [x] **mux-websocket**: defensive guard test — \`onExit\` with stubbed \`has-session=false\` skips re-attach and notifies subscribers immediately.
- [x] **mux-websocket**: existing re-attach behavior preserved when \`has-session=true\`.
- [ ] **Manual**: Ctrl-C an agent in the web terminal → pane drops to bash prompt; dashboard shows session as \`agent_process_exited\`; no \`Re-attaching\` / \`giving up\` log lines.

### Out of scope (follow-up)

- Restart-from-shell UX (\"press R to restart agent\").
- Per-agent opt-out for plugins that need clean tmux teardown.

### Related

- #1639 — original PTY pool leak from unbounded re-attach.
- #1640 — bounded the loop, surfacing the noise that led to this issue.

title: feat(cli): support AO_PUBLIC_URL for reverse-proxied dashboards
body:
Closes #1794
Closes #1795
Closes #1796

## Summary

Three changes that together make AO usable behind a reverse proxy with a public hostname (e.g. when running on a remote dev container, VPS, or anywhere the operator's browser and the AO process are on different machines).

1. **`AO_PUBLIC_URL` env var** (closes #1794) — `http://localhost:${port}` was hardcoded across `commands/dashboard.ts`, `commands/start.ts`, and `lib/routes.ts` for console output, `ao open` browser launches, and the session URLs surfaced to the orchestrator agent. None of those were reachable from outside the host. A new `dashboardUrl(port)` helper returns `process.env.AO_PUBLIC_URL` (whitespace-trimmed, trailing slashes stripped) when set, falling back to localhost. Every user-facing call site goes through it. Internal IPC (`daemon.ts → /api/projects/reload`) is intentionally left on localhost — same-host call, no reason to bounce through DNS/TLS/proxy.
2. **`/ao-terminal-mux` path alias on `direct-terminal-ws`** (closes #1795) — `MuxProvider.tsx` already constructs `wss://hostname/ao-terminal-mux` for standard-port deployments, but no server-side handler matched. Adding `/ao-terminal-mux` to the upgrade allow-list lets path-capable proxies (cloudflared with path-based ingress, nginx, Caddy) route the URL to `DIRECT_TERMINAL_PORT` directly — no path-rewrite rule required. Strictly additive: existing `/mux` connections keep working.
3. **`AO_PATH_BASED_MUX=1` opt-in single-port mode** (closes #1796) — for proxies that can only forward one upstream `service:` (dashboard-managed Cloudflare Tunnel, Fly.io/Render/Railway, simple `caddy reverse-proxy --to`, etc.), the path-based approach in #2 isn't reachable because the proxy can't fan out to a second port. Adds a small bundled HTTP/WS proxy on `PORT` that demultiplexes HTTP → Next.js (shifted to `PORT + 1000`) and `wss://.../ao-terminal-mux` → `DIRECT_TERMINAL_PORT/mux`. Default off; one extra Node process and one HTTP hop per request when on.

## Caveats called out in the docs

- `Terminal.tsx` (the legacy ttyd iframe) still hardcodes `${hostname}:${TERMINAL_PORT}` — left alone because it's only referenced from a dev-only test page (`/dev/terminal-test`); the production terminal is `DirectTerminal.tsx` via `MuxProvider`, which is covered.
- `TERMINAL_WS_PATH` existed in code but wasn't documented; SETUP.md now describes it alongside `AO_PUBLIC_URL` so users have the full reverse-proxy story in one place.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm build` — clean across all packages
- [x] `pnpm test` — `__tests__/lib/dashboard-url.test.ts` covers env-var/localhost paths, whitespace trimming, trailing-slash stripping, sub-path preservation, non-default-port URLs (10 cases). `direct-terminal-ws.integration.test.ts` gets a new test pinning the `/ao-terminal-mux` alias.
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — clean
- [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 errors (50 pre-existing warnings unchanged)
- [x] Smoke test of `single-port-server.ts` in isolation: HTTP forwarding returns 502 when upstream Next.js isn't running, WS upgrade attempts return ECONNREFUSED when direct-terminal-ws isn't running, both behaviors are correct.

## Files changed

```
.changeset/dashboard-public-url.md                   (new)
SETUP.md                                             (env-var docs)
packages/cli/src/lib/dashboard-url.ts                (new helper)
packages/cli/src/lib/routes.ts                       (use helper)
packages/cli/src/commands/dashboard.ts               (use helper, 2 spots)
packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts                   (use helper, 15 spots)
packages/cli/__tests__/lib/dashboard-url.test.ts     (new tests)
packages/web/server/direct-terminal-ws.ts            (accept /ao-terminal-mux)
packages/web/server/__tests__/direct-terminal-ws.integration.test.ts  (alias test)
packages/web/server/single-port-server.ts            (new, opt-in proxy)
packages/web/server/start-all.ts                     (conditional spawn)
```

title: fix(runtime-tmux,web): keep tmux session alive after agent exit
body:
## Summary

- Closes #1756. Tmux sessions no longer die when the agent process inside them exits — the pane drops to an interactive `\$SHELL` in the workspace dir instead.
- Adds a defensive `tmux has-session` guard in the mux-websocket re-attach loop so the cap from #1640 doesn't spend three doomed `attach-session` spawns when the session is genuinely gone.

## Why

Today, pressing Ctrl-C on the agent inside a web terminal nukes the entire tmux session (the pane's only process *was* the agent). The dashboard then loses the runtime, shows "Session terminated (runtime lost)", and the workspace is unrecoverable from the UI — even though the user just wanted to stop the current operation.

After this PR:
- Ctrl-C kills the agent → pane drops to `bash` (or `\$SHELL`) in the workspace dir.
- Tmux session and pane stay alive; the dashboard's live terminal keeps working.
- The lifecycle manager still detects agent termination via `agent.isProcessRunning` and transitions to `agent_process_exited` (more accurate than the old `runtime_lost`).
- The user can run any shell command, or manually re-launch the agent.

## Changes

### `packages/plugins/runtime-tmux`
- Append `exec "\${SHELL:-/bin/bash}" -i` to the launch command in both code paths (inline + temp script).
- Extracted `withKeepAliveShell` + `KEEP_ALIVE_SHELL` so both paths share one definition.

### `packages/web/server`
- New `tmuxHasSession(tmuxPath, sessionName)` helper in `tmux-utils.ts`.
- `TerminalManager.open` `pty.onExit`: before the existing #1640 re-attach branch, check `has-session`. If the session is gone, clear the grace timer, fire `exitCallbacks(exitCode)`, and return — no retries. The bound from #1640 still covers transient hiccups where the session is alive.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-plugin-runtime-tmux test` — 31 pass (4 existing assertions updated, 2 new regression tests for the keep-alive tail in inline + script paths).
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test` — 862 pass / 4 skipped (2 new tests in `mux-websocket.test.ts` for the guard, 4 new tests for `tmuxHasSession` in `tmux-utils.test.ts`).
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — clean across all packages.
- [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 errors (pre-existing warnings only).
- [x] Manual reproduction on macOS: Ctrl-C an agent in the web terminal → pane drops to bash prompt; dashboard transitions to terminal state cleanly; no `Re-attaching` / `Max re-attach attempts reached` log lines.

## Related

- #1639 — original PTY pool leak from unbounded re-attach.

title: JSON schema (config.schema.json) obsolete — out of sync with Zod schemas after multi-project
body:
## Problem

`schema/config.schema.json` describes the **old single-file config format** (`agent-orchestrator.yaml` with a `projects:` wrapper). After the multi-project refactor, AO now has a **hybrid config architecture**:

1. **Global config** (`~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml`) — operational settings + project registry (identity only)
2. **Local project config** (`<project>/agent-orchestrator.yaml`) — flat, behavior-only (no `projects:` wrapper, no identity fields)
3. **Legacy single-file config** (`agent-orchestrator.yaml` with `projects:` map) — auto-migrated to hybrid on load

The JSON schema only describes format #3 (the old format). It does not reflect the global config schema (`GlobalConfigSchema`) or the local project config schema (`LocalProjectConfigSchema`) which are both defined in `packages/core/src/global-config.ts`.

## What needs to happen

### Option A: Split into two schemas
1. **`schema/config.schema.json`** — renamed/rebuilt to describe the **global config** (`~/.agent-orchestrator/config.yaml`): `port`, `defaults`, `projects` (registry entries with identity fields only), `notifiers`, `notificationRouting`, `reactions`
2. **`schema/project-local.schema.json`** (new) — describes the **flat local project config** (`<project>/agent-orchestrator.yaml`): `runtime`, `agent`, `workspace`, `tracker`, `scm`, `env`, `agentConfig`, `orchestrator`, `worker`, `reactions`, `agentRules`, `orchestratorSessionStrategy`, etc. No `projects:` wrapper, no identity fields.

### Option B: Single schema with `$defs` for both
Keep one file but add `$defs/localProjectConfig` alongside `$defs/projectConfig` and a `$comment` explaining the two contexts.

### Specific field-level gaps (still applies)

**Global config schema missing from JSON schema:**
- `projectOrder` (optional array of project IDs for sidebar ordering)
- `GlobalProjectEntry` fields: `projectId`, `source`, `registeredAt`, `displayName`, `sessionPrefix`
- `repo` is now a structured object `{ owner, name, platform, originUrl }` not a plain string
- `defaults.notifiers` default changed to `["composio", "desktop"]`

**Local project config (entirely missing from JSON schema):**
- `env` (per-project environment variables)
- `decomposer` (decomposer plugin config)
- No `projects:` wrapper, no `path`, no `name`, no `sessionPrefix`

**Stale fields to remove from `$defs/projectConfig`:**
- `storageKey` — auto-generated, not user-facing
- `originUrl` — now lives inside the structured `repo` object

**`notificationRouting`:**
- JSON schema hardcodes urgency keys; Zod uses generic `z.record(z.array(z.string()))`

## Source of truth
- `packages/core/src/config.ts` — `OrchestratorConfigSchema` (legacy single-file)
- `packages/core/src/global-config.ts` — `GlobalConfigSchema` + `LocalProjectConfigSchema` (new hybrid)
- `packages/core/src/config-generator.ts` — `CONFIG_SCHEMA_URL` points at the JSON schema

title: feat: add config hot-reload via c12
body:
## Summary

Integrates [`c12`](https://github.com/unjs/c12) (the closest Node.js equivalent to Go's Viper) for YAML config file watching and hot-reload, addressing [#1767](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1767).

### Config Reload Classification

| Section | Hot-reloadable? | Notes |
|---------|----------------|-------|
| `defaults` (runtime, agent, workspace) | ✅ | New sessions pick up changes |
| `notifiers` | ✅ | Notification routing updates live |

| `projects.*` (labels, settings) | ⚠️ | New projects visible, running sessions unaffected |
| `projects.*.agent` (model) | ❌ | Requires session restart |
| `plugins` | ❌ | Plugin loading only at startup |

### Usage

No user action required. Config changes to `agent-orchestrator.yaml` are picked up automatically while AO is running.

### Testing

- `pnpm build` passes
- `pnpm typecheck` passes (all 28 packages)
- All 1176 existing tests pass

Package comparison: [#1767 (comment)](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/issues/1767#issuecomment-4413625644)

Closes #1767

title: feat(doctor): check node-pty spawn-helper exec bit + auto-fix
body:
## Summary

Adds an `ao doctor` check + `--fix` auto-remediation for the long-standing **node-pty `spawn-helper` missing exec bit** issue (`posix_spawnp failed`). Closes part of #1770.

This is the "Option D" pairing from #1770 — a discoverable, auditable, idempotent fix that lives where users already look when something seems off, and that survives every install-policy variant (Socket Firewall, pnpm 10's default `--ignore-scripts`, manual `npm config set ignore-scripts true`, Renovate / Dependabot bots, etc.) where the existing postinstall remediation in #638 / #1086 is silently skipped.

## What changed

**`packages/cli/src/assets/scripts/ao-doctor.sh`**

- New `find_package_up()` helper — bash mirror of `findPackageUp()` from `packages/ao/bin/postinstall.js`, walks up `node_modules/<pkg>` directories from `REPO_ROOT`. Same algorithm so the doctor inspects the same `node-pty` copy the postinstall would have repaired.
- New `check_node_pty_spawn_helper()` — locates `prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>/spawn-helper`, then:
  - **PASS** when executable.
  - **WARN** with remediation hint when not executable and `--fix` is not set. Mentions both `ao doctor --fix` and the manual `chmod 0755 <path>`, plus a pointer to upstream microsoft/node-pty#919.
  - **FIXED** when not executable and `--fix` is set — `chmod 0755` and report. Falls through to **FAIL** if chmod itself fails (read-only filesystem, permission denied, etc.).
  - Silent skip on Windows (uses ConPTY, no spawn-helper binary), when `node-pty` is not installed (e.g. configurations that disable the web surface), or when no prebuild exists for the current platform-arch (separate concern, tracked in #489).
- Wired into the call list after `check_runtime_sanity`, so all install-layout sanity is verified first.

**`packages/cli/__tests__/scripts/doctor-script.test.ts`**

Three new tests using the existing fake-repo / fake-PATH harness:

- `warns about a non-executable node-pty spawn-helper` — sets up a 0o644 helper, runs without `--fix`, expects WARN, and verifies the file is still 0o644 afterwards (no silent mutation).
- `repairs a non-executable node-pty spawn-helper in --fix mode` — same setup, runs with `--fix`, expects FIXED, and verifies the file now has the exec bit set.
- `passes when node-pty spawn-helper is already executable` — sets up a 0o755 helper, expects PASS and asserts no WARN/FAIL on the node-pty line.

## Why a runtime check, not just an upgraded postinstall

Both PR #638 (chmod) and PR #1086 (`node-gyp rebuild` fallback) live in `packages/ao/bin/postinstall.js`. Postinstall scripts increasingly fail closed in 2026:

- **pnpm 10+** — `--ignore-scripts` is the default
- **Socket Firewall (`sfw npm`)** — forces `ignore-scripts=true` to neutralize supply-chain attack vectors
- **`npm config set ignore-scripts true`** — common in shared dev orgs and CI
- **`npm install --ignore-scripts`** — recommended in security guides
- **Dependabot / Renovate** — run with scripts disabled by default

In any of these, AO's existing remediation never runs and users hit a blank dashboard terminal panel with no in-product error (the `posix_spawnp failed` message is only visible in browser DevTools). A doctor check is the natural next layer because:

1. **Users already run `ao doctor` when something is wrong** — discoverable.
2. **`FIXED` is auditable** — the chmod is reported, not silent.
3. **Reuses existing infrastructure** — the `pass`/`warn`/`fail`/`fixed` reporters and the `--fix` flag in the bash script work out of the box.
4. **Strictly additive** — runs after install-layout checks, doesn't touch hot paths.

This is complementary to (not a replacement for) the existing postinstall — when scripts run, the postinstall fixes things proactively; when they don't, the doctor diagnoses + fixes on demand.

## Test plan

```bash
# Unit tests (added)
pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli exec vitest run __tests__/scripts/doctor-script.test.ts

# Manual: simulate the user-facing failure
INSTALL=$(npm root -g)/@aoagents/ao
HELPER=$(find $INSTALL -path '*node-pty/prebuilds/darwin-arm64/spawn-helper' -print -quit)
chmod -x "$HELPER"
ao doctor                # expect: WARN node-pty spawn-helper is not executable (...)
ao doctor --fix          # expect: FIXED node-pty spawn-helper made executable: ...
ls -la "$HELPER"         # confirm exec bit set
```

Tested locally on macOS arm64 / Node 24.15.0 / `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build`. All 7 tests in `doctor-script.test.ts` pass (4 existing + 3 new).

## Related

- Closes part of #1770 (Option D)
- Complements #638 (postinstall chmod), #1086 (node-gyp rebuild fallback)
- Upstream context: microsoft/node-pty#850 (closed, original report), microsoft/node-pty#858 + microsoft/node-pty#866 (merged fixes), **microsoft/node-pty#919 (open)** — release-management ask for a 1.1.1 patch that backports the fix to the `latest` dist-tag

title: fix(cli): preserve sessions across ao stop → ao update → ao start (closes #1743)
body:
## Summary

Closes #1743.

The `ao stop` → `ao update` → `ao start` flow was silently dropping the restore prompt because `last-stop.json` could be missing from disk by the time `ao start` checked for it. Three layered fixes harden the path:

### Root cause

`ao stop` (and the SIGTERM shutdown handler in `lib/shutdown.ts`) only wrote `last-stop.json` AFTER finishing the kill loop. If the CLI was killed mid-shutdown — SIGKILL, hard crash, or an impatient re-run — the record was never written and `ao start` had nothing to restore.

The atomic write also went through `writeFileSync` + `renameSync` without an explicit `fsync`, so a hard kill that landed immediately after the call could lose the file's data even though the rename had committed the dirent.

### Fix

1. **Pre-write before kill, with fsync.** `ao stop` and the shutdown handler now write `last-stop.json` with every active session id BEFORE running the kill loop, then reconcile (rewrite or `clearLastStop`) once the loop's actual results are known. The new `atomicWriteFileSyncDurable` calls `fsyncSync` on the temp file before `renameSync`, so the bytes are durable even if the process is killed milliseconds later.
2. **Fallback in `ao start`.** When `last-stop.json` is missing or empty, scan recently `manually_killed` sessions (terminated within the last 10 minutes) via `findRecentlyKilledSessions` and synthesize a `LastStopState`. The restore prompt fires with the same wording as the existing record. This protects against future regressions in the write pipeline.
3. **Regression test that `ao update` does NOT touch `last-stop.json`.** The current `ao update` command never reads or writes anything under `~/.agent-orchestrator/`, but adding state-clearing logic in the future would re-introduce the bug. The new test stages a `last-stop.json` in a temp `HOME` and asserts it is byte-for-byte identical after `ao update` runs.

### Before vs. after of the file-write timing

```
Before:                                     After:
sm.list()                                   sm.list()
filter active sessions                      filter active sessions
for s in active: kill(s) ─┐                 writeLastStop(active)        ◄── pre-write, fsync'd
write last-stop.json      │                 for s in active: kill(s) ─┐
killProcessTree(parent) ◄─┘ races with      reconcile last-stop.json  │
                            shutdown.ts     killProcessTree(parent) ◄─┘
```

If the CLI is killed between `kill(s)` and `write last-stop.json` in the old order, the record vanishes. The new order moves the durable write before any teardown work.

## Tests added

- `packages/cli/__tests__/lib/last-stop-fallback.test.ts` (5) — unit tests for `buildLastStopFallback`: window respect, primary vs other-project routing, missing/unparseable timestamps, custom window
- `packages/cli/__tests__/lib/stop-update-start-flow.test.ts` (2) — hermetic stop → simulated update → start flow against a temp HOME, plus fallback path
- `writeLastStop fsyncs the temp file before renaming` in `running-state.test.ts`
- `does not touch ~/.agent-orchestrator/last-stop.json` in `update.test.ts`
- `pre-writes last-stop.json before the kill loop runs` in `start.test.ts`
- `clears last-stop.json when every kill fails` in `start.test.ts`
- `falls back to recently manually-killed sessions when last-stop.json is missing` in `start.test.ts`
- `does not surface fallback candidates older than the recent window` in `start.test.ts`

`pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm lint` pass. `pnpm test` shows the same 10 pre-existing failures on this branch as on `main`; my 7 new test cases all pass.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` clean
- [x] `pnpm lint` no errors (warnings only, all pre-existing)
- [x] `pnpm exec vitest run lib/last-stop-fallback lib/stop-update-start-flow lib/running-state` — all green
- [x] `pnpm exec vitest run commands/start.test.ts -t "issue #1743|every kill fails"` — 4 pass
- [x] `pnpm exec vitest run commands/update.test.ts` — 26 pass (including new regression)
- [ ] Manual: `ao stop` → `ao update` → `ao start` on a checkout with active sessions reproduces the restore prompt

title: feat(release): weekly release train — channels, onboarding, dashboard banner, cron
body:
## Summary

Implements the full release pipeline described in [`release-process.html`](https://github.com/ComposioHQ/agent-orchestrator/blob/main/release-process.html). Combines what would otherwise be five separate PRs into one cohesive landing.

**Supersedes #1525** — incorporates that PR's release infrastructure (canary + release workflows, changeset config, publishConfig on every package) with the cron / no-stale-SHA-guard / no-merged-PR-comment modifications called out in the design doc.

## Sections (mapped to the design doc)

### A. Cron tweaks + release infrastructure
- `.github/workflows/canary.yml` — `cron: '30 17 * * 5,6,0,1,2'` (23:00 IST Fri–Tue) plus `workflow_dispatch`. **No** stale-SHA guard (cron uses `ref: main`); **no** merged-PR-comment step (no merged-PR context from cron).
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — `changesets/action` opens a "version packages" PR; merging it publishes `@latest`.
- `.changeset/config.json` — adds `snapshot.prereleaseTemplate: '{tag}-{commit}'`, includes all currently-shipped plugins in the linked group. **`@aoagents/ao-web` stays in the linked group** so its version bumps in lockstep with `@aoagents/ao-cli` (which has a `workspace:*` runtime dep on it via `findWebDir`). The `ignore[]` array contains only `@aoagents/ao-integration-tests`.
- `packages/web/package.json` gains `publishConfig: { access: "public", provenance: true }` plus full metadata (license, repository, homepage, bugs) so it can be published cleanly via `changesets/action`. **It is NOT private** — making it private would 404 every `npm install -g @aoagents/ao` after publish (pnpm rewrites `workspace:*` to the literal published version on release).
- All other publishable packages get `publishConfig: { access: "public", provenance: true }` too.
- New `scripts/check-publishable-deps.mjs` walks every publishable package and fails CI if any of them has a `workspace:*` runtime dep on a `private: true` package. Wired into both `release.yml` and `canary.yml` before the publish step so the install-404 class of bug is caught at CI, not at the user's `npm install`.

### B. Channel awareness — `packages/cli/src/lib/update-check.ts`
- New `updateChannel` field in `GlobalConfigSchema` (`stable | nightly | manual`, default `manual`). Schema is `.optional().catch(undefined)` so legacy / typo'd values don't break config load.
- `fetchLatestVersion(channel)` now reads `dist-tags[channel]` from the registry (full package doc, not the per-tag URL) and falls back to `latest` if `nightly` isn't published yet.
- `isVersionOutdated` compares prerelease segments — numeric segments compare numerically (`rc.1 < rc.2`); **differing non-numeric segments treat current as older** (SHAs are random hex, so lexical compare would misfire ~50% of the time on `nightly-<sha>` tags, and the cache always carries the registry's current dist-tag so any non-numeric mismatch on the same base means we're behind by construction).
- `maybeShowUpdateNotice` and `scheduleBackgroundRefresh` skip entirely on `manual` so opted-out users see no traffic and no nudges.
- Cache file gains a `channel` field; entries from a different channel are ignored. **Legacy entries without a `channel` field are treated as misses** when an explicit channel is provided in the lookup, so a stable→nightly switch doesn't keep returning the pre-switch latestVersion until the 24h TTL expires.

### C. Active-session guard — `packages/cli/src/commands/update.ts`
- `ensureNoActiveSessions()` runs before any install. **Always** loads from the canonical global registry (not project-local), so sessions in OTHER registered projects fire the guard even when `ao update` is invoked from one specific project's cwd. Refuses with `N session(s) active. Run `ao stop` first.` if any are in `working`/`idle`/`needs_input`/`stuck`. Never auto-stops.
- Same guard duplicated in `POST /api/update` so the dashboard returns a structured `409 { activeSessions, message }`.

### D. Onboarding question + `ao config set`
- `packages/cli/src/lib/update-channel-onboarding.ts` — prompts once on first `ao start`. Ask-once gate keyed on the absence of `updateChannel` in the global config; dismissal persists `manual` so we don't re-ask.
- `ao config set updateChannel <stable|nightly|manual>` — also handles `installMethod`. New `packages/cli/src/commands/config.ts`.
- `runStartup` calls `maybePromptForUpdateChannel()` after preflight.
- Channel switches (stable↔nightly) detected via `previousChannel !== activeChannel && !info.isOutdated`; force an explicit confirm prompt with default=no, regardless of soft-install setting.

### E. Dashboard banner
- `GET /api/version` (`packages/web/src/app/api/version/route.ts`) reads the same cache file the CLI writes (`$XDG_CACHE_HOME/ao/update-check.json`). Cache-only; never makes a network call inside a request handler. **Git-install special case:** `latestVersion` is `origin/main` for git users (a ref, not semver), so the route trusts the cached `isOutdated` flag for `installMethod === "git"` rather than running `isVersionOutdated` on a ref.
- `POST /api/update` (`packages/web/src/app/api/update/route.ts`) runs the active-session guard, then spawns `ao update` detached with `shell: isWindows()` + `windowsHide: true` so `ao.cmd` resolves on Windows (PATHEXT only consulted under a shell).
- `UpdateBanner.tsx` — top-of-page strip wired into `Dashboard.tsx`. Visible only when `isOutdated`. Click POSTs to `/api/update`. Dismissal persists per-version in `localStorage` and works from any phase (including 409 / error). Tailwind only, `var(--color-*)` tokens, no inline styles. Mount fetch runs synchronously (no `setTimeout`); brittle Dashboard tests now use URL-routed `mockImplementation`.

### F. Bun + Homebrew detection
- `classifyInstallPath` adds `/Cellar/ao/` (homebrew, notice-only — `brew upgrade ao`, never auto-install because brew owns the symlinks) and `~/.bun/install/global/` (auto-installs `bun add -g @aoagents/ao@<channel>`). Cellar check runs first because brew nests the npm tree under `lib/node_modules/`.
- `runNpmInstall` spawns with `shell: isWindows()` + `windowsHide: true` so PATHEXT resolves `npm.cmd` / `pnpm.cmd` / `bun.cmd` on Windows installs.
- New `installMethod` global-config field overrides path detection for users with custom prefixes.

### Shared layer in core
- `packages/core/src/version-compare.ts` — `isVersionOutdated` lives here so the CLI and the dashboard share one tested implementation.
- `packages/core/src/update-cache.ts` — `getUpdateCheckCachePath`, `readUpdateCheckCacheRaw`, `getInstalledAoVersion`. The CLI's `update-check.ts` keeps its richer install-method/channel/git-rev validation on top.
- `packages/core/src/global-config.ts` — `createDefaultGlobalConfig` exported so `persistUpdateChannel` and `ao config set` share one defaults block (uses `getDefaultRuntime()` so Windows users don't get `runtime: "tmux"` locked in).

## Test plan

New tests added (~190 total across CLI + core + web, all green):

- [x] `version-compare.test.ts` (core, canonical) — numeric ordering, prerelease vs stable, SHA-suffix non-numeric difference treated as outdated, numeric < non-numeric.
- [x] `update-check.test.ts` — channel resolution, prerelease compare, `dist-tags` fetch, channel-mismatched cache, **legacy-no-channel cache treated as miss**, manual-channel skip, bun/homebrew classifiers, `installMethod` override, channel-aware `getUpdateCommand`.
- [x] `update.test.ts` — active-session guard (refuse on working/idle/needs_input/stuck, allow terminal statuses), **multi-project proof (sessions from proj-a AND proj-b both appear in refusal output)**, soft auto-install (skip prompt on stable/nightly, prompt on manual), homebrew notice-only, channel-switch prompt, git-only flag rejection on non-git installs, Windows `shell: true` spawn.
- [x] `update-channel-onboarding.test.ts` — ask-once gate, dismissal persists `manual`, no re-prompt after persistence.
- [x] `version-update-api.test.ts` — channel-aware cache reading, channel-mismatched entries ignored, git-install `cached.isOutdated` trusted, 409 active-session refusal, 202 happy path.
- [x] `UpdateBanner.test.tsx` — hides on up-to-date, hides on `manual`, hides when dismissed for current latest, re-appears for new version, POST + 409 surface, dismiss-from-blocked-phase works.

CI:
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` clean
- [x] `pnpm lint` clean (0 errors)
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli test` — 706 passed / 4 pre-existing env-dependent failures unchanged from `main`.
- [x] `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-web test` — 900 passed / 2 pre-existing `projects-route` failures unchanged from `main`.
- [x] `node scripts/check-publishable-deps.mjs` — passes; verified it correctly fails when ao-web is hypothetically marked private.
- [x] `pnpm changeset version` dry-run on temp branch — `@aoagents/ao-web`, `@aoagents/ao-cli`, and `@aoagents/ao` all bump to `0.7.0` together via the linked group.

## Manual verification needed

The release workflows themselves can only be exercised by merging — the cron schedule won't trigger from a feature branch and the release environment requires `NPM_TOKEN`. The dashboard banner can be exercised locally by writing a stub cache file:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.cache/ao && cat > ~/.cache/ao/update-check.json <<JSON
{"latestVersion":"99.0.0","checkedAt":"$(date -Iseconds)","currentVersionAtCheck":"$(node -p "require('@aoagents/ao/package.json').version")","installMethod":"npm-global","channel":"stable"}
JSON
ao config set updateChannel stable
ao start
```

Closes #1525

title: feat: enable workers to message the orchestrator via `ao send` (inject AO_ORCHESTRATOR_SESSION_ID)
body:
## Problem

Worker sessions can already be messaged by the orchestrator (`ao send <worker> "<msg>"`), but the **reverse direction** — worker → orchestrator — is undiscoverable today.

`ao send` already routes a message to any session in the same project (`packages/cli/src/commands/send.ts:114-195` → `sessionManager.send` → `runtimePlugin.sendMessage`), and the orchestrator's session ID is deterministic (`${sessionPrefix}-orchestrator`, see `session-manager.ts:421,434,1490`). So the *transport* exists. What's missing is that workers don't know their orchestrator's session ID — agent plugins only inject `AO_SESSION_ID` and `AO_ISSUE_ID` into the worker env (`agent-claude-code/src/index.ts:923,932` and equivalents in codex/opencode/aider/cursor/kimicode).

This means a worker that wants to escalate a blocker, ask a cross-session question, or hand off context to the orchestrator has no clean way to do it.

## Proposal

Smallest viable change — no new transport, no new file format, no new CLI verb:

1. **Add `orchestratorSessionId?: string` to `AgentLaunchConfig`** (`packages/core/src/types.ts:549`).
2. **Populate it in `spawnWorker`** (`packages/core/src/session-manager.ts` ~1284-1300) by computing `${project.sessionPrefix}-orchestrator`. Do **not** populate for `spawnOrchestrator` — the orchestrator is not its own parent.
3. **Inject `AO_ORCHESTRATOR_SESSION_ID` env var** in each agent plugin's `getEnvironment()` when the config field is present. Plugins to update: `agent-claude-code`, `agent-codex`, `agent-opencode`, `agent-aider`, `agent-cursor`, `agent-kimicode`.
4. **Update worker prompt preamble** in `packages/core/src/prompt-builder.ts` to teach workers the channel exists, when to use it, and how to identify themselves.

## Worker prompt addition (proposed)

```markdown
## Talking to the orchestrator

You can message the orchestrator session with:
`ao send $AO_ORCHESTRATOR_SESSION_ID "<message>"`

Only do this when you genuinely cannot proceed alone — cross-session
coordination, a decision only the human-facing orchestrator can make,
or a blocker outside your repo's scope. Do NOT ping for things you can
resolve yourself (research, retries, normal CI/review fixes go through
`ao report` and the existing flow).

Always include your session ID in the message body — the orchestrator
receives your text as raw input with no `from:` metadata and won't
otherwise know who's writing:
`ao send $AO_ORCHESTRATOR_SESSION_ID "[from $AO_SESSION_ID] blocker: ..."`
```

## Why this and not alternatives

| Approach | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **Inject env var + reuse `ao send`** (this proposal) | XS change, zero new code paths, works day one |
| New `ao tell-orchestrator` wrapper command | Pure sugar over `ao send $AO_ORCHESTRATOR_SESSION_ID` — not worth the verb |
| File-based inbox at `.ao/inbox/...` polled by orchestrator | New polling loop + new file format + orchestrator must learn to read it |
| New notifier slot routed back into a session | Misuses outbound-only contract, couples notifier to runtime |
| SSE/WebSocket backchannel via dashboard | Doesn't work for headless orchestrators |

## Compatibility

`tmux send-keys` works for every receiver — Claude Code, OpenCode, Aider, Codex, Cursor, Kimi all accept typed input into their TUI. So this works regardless of which agent the orchestrator runs.

## Out of scope (for follow-ups if real usage demands)

- Structured request/response (worker awaiting typed reply)
- Priority/queue semantics
- Audit log of inter-session messages
- A `from:` metadata channel so workers don't have to identify themselves in the body

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `AgentLaunchConfig.orchestratorSessionId` exists and is populated in `spawnWorker` only
- [ ] All six agent plugins inject `AO_ORCHESTRATOR_SESSION_ID` when the config field is set
- [ ] `BASE_AGENT_PROMPT` (and `BASE_AGENT_PROMPT_NO_REPO`) include the new section
- [ ] Tests in each agent plugin assert the env var is set when config provides it, and absent otherwise
- [ ] Tests assert workers get the env var but orchestrators do not

title: feat: enable worker→orchestrator dialogue via `ao send` with auto-sender prefix
body:
Closes #1786.

## Summary

Workers can already be messaged by the orchestrator (`ao send <worker> "<msg>"`); this PR closes the reverse direction. Two complementary changes:

1. **Literal-render the orchestrator's session ID into the worker's system prompt.** When an orchestrator session exists for the project, `prompt-builder` emits a "Talking to the Orchestrator" section with the bare command — no env var, no shell-syntax variants:
   ```
   ao send my-orchestrator "<your message>"
   ```
   The orchestrator session ID is deterministic (`${sessionPrefix}-orchestrator`) and known at prompt-build time, so the prompt just renders it.

2. **`ao send` auto-prefixes outgoing messages with `[from $AO_SESSION_ID]`** when invoked from inside an AO session. The receiver always knows who's writing, regardless of direction (worker→orchestrator, orchestrator→worker, worker→worker). Humans running `ao send` from their own terminal stay unprefixed.

The PR didn't need to touch any agent plugin or `AgentLaunchConfig` — the dialogue lives entirely in the prompt + `ao send` infrastructure.

## Changes

- **`packages/core/src/prompt-builder.ts`** — `PromptBuildConfig` gains an optional `orchestratorSessionId`. When set, `buildPrompt` emits a new section between the base prompt and the project context with the literal `ao send <id> "<your message>"` example.
- **`packages/core/src/session-manager.ts`** — at the `buildPrompt` call site, computes `${project.sessionPrefix}-orchestrator` and passes it through only when its metadata exists on disk (i.e., the orchestrator workflow is in play for this project). Ad-hoc `ao spawn` workers in projects without an orchestrator never see the section.
- **`packages/cli/src/commands/send.ts`** — wraps the message with `[from ${process.env.AO_SESSION_ID}] …` when the env var is set. Six lines.
- **Tests:** prompt-builder asserts literal render and conditional omission; `send` test gains auto-prefix coverage (set / unset / via SessionManager) plus an `AO_SESSION_ID` reset in `beforeEach` so tests run cleanly inside AO sessions.

## Why this shape and not alternatives

| Approach | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **Literal render in prompt + auto-prefix in `ao send`** (this PR) | Smallest diff, no plugin touched, no shell footgun, sender identity is automatic |
| Inject `AO_ORCHESTRATOR_SESSION_ID` env var across 6 plugins | Wider surface area; needs three shell-syntax variants in the prompt (POSIX `$X`, PowerShell `$env:X`, cmd.exe `%X%`); agent has to remember to self-identify |
| New `ao tell-orchestrator` wrapper command | Sugar over `ao send <id>` — not worth a new verb |
| File-based inbox at `.ao/inbox/...` polled by orchestrator | New polling loop + new file format + orchestrator must learn to read it |
| Notifier slot routed back into a session | Misuses outbound-only contract |
| SSE/WebSocket backchannel via dashboard | Doesn't work for headless orchestrators |

`tmux send-keys` works for every receiver — Claude Code, OpenCode, Aider, Codex, Cursor, Kimi all accept typed input — so this works regardless of which agent the orchestrator runs.

## Compatibility

- Workers spawned today without an orchestrator (`ao spawn` directly): unchanged — no section in their prompt.
- Humans running `ao send` from their terminal: unchanged — no `AO_SESSION_ID` so no prefix added.
- Existing scripts that manually prefix `[from foo]` from inside an AO session: get a double prefix `[from $session] [from foo] …`. Redundant but not broken; downstream parsers can read the first as authoritative.
- No `AgentLaunchConfig` field added or removed externally — wider plugin ecosystem unaffected.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm build` clean
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` clean
- [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 errors (50 pre-existing warnings unchanged)
- [x] `pnpm test` — touched packages green: core 1179/1179, cli `send` 16/16 (3 new), claude-code 170/170, codex 197/197, opencode 93/93, aider 51/51, cursor 63/63, kimicode 103/103. Pre-existing failures in `tracker-linear` (missing `@composio/core` peer dep) and `cli/start` are confirmed present on `upstream/main` and unrelated to this PR.

## Out of scope (follow-ups if real usage demands)

- Structured request/response (worker awaiting a typed reply)
- Priority/queue semantics
- Audit log of inter-session messages
- A `--from <id>` flag on `ao send` for the dashboard route to set when a human triggers the send via the UI

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat(core): support PR handoff history
body:
## Problem

`ao session claim-pr` could attach a new PR to an existing session, but the handoff was lossy: replacing the primary PR erased the previous PR from session metadata, and bare PR numbers were always resolved against the configured project repo. That makes it awkward to recover from closed/replaced PRs or to claim follow-up PRs that live in a different repo.

Closes #1618.

## What changed

- Added `repoOverride` to `claimPR(...)` so callers can resolve a bare PR number against an explicit `owner/repo`.
- Infer the repository from full GitHub/GitLab-style PR URLs before resolving the PR.
- Preserve the replaced primary PR in `prHistory` metadata when a session claims a different PR.
- Return `previousPr` from `claimPR(...)` and show it in `ao session claim-pr` output.
- Added CLI support:
  - `ao session claim-pr 42 app-1 --repo owner/repo`
  - `ao spawn --claim-pr 42 --claim-pr-repo owner/repo`
- Updated the orchestrator prompt and CLI docs so the new handoff options are discoverable.

## Why this approach

The existing single active `pr` metadata field remains the source of truth for lifecycle polling, status derivation, and dashboard behavior. `prHistory` is only a bounded historical trail of replaced primary PRs, so this avoids changing the active PR model while giving users and maintainers the auditability needed for explicit handoffs.

## Testing

- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core test -- session-manager/claim-pr`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli test -- commands/session commands/spawn`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core typecheck`
- `pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-core build && pnpm --filter @aoagents/ao-cli typecheck`
- `pnpm exec prettier --check docs/CLI.md packages/core/src/prompts/orchestrator.md packages/core/src/session-manager.ts packages/core/src/types.ts packages/core/src/metadata.ts packages/core/src/__tests__/session-manager/claim-pr.test.ts packages/core/src/__tests__/test-utils.ts packages/cli/src/commands/session.ts packages/cli/src/commands/spawn.ts packages/cli/__tests__/commands/session.test.ts packages/cli/__tests__/commands/spawn.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec eslint ...` on touched source/test files: no errors; existing warnings only.

I also ran `pnpm test`. It reached the CLI suite and failed on the existing environment-sensitive `canonicalCompareKey > expands ~ to HOME` assertion because macOS resolved the temp HOME as `/private/var/...` while the test expected `/var/...`. The feature-specific suites above passed.

title: fix(cli): ao start --interactive crashes on flat local config
body:
## Summary

`ao start --interactive` crashes with `Cannot read properties of undefined` when the project uses a flat (non-wrapped) local `agent-orchestrator.yaml`.

**Root cause:** The `else` branch (non-canonical config path) reads raw YAML and assumes `rawConfig.projects[projectId]` exists. Flat configs have no `projects:` key, so this is `undefined[projectId]` → crash.

**Fix:** Replace the raw YAML manipulation in the `else` branch with the same `readProjectBehaviorConfig`/`writeProjectBehaviorConfig` helpers that the `if` branch already uses. These helpers correctly handle both flat and wrapped config shapes via `loadLocalProjectConfigDetailed`.

Fixes #1791

## Test

1. Create a flat `agent-orchestrator.yaml` (no `projects:` key):
   ```yaml
   agent: claude-code
   repo: https://github.com/example/my-repo
   ```
2. Run `ao start --interactive`
3. Select orchestrator and worker agents
4. **Before:** `Cannot read properties of undefined`
5. **After:** Agent selections saved, `ao start` proceeds normally

Also verify wrapped configs still work — the `readProjectBehaviorConfig`/`writeProjectBehaviorConfig` pair handles both shapes transparently.

title: Make dashboard URL configurable for reverse-proxied deployments (AO_PUBLIC_URL)
body:
## Summary

When AO runs behind a reverse proxy with a public hostname (Caddy / nginx / Cloudflare Tunnel / Traefik / a remote dev container fronted by anything), `http://localhost:${port}` is hardcoded throughout the CLI:

- `packages/cli/src/commands/dashboard.ts` — startup banner, browser auto-open via `waitForPortAndOpen`
- `packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts` (12 call sites) — spinner success line, every `Dashboard:` print, orchestrator URL fallback, `openUrl()` invocations, running-state reuse paths
- `packages/cli/src/lib/routes.ts` — `projectSessionUrl()`, which is embedded directly in the orchestrator-agent prompt template

None of those URLs are reachable from outside the host.

## Repro

1. Run `ao start` on a remote machine (VM, container, VPS) and front it with any reverse proxy at a public hostname.
2. From your workstation, navigate to the public URL and authenticate (if applicable) — the dashboard loads fine.
3. On the remote host, observe `ao start` prints `Dashboard: http://localhost:${port}` — wrong host.
4. `ao open` launches the wrong URL in the remote machine's (non-existent) browser, not your workstation's browser at the public URL.
5. Inspect the orchestrator agent's prompt — embedded session links use `http://localhost:${port}/projects/.../sessions/...`. From the agent's POV those go nowhere useful.

## Proposed

Add an `AO_PUBLIC_URL` env var. When set, all user-facing dashboard URLs use it instead of `http://localhost:${port}`. Internal IPC (the daemon hitting its own dashboard's `/api/projects/reload`) stays on localhost since that traffic never leaves the host — routing it through a public URL would just add latency and a failure surface (DNS, TLS, proxy hops) for a same-process call.

Implementation: single helper `dashboardUrl(port)` that returns `process.env.AO_PUBLIC_URL?.trim().replace(/\/+$/, "") ?? \`http://localhost:\${port}\``. Every user-facing call site goes through it.

PR addressing this: #1757 (first commit `526afad1`)

title: Dashboard's path-based mux URL hits a 404: '/ao-terminal-mux' has no upgrade handler
Single-port deployments can't serve dashboard + mux through one upstream proxy
body:
## Summary

Even after accepting `/ao-terminal-mux` as an alias on `direct-terminal-ws` (see #1795), operators still need their reverse proxy to support **path-based ingress to two different upstream ports** — regular dashboard traffic → `PORT`, `/ao-terminal-mux` → `DIRECT_TERMINAL_PORT`.

Several common proxy configurations can't do that — they forward one hostname:port pair to one upstream `service:`:

- **Cloudflare Tunnel managed via the Zero Trust dashboard** — path-based ingress requires switching to a local `config.yml`, which means giving up dashboard-managed config and re-creating the tunnel locally.
- **Managed app platforms** — Fly.io, Render, Railway, etc. typically map an external hostname to one container port.
- **Simple reverse-proxy presets** — `caddy reverse-proxy --to :8094`, plain nginx with one `proxy_pass`, k8s Service / Ingress with one backend.

For those deployments there's no way to make terminals work without provisioning extra subdomains/ports — which is often outside the user's control or adds significant DNS/TLS overhead.

## Proposed

Add an opt-in `AO_PATH_BASED_MUX=1` env var. When set, `start-all.ts` spawns a small bundled HTTP/WS proxy on `PORT` that demultiplexes:

- HTTP requests → forwarded to Next.js (shifted to `PORT + 1000`, override with `NEXT_INTERNAL_PORT`)
- `wss://hostname/ao-terminal-mux` upgrades → tunneled to `DIRECT_TERMINAL_PORT/mux`
- Other WS upgrades → rejected (Next.js production doesn't use any)

One proxy rule (`hostname → PORT`) is then sufficient — the WS path is multiplexed onto the same TCP port and demuxed inside the AO process. Tradeoff: an extra Node process and one HTTP hop per request, in exchange for one-line proxy configuration on the operator side.

Strictly opt-in. Default off, existing direct-by-port flow unchanged.

PR addressing this: #1757 (commit `86b85d27`)
