title: TestE2E_Lifecycle fails on main: daemon removes run-file but does not exit within ao stop timeout
body:
## Summary

`TestE2E_Lifecycle` (CLI E2E, `-tags e2e`) fails deterministically on `main` HEAD on macOS and Linux runners. `native (macos-latest)` and `native (ubuntu-latest)` are red; `native (windows-latest)` passes. This is fallout from the #2185 daemon-liveness rework, not from any single open PR (it reproduces on a clean `main` checkout).

## Reproduction

On `main` HEAD (`514946fd8`):

```
cd backend && go test -tags e2e -run TestE2E_Lifecycle -count=1 ./internal/cli/...
```

Fails locally (macOS) and in CI on macOS + Linux with:

```
daemon pid <N> removed run-file but did not exit within 10s
stop: exit 1
--- FAIL: TestE2E_Lifecycle
```

Verified identical failure on a clean `upstream/main` checkout and on an unrelated feature branch based on it, so it is pre-existing on `main`, not introduced by the branch under test.

## Root cause

`ao stop` -> `waitForStopped` (`backend/internal/cli/stop.go:98-138`) removes the run-file and then waits for the daemon **process** to actually exit within `defaultStopTimeout` (10s). It hits the `info == nil` branch (daemon has already removed `running.json`) but `ProcessAlive(pid)` stays true past the deadline, so it errors with "removed run-file but did not exit within 10s".

After #2185, daemon shutdown is supervisor-socket based (the daemon self-stops ~5s after the last client drops its connection). In the e2e harness there is no Electron client holding the supervisor socket, so the stop path that the test relies on (run-file removal -> process exit) no longer drives the process to exit in time. Windows passes because its supervisor-socket teardown path differs.

## Why it matters

- `main` is red on these checks; every PR branched off `main` inherits the failure (e.g. it shows up on #2204). These checks appear non-required (both #2185 and #2201 merged with this test already failing), but the persistent red is misleading and erodes signal.
- It belongs to the daemon-lifecycle workstream (the #2185 OS-native liveness link), not to feature PRs.

## Suggested direction (pick one)

- Make `ao stop` treat "daemon removed its run-file" as stopped (the run-file is the daemon's own liveness marker), instead of additionally waiting on process-exit; or
- Ensure the daemon exits promptly on an explicit stop even when no supervisor-socket client is connected (so the e2e harness path still terminates the process); or
- Update the e2e harness to drive shutdown via the supervisor-socket disconnect path that production now uses.

Either of the first two also fixes the user-facing `ao stop` UX on a machine with no connected desktop client.

title: fix(cli): treat run-file removal as stopped in `ao stop` (#2214)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2214. `ao stop` -> `waitForStopped` removed the daemon's run-file and then *additionally* waited for the daemon process to fully exit, erroring with `daemon pid <N> removed run-file but did not exit within 10s` when the process lingered past the stop timeout. This is the `TestE2E_Lifecycle` failure described in the issue.

The run-file is the daemon's **own liveness marker**. Once the daemon has removed it, the daemon has committed to stopping. When no desktop/supervisor client is connected (as in the e2e harness, and on a user's machine with no running app), the daemon can drain its background workers slower than the 10s stop timeout, so insisting on process-exit made `ao stop` spuriously report failure even though shutdown was already underway.

## Change

In `waitForStopped`, when the run-file is gone (`info == nil`) we now treat the daemon as **stopped**. We still poll for full process exit as a best effort (so Windows releases inherited handles such as `daemon.log` before callers clean up the data dir), but exceeding the grace is no longer an error: it returns `stopped` instead.

This is suggested direction #1 from the issue and also fixes the user-facing `ao stop` UX on a machine with no connected desktop client.

## Tests

- New unit test `TestWaitForStoppedReportsStoppedWhenRunFileGoneButProcessLingers`: run-file gone + process never exits before deadline -> reports `stopped`, no error.
- Existing `waitForStopped` unit tests still pass (concurrent-start guard, own-run-file removal, wait-until-process-exits).
- `go test -tags e2e -run TestE2E_Lifecycle` passes; full `./internal/cli/...` suite (151 tests) passes; `go vet` clean.

title: ci(release): build darwin-x64 on macos-13 for Intel Mac ao start
body:
## Problem

The desktop release workflow only builds on `macos-latest`, which is GitHub's Apple-Silicon (arm64) runner. Because each runner only packages its host arch, the `darwin-x64` stable alias `agent-orchestrator-darwin-x64.zip` is never produced. As a result, `ao start` on Intel Macs 404s when it fetches that constant `releases/latest/download/agent-orchestrator-darwin-x64.zip` URL.

## Fix

- Add `macos-13` (GitHub's Intel x64 runner) to the job matrix `os: [...]`.
- Broaden the "Upload stable asset aliases (macOS)" step's condition from `if: matrix.os == 'macos-latest'` to `if: startsWith(matrix.os, 'macos')` so it runs on both macOS runners. The step already derives the arch via `uname -m` (`arm64` -> arm64 alias, `x86_64` -> x64 alias) and globs `out/make/zip/darwin/*/*.zip`, so the Intel runner now emits and uploads the x64 alias with no other changes.
- Update the now-stale comment that noted the darwin-x64 gap to reflect that both arm64 and x64 aliases are now built.

No changes to the Windows or Linux steps.

## Verification

No real CI run is available. Validated the workflow YAML parses cleanly and confirmed the matrix now lists `macos-13` and the macOS alias step's `if` (`startsWith(matrix.os, 'macos')`) matches both `macos-latest` and `macos-13`.

title: Auto-update feed metadata (latest.yml / nightly.yml) is not generated on any platform
body:
## Summary

The channel-aware auto-updater (electron-updater) cannot resolve any update because no feed metadata is published on **any** platform. This is the load-bearing prerequisite the auto-update design spec originally missed (it assumed Windows/Linux emit the yml "naturally"). Verified against the installed `app-builder-lib`.

## Root cause (verified)

Both custom makers set `config.publish: null` (deliberately, so electron-builder does not try to upload, electron-forge owns publishing):
- `frontend/makers/maker-nsis.ts`
- `frontend/makers/maker-appimage.ts`

With `publish: null`, `getPublishConfigs` returns `null` (`app-builder-lib/out/publish/PublishManager.js:356`), and `artifactCreatedWithoutExplicitPublishConfig` returns early at line 143, **before** the `createUpdateInfoTasks` call at line 163 that writes the update-info `*.yml`. So no `latest.yml` / `nightly.yml` (nor `.blockmap`) is generated on Windows or Linux. macOS ships via forge `maker-zip`, which never emitted it either.

Net: `autoUpdater.checkForUpdates()` 404s on the channel yml on every platform. The runtime updater is inert until this lands.

## What is needed (the "feed-publishing" workstream)

1. Generate the electron-updater feed `*.yml` (+ `.blockmap`) on all three platforms **without** letting electron-builder upload (forge owns the upload), e.g. provide a github publish *config* but run with publish policy `never`, or generate the yml explicitly.
2. Upload the `*.yml` to each GitHub release in both `frontend-release.yml` (stable, `latest*.yml`) and `frontend-nightly.yml` (nightly, `nightly*.yml`).
3. macOS is additionally blocked on Track-B code signing + notarization (Squirrel.Mac refuses unsigned updates).

This is verifiable only on real CI per platform and is coupled to Track-B signing. The in-app updater runtime (electron-updater wiring, `~/.ao` settings, opt-in/channel/nightly-disclaimer prompts, nightly build pipeline) ships first as groundwork and is inert-but-harmless until this lands.

See `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-26-auto-update-channels-design.md` (Feed section + prerequisites table, corrected).

title: feat: electron-updater feed publishing + macOS signing (#2220)
body:
## What this does

Makes the auto-update runtime merged in #2221 functional. Adds the electron-updater feed (`latest*.yml` / `nightly*.yml` + `.blockmap` sidecars) on all three platforms, and signs + notarizes the macOS build in CI so Squirrel.Mac will apply mac updates.

Closes #2220.

## Background

#2221 shipped the in-app updater inert because no platform emitted a feed: both custom makers set `publish: null`, which short-circuits app-builder-lib's update-info generation (verified against `PublishManager` / `updateInfoBuilder`). This PR generates the feed in a post-matrix job (no maker changes, no artifact mutation) and adds the missing macOS code-signing wiring.

## Changes

- `frontend/scripts/blockmap.mjs` (+ test): isolates app-builder-lib's pure-JS `buildBlockMap` (gzip sidecar mode); returns `{ sha512, size }` and never surfaces `blockMapSize`.
- `frontend/scripts/feed.mjs` (+ test): selects the versioned installers from a release download, writes sidecar blockmaps + the channel yml. Excludes the `ao start` aliases and `.deb`/`.rpm`. macOS merges both arches into one `latest-mac.yml` (arm64 first; discriminated by the `arm64` url substring).
- `frontend/forge.config.ts`: `osxNotarize` rewired to the App Store Connect API-key (`.p8`) path; removes the one pre-existing typecheck cast.
- `.github/actions/macos-signing-setup/action.yml`: composite action that imports the Developer ID cert into a keychain (`apple-actions/import-codesign-certs`), decodes the `.p8`, and exports notarization env via `$GITHUB_ENV`.
- `.github/workflows/frontend-release.yml` + `frontend-nightly.yml`: the macOS signing step plus a post-matrix `publish-feed` job (`latest` / `nightly` channels).

## Design

Sidecar-only blockmaps on all platforms: omitting `blockMapSize` from the yml puts electron-updater on its sidecar differential path, so we never mutate the built artifacts. Verified against the installed `app-builder-lib@26.15.3`, `builder-util-runtime@9.7.0`, `electron-updater@6.8.9`. Full spec + plan: `docs/superpowers/{specs,plans}/2026-06-27-feed-publishing-and-macos-signing*`.

## Required repository secrets (set on the fork first, then AgentWrapper)

- `CSC_LINK` (base64 Developer ID Application `.p12`), `CSC_KEY_PASSWORD`
- `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY` (`Developer ID Application: <Holder> (<TEAMID>)`)
- `APPLE_API_KEY_BASE64` (base64 App Store Connect `.p8`), `APPLE_API_KEY_ID`, `APPLE_API_ISSUER`

## Verification done locally

- Feed module unit tests: 9/9 pass (blockmap smoke + feed selection/yml assembly + nightly-version).
- `npm run typecheck`: clean (the previously-known `osxNotarize` cast error is gone).

## CI-only verification (validate on the first fork `desktop-v*` run)

- [ ] Notarization succeeds via the `.p8` API-key path.
- [ ] `latest*.yml` / `nightly*.yml` + `.blockmap` sidecars land on the release (HTTP 200).
- [ ] Squirrel.Mac accepts the maker-zip as an update payload.
- [ ] An installed older build auto-updates: Windows/Linux end to end; macOS once signed.

## Out of scope / follow-ups

- Windows code signing (separate EV-cert concern; Windows auto-update works unsigned).
- Stable version stamping off `0.0.0` (Track B): the nightly channel stamps its own version, but the stable channel needs the tag version stamped into the build before it can deliver updates (an app at `0.0.0` reading a `0.0.0` feed never updates). Tracked separately.
- No custom entitlements plist: the proven local runbook signs + notarizes with `osxSign: { identity }` and the default `@electron/osx-sign` entitlements (including the nested Go daemon with hardened runtime). Add one only if CI notarization rejects on a specific entitlement.

title: ao start: show download/install progress (a silent fetch looks like a failure)
body:
## Problem

When `ao start` has to fetch the desktop app (no existing install resolved), it downloads a hundreds-of-MB release asset with zero output until the whole thing is done, then silently runs the install step. On anything but a fast connection this reads as a hang or a failure: the user sees `ao start`, then nothing, and assumes it broke. Encountered this directly while testing the fork `v0.10.4` build on Windows.

Asset sizes today:
- macOS zip ~112 MB
- Windows NSIS installer ~91 MB
- Linux AppImage ~120 MB

## Where

`backend/internal/cli/start.go`:
- `download()` streams `io.Copy(f, resp.Body)` with no progress reporting.
- `fetchAppDarwin` / `fetchAppWindows` / `fetchAppLinux` print nothing before the download, and nothing before the silent post-download step (`ditto` unpack on macOS, NSIS `/S` install on Windows).

So the entire fetch + install is invisible.

## Proposed

- Print a line before the download starts, e.g. `Downloading Agent Orchestrator (<asset>, ~NN MB) from <repo>...`.
- Show download progress during `io.Copy` (percentage when `Content-Length` is present, else bytes transferred). A small counting `io.Writer` / `io.TeeReader` wrapping the copy, writing to stderr. No new dependency.
- TTY-aware: a live progress bar / carriage-return updates on a terminal; degrade to a plain start/done line when stderr is not a TTY (CI, pipes), so logs do not fill with `\r` spam.
- Print a short line before the silent install/unpack step too (`Installing...`), since that is also a multi-second silent gap.

## Notes

- Keep it dependency-light: a hand-rolled progress reader is enough; no need for a progress-bar library.
- Only the fetch path needs this; the resolve-and-launch fast path (existing install) stays quiet.
- Relates to the broader first-run UX of the npm launcher.

## Severity

UX, but high-impact: the very first thing a new user does is `ao start`, and right now a normal slow download looks like a broken tool.

title: publish-feed blocked by scarce macos-13 Intel runner (feed never ships when Intel leg queues)
body:
## Problem

The `publish-feed` job (added in #2226) declares `needs: release`, which waits for **every** leg of the build matrix `[macos-latest, macos-13, windows-latest, ubuntu-latest]`. Because GitHub-hosted **Intel macOS (`macos-13`) runners are scarce and queue for a long time**, a single stuck Intel leg blocks the entire electron-updater feed (`latest*.yml` + `.blockmap` sidecars) from ever being uploaded, even when win/linux/mac-arm all built successfully.

Net effect: the feed (the whole point of auto-update) is hostage to the slowest, scarcest runner.

## Observed

Fork test run for `desktop-v0.10.4` (`harshitsinghbhandari/agent-orchestrator`, run 28290189501):
- `release (windows-latest)`, `release (ubuntu-latest)`, `release (macos-latest)` -> success.
- `release (macos-13)` -> **queued for 1h35m+** (no runner assigned).
- `publish-feed` -> never created (its `needs: release` gate is unmet), so **no `latest*.yml` published**.

So a release can have all its installers up and still ship no updater feed for hours, purely due to Intel-runner queueing.

## Where

- `.github/workflows/frontend-release.yml` and `.github/workflows/frontend-nightly.yml`: the `publish-feed` job's `needs: release`.
- `frontend/scripts/feed.mjs`: `selectInstallers` already includes only the versioned installers actually present on the release, and `latest-mac.yml` lists whatever mac arch zips exist (the updater filters by the `arm64` url substring). So the feed generator already degrades gracefully to fewer assets; the gating is purely the workflow `needs`.

## Proposed

A few options, roughly in order of preference:

1. **Don't hard-block the feed on the Intel leg.** Let `publish-feed` run once the non-Intel legs finish and generate from whatever versioned assets are on the release. A missing Intel mac zip simply yields an arm64-only `latest-mac.yml` (Intel mac users don't auto-update until the Intel asset lands). Needs a way to re-run/refresh the feed when the Intel leg eventually completes (e.g. `publish-feed` also triggers on the Intel job finishing, or a manual re-dispatch).
2. **Make the Intel leg non-blocking** for the feed: split it into its own job that `publish-feed` does not `need`, or add a guard so `publish-feed` proceeds after the platforms that finished.
3. **Re-evaluate `macos-13` itself** given runner scarcity (#2216 added it for Intel `ao start` coverage) — weigh whether Intel mac is worth gating releases on, or should be best-effort.

## Severity

Important: blocks auto-update feed publication on stable + nightly whenever the Intel runner queues, which is frequent. The installers still publish, so it is not a total release failure, but the updater stays inert until the feed lands.

Related: #2226 (feed publishing), #2216 (added the `macos-13` Intel leg).

title: fix(ci): decouple macos-13 Intel runner from publish-feed (#2237)
body:
## What / why

Closes #2237. The `publish-feed` job declared `needs: release`, which waits for **every** leg of the build matrix including the scarce GitHub `macos-13` (Intel) runner. When that runner queues for hours, the entire electron-updater feed (`latest*.yml` + `.blockmap`) is blocked from publishing even though win/linux/mac-arm built successfully. Observed on the fork `v0.10.4` run: `macos-13` queued 1.5h+, `publish-feed` never started, no feed shipped.

## Change

Both `frontend-release.yml` and `frontend-nightly.yml`:

- **Remove `macos-13` from the `release` matrix** -> `[macos-latest, windows-latest, ubuntu-latest]`.
- **Add a non-blocking `release-intel` job** on `macos-13` that mirrors a macOS build leg (checkout, node 20, go, `macos-signing-setup`, `npm run publish`, the darwin-x64 stable-alias upload). In the nightly workflow it also carries `needs: guard`, `if: should_build`, the nightly version stamp, and `AO_RELEASE_PRERELEASE: "true"`.
- **`publish-feed` stays `needs: release`** (now satisfied by the three fast legs), so the feed publishes as soon as they finish.

The Intel installer + the `darwin-x64` alias still build and upload (for `ao start` and direct download). `feed.mjs` already generates the mac feed from whatever versioned mac zips are present, so `latest-mac.yml` is arm64-first and includes the x64 entry when `release-intel` happens to finish before `publish-feed`.

## Tradeoff

When the Intel runner lags, `latest-mac.yml` ships arm64-only until the next run, so Intel-mac users do not auto-update until the x64 entry lands. That is the accepted tradeoff in #2237 (option 1): the alternative is the entire feed blocked indefinitely on every release. The Intel installer itself is never blocked.

## Note

The macOS build steps are intentionally duplicated between `release` and `release-intel` (GitHub Actions cannot share a leg across a matrix boundary). Keep them in sync.

## Validation

- Both workflows parse (js-yaml load).
- Structural review: `macos-13` is out of both matrices, `release-intel` is a top-level job mirroring the macOS leg, `publish-feed` is unchanged and still `needs: release`. The rest is only verifiable on a real CI run.

title: fix(update): bundle app-update.yml so electron-updater can install (forge omits it)
body:
## What / why

Critical auto-update bug: electron-updater detects a release but crashes during download/install with `ENOENT ... Contents/Resources/app-update.yml`. electron-forge (unlike electron-builder) never generates `app-update.yml`, which electron-updater requires at runtime. The #2221 design assumed `setFeedURL(...)` alone was enough; a real fork build's log disproves it:

```
Checking for update
Found version 0.10.6 (url: Agent.Orchestrator-darwin-arm64-0.10.6.zip)
Downloading update from Agent.Orchestrator-darwin-arm64-0.10.6.zip
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/Applications/Agent Orchestrator.app/Contents/Resources/app-update.yml'
```

This affects every forge build, prod included: updates are found but never install.

## Fix

- **`forge.config.ts`**: a `postPackage` hook writes `app-update.yml` (provider github + owner/repo from the existing `parseReleaseRepo(AO_RELEASE_REPO)` + `updaterCacheDirName`) into each packaged app's resources dir (mac: `<App>.app/Contents/Resources`, win/linux: `resources/`). The repo is baked at build time, so a build auto-updates from whatever repo it was published to.
- **`auto-updater.ts`**: drop the runtime `setFeedURL`/`repo()` override (which read the absent `AO_RELEASE_REPO` env and wrongly defaulted to prod in installed apps). `configureFeed` now only sets channel + `allowDowngrade`; electron-updater loads the bundled `app-update.yml`. This also removes the need for any runtime env to point a fork build at the fork.

## Verification

- typecheck clean; `update-settings` vitest green.
- The packaged-app write is CI-verifiable only (local `npm run package` is a no-op on the build host, pre-existing). Validated by a fresh fork build: confirm `app-update.yml` is in the `.app` and an installed older build updates to completion.

title: ci(release): gate signed release on the release environment
body:
## Why
The Desktop release workflow triggers on any `desktop-v*` tag push (or `workflow_dispatch`) and consumes the repo-level macOS signing secrets. There is no tag protection and no environment gate, so **any of the ~10 write-access collaborators can cut a fully signed, notarized production build** to ~7.6k users. Now that live Developer ID + notarization secrets are configured on this repo, that surface should be closed.

## What
Adds `environment: release` to the `release` and `release-intel` jobs so the build that uses the signing secrets cannot run until a **required reviewer approves** the deployment to the `release` environment.

## Required to take effect (admin)
This PR is inert until an admin configures the `release` environment (Settings > Environments > release) with **required reviewers**. Until then, behavior is unchanged (no worse than today). Recommended companion control: a tag ruleset restricting who can create `desktop-v*` tags.

UI : use React.Memo position for SelectContent to prevent scroll reset
body:
Issue

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f4eed2d6-4e3d-4882-9757-e939bf5182dc

 ### Bug Description:

  While trying to scroll down to see the complete list of worker and orchestrator agents in the dropdown, the list would automatically snap back to the top every few seconds, causing a bad user
  experience.

 ### Cause & Fix:

  This issue occurred because the Radix UI  <Select>  component uses an  item-aligned  positioning strategy by default. Whenever the UI received live background updates (like workspace status
  broadcasts), the parent component re-rendered. This caused the dropdown to recalculate its alignment and reset the scroll position to the top.

### After the fix


wrapped the  RequiredAgentField  component with  React.memo . This ensures the dropdown component isolates itself from unrelated parent re-renders caused by background SSE events. The component now only re-renders when the actual agent selection changes, preserving the user's scroll position while maintaining the correct native alignment.

title: ci(nightly): don't gate the nightly feed on the flaky Intel leg
body:
## Problem
Every recent nightly failed, so the nightly update channel 404s (`nightly-mac.yml` not found). Root cause: `publish-feed` was set to `needs: [guard, release, release-intel]`, so **any** Intel-leg hiccup skips the entire nightly feed, for all platforms.

The Intel macOS leg is genuinely flaky:
- transient notary `-1009 "connection offline"` reaching Apple, and
- `osx-sign` keychain races → `Agent Orchestrator.app: code object is not signed at all`.

Both pass on re-run, but a **daily, unattended** nightly shouldn't need a manual re-run to publish anything.

## Fix
Revert nightly's `publish-feed` to `needs: [guard, release]` (its pre-#2244 state):
- arm64 / Windows / Linux nightlies publish **every day regardless of Intel**.
- `feed.mjs` still includes the x64 entry **when the Intel leg finishes in time** (best-effort).

The **stable** release stays gated on Intel , it's manual, re-runnable, and verified, so guaranteeing x64 in the stable feed is worth the gate there. Different reliability needs: stable = correctness, nightly = resilience.

title: fix(update): nightly channel never resolves (missing allowPrerelease)
body:
## Problem
On the **nightly** channel the app 404s:
`Cannot find nightly-mac.yml in the latest release artifacts (.../releases/download/v0.10.0/nightly-mac.yml)`

Nightly builds publish as GitHub **prereleases**, but `configureFeed` set `autoUpdater.channel` and `allowDowngrade` and **never set `allowPrerelease`**. With `allowPrerelease` at its default `false`, electron-updater only inspects the latest **non-prerelease** release (`v0.10.0`) and looks for `nightly-mac.yml` there → 404. So the nightly channel never resolved, even with a valid nightly published.

## Fix
```ts
autoUpdater.allowPrerelease = channel === "nightly";
```
Nightly scans prereleases (finds the `*-nightly-*` feed); stable stays on non-prereleases only.

## Note
Ships in the next desktop release. The currently-installed `v0.10.0` can't self-heal on nightly (that's the bug), users on nightly should switch to Stable once to pick up the build that contains this fix, then nightly works.

title: ci: retry transient macOS sign/notary flakes in the publish step
body:
## Why
Releases fail intermittently on **transient** macOS issues that hit **either** macOS leg, not just Intel:
- Apple notary `-1009 "connection appears to be offline"` , observed on **`macos-latest` (arm64)** in the stable `v0.10.0` run (attempt 1: `release (macos-latest)` failed, `release-intel` succeeded).
- `osx-sign` keychain race → `code object is not signed at all` , observed on **`macos-15-intel`** in the nightly run.

Both pass on a manual re-run. The flakiness is general (Apple/runner), so decoupling only the Intel leg (#2264) doesn't fix it , an arm64 flake still fails `needs: release` and skips the feed.

## Fix
Wrap `npm run publish` in a 3× retry with 30s backoff across all four publish steps (release + release-intel, in both release and nightly workflows). Transient sign/notary failures self-heal in-place. The Intel leg stays coupled, so the x64 feed entry remains guaranteed.

Supersedes #2264.

title: fix(ci): Windows publish shell + fresh-install smoke check (#2267)
body:
Two CI fixes.

## 1. Windows publish fails to parse (regression from #2266)

The 3x publish retry added in #2266 is bash (`for i in 1 2 3; do ... done`), but the `release` matrix Publish step had no explicit `shell:`. On `windows-latest` the default shell is PowerShell, so the step failed deterministically:

```
ParserError: Missing opening '(' after keyword 'for'.
```

Every Windows publish (stable and nightly) breaks; this is what failed the v0.10.1 cut. macOS/Ubuntu passed only because their default shell is already bash. Fix: pin `shell: bash` on all four Publish steps (release + release-intel + nightly + nightly-intel). Git Bash ships on `windows-latest`.

Verified green end to end on a fork run of the full Desktop release workflow: all legs including `release (windows-latest)` succeeded and published the Windows `.exe` plus the `latest*.yml` feed.

## 2. Fresh-install smoke check is red on main (#2267)

The container check asserts `ao start` fails cleanly on a fresh box "with no published asset". Now that AgentWrapper publishes a `linux-x64.AppImage`, the unpinned smoke binary downloads it and exits 0, tripping the assertion. Fix: build the smoke binary against a release repo with no assets, so the fetch path deterministically 404s and `start` exits non-zero with a clear error, preserving the test's intent without depending on what the real repo publishes.

Fixes #2267.

title: fix(conpty): avoid integer overflow in payload size validation
body:
## Summary

Fixes a Windows build failure in `EncodeMessage` caused by comparing `len(payload)` with `math.MaxUint32`.

`len()` returns an `int`, and on Windows this comparison can trigger an integer overflow compilation error due to implicit type conversion.

This change replaces the comparison with explicit `uint64` conversions and removes the now-unused `math` import.

## Changes

* Added a typed `maxPayloadSize` constant using `^uint32(0)`
* Replaced the payload size comparison with explicit `uint64` conversion
* Removed the unused `math` import
* Preserved existing protocol behavior and validation logic

## Why this fix

The previous implementation relied on implicit type handling between `int` and `math.MaxUint32`, which caused platform-dependent compilation issues on Windows.

Using explicit `uint64` comparison avoids architecture-specific integer overflow behavior while keeping the original bounds check intact.

## Verification

Tested successfully on:

* Windows 11
* Go 1.25

Build command used:

```bash
go build ./cmd/ao/main.go
```

title: New task dialog ignores the project's default agent and can only spawn 4 of 23 supported agents
body:
### Summary
The **New task** dialog always sends a hardcoded `harness` (defaulting to `codex`) and only exposes 4 of the 23 supported agents. This silently overrides the project's configured **default worker agent**, and makes it impossible to spawn the other 19 agents from the quick-create flow — even though the daemon fully supports them and is explicitly designed to inherit the project default when `harness` is omitted.

### Expected behavior
- The agent selector should default to the project's configured **default worker agent**, not a hardcoded `codex`.
- All supported agents (the 23 in the spawn enum) should be selectable — or, when the user hasn't explicitly chosen one, the request should omit `harness` so the daemon applies the project default.

### Actual behavior
- The dropdown always opens on **Codex**, regardless of the project's configured default worker agent.
- Submitting without changing it spawns **Codex**, ignoring the configured default.
- Only **Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Aider** are selectable. If a project's default is any other agent (Cursor, Amp, Goose, etc.), there is **no way** to launch it from New task, and it silently spawns Codex instead.

### Root cause
The frontend defeats a backend design that already supports project-default inheritance:

1. **`harness` is optional on the API.** `SpawnSessionRequest.Harness` is `json:"harness,omitempty"` with a 23-value enum.
   `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/dto.go:146`

2. **The daemon falls back to the project default when `harness` is empty.**
   ```go
   func effectiveHarness(explicit domain.AgentHarness, kind domain.SessionKind, cfg domain.ProjectConfig) domain.AgentHarness {
       if explicit != "" {
           return explicit
       }
       if role := roleOverride(kind, cfg).Harness; role != "" {
           return role // project's worker/orchestrator default agent
       }
       return ""
   }
   ```
   `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go:320`

3. **But the dialog hardcodes the agent list to 4 entries:**
   ```ts
   const AGENTS = [
     { value: "codex", label: "Codex" },
     { value: "claude-code", label: "Claude Code" },
     { value: "opencode", label: "OpenCode" },
     { value: "aider", label: "Aider" },
   ];
   ```
   `frontend/src/renderer/components/NewTaskDialog.tsx:17`

4. **defaults the selection to `codex` without reading project config:**
   `const [agent, setAgent] = useState<AgentProvider>("codex");` — `NewTaskDialog.tsx:31`

5. **and always sends it explicitly**, so the daemon's fallback never runs:
   ```ts
   body: { projectId, kind: "worker", harness: agent, issueId: cleanTitle, prompt: cleanPrompt, branch: cleanBranch || undefined }
   ```
   `frontend/src/renderer/components/NewTaskDialog.tsx:65`

### Steps to reproduce
**A — default agent ignored:**
1. Open **Project Settings**, set **Default worker agent** to e.g. *Claude Code*. Save.
2. Go to the board → **New task**.
3. Note the Agent dropdown shows **Codex**, not Claude Code.
4. Enter a title + brief, click **Start task** without changing the dropdown.
5. Open the spawned session → the running agent is **Codex**, not the configured default.

**B — most agents unreachable:**
1. Set the project default to an agent outside the 4 (e.g. *Cursor*).
2. Open **New task** — Cursor is not in the dropdown; only the 4 hardcoded agents are available.
3. Any task created spawns one of the 4 (Codex by default), never Cursor.

### Affected files
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/NewTaskDialog.tsx` (lines 17–22, 31, 65)
- Backend behavior is correct; no change needed there. References: `backend/internal/httpd/controllers/dto.go:146`, `backend/internal/session_manager/manager.go:320`

title: Activity panel shows derived status instead of agent activity state
body:
## Description

The Session Inspector **Activity** section currently renders derived `session.status` via `workerDisplayStatus(session)` instead of the raw backend `session.activity.state`.

This causes incorrect labels. Example: a Codex session can have:

```text
activity.state = idle
status = review_pending
```

but the Activity section shows:

```text
Input needed
```

because `review_pending -> needs_you -> Input needed` in the frontend display mapping.

## Expected behavior

The Activity section should show only the agent lifecycle activity state:

```text
active        -> Working
idle          -> Idle
waiting_input -> Input needed
exited        -> Exited
```

It should use `session.activity.lastActivityAt` for the timestamp, not `session.updatedAt`.

## Scope

- Preserve `session.activity` in the frontend workspace model.
- Map backend `session.activity` in `useWorkspaceQuery`.
- Update `SessionInspector` Activity section to render raw activity state.
- Do not use PR-derived `session.status` for the Activity section.
- Move or remove synthetic rows like `Opened PR #...` and `Created worktree & branch` if they remain misleading in the Activity section.

## Acceptance criteria

- A session with `activity.state = idle` and `status = review_pending` renders `Idle`, not `Input needed`.
- A session with `activity.state = active` renders `Working`.
- A session with `activity.state = waiting_input` renders `Input needed`.
- Activity timestamp reflects `activity.lastActivityAt`.
- Add or adjust tests covering these cases.

title: fix(docs): resolve MDX parsing error in installation tabs
body:
## Description
This PR fixes a critical MDX compilation error (Expected a closing tag for <Tab>) that causes a 500 server error on the Installation documentation page.

## Root Cause:
The bug was inadvertently introduced in commit 598205165. The bash commands inside the "from source" <Tab> component were placed on a single line. This formatting caused the underlying Markdown parser to misinterpret the closing backticks (```), which subsequently swallowed the closing JSX </Tab> tag and broke the page build. Additionally, the bash commands were chained with spaces instead of newlines or && operators, causing terminal execution failures.

## Changes Made:

Reformatted the MDX code blocks across all tabs so that the opening and closing code fences (```) are placed on their own distinct lines, satisfying the strict MDX parser requirements.

Separated the chained bash commands (cd, pnpm install, pnpm build, etc.) in the "from source" tab onto individual lines to ensure they execute sequentially and correctly in the user's terminal.

## Testing:

Verified locally that the docs page now compiles successfully without the Fast Refresh/Webpack serialization errors.

title: Agent Orchestrator New Landing Page UI/UX Audit 1
body:
A practical fix-it sheet to close the gap with superset.sh. Read it top to bottom, fix in order. Nothing here needs a redesign. It is mostly tightening what already exists.

The short version of what is going wrong: Superset breathes, your site holds its breath. They give every section room, one clear idea, and a calm rhythm. Your page is dense, the type fights itself, and things sit wherever they landed. The fixes below are about restraint, spacing, and a proper scale.

---

## Part 1: Issues

These are the things actively hurting the site right now. The first two are the ones you flagged, and they are real bugs, not taste. Fix these first because a broken scroll kills the premium feel faster than any font choice.

**1. The hero scroll break and the navbar stacking are one bug, not three.** This is the important correction. On a fresh page load everything works fine. The break only happens on this exact path: click into a doc from the nav, then click the Agent Orchestrator logo to come back home. After that return trip the hero will not scroll back to the top and the navbar starts sitting on top of the headings. Because it only triggers on the return and never on a cold load, this is a client-side navigation problem, not a styling problem. The hero almost certainly runs a scroll animation (a pinned or scroll-jacked setup, likely GSAP ScrollTrigger, Lenis, Locomotive, or a custom scroll listener). When you navigate to the docs page, that scroll instance is not being destroyed. It lingers with stale measurements, old pin spacers, and listeners bound to a DOM that no longer exists. When you come back home, a fresh hero mounts on top of the dead one, and the two fight. The zombie instance holds the page at a pin point calculated for the old layout, which is why scroll will not return to the top. The navbar offset breaks for the same reason, because the navbar reads its scroll position from the same poisoned state. Fix the teardown and both symptoms go away together.

**2. Snippet interactions feel clunky.** The copy buttons, the tab switches on code blocks, the hover states all feel heavy and slightly off. Superset's snippets feel weightless. Yours have visible jank on switch and no satisfying copy feedback.

**3. The whole page is too dense.** This is the big one. Look at the two sites side by side. Superset uses roughly twice the vertical space between sections. Your sections are stacked tight, so the eye never gets a rest and nothing feels important because everything is competing.

**4. Hierarchy is flat.** On your homepage, the section label, the heading, and the body text are all close in size and weight. The reader cannot tell at a glance what is a heading and what is supporting copy. Superset has a very clear three-step ladder: tiny uppercase label, big bold heading, muted body.

**5. The docs page reads like a wall.** The left nav, the content, and the right "On this page" rail are all the same visual weight and the tables are cramped. It works, but it does not feel like the marketing site. There is no shared design language between the two.

**6. Icon and logo row feels heavy.** Your "One Daemon. 23 Agent Harnesses." logo strip and the trust-logos idea are good, but the icons are inconsistent in size and weight, so the row looks busy rather than reassuring.

**7. Inconsistent card treatment.** The feature cards in the middle of the homepage use different background tones, border weights, and corner radii. Superset keeps every card identical so the content is the star. Yours draw attention to the containers instead.

---

## Part 2: Improvements

Now the fixes. Grouped so you can hand each block to whoever owns it.

### Fix the navigation bug first

Remember this is one bug, not three. The hero scroll lock and the navbar stacking both come from the scroll instance not being destroyed when you leave the homepage. Kill it on the way out and rebuild it clean on the way back, and both symptoms disappear.

- Tear down the scroll setup when the homepage unmounts. If you are on GSAP ScrollTrigger, kill the triggers and pin spacers in the cleanup function, then refresh so measurements recalculate from the clean DOM. If you are on a smooth-scroll library like Lenis or Locomotive, call its destroy method on unmount and create a fresh instance on mount. The old instance must not survive the trip to the docs page.
- On returning to the homepage, force scroll to the top and refresh the scroll library after the new hero has mounted. Many client routers restore the previous scroll position by default, which lands the page at a spot the freshly mounted hero cannot satisfy. Resetting to top on route change clears it.
- Once the teardown is in place, confirm the navbar offset behaves again. It was reading position from the same stale state, so it should fix itself. If any residual overlap remains on the docs page, add `scroll-margin-top` equal to the navbar height plus about 16px on every heading and anchor target.
- Keep the logo a plain link to `/`. This is good practice regardless and keeps browser back and forward behaving correctly.
- Test the exact failing path every time: cold load, click into a doc, click the logo to return, then scroll to the bottom and flick all the way back up. It must land at the very top with the navbar sitting correctly.

### Open up the spacing

This is the highest-leverage change for looking premium. Spacing is what separates the two sites more than any other single thing.

- Use one spacing scale and stick to it. Something like 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128. Every margin and padding should be a value from this list, nothing in between.
- Push section-to-section vertical space up hard. Aim for around 120 to 160px between major sections on desktop. It will feel like too much in the editor and just right in the browser.
- Give the hero more room to breathe above and below the headline. Let the headline be the only thing in the viewport for a beat.
- Add internal padding to your feature cards. Cramped cards read as cheap. Generous padding reads as considered.

### Rebuild the hierarchy

Copy Superset's three-step ladder exactly. It is the reason their sections feel calm.

- **Section label.** Tiny, uppercase, letter-spaced, muted colour. Example: `PARALLEL EXECUTION`. This is the quiet signpost.
- **Heading.** Large, bold, high contrast. This is the one thing the eye should land on.
- **Body.** Mid-grey, comfortable line height, kept to a readable measure of about 60 to 70 characters per line.

Right now your label, heading and body are too close in size. Pull them apart. The heading should be at least 2x the body size, and the label should be clearly smaller than the body with the uppercase treatment doing the work.

### Calm the cards and logos

- Pick one card style. One background tone, one border, one radius, one shadow. Apply it everywhere with zero exceptions.
- Normalise every icon in the logo strip to the same optical size and the same stroke weight. If they come from different sources, redraw or rescale them so they read as a set.
- For the trust and harness logos, set them all to a single muted tone (a soft grey works) so the row reads as a calm wall of names, not a rainbow.

### Make the snippets feel light

- On code-tab switch, swap content instantly with a very short cross-fade, around 120 to 150ms. No layout shift, no height jump. Lock the snippet height so switching tabs does not move the page.
- The copy button should give instant feedback. Icon flips to a tick, label changes to "Copied", reverts after about 1.5 seconds. Keep the button quiet until hover.
- Keep one syntax highlighting theme across the whole site, marketing and docs. Two different code themes is an instant tell that the site was built in pieces.

### Bring the docs in line

- Use the same type scale, the same spacing scale, and the same colours as the marketing site. The docs should feel like the same product, just denser.
- Give the tables more row height and a touch more horizontal cell padding. Right now they are tight enough to feel like a spreadsheet.
- Make the left nav active state and the right rail active state share one accent colour. Pick one accent and use it everywhere, links, active states, primary buttons.

### Add motion, sparingly

Superset's polish is partly its restraint with animation. Match that.

- One pattern only: a gentle fade-and-rise on each section as it enters the viewport. Around 24px of travel, 400 to 500ms, ease-out. Trigger once, do not replay on scroll back.
- Do not animate everything. Animate sections in, and that is mostly it. Buttons and links get quick hover transitions, nothing more.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` and switch all of this off for users who ask for it.

---

## Part 3: Typography, Iconography, Spacing and Hierarchy

The reference sheet. Set these as tokens and the rest of the site falls into place.

### Typography

- **Two families maximum.** A clean sans for everything (Inter, Geist, or similar) and one mono for code and the small uppercase labels. Superset uses a mono accent for its labels and hero, and it works well for a developer tool. You can do the same, just be consistent.
- **Set a real scale.** Do not eyeball sizes. Use a fixed set and only these values:
  - Hero headline: 56 to 64px, bold, tight line height around 1.05
  - Section heading: 32 to 40px, bold
  - Subheading: 20 to 24px
  - Body: 16 to 18px, line height around 1.6
  - Small label: 12 to 13px, uppercase, letter-spacing around 0.08em, muted
  - Caption and meta: 13 to 14px
- **Line length.** Cap body paragraphs at roughly 65 characters. Long lines are one of the reasons your page feels like a wall.
- **Weight does the work.** Use weight, not colour, to show importance in headings. Body stays regular, headings go bold. Avoid more than three weights total.
- **Colour for text.** Near-white for headings, a clear mid-grey for body, a dimmer grey for labels and captions. Three text colours, no more.

### Iconography

- **One icon set, one stroke weight.** Pick a single library (Lucide is a safe choice) and never mix in icons from elsewhere. Mixed icon styles are the fastest way to look unpolished.
- **Consistent size.** Inline icons at 16 or 20px, feature icons at 24px. Pick the sizes and stick to them.
- **Optical sizing.** Some logos look bigger than others at the same pixel size. Adjust each one so they look the same size to the eye, not just on paper.
- **Muted by default.** Icons sit in grey and only pick up the accent colour when they are interactive or active.

### Spacing

- **One scale, applied everywhere:** 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128.
- **Section padding:** 120 to 160px top and bottom on desktop, scaling down to about 64 to 80px on mobile.
- **Card padding:** 24 to 32px inside.
- **Gap between label, heading and body:** label to heading around 12 to 16px, heading to body around 16 to 24px.
- **Content width:** cap your main content column at around 1100 to 1200px and centre it. Full-width text is part of why the page feels unstructured.

### Hierarchy checklist

For every section on the site, it should pass this test at a glance:

1. There is exactly one thing the eye lands on first. That is the heading.
2. The tiny uppercase label sits above it as a quiet signpost.
3. The body sits below in muted grey at a comfortable measure.
4. There is clear empty space around the whole block, so it reads as one unit.
5. Every card, icon and code block on the page matches every other one of its kind.

If a section fails any of these, it is the section that is making the site feel cluttered. Fix it against the checklist and move on.

---

## Where to start

If you only do three things, do these:

1. Fix the navigation bug. Destroy the scroll instance when leaving the homepage and rebuild it clean on return. This one fix clears both the stuck scroll and the navbar stacking, since they share a root cause.
2. Double your section spacing and set the type scale. This alone closes most of the gap.
3. Pick one card style, one icon set, one accent colour, and apply them with zero exceptions.

Everything else is refinement on top of those three.

The daemon panics on startup with a `goose: duplicate version 20 detected` error. Two migration files in `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/migrations/` both use version number `20`:

title: fix: resolve duplicate migration version 20 collision
body:
Fixes #2293
Two PRs (#2193, #2200) merged ~2h apart each added a migration file numbered 0020, since each branch only saw one such file at CI time and neither was rebased against the other before merge. Renumbers 0020_pr_reviews.sql to 0021_pr_reviews.sql.

TestMigrationVersionsAreUnique already existed and is correct; it didn't catch this because it only runs against each PR's branch state, not the merged result of both PRs together.

title: Electron app shows default Dock icon instead of AO app icon
feat(icon): apply runtime app icon on macOS
body: ## Description This PR updates the Electron app icon handling so the app uses our AO icon consistently instead of showing the default Electron icon or a hard square icon in the macOS Dock. ## Changes ### Code Updates - **Added macOS runtime Dock icon support in `frontend/src/main.ts`** - Implemented `app.dock.setIcon(...)` to set the Dock icon at runtime - Ensures the correct icon displays in the macOS Dock during development and packaged builds ### Icon Asset Updates - **Reused existing `windowIconPath()` resolution** - Dev mode: loads `frontend/assets/icon.png` - Packaged builds: loads from `process.resourcesPath/icon.png` - Maintains consistency across build modes - **Updated icon assets with rounded corners** - Modified `frontend/assets/icon.png` to have transparent corners - Replaced opaque square background with transparent pixels - Regenerated platform-specific icon assets: - `frontend/assets/icon.ico` (Windows) - `frontend/assets/icon.icns` (macOS, if applicable) ## Why This Change? ### Problem - `BrowserWindow({ icon })` works for Windows/Linux window and taskbar icons - macOS **ignores** `BrowserWindow.icon` for the Dock icon display - Without explicit runtime configuration, the Dock showed: - Electron's default icon - Hard square appearance (opaque background) - Stale/unrounded icon during development ### Solution 1. **macOS Dock requires `app.dock.setIcon(...)`** at runtime - The Dock icon is a separate entity from the window icon on macOS - Must be set after `app.whenReady()` and before window creation 2. **Transparent corners for proper appearance** - PNG corners are now transparent instead of opaque - Provides the rounded, polished look expected on modern macOS 3. **Consistent icon resolution** - Reuses existing `windowIconPath()` logic - Ensures dev and packaged builds both use the correct asset ## Screenshots / Evidence Closes ## Description This PR updates the Electron app icon handling so the app uses our AO icon consistently instead of showing the default Electron icon or a hard square icon in the macOS Dock. ## Changes ### Code Updates - **Added macOS runtime Dock icon support in `frontend/src/main.ts`** - Implemented `app.dock.setIcon(...)` to set the Dock icon at runtime - Ensures the correct icon displays in the macOS Dock during development and packaged builds ### Icon Asset Updates - **Reused existing `windowIconPath()` resolution** - Dev mode: loads `frontend/assets/icon.png` - Packaged builds: loads from `process.resourcesPath/icon.png` - Maintains consistency across build modes - **Updated icon assets with rounded corners** - Modified `frontend/assets/icon.png` to have transparent corners - Replaced opaque square background with transparent pixels ## Why This Change? title: ao spawn: add --name flag for sidebar display name (20 char limit)
body: Add a `--name` flag to `ao spawn` that sets a custom display name for the session, shown in the sidebar. Limit to 20 characters.

title: Sidebar: edit a session's display name inline via hover pencil button
body: Make each session's display name editable from the sidebar. Show a small pencil button on hover over a session row; clicking it lets the user edit the name in place (inline), and the change persists. Keep the same 20-character limit as the spawn `--name` flag (see #2299).

title: feat(spawn): add required --name flag for sidebar display name
body:
Closes #2299

## What

Adds a `--name` flag to `ao spawn` that sets the session's display name shown in the sidebar, capped at 20 characters.

`--name` is **required**: `ao spawn` errors out before touching the network if it is missing or longer than 20 characters. There is no auto-generated default-name fallback for the flag.

## Data flow (end to end)

`ao spawn --name` -> `spawnRequest.displayName` (CLI JSON) -> `SpawnSessionRequest.DisplayName` (POST /api/v1/sessions) -> `ports.SpawnConfig.DisplayName` -> `seedRecord` -> session record (already persisted/read by the store) -> read model. The frontend already renders `session.displayName ?? session.issueId ?? session.id` (`useWorkspaceQuery.ts`), so no renderer logic change was needed; the sidebar picks up the name automatically (the same path the existing rename feature uses).

## 20-character limit

Reject (not truncate), since that is the cleaner rule for a required flag and matches the "error out with a clear message" UX:
- CLI: `--name must be 20 characters or fewer` (counts runes via `utf8.RuneCountInString`, trims surrounding whitespace).
- Daemon: enforces the same cap server-side (`DISPLAY_NAME_TOO_LONG`) so a direct API call cannot exceed it.

## Why the daemon keeps `displayName` optional

The required-ness lives at the `ao spawn` CLI surface (the issue's scope). The daemon's `POST /api/v1/sessions` keeps `displayName` **optional** on purpose: the desktop new-task dialog (`NewTaskDialog.tsx`) spawns workers without a name and relies on the read-model id fallback. Making the field server-required would break that flow (and the generated TS type). The daemon still enforces the 20-char cap whenever a name is present.

## Notes

- No changeset file: this Go rewrite has no changeset tooling. Semver is conveyed via the conventional commit (`feat:` = minor).
- Orchestrator sessions spawn through the same `SpawnConfig` with an empty name and fall back to the session id, unchanged.
- The rename endpoint (`PATCH /sessions/{id}`) is left untouched (separate surface, out of scope); a follow-up could share the 20-char cap there for consistency.

## Tests

- `internal/cli`: new `--name` required + overlong guards; existing spawn tests updated to pass `--name`; DTO round-trip asserts `displayName` reaches `SpawnConfig`.
- `internal/httpd/controllers`: spawn round-trip asserts `displayName` flows to the read model; new test asserts the server-side 20-char cap (`DISPLAY_NAME_TOO_LONG`).
- OpenAPI spec + `schema.ts` regenerated via `npm run api`.

## Verification

- `cd backend && go build ./... && go test ./...` -> 1650 passed, 80 packages.
- `go vet` on touched packages: clean.
- Manual: `ao spawn --project demo` -> `--name is required`; `--name <21 chars>` -> `--name must be 20 characters or fewer`.

title: fix: show latest reviewer verdict after PR updates
body:
Fixes #2300.

## Before
- Review state was selected only by the current PR head SHA.
- If a reviewer completed `changes_requested` on `sha-old` and the worker pushed `sha-new`, the planner found no run for `sha-new`.
- The Reviews tab row became `needs_review`, but had no `latestRun` attached for display.
- The visible row verdict and top badge could fall back to `Not run`, even though the latest actual review verdict was `changes_requested` or `approved`.
- The `Run review` button was available, which was correct.

## After
- The planner still marks the PR as `needs_review` when the head SHA changes, so the button stays available.
- It also attaches the newest review run for that PR as `latestRun`, even if that run was for a previous SHA.
- The Reviews tab now prefers `latestRun.verdict` when choosing the visible label.
- After `changes_requested` on `sha-old` and a push to `sha-new`, the row and top badge still show `Changes requested`.
- The user can still click `Run review` to send the next review request for `sha-new`.

## Reviewer trigger behavior
- No auto-triggering is added.
- Existing trigger flow already sends a message to a live reviewer terminal via `Notify`/`SendMessage`.
- If the reviewer pane is not alive, it spawns a new reviewer with the review prompt in the launch command.

## Tests
- `npm run lint`
- `npm run frontend:typecheck`
- `cd backend && go test ./internal/review ./internal/httpd/...`

title: fix(migrations): resolve duplicate version 20 collision
body:
## Summary

`main` ships **two SQLite migrations at version 20**. Goose panics on every fresh daemon boot before either runs, breaking `ao daemon` and most of the backend test suite.

Renumber the later-merged file (`0020_review_run_unique_pr_sha.sql` → `0021_review_run_unique_pr_sha.sql`) so versions are unique again.

## Why it's broken

Two PRs added migration version 20 unaware of each other:

- #2193 (`cb456bb2`) → `0020_pr_reviews.sql`
- #2200 (`a31cf1b5`) → `0020_review_run_unique_pr_sha.sql`

Goose stable-sorts pending migrations by version on every `Open`, and Go's `sort.Sort` requires a **strict weak ordering**. Two equal versions violate that contract; `Migrations.Less` panics:

```
goose.Migrations.Less
goose.sortAndConnectMigrations
goose.collectMigrationsFS
sqlite.migrate -> sqlite.Open -> daemon.Run
```

## Verified

Repro on isolated `AO_DATA_DIR` with both files present:

```
AO_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ao-fresh AO_PORT=3098 go run ./cmd/ao daemon
# panic before "daemon listening"
```

With the rename applied:

```
AO_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ao-fresh-fixed AO_PORT=3097 go run ./cmd/ao daemon
# daemon listening addr=127.0.0.1:3097 pid=...
sqlite3 .../ao.db 'SELECT version_id FROM goose_db_version ORDER BY version_id;'
# 17, 18, 19, 20, 21 — applied in order
```

- `go test ./...` → **zero failures** (was hitting the panic in every sqlite-touching package)
- `go test -race ./internal/storage/sqlite/... ./internal/daemon/...` → green

## Renaming a merged migration

AGENTS.md normally bans renaming merged migrations — the rule protects live DBs whose `goose_db_version` table records the old `version_id`. Here that risk does not apply: **no live DB can have recorded `version_id = 20` for either file**, because goose panics on sort before applying either. The rename is the smallest fix that restores boot.

Body of the renumbered file is unchanged. Its unique-index DDL does not depend on the `pr_reviews` table, so ordering is free.

## Risk

Anyone whose working tree silently lost one of the two files (filesystem case quirks, stale checkout) has been booting on a half-applied state. Their next pull restores the file under version 21; goose applies it on top of the existing DB. Idempotent.

Closes #2305.

title: Daemon panics on fresh boot: duplicate SQLite migration version 20
body:
## Bug

`main` ships two SQLite migrations at version 20:

- `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/migrations/0020_pr_reviews.sql` (from #2193, `cb456bb2`)
- `backend/internal/storage/sqlite/migrations/0020_review_run_unique_pr_sha.sql` (from #2200, `a31cf1b5`)

Goose stable-sorts pending migrations by version on every `Open`. Go's `sort.Sort` requires a **strict weak ordering**; two entries with equal versions violate that contract and panic `Migrations.Less`. The panic fires inside `sqlite.Open` → so every fresh `ao daemon` boot and every test that opens a SQLite store crashes.

## Repro

```bash
git clone https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator.git
cd agent-orchestrator/backend
AO_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ao-repro AO_RUN_FILE=/tmp/ao-repro/running.json AO_PORT=3098 \
  go run ./cmd/ao daemon
```

Result: panic before `daemon listening`. Stack trace:

```
panic: runtime error: comparing uncomparable type
goose.Migrations.Less        github.com/pressly/goose/v3@v3.27.1/migrate.go:37
goose.sortAndConnectMigrations                          migrate.go:180
goose.collectMigrationsFS                               migrate.go:170
goose.UpToContext                                       up.go:46
sqlite.migrate                  internal/storage/sqlite/db.go:96
sqlite.Open                     internal/storage/sqlite/db.go:64
daemon.Run                      internal/daemon/daemon.go:58
cli.NewRootCommand.newDaemonCommand.func3   internal/cli/root.go:267
```

`go test ./...` hits the same panic in every package that opens a store (`internal/daemon`, `internal/storage/sqlite/store`, `internal/service/*`, etc.).

## Impact

- Any fresh clone of `main` cannot start the daemon
- `go test ./...` fails for any sqlite-touching package
- Existing developers whose working trees silently lost one of the two files (filesystem case quirks, stale checkouts) keep booting fine until they refresh — then they hit the panic

## Why it slipped through

The two PRs were authored concurrently and neither review surfaced the version collision because goose only fails at the open call, not at `go build` or `go vet`. CI doesn't currently fail on fresh-boot smoke either, so both merged green.

## Fix

PR #2304 renames the later-merged file to `0021_review_run_unique_pr_sha.sql`. Renaming a merged migration normally violates AGENTS.md, but the rule's purpose (protect live DBs that recorded the old version) does not apply here: goose panics on sort before applying either file, so no live DB can have `version_id = 20` for either.

Body of the renumbered file is unchanged. Its unique-index DDL does not depend on the `pr_reviews` table, so ordering is free.

## Suggested follow-up

Add a CI guard that fails when two migrations share a version number — a one-line `find` / `sort | uniq -d` check would have caught this at merge time.

title: feat(review): support additional reviewer harnesses
body:
## Summary

Reviewer sessions can now use the two additional harnesses requested in #2298, including automatic reuse of a worker's harness when no reviewer override is configured. Both adapters reuse the existing worker launchers while applying reviewer-specific read-only controls, and Project Settings exposes the expanded reviewer choices.

## Validation

- `cd backend && go test -race ./...`

- Live Settings flow against an isolated daemon: selected a new reviewer, saved it through the UI, and verified the persisted project config over the daemon API.
- Verified the installed CLI resolves the inline read-only permission policy exactly as authored.

- Search daemon logs for `no reviewer adapter`, `reviewer command`, and `reviewer runtime` after review launches.
- Healthy signal: configured reviews enter `running`, open a reviewer pane, and submit a verdict without modifying the worker checkout.
- Failure signal: repeated launch errors, permission prompts that stall the pane, or a reviewer unable to post/submit its result. Roll back this PR if those failures reproduce with a supported local installation.

## Testing Codex and OpenCode reviewer harnesses end-to-end

Concrete recipe for running a review with each new harness against a live daemon, requested in [this comment](https://github.com/AgentWrapper/agent-orchestrator/pull/2306#issuecomment-4846398715).

### Prerequisites

- `codex` and/or `opencode` CLIs installed and on `$PATH` (verify with `codex --version` / `opencode --version`)
- AO daemon running (`ao start` or the desktop app)
- A worker session with at least one open PR — this is the review target

### 1. Set the reviewer harness for a project

Two ways:

**Settings UI** — `Project → Settings → Reviewers → Default reviewer agent`. The Select now lists `codex` and `opencode` alongside `claude-code`.

**CLI** — write the config directly:

```bash
ao project set-config <project-id> --config-json '{
  "worker":       {"agent": "codex"},
  "orchestrator": {"agent": "claude-code"},
  "reviewers":    [{"harness": "codex"}]
}'
# or "harness": "opencode"
```

Verify it persisted:

```bash
ao project get <project-id> --json | jq '.config.reviewers'
# → [{"harness":"codex"}]
```

### 2. Trigger a review on the worker's open PR

```bash
SESSION=<worker-session-id>
curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:${AO_PORT:-3001}/api/v1/sessions/${SESSION}/reviews/trigger"
```

The daemon resolves the reviewer harness via `ProjectConfig.ResolveReviewerHarness`, picks the matching adapter (`reviewer/codex` or `reviewer/opencode`), and spawns a reviewer pane in the same workspace.

### 3. Verify the reviewer pane launched with the right sandbox

**Codex** — the adapter inserts `--sandbox read-only` and forwards AO location env vars via Codex's `-c shell_environment_policy.set.*`. Inspect the live process:

```bash
ps -axo pid,command | grep '[c]odex' | grep review
# Look for: --sandbox read-only
# Look for: -c shell_environment_policy.set.AO_PORT="3001"
#           -c shell_environment_policy.set.AO_DATA_DIR="/Users/.../.ao"
#           -c shell_environment_policy.set.AO_RUN_FILE="/Users/.../.ao/running.json"
```

Attempt an edit inside the codex pane (e.g. `:!echo x >> README.md`) — Codex refuses because the sandbox is read-only. `git diff`, `gh api`, and `ao review submit` remain available.

**OpenCode** — the adapter injects the permission policy via the `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` env var. Inspect:

```bash
ps -axEo pid,command,env | grep '[o]pencode' | grep -o 'OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT=[^ ]*'
# → JSON: "*":"deny","read":"allow","glob":"allow","grep":"allow",
#         "bash":{"*":"deny","gh api *":"allow","git diff*":"allow",
#                 "git log*":"allow","git show*":"allow","git status*":"allow",
#                 "ao review submit *":"allow"}
```

Inside the OpenCode pane: read/grep/glob and the listed bash commands work; every other tool and bash command is denied.

### 4. Verify the verdict round-trip

The reviewer pane runs `ao review submit --review-id <id> --reviews <json>`. Daemon writes the verdict and emits a notification:

```bash
ao session get "$SESSION" --json | jq '.reviews[-1]'
# → {"id":"...", "verdict":"approved" | "changes_requested", "harness":"codex", ...}
```

### Unit + build coverage already in CI

- `backend/internal/adapters/reviewer/codex/codex_test.go`:
  - `TestReviewCommandUsesReadOnlySandbox` — asserts `--sandbox read-only` is inserted before the prompt argument and each AO_* env var becomes a `-c shell_environment_policy.set.*` entry
  - `TestReviewMessageReturnsTaskPrompt` — confirms a follow-up message reuses the same task prompt
- `backend/internal/adapters/reviewer/opencode/opencode_test.go`:
  - `TestReviewCommandUsesReadOnlyPermissionPolicy` — asserts the exact policy JSON travels via the `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` env var and the system prompt is folded into the prompt
  - `TestReviewMessageReturnsTaskPrompt`
- `backend/internal/domain/projectconfig_test.go` — `Validate` table rows reject configs that name an unsupported reviewer harness and accept the two new ones
- `frontend/src/renderer/components/ProjectSettingsForm.test.tsx` — Reviewer `<Select>` round-trips `codex` and `opencode` through save

Run locally:

```bash
go test ./backend/internal/adapters/reviewer/codex/... \
        ./backend/internal/adapters/reviewer/opencode/... \
        ./backend/internal/domain/... -race -v
cd frontend && npm test -- ProjectSettingsForm
```

title: feat: add agent catalog/auth API and safer orchestrator switching
body:
Summary
This PR adds a daemon-backed agent catalog, exposes installed/authorized agent state to the frontend, and uses that data in project settings so users can choose worker/orchestrator agents more safely.

It also adds orchestrator replacement handling: when the saved orchestrator agent changes, AO starts the replacement first and only retires the previous orchestrator after the new one is up, so a failed replacement does not cause downtime.

A key caveat is that agent-auth/login flows can interfere with replacement startup. If switching agents triggers the agent’s own bootstrap path, the replacement may come up outside AO’s normal orchestrator initialization path and miss the AO orchestrator system prompt.

What Changed
Backend
Added agent inventory service for:

supported agents
installed agents
authorized agents
counts for each
Added optional AgentAuthChecker capability on adapters.

Added shared CLI auth probing helper for adapters with cheap local auth checks.

Added GET /api/v1/agents.

Extended registry inventory entries to carry adapter manifest metadata for user-facing labels.

Added orchestrator replacement flow in the session service:

spawn replacement first
retire previous orchestrator only after successful replacement
preserve previous orchestrator when replacement startup fails
Added backend tests for agent catalog, controller responses, session replacement behavior, and related project/service wiring.

Frontend
Regenerated API types for the new agents endpoint/DTOs.

Updated ProjectSettingsForm to:

load agent catalog from the daemon
show authorized agent options
handle installed-but-not-authorized states
surface orchestrator replacement pending state
allow retry once replacement is safe to perform
Added/updated tests for the new settings behavior.



https://github.com/aoagents/ReverbCode/pull/276.   extended version of this pr

title: Project Settings allows switching to unsupported orchestrator agents without preflight install/auth checks
body:
Summary

The orchestrator agent picker currently lets users switch to agents even when AO does not know whether that agent is installed or authenticated. That creates a
broken switch flow:

if the agent is not installed, it should not be selectable as a runnable orchestrator target
if the agent is installed but not authenticated, should not be selectable as a runnable orchestrator target
if switching triggers the agent’s own login/bootstrap flow, that can spawn a fresh session outside AO’s normal orchestrator startup path, so the replacement
session may miss AO’s system prompt / expected initialization
This means the settings UI can present options that are not actually safe to switch to.

Problem

Today the user can pick an orchestrator agent without a reliable preflight check for:

supported by AO
installed locally
authenticated / ready to run
That leads to two bad outcomes:

The agent still appears in the switcher.
The user can save and attempt a restart.
Restart then fails late instead of the UI blocking the choice up front.
The switch is allowed.
The agent may prompt for login during startup.
That login flow can create a new session/process that AO did not initialize the normal way.
The resulting session may not receive AO’s system prompt and expected orchestrator bootstrap.
Expected behavior

The switcher should only present agents in states the user can act on clearly.
Unsupported or unavailable agents should not look like normal selectable options.
If an agent is not installed, the UI should show that state and block switching.
If an agent is not authenticated, the UI should show that state before save/restart, not only after failure.
AO should only cut over to a new orchestrator when the target agent is actually ready to launch through AO’s normal startup path.
Why this matters

This is not just a UX issue. It can produce orchestrator sessions that start outside AO’s intended initialization path, which risks missing the system prompt
and breaking orchestrator behavior in subtle ways.

Acceptance criteria

Agent catalog API exposes per-agent readiness state: supported, installed, authenticated.
Project Settings uses that catalog instead of treating every known agent as equally selectable.
Uninstalled agents are not shown as normal switch targets, or are visibly disabled with an install-required reason.
Installed but unauthenticated agents are clearly marked before switching.
Save/restart is blocked unless the selected orchestrator agent is runnable through AO.
Switching cannot fall into an external login/bootstrap path that bypasses AO’s normal orchestrator initialization.
Tests cover:
uninstalled agent
installed but unauthenticated agent
installed and authenticated agent
restart path preserving AO system-prompt initialization

closes #2310

title: Killed sessions resurrect as alive after Cmd+Q restart (stale session_worktrees restore marker)
body:
## Bug

After Cmd+Q quitting the desktop app and reopening it, sessions the user **killed** reappear as if alive. Killed sessions should stay dead across an app restart (while still being manually restorable on demand).

## Root cause

Category **(c): startup resurrects terminated rows.** `Kill` correctly persists `is_terminated=1`; quit doesn't tear sessions down at all. The fault is the **`session_worktrees` restore-marker lifecycle**: the marker is write-only and never cleared, so the boot-time `RestoreAll` mistakes a user-killed session for a "shutdown-saved" one and relaunches it.

`RestoreAll` gates auto-relaunch solely on whether a `session_worktrees` row exists (`session_manager/manager.go:777-786`):

```go
rows, err := m.store.ListSessionWorktrees(ctx, rec.ID)
if len(rows) == 0 {
    // No marker: this session was killed by the user before shutdown.
    continue
}
// ...otherwise relaunch via m.Restore -> MarkSpawned
```

That comment encodes an invariant ("user-killed sessions have no marker row") that is **false**, because nothing deletes the marker:

- `DeleteSessionWorktrees` exists in the store/gen layer but is **never called in production**.
- `Kill` (`manager.go:430-465`) marks terminated and destroys runtime/worktree but **never touches the marker**.
- `RestoreAll` relaunches a session but **never deletes the marker after consuming it** (`manager.go:768-840`) — the marker is not one-shot.
- The marker is created by `reconcileLive` on boot (`manager.go:683`) and `saveAndTeardownOne` (`manager.go:608`).

On relaunch, `MarkSpawned` (`lifecycle/manager.go:243`) sets `IsTerminated = false` and activity to `idle` — which is why resurrected sessions show up alive.

## Live DB proof (`agent-orchestrator` project)

```
 id    activity_state  is_terminated  markers
 2     exited               1            0     <- killed, NO marker -> stays dead (control)
 7     exited               1            1     <- KILLED but marker present -> will resurrect next launch
 8     exited               1            1     <- same
 9     exited               1            1     <- same
 3,4,5,6,10,11,12  idle    0            1     <- already resurrected once (term cleared), still carry marker
 13,14,15,16  waiting_input 0           0     <- genuinely alive, never saved
```

Session 2 vs 7/8/9 is decisive: all are killed, but only the ones carrying a leftover marker are time-bombs. Sessions 3-6/10-12 are the bug already manifested.

## Repro

1. Spawn session N; let it be alive.
2. Cmd+Q (daemon exits without teardown; runtime dies with it).
3. Reopen -> `Reconcile`/`reconcileLive` writes a marker, marks terminated, then `RestoreAll` relaunches N (`MarkSpawned` clears `is_terminated`). **Marker left in place.**
4. User kills N -> `Kill` sets `is_terminated=1`. **Marker still in place.**
5. Cmd+Q, reopen -> `RestoreAll` finds the stale marker -> relaunches the killed session. **Bug.**

A session spawned and killed without ever surviving a reopen cycle (like session 2) never gets a marker and correctly stays dead, which is why the bug looks intermittent.

## Fix direction

Restore the invariant the `RestoreAll` guard already assumes; two layers:

1. **`Kill` clears the marker** — call `DeleteSessionWorktrees(ctx, id)` in `Kill`. A user kill is explicit terminal intent and must not leave a resurrection marker.
2. **Marker is one-shot** — `RestoreAll` deletes the marker after it successfully relaunches (or leaves terminated), so it never outlives a single restart. A still-live session re-acquires a fresh marker via `reconcileLive` at the next quit.

**Restorability is preserved:** manual restore (`POST /sessions/{id}/restore` -> `manager.Restore`, `manager.go:470`) is marker-independent (only needs `IsTerminated && WorkspacePath && Branch`; re-creates the worktree from the branch). Deleting the marker removes only the *auto-relaunch-on-boot* flag, not the ability to manually restore a killed session later.

One-time cleanup: delete `session_worktrees` rows for sessions where `is_terminated=1` to defuse existing time-bombs.

title: fix(session): keep killed sessions dead across restart (clear stale restore marker)
body:
## What

Killed sessions reappear as alive after a Cmd+Q quit + reopen. This fixes the stale-restore-marker lifecycle so a killed session stays dead across restart, while remaining manually restorable on demand.

Fixes #2319.

## Root cause

The boot-time `RestoreAll` auto-relaunches any terminated session that still has a `session_worktrees` row (the "shutdown-saved" marker). That marker was write-only: nothing ever deleted it. `Kill` left it in place, and `RestoreAll` never consumed it. So a session that survived one reopen cycle (which gave it a marker via `reconcileLive`) and was then killed still carried the marker, and the next boot resurrected it. On relaunch `MarkSpawned` clears `is_terminated`, so it shows up alive.

`DeleteSessionWorktrees` already existed on the store but was never called in production.

## Fix

1. Add `DeleteSessionWorktrees` to the Manager `Store` interface (concrete store already implements it).
2. `Kill` deletes the restore marker after `MarkTerminated` (best-effort, logged on failure). A user kill is explicit terminal intent and must not leave a resurrection marker.
3. `RestoreAll` deletes the marker after consuming it, making it one-shot so it never outlives a single restart. A still-live session re-acquires a fresh marker via `reconcileLive`/`saveAndTeardownOne` at the next quit.

Manual restore (`POST /sessions/{id}/restore`) is untouched and marker-independent, so a killed session stays restorable on demand, just not auto-resurrected on boot.

## Tests

- `TestKill_DeletesRestoreMarker`: after Kill, the marker is gone.
- `TestRestoreAll_DeletesMarkerAfterRelaunch`: marker is one-shot.
- `TestRestoreAll_KilledSessionNotResurrectedOnSecondBoot`: a killed session relaunches at most once and stays terminated on the second boot.

All three failed before the fix for the right reason. `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `go test ./internal/session_manager/... ./internal/lifecycle/... ./internal/storage/...` (173 tests) all pass.

## Note for existing installs

Existing DBs may carry `session_worktrees` rows on already-killed sessions (time-bombs). A one-time cleanup `DELETE FROM session_worktrees WHERE session_id IN (SELECT id FROM sessions WHERE is_terminated=1)` defuses them; not included here since it is environment state, not code.
